src: It was a hot summer day in July when I finally turned 16 years old.
trg: Ezalaki mokolo ya moi makasi na eleko ya molunge na sanza ya Nsambo ntango nsukansuka nakokisaki mibu 16.

src: I had been eagerly anticipating this day for as long as I could remember, and now that it was finally here, I couldn't wait to get started on my road to freedom.
trg: Nazalaki kozela mokolo oyo na mposa makasi ndenge nazali kokanisa, mpe sikoyo nsukansuka ekomi, nakoki kozela te na kobanda nzela na nga ya bonsomi.

src: The first step was to take the written test.
trg: Etape ya liboso ezalaki kosala ekzame ya kokoma.

src: I studied hard for weeks, and I was confident that I would pass.
trg: Nayekolaka makasi bamposo ebele, mpe nazalaki kondima nakolonga.

src: On the day of the test, I arrived at the DMV early and took my seat in the waiting room.
trg: Na mokolo ya ekzame, nakomaki na DMV liboso mpenza mpe nafandaki na esika ya kozela.

src: After a few hours, my name was called, and I was ushered into a small room with a computer.
trg: Mwa bangonga moke na nsima, babengaki nkombo na nga, mpe bakotisaki nga na ndako ya moke ezali na ordinatere.

src: The test was surprisingly easy, and I finished it in no time.
trg: Ekzame ezalaka pete makasi, mpe naumelaki te na kosilisa yango.

src: A few days later, I received a letter in the mail informing me that I had passed the written test.
trg: Mwa mikolo na nsima, nazwaki mokanda ezali koyebisa nga ete nalongaki na ekzame ya kokoma.

src: The next step was to schedule a driving test.
trg: Etape elandaki ezalaki kozwa rendez-vous ya ekzame ya kokumba.

src: I called the DMV and made an appointment for the following week.
trg: Nabengaki DMV mpe nazwaki rendez-vous mpo na mposa ezali koya.

src: The day of my driving test arrived, and I was more nervous than I had ever been in my life.
trg: Mokolo ya ekzame na nga ya kokumba ekokaki, mpe nazalaki komitungisa ndenge nasala nanu te bomoi mobimba.

src: I drove to the DMV with my mom, who would be accompanying me on the test.
trg: Nakendaki na DMV na mama, oyo akendaki kotika nga na ekzame wana.

src: Global warming is the long-term heating of Earth's climate system observed since the pre-industrial period (between 1850 and 1900) due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.
trg: Molunge ya mokili mobimba ezali komata ya molunge ya ntango moali na climat ya Mabele oyo tomona banda na eleko ya liboso ya ba izine (banda 1850 kino 1900) euti na misala ya bato, mingimingi na kozikisa bafosile to biloko ya kala, oyo ezali komatisa banivo ya ba gaz à fer de serre na mopepe ya Mabele.

src: The term is frequently used interchangeably with the term climate change, though the latter refers to both human- and naturally produced warming and the effects it has on our planet.
trg: Bazali kosalela mpe liloba wana mpo na kolobela mbongwana ya climat, kasi mbongwana ya climat ezali kolobela bato mpe molunge oyo bazali kobimisi mpe bopusi na yango na planete na biso.

src: Since the pre-industrial period, human activities are estimated to have increased Earth's global average temperature by about 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit), a number that is currently increasing by 0.2 degrees Celsius (0.36 degrees Fahrenheit) per decade.
trg: Banda ntango ya liboso ya ba izine, bakanisi ete misala ya bato ematisa temperature ya Mabele na pene ya 1 degre Celsuis (1,8 degre Fahrenheit), motango oyo ezali sikoyo komata na 0.2 degre Celsius (0.36 degre Fahrenheit) mbala na mbala nsima ya mibu zomi.

src: Most of the current warming trend is extremely likely (greater than 95 percent probability) the result of human activity since the 1950s and is proceeding at an unprecedented rate over decades to millennia.
trg: Bamolunge mingi ya lelo euti mingimingi (koleka 95 na kati ya nkama) na misala ya bato banda na mibu 1950 mpe emata na lolenge ya kokamwa na bambula oyo elanda.

src: The largest human influence on climate change has been the emission of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
trg: Bopusi ya makasi oyo bato bazala na yango na mbongwana ya climat ezali kobimisa gaz à effet de serre neti dixode ya carbone, methane mpe oxide nitrique.

src: The primary source of these emissions is from burning fossil fuels for electricity, heat and transportation.
trg: Biloko oyo eutaka libosoliboso na kozitisa bafosile to biloko ya kala mpo na lotiliki, molunge mpe transport.

src: I'm Dr. Boakye, a pediatrician at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.
trg: Nazali monganga Boake, monganga ya bana na Lopitalo Korle Bu Teaching.

src: I'm here today to talk to you about the new malaria vaccine that's been approved for use in Ghana.
trg: Nazali awa lelo mpo na kolobela bino mangwele ya sika ya malaria oyo bandimi mpo na kosalela na Ghana.

src: Father: I'm not interested in having my children vaccinated.
trg: Papa: Nazali kosepela te bana na nga bazwa mangwele.

src: Doctor: I understand that you're concerned, but I'd like to take a few minutes to explain why I think it's a good idea to vaccinate your children against malaria.
trg: Monganga: Nayebi ete ozali komitungisa, kasi nalingi kozwa mwa miniti mpo na kolimbolela yo mpo na nini nakanisi kopesa bana na yo mangwele ya malaria ezali likanisi ya malamu.

src: Father: I don't need to be convinced. Malaria is a serious disease, but it's not that common in our village.
trg: Papa: Ezali na ntina te ondimisa nga. Malaria ezali maladi ya makasi, kasi ezalaka mingi te na mboka na biso.

src: Doctor: That's true, but malaria is still a major public health problem in Ghana. In 2020, there were over 24 million cases of malaria in Ghana, and over 4,000 people died from the disease
trg: Monganga: Ezali solo, kasi malaria ezali kaka likambo ya mpasi ya kolongono ya nzoto ya bato nyonso na Ghana. Na 2020, ezalaki na bamilio 24 ya bato oyo babelaka malaria na Ghana, mpe bato koleka 4 000 bakufaki na maladi oyo

src: Father: But my children are healthy. They've never had malaria
trg: Papa: Kasi bana na nga bazali nzoto kolongono. Batikala kobela malaria te

src: Doctor: That's good, but it doesn't mean they're immune. Anyone can get malaria, even if they've never had it before.
trg: Monganga: Ezali malamu, kasi elakisi te ete bakoki kobela yango te. Moto nyonso akoki kobela malaria, ata soki atikala kobela yango nanu te.

src: Facebook Users Drunkenly Post About Their Lives
trg: Basaleli ya Facebook Oyo Balangwe Bazali Kotya Bansango ya Bomoi na Bango na Molangwa

src: Facebook users are getting drunk and posting about their lives, and it's causing a stir.
trg: Basaleli ya Facebook bazali kolongwa mpe kotya bansango ya bomoi na bango, mpe ezali koningisa.

src: The social media platform has been flooded with photos and videos of people who are clearly intoxicated, and many of them are sharing personal details about themselves that they wouldn't normally share.
trg: Basite ya reseaux sociaux etondi na bafoto mpe bavideo ya bato oyo balangwe mpenza, mpe mingi kati na bango bazali kotya bansango ya bomoi na bango oyo basengelaki ata moke te kokabola na bato mosusu.

src: Some users are concerned that the trend is dangerous, as it could lead to people making poor decisions or doing things they regret.
trg: Basaleli mosusu bazali komitungisa ete ezali oyo ezali likama, mpo ekoki komema bato na kozwa bikateli ya mabe to kosala makambo oyo bakoyoka mawa nsima.

src: Others are simply amused by the antics of their fellow drunk Facebook users.
trg: Basusu bazali koseka kaka na bizaleli mabe ya baninga na bango balangwi oyo basalelaka Facebook.

src: One user posted a photo of herself passed out on the floor with the caption, "I'm so drunk I can't even stand up."
trg: Mosaleli moko atyaki foto na ye na mabele na maloba, "Nalangwe makasi, nazali kokoka kutu te kotelema."

src: Another user shared a video of herself dancing on a table while shouting, "I'm the life of the party!"
trg: Mosaleli mosusu akabolaki video na ye moko azali kobina na mesa ntango azali koloba, "Nazali bomoi ya feti!"

src: The trend has even caught the attention of celebrities.
trg: Ezaleli oyo ebendi kutu likebi ya bato bayebana.

src: Comedian Amy Schumer posted a photo of herself on Twitter with the caption, "I'm so drunk I can't even spell my own name."
trg: Moto asekisaka bato Amy Schumer atyaki foto na yo moko na Twitter na maloba, "Nalangwe makasi, nazali kokoka kutu te koloba nkombo na nga moko."

src: Facebook has not commented on the trend, but it's clear that it's causing a stir.
trg: Facebook elobi eloko te mpo na ezaleli wana, kasi ezali polele ete ezali koningisa.

src: Only time will tell whether the trend will continue or fade away.
trg: Ntango mpamba ekoyebisa soki ezaleli wana ekokoba to ekosila na yango.

src: Birthdays are a time to celebrate the day you were born.
trg: Mikolo ya mbotma ezali ntango ya kosepela mokolo oyo obotamaki.

src: It is a day to reflect on all the good things in your life and to thank those who have made you who you are.
trg: Ezali mokolo ya kokanisa makambo nyonso ya malamu ya bomoi na yo mpe kopesa matondi na bato basala ozala oyo ozali.

src: It is also a day to set goals for the year ahead and to make plans for the future.
trg: Ezali mpe mokolo ya komityela mikano mpo na mbula ya sika mpe kosala miango mpo na mikolo ezali koya.

src: To make the most of your birthday, start by making a list of all the things you are grateful for.
trg: Mpo na kosepela mpenza na mokolo ya mbotama, banda kosala liste ya makambo nyonso oyo azali na botondi mpo na yango.

src: This could include your family, friends, health, home, job, or anything else that is important to you.
trg: Ekoki kozala libota, baninga, kolongono ya nzoto, ndako, mosala, to eloko nyonso mosusu oyo ezali ntina mpo na yo.

src: Once you have made your list, take some time to reflect on each item and how it has made your life better.
trg: Soki osilisi liste wana, zwa mwa ntango ya kokanisa eloko mokomoko mpe ndenge ekomisa bomoi na yo malamu koleka.

src: Next, set some goals for the year ahead.
trg: Na nsima, mityela mwa mikano mpo mbula ya sika.

src: These goals can be anything you want them to be, but they should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.
trg: Mikano oyo ekoki kozala eloko nyonso olingi kozala, kasi esengeli kozala ya sikisiki, ya malamu, oyo okoki kokokisa, ya ntina, mpe na ndelo.

src: For example, you might set a goal to lose weight, get a promotion at work, or travel to a new place.
trg: Na ndakisa, okoki komityela mokano ya kokonda, ya komata garde na mosala, to ya kosala mobemo na esika ya sika.

src: Finally, make plans for the day of your birthday.
trg: Na nsuka, sala miango mpo na mokolo ya mbotama.

src: This could include spending time with your loved ones, eating your favorite foods, or doing something you have always wanted to do.
trg: Ekoki kozala kolekisa ntango na bato oyo olingaka, kolya bilei olingaka mingi, to kosala likambo moko oyo azalaka ntango nyonso na mposa ya kosala.

src: When I was a kid, I would spend hours poring over magazines.
trg: Ntango nazalaki mwana ya moke, nazalaki kolekisa bangonga ebele na kotanga bazulunalo.

src: I would read every article, look at every picture, and cut out the ones I liked to put in my scrapbook.
trg: Nazalaki kitoko masolo nyonso, kotala foto nyonso, mpe kokata oyo nalingaka mpo na kotya yango na album na nga.

src: I loved the way magazines could transport me to different worlds and make me think about things in new ways.
trg: Nazalaki kosepela ndenge bazulunalo ezalaki komema nga na bisika ekeseni ya mokili mpe kopusa nga na kotalela makambo na ndenge ya sika.

src: One day, I was reading an article about brain science in a magazine.
trg: Mokolo moko, nazalaki kotanga lisolo ya siansi ya boongo na zulunalo moko.

src: The article was really interesting, and it made me think about how my brain works.
trg: Lisolo yango ezalaki ya kitoko mingi, mpe epusaki nga nakanisa ndenge boongo na nga esalaka.

src: I realized that I could use my brain to learn anything I wanted, and that was an amazing feeling.
trg: Namonaki ete nakoki kosalela boongo na nga mpo na koyekola likambo nyonso nalingi, mpe ezalaki mayoki ya kitoko makasi.

src: I've been reading magazines ever since, and I still love the way they can open my mind to new ideas.
trg: Natangaka bazulunalo banda ntango wana, mpe nakobaka kolinga lolenge ekoki kopesa nga makanisi ya sika.

src: "Royalty," said the Blacksmith, "is a curious thing. It's a kind of magic, really.
trg: "Bokonzi," wana maloba ya Mosali ya bibende, "ezali eloko tolukaka koyeba. Ezali mpenza mazi moko boye.

src: People get all worked up about it, and they don't even know why.
trg: Bato basalaka nyonso mpo na yango, mpe bayebi kutu te mpo na nini.

src: It's not as if kings and queens have any real power, these days. They're just figureheads.
trg: Ezali te nieti soki bakonzi mpe bakonzi ya basi bazali na nguya solo, na mikolo wana. Bazali kaka bakambi.

src: But people still seem to need them.
trg: Kasi emonanaki ete bato bazali na mposa na bango.

src: They need someone to look up to, someone to represent the idea of the nation." The Blacksmith paused.
trg: Bazali na mposa ya moto oyo bakoki koluka, moto oyo azali komonisa makanisi ya ekolo." Mosali ya bibende apemaki.

src: "I suppose it's a kind of comfort," he continued.
trg: "Nakanisi ezali lolenge ya libondisi," akobaki.

src: "To know that there's someone out there who's better than you.
trg: "Koyeba ete ezali na moto moko kuna oyo aleki yo.

src: Someone who's got it all sorted out.
trg: Moto oyo abongisa yango nyonso.

src: Someone who can make the world a better place.
trg: Moto oyo akokisi kokomisa mokili esika ya malamu koleka.

src: Of course, it's all an illusion. But that doesn't make it any less important.
trg: Ya solo, ezali kaka makanisi ya lokuta. Kasi elakisi te ete ezali na ntina te.

src: People need their illusions. They need to believe in something.
trg: Bato bazali na mposa ya makanisi na bango ya lokuta. Basengeli kondima eloko moko.

src: And if that something is a king or a queen, then so be it."
trg: Mpe soki eloko yango ezali mokonzi to mokonzi ya mwasi, wana tika ezala bongo."

src: The Blacksmith paused for a moment, then smiled.
trg: Mosali ya bibende apemaki moke, na nsima asekaki.

src: The flavors dance on your tongue, creating a symphony of delight.
trg: Elengi ebinaka na lolemo na yo, esalaka bilengi ebele.

src: The pineapple is sweet and tart, the apple is crisp and juicy, the stone fruit is juicy and flavorful, and the pear is sweet and refreshing.
trg: Linanasi ezalaka elengi mingi, pomme ezalaka kitoko mpe na mai ebele, fruit ezalaka na mbuma na kati ezalaka na mai ebele mpe elengi, mpe poire ezali elengi mpe ekitisaka motema.

src: The flavors are perfectly balanced, and each one complements the others.
trg: Bilengi ezalaka mpenza na bokatikati, mpe moko ebakisamaka likolo ya mosusu.

src: The combination is simply irresistible.
trg: Bosangani ezali kitoko makasi.

src: You can enjoy this delicious fruit salad on its own, or as a topping for yogurt or ice cream.
trg: Okoki kosepela na mbuma oyo ya salade ya kitoko yango moko, to lokola eloko ya kotya likolo ya yaourt to creme ya malili.

src: It is also a great addition to a summer picnic or potluck.
trg: Ezali mpe eloko ya kitoko ya kobakisa na pique-nique to na bilei ya eleko ya molunge.

src: No matter how you enjoy it, you are sure to love this fruit salad.
trg: Ata osepeli na yango ndenge nini, okosepela mpenza na mbuma oyo ya salade.

src: Pottery is a craft that involves making objects out of clay.
trg: Kosala bambeki ezali mosala esengaka kosala biloko na argile.

src: Pottery is often used for utilitarian purposes, such as storing food or water, but it can also be used for decorative purposes.
trg: Basalelka mbala mingi kosala bambeki mpo na bantina ya motuya, neti kobomba bilei to mai, kasi bakoki kosalela yango mpe mpo na kokomisa ndako kitoko.

src: The process of making pottery begins with gathering clay.
trg: Mosala ya kosala bambeki ebandaka na kosangisa argile.

src: Clay is a natural material that is found in the ground.
trg: Argile ezali eloko nzambe asala oyo ezalaka na mabele.

src: Once the clay has been gathered, it is mixed with water and kneaded until it is soft and pliable.
trg: Nsima ya kozwa argile, basangisaka yango na mai mpe babalusaka yango kino ekokoma pete mpe pliable.

src: The potter then uses a variety of tools to shape the clay into the desired form.
trg: Na nsima mosali-mbeki asalelaka bisaleli ebele mpo na kopesa argile forme oyo alingi.

src: Once the clay is shaped, it is dried and fired in a kiln.
trg: Nsima ya kopesa argile forme, bakausaka mpe batumbaka yango na foure.

src: New Study Finds That Breast Cancer Screenings Can Lead to False Positives
trg: Bolukiluki Moko Emonisi ete Depistage ya Kansere ya Mabele Ekoki Komema na Kokanga Maladi na Bato oyo Bazali na Yango te

src: A new study published in the journal JAMA Internal Medicine has found that breast cancer screenings can lead to false positives.
trg: Bolukiluki ya sika oyo babimisaki na zulunalo JAMA ya Kimonganga ya Kati emonisaki ete depistage ya kansere ya mabele ekoki komema na kokanga maladi na bato oyo bazali na yango te

src: The study, which was conducted by researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, found that one in five women who underwent a mammogram had a false positive result.
trg: Bolukiluki, oyo ekambamaki na balukiluki ya Iniversite ya Californie, na San Francisco, emonaki ete mwasi moko na kati ya basi mitano oyo basalaki ekzame ya mabele babengi mamographie bakangaki ye maladi atako azalaki na yango te.

src: A false positive result is when a mammogram shows that a woman has breast cancer, when she actually does not.
trg: Resultat ya mabe ezalaka ntango mamographie emonisi ete mwasi moko azali na kansere ya mabele, ntango azali na yango te.

src: This can lead to unnecessary anxiety and stress, as well as unnecessary medical procedures, such as biopsies.
trg: Ekoki komema na basusi mpe mitungisi ezangi ntina, ba procedure ya kimonganga ezangi ntina, neti babiopsie.

src: The study found that the rate of false positives was higher among women who were younger, had dense breasts, and had a family history of breast cancer.
trg: Bolukiluki emonaki mpe ete taux ya bato oyo bakangaki kansere kasi bazalaki na yango te ezalaki mingi na kati ya basi oyo bazalaki bilenge, bazali na tissue ya fibre mpe ya glandulaire ebele na mabele, mpe bazali na bato ya mabota na bango oyo babela kansere ya mabele.

src: The researchers say that these findings are important because they highlight the need for women to understand the risks and benefits of breast cancer screening before they decide whether or not to undergo a mammogram.
trg: Balukiluki balobi ete makambo oyo bamoni ezali ntina mpo ezali komonisa polele ete basi basengeli koyeba makama mpe matomba ya depistage ya kansere ya mabele liboso bazwa ekateli soki bakosala bango mamographie to te.

src: The study also found that the use of sound waves, known as ultrasound, to screen for breast cancer can help to reduce the number of false positives.
trg: Bolukiluki emonisaki mpe ete kosalela ba onde sonore, oyo eyebana na nkombo ya ultrason, mpo na koluka koyeba kansere ya mabele ekoki kosalisa na kokitisa motango ya maladi ya lokuta oyo emonanaka.

src: Ultrasound is a safe and non-invasive imaging technique that can be used to identify abnormalities in the breast.
trg: Ultrason ezali mayele ya malamu mpe ya polele ya kosala bafoto oyo bakoki kosalela mpo na komona nkokoso na mabele.

src: Freedom of the press is the freedom of communication and expression through mediums including printed media and the internet.
trg: Bonsomi ya bapanzi-nsango ezali bonsomi ya koloba mpe kobimisa makanisi na nzela ya media ata mpe ya mikanda ya kokoma mpe na internet.

src: It is a fundamental human right recognized by Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and reaffirmed in Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
trg: Ezali lotomo ya bato ya ntina mingi oyo endimami na Artikle 19 ya Maloba ya Mokili Mobimba ya Balotomo ya Bato mpe endimisami na Artikle 19 ya Boyokani ya Mikili Mingi ya Balotomo ya Sivile mpe ya Politiki.

src: The right to freedom of expression is recognized as a necessary precondition for the enjoyment of all other human rights.
trg: Lotomo ya bonsomi ya koloba endimami ete ezali ntina mingi mpo na kozala na balotomo nyonso mosusu oyo bato bazali na yango.

src: Freedom of the press is essential for a healthy democracy.
trg: Bonsomi ya bapanzi-nsango ezali ntina mpo na demokrasi ya malamu.

src: It allows citizens to access information and to hold their government accountable.
trg: Epesaka bana-mboka nzela ya kozwa bansango mpe kosenga bakonti na guvernema na bango.

src: It also helps to ensure that all voices are heard, and that the public is informed about important issues.
trg: Esalisaka mpe mpo bayoka mingongo ya bato nyonso, mpe ete bayebisa bato nyonso makambo ya ntina.

src: In recent years, there have been growing threats to freedom of the press around the world.
trg: Na bambula euti koleka, ezali na makambo oyo ezalaki kokanga bonsomi ya bapanzi-nsango nzela na mokili mobimba.

src: Governments have been using laws to restrict the media, and journalists have been harassed and attacked.
trg: Baguvernema esalela mibeko mpo na kotya bandelo na bapanzi-nsango, mpe batungisa mpe babundisa bajournaliste.

src: These threats are a serious concern, and they need to be addressed.
trg: Ba menace oyo ezali motungisi monene, mpe esengeli kosilisa yango.

src: We must all stand up for freedom of the press.
trg: Biso nyonso tosengeli kotelema mpo na bonsomi ya bapanzi-nsango.

src: We must defend the right of journalists to report the news without fear of reprisal.
trg: Tosengeli kobundela lotomo ya bajournaliste ya kopesa bansango kozanga kobanga ete bakonyola bango.

src: We must also support independent media outlets, and we must encourage people to read and share news from a variety of sources.
trg: Tosengeli mpe kosunga bapanzi-nsango ya lipanda, mpe tosengeli kolendisa bato na kotanga mpe kokabola bansango euti na bisika ebele.

src: Freedom of the press is a precious right.
trg: Bonsomi ya bapanzi-nsango ezali lotomo ya motuya.

src: We must all do our part to protect it.
trg: Biso nyonso tosengeli kopesa maboko na kobatela yango.

src: The Uganda Martyrs are a group of 23 Anglican and 22 Roman Catholic Christians who were killed between 1885 and 1887.
trg: Bamartire ya Ouganda ezali etuluku ya Anglican 23 mpe ya Baklisto 22 ya Katolika ya Roma oyo babomaki kati ya 1885 mpe 1887.

src: They were killed by the king of Buganda, Mwanga II, for refusing to renounce their faith.
trg: Moto abomaki bango ezali mokonzi ya Buganda, Mwanga II, mpo baboyaki kobwakisa bindeli na bango.

src: The martyrs were canonized by Pope Paul VI in 1964.
trg: Pape Paul VI akotisaki bamartire wana na canon na 1964.

src: They are considered to be among the most important figures in the history of Christianity in Uganda.
trg: Bato bamonaka bango bazali kati ya bato ya ntina mingi na lisolo ya Boklisto na Ouganda.

src: The Uganda Martyrs' Day is celebrated on June 3rd every year.
trg: Basalaka feti ya Mokolo ya Bamartire ya Ouganda na 3 sanza ya Motoba mbula nyonso.

src: It is a national holiday in Uganda and is observed by Christians all over the world.
trg: Ezali feti ya ekolo mobimba na Ouganda mpe Baklisto basalaka feti wana na mokili mobimba.

src: The martyrs are remembered for their courage and their willingness to die for their faith.
trg: Bakanisaka bamartire mpo na mpika mpo bolingo na bango ya kokufa mpo na bindimeli na bango.

src: They are an inspiration to Christians everywhere.
trg: Balendisaka Baklisto ya bisika nyonso.

src: In the upcoming months, I will be honored to receive an award for my work in the field of French language studies.
trg: Na basanza ezali koya, nakozala na lokumu ya kozwa mbano mpo na mosala na nga ya boyekoli ya lokota ya Français.

src: The award will be presented by the Société Française de Linguistique, a prestigious organization dedicated to the advancement of French language and linguistics.
trg: Mbano ekopsaka na Société Française de Linguistique, lisanga moko ya lokumu mingi oyo emipesa na kotombola lokota ya Français mpe makambo na yango.

src: I am humbled and grateful to be recognized by such a distinguished organization, and I look forward to continuing my work in French language studies.
trg: Nazali na komikitisa mpe na botondi ndenge bandimi nga na lisanga ya lokumu ya ndenge wana, mpe nazali kozela kokoba mosala na nga ya boyekoli ya lokota ya Français.

src: My research interests lie in the area of historical linguistics, and I have focused my work on the development of French from its origins in the Gallo-Romance dialects of the early Middle Ages.
trg: Mposa na nga ya bolukiluki ezali na lisolo ya lokota, mpe mosala na nga ezali kotya likebi na bokoli ya Français banda na bisika euta na nkota ya Gallo-Romance ya ebandeli ya Moyen Âge.

src: I am particularly interested in the ways in which French has been influenced by other languages, such as Latin, Germanic languages, and Arabic.
trg: Nazali kotya likebi mingi koleka na balolenge oyo Français ezwa bopusi ya nkota mosusu, neti nkota ya Latini, ya Germanique, mpe ya Arabe.

src: My research has been published in leading journals in the field of linguistics, and I have presented my work at conferences around the world.
trg: Bolukiluki ya nga ebimisaka na bazulunalo ya minene oyo elobelaka makambo ya nkota, mpe nalakisa misala na nga na mikita ya minene na mokili mobimba.

src: I am based at a university located near the French border, and I have had the opportunity to collaborate with scholars from France and other Francophone countries.
trg: Nazali na iniversite moko oyo ezali pene ya ndelo ya France, mpe nazali na libaku ya kosala elongo na bato ya mayele ya France mpe ya bamboka misusu oyo balobaka Français.

src: My research has made a significant contribution to the field of French language studies, and I am proud to have been recognized for my work.
trg: Bolukiluki na nga ebakisa makambo ebele na boyekoli ya lokota ya Français, mpe nazali na esengo ndenge bandimi mosala na nga.

src: Akosua Aunty: Hello, children. What can I do for you?
trg: Tata-Mwasi Akosua: Mbote bana. Nakoki kosala nini mpo na bino?

src: Cousin 1: We need your help with a decision.
trg: Cousin 1: Tozali na mposa ya lisalisi na yo na ekateli moko.

src: We're all trying to decide whether or not to cheat on a test tomorrow.
trg: Biso nyonso tozali koluka kozwa ekateli soki tokoyiba to te na ekzame lobi.

src: Cousin 2: Yeah, we know it's wrong, but we're all really scared of failing.
trg: Cousin 2: Ee, toyebi ezali mabe, kasi tozali mpenza kobanga kobela.

src: Akosua Aunty: I understand that you're scared, but cheating is never the answer.
trg: Tata-Mwasi Akosua: Nayebi ete bozali kobanga, kasi koyiba ezali ata moke te eyano.

src: It's important to remember that integrity is one of the most important things in life.
trg: Ezali ntina kobosana ete bosembo ezali likambo ya ntina mingi koleka na bomoi.

src: When you cheat, you're not just cheating yourself, you're also cheating everyone else who has worked hard to learn the material.
trg: Soki oyibi, ozali komiyibela te, ozali mpe koyiba bato nyonso oyo basalaki makasi mpo na koyekola makambo wana.

src: Cousin 1: But what if we really do fail?
trg: Cousin 1: Ebongo soki tobeli makasi?

src: Akosua Aunty: If you fail, then you fail. That's life.
trg: Tata-Mwasi Akosua: Soki bolongi te, bolongi te. Bomoi ezali bongo.

src: But at least you'll know that you did your best and you didn't cheat.
trg: Kasi oyebi ete osalaki makasi mpenza mpe oyibaki te.

src: And that's what matters most.
trg: Mpe wana likambo eleki ntina.

src: Cousin 2: You're right, Aunty.
trg: Cousin 2: Olobi solo Tata-Mwasi.

src: We need to do the right thing, even if it's hard.
trg: Tosengeli kosala makambo ya malamu, ata soki ezali mpasi.

src: "Dance, Henry, dance" the old woman cried "Dance and let the colors of life flow through you.
trg: "Bina, Henry, bina" mwasi ya mobange agangaki "Bina mpe tika balangi ya bomoi ebima kati na yo.

src: Let the music fill your soul and your body will move of its own accord.
trg: Tika miziki etondisa molimo na yo mpe nzoto na yo ekotambola elongo moko.

src: Dance and be free" Henry looked at the old woman with confusion.
trg: Bina mpe zala na bonsomi" Henry azalaki kotala mobange ya mwasi na kokamwa.

src: He had never been a dancer, and he didn't understand why she was so insistent that he should start now.
trg: Atikala kozala te mobini, mpe azalaki koyeba nde mpo na nini mobange wana atingamaki ete abanda kobina sikoyo.

src: But the old woman's eyes were bright and her face was filled with joy, and Henry couldn't help but be drawn in.
trg: Kasi miso ya mobange ya mwasi ezalaki kongenga mpe elongi na ye etondaki na esengo, mpe likambo Henry asalaki ezalaki kaka kosepela na ye.

src: He took a deep breath and began to move.
trg: Apemaki makasi mpe abandaki koningana.

src: At first, his movements were awkward and hesitant, but as he continued to dance, he began to relax and let the music take over.
trg: Na ebandeli, mivema na ye ezalaki ya bongobongo mpe na badute, kasi ntango akobaki kobina, abandaki komiyoka malamu mpe kotika miziki emema ye.

src: The colors of the world swirled around him, and he felt a sense of freedom and joy that he had never experienced before.
trg: Balangi ya mokili ezingaki ye, mpe ayokaki azali na bonsomi mpe esengo oyo atikala koyoka nanu te.

src: When the music stopped, Henry was breathless and exhilarated.
trg: Ntango miziki ekataki, Henry azalaki na mpema te mpe na esengo makasi.

src: He looked at the old woman and smiled "Thank you," he said "I don't know why I didn't dance before.
trg: Atalaki mobange wana ya mwasi mpe asekaki "Matondi," wana ndenge alobaki "Nayebi te mpo na nini nazalaki kobina te na kala.

src: “So, what are you looking for in a life partner?”
trg: "Yango wana, nini ozali koluka na moninga ya bomoi?"

src: The question hung in the air, heavy with expectation.
trg: Motuna ezali kaka, etondi na makambo ebele.

src: I took a sip of my drink and glanced across the table at the woman I’d been on a few dates with.
trg: Namelaki masanga moke mpe natalaki na mesa mwasi oyo nazalaki kobima na ye banda mwa mikolo.

src: She was beautiful, with long dark hair, piercing blue eyes, and a smile that could light up a room.
trg: Azalaki kitoko, na nsuki ya milai, meso ya bleu ya kitoko, mpe koseka oyo ezalaki kotya pole na shambre.

src: But was she the one for me?
trg: Kasi abongaki mpo na nga?

src: I thought about it for a moment.
trg: Nakanisaki mwa moke mpo na yango.

src: “I’m looking for someone who is kind, intelligent, and funny,” I said.
trg: "Nazali koluka moto oyo azali motema-malamu, mayele, mpe asekisaka," wana ndenge nalobaki.

src: “Someone who I can connect with on a deep level.”
trg: "Moto oyo nakoki kokangama na ye na nivo ya likolo."

src: She nodded “That sounds like a good start,” she said “What about physical attraction? Is that important to you?”
trg: Aningisaki moto "Ezali komonana ezali ebandeli ya malamu," ndenge alobaki "Okanisi boni mpo na kobendana ya nzoto? Ezali mpe ntina mpo na yo?"

src: I shrugged “It’s not the most important thing,” I said “But it’s definitely a factor.”
trg: Naningisaki mapeka "Ezali te likambo ya ntina koleka," nalobaki "Kasi ezali mpenza likambo ya kotalela."

src: She smiled “I know what you mean,” she said “I’m the same way.”
trg: Asekaki "Nayebi nini olingi koloba," ndenge alobaki "Nazali ndenge moko."

src: We talked for a while longer, about our hopes and dreams, our goals and aspirations.
trg: Tosololaki mwa mingi, mpo na bilikya mpe bandoto na biso, mikano mpe makambo tozali kozela.

src: The more we talked, the more I felt like I was getting to know the real her.
trg: Ntango tozalaki kosolola mingi, nazalaki komona ete nazali koyeba ye malamu.

src: And the more I liked her.
trg: Mpe nazalaki kolinga ye mingi.

src: The recent rise of social media has given rise to a new breed of celebrities: the social media influencer.
trg: Bokoli ya kala te ya reseau sociaux ebimisi lolenge ya sika ya bato bayebana: influenceur ya reseau sociaux.

src: These individuals have amassed large followings on platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube, and they use their influence to promote products, services, and ideas.
trg: Bato oyo bazwi bato ebele oyo bazali kolanda bango na bisika neti Twitter, Instagram, mpe YouTube, mpe basalelaka nguya na bango mpo na kolendisa biloko, misala mpe makanisi.

src: One of the most popular social media influencers in the world is Kim Kardashian.
trg: Moko ya ba influenceur ya reseau sociaux ayebana mingi na mokili mobimba ezali Kim Kardashian.

src: With over 200 million followers on Instagram, Kardashian is a powerful force in the fashion, beauty, and lifestyle industries.
trg: Azali na balandi koleka 200 milio na Instagram, Kardashian azali nguya makasi na mosala ya modele, ya kitoko, mpe ya lolenge ya bomoi.

src: She has also used her platform to speak out about social issues, such as criminal justice reform and women's rights.
trg: Asalela mpe biloko wana mpo na kolobela makambo ya bomoi, neti kobongola boyengebene ya bacrime mpe balotomo ya basi.

src: However, there is a dark side to the world of social media influencers.
trg: Kasi, ezali na likambo eyebani te na makambo ya ba influenceur ya reseaux sociaux.

src: Some influencers are paid by foreign governments to spread propaganda and disinformation.
trg: Bafutaka ba influenceur mosusu na baguvernema ya bapaya mpo na kopanza propagande mpe bansango ya lokuta.

src: This is a serious problem, as it can greatly influence public opinion and undermine democracy.
trg: Ezali mokakatano makasi, mpo ekoki kozala na bopusi makasi na makanisi ya bato mpe kobebisa demokrasi.

src: In 2016, it was revealed that Russian trolls used social media to spread propaganda and disinformation during the US presidential election.
trg: Na 2016, eyebisamaki ete Rusie esalelaki batrole ya reseau sociaux mpo kopanza propagande mpe bansango ya lokuta na ntango ya maponi ya prezida ya Étas-Unis.

src: The trolls created fake accounts and used them to post pro-Trump messages and anti-Hillary Clinton messages.
trg: Batrole basalaki bakonti ya lokuta mpe basalelaki yango mpo na kotinda bansango ya kokotela Trump mpe bansango ya koboya Hilary Clinton.

src: This had a significant impact on the election, as it helped to sway public opinion in favor of Trump.
trg: Ezalaki na bopusi makasi na maponi, mpo esalisaka na komema bato na kokotela Trump.

src: Cairo, the capital of Egypt, is the largest city in the Middle East and the third largest city in Africa.
trg: Caire, mboka-mokonzi ya Ezipito, ezali engumba eleki monene ya Moyen Orient mpe engumba ya misato ya monene na Afrika.

src: It is home to some of the world's most famous landmarks, including the Pyramids of Giza, the Sphinx, and the Egyptian Museum.
trg: Ezali na mwa bisika ya kitoko oyo eyebana na mokili mobimba, neti Piramide ya Giza, Sphinx, mpe Mize ya Ezipito.

src: Other important places in Egypt include Alexandria, Luxor, Aswan, and the Sinai Peninsula.
trg: Bisika mosusu ya ntina na Ezipito ezali Alexandrie, Luxor, Aswan, mpe Peninsule ya Sinai.

src: Alexandria is Egypt's second largest city and was once the capital of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.
trg: Alexandrie ezali engumba ya mibale ya monene mingi na Ezipito mpe ezali na kala mboka-mokonzi ya Bokonzi ya ba Ptolemée.

src: Luxor is home to the Valley of the Kings, where many of the pharaohs of ancient Egypt were buried.
trg: Luxor ezali na Lobwaku ya Bakonzi, esika bakunda bafarao mingi ya Ezipito ya kala.

src: Aswan is located on the Nile River and is known for its beautiful scenery and its many ancient temples.
trg: Aswan ezali na Ebale Nile mpe eyebana mpo na kitoko na yango mpe batempelo na yango ebele ya kala.

src: The Sinai Peninsula is located in the eastern part of Egypt and is home to the famous Mount Sinai, where Moses is said to have received the Ten Commandments.
trg: Peninsule ya Sinai ezali na eteni ya este ya Ezipito mpe ezali na Ngomba Sinai oyo eyebana mingi, esika balobaki ete Moize azwaki Mibeko Zomi.

src: The gardener's journey began with a simple drive to the local nursery.
trg: Mobembo ya mosali-bilanga ebamdalo ma kokende ya kozanga mindondo na creche.

src: He had been planning this trip for weeks, ever since he had seen the advertisement in the paper.
trg: Abongisaki mobembo oyo bamposo ebele liboso, banda amonaki piblisite na zulunalo.

src: The nursery was offering a 20% discount on all plants, and he was determined to take advantage of the sale.
trg: Creche ezalaki kokitisa ntalo na 20% na banzete nyonso, mpe azalaki na mokano ya kosalela koteka wana.

src: When he arrived at the nursery, he was immediately overwhelmed by the selection of plants.
trg: Ntango akomaki na creche, na mbala moko akamwaki makasi na banzete oyo ezalaki kuna.

src: There were flowers of every color and shape, vegetables of all sizes, and trees that reached for the sky.
trg: Ezali na bafololo ya langi mpe ya baforme nyonso, bandunda ya minene nyonso, mpe banzete oyo ezalaki kokoma na lola.

src: He wandered around for hours, admiring the plants and dreaming of the beautiful garden he would create.
trg: Atambolaki zingazinga bangonga ebele, azali kosepela na banzete mpe kolota elanga ya kitoko oyo akosala.

src: Finally, he made his selections and headed to the checkout counter.
trg: Nsuka-nsuka, aponaki oyo alingaki mpe akendaki na caisse.

src: As he was paying for his plants, he noticed a sign that said "Free delivery for orders over $50" He smiled and added a few more plants to his cart.
trg: Ntango azalaki kofuta mosolo ya banzete, amonaki elembo moko elobi ete "Kotika na ndako ya ofele mpo na bakomande ya koleka $50" Asekaki mpe abakisaki banzete mosusu na pusupusu na ye.

src: A few days later, the gardener received a delivery of his new plants.
trg: Mwa mikolo na nsima, moto ya bilanga azwaki banzete na ye oyo bayaki kotikela ye.

src: He eagerly unpacked them and began to plant them in his garden.
trg: Afungolaki yango na esengo mpe abandaki kolona yango na bilanga na ye.

src: He worked for hours, carefully placing each plant in the perfect spot.
trg: Asalaki bangonga ebele, azali kotya nzete mokomoko na esika na yango ebongi.

src: When he was finished, he stood back and admired his work.
trg: Ntango asilisaki, azongaki nsima mpe asepelaki na mosala na ye.

src: The garden was beautiful, and he knew that he would enjoy spending many hours tending to it.
trg: Elanga ezalaki kitoko, mpe ayebaki ete akosepela kolekisa bangonga ebele mpo na kobongisa yango.

src: These are just a few of the issues that can plague a car that has been in a minor accident.
trg: Oyo ezali kaka ndambo ya makambo oyo etungisaka motuka oyo esali mwa aksida ya moke.

src: While the damage may not seem significant, it can still be dangerous and expensive to fix.
trg: Ata esika ya kobeba ekoki komonana ete eza ya makasi te, ekoki kozala likama mpe kosenga mbongo ebele na kobongisa.

src: In the case of worn or falling apart rubber pieces, this can be a safety hazard.
trg: Soki ezali biloko ya caoutchouc oyo ebeba to ezali kokwea, ekoki kozala likama mpo na securité.

src: Rubber is used in a variety of places on a car, including the tires, brake pads, and seals.
trg: Caoutchouc esalelamaka na bisika ebele na motuka, ata na bapneu, plaquete ya frein mpe ba joint.

src: When rubber becomes worn, it can crack, split, or otherwise deteriorate.
trg: Soki caoutchouc ebebi, ekoki kopasuka, kopanzana, to kobeba ndenge mosusu.

src: This can lead to a number of problems, such as reduced traction, decreased braking performance, and leaks.
trg: Ekoki komema mikakatano ebele, neti kokitisa traction, kolembisa makasi ya frein, mpe kotangisa mafuta.

src: Missing roof rail pieces can also be a safety hazard.
trg: Biloko ezanga ya mabende ya nsamba ekoki mpe kozala likama mpo na sécurité.

src: Roof rails are designed to help protect passengers in the event of a rollover accident.
trg: Mabende ya nsamba esalema mpo na kobatela baleki soki basieti.

src: If the roof rails are missing, the roof of the car is more likely to collapse in a rollover, which can cause serious injuries or death.
trg: Soki mabende ya nsamba ezali te, nsamba ya motuka ekoki mpenza kokwea soki ebaluki, yango ekoki kozokisa makasi to koboma bato.

src: A broken fuel tank door lock can also be dangerous.
trg: Serrure ya porte ya reservoir ya carburant ebukana ekoki mpe kozala likama.

src: If the fuel tank door cannot be locked, it could come open while the car is moving.
trg: Soki bakoki kokanga te porte ya reservoir ya carburant, ekoki kofungwama ntango motuka ezali kotambola.

src: This could spill fuel onto the road, which could cause a fire or explosion.
trg: Ekoki kopanza carburant na balabala, yango ekoki kopelisa moto to kosala explosion.

src: In addition to the safety risks, these types of damage can also be expensive to fix.
trg: Longola makama ya sécurité, kobeba ya lolenge oyo ekoki kosenga mbongo ebele mpo na kobongisa yango.

src: Rubber pieces can be difficult to replace, and roof rails and fuel tank door locks can be expensive to repair or replace.
trg: Biloko ya caoutchouc ekoki kozala mpasi na kolongola mpe kotya ya sika, mpe banzela ya nsama baserrure ya reservoir ya carburant ekoki kosenga mbongo ebele mpo na kobongisa to kotya ya sika.

src: In some cases, it may be more cost-effective to total the car and buy a new one.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu, ekoki kozala malamu na kobwaka motuka mpe kosomba ya sika.

src: If you are considering buying a used car that has been in a minor accident, be sure to have it inspected by a qualified mechanic.
trg: Soki ozali kokana kosomba motuka basalela esala aksida ya moke, senga mechanicien ayebi mosala malamu atala yango nanu.

src: They will be able to identify any damage that may not be visible to the naked eye, and they can advise you on whether or not the car is safe to buy.
trg: Akoki komona bisika ebeba oyo ekoki komonana te na miso, mpe akoki koyebisa yo soki ezali malamu to te na kosomba motuka yango.

src: A bicycle is a thing of beauty, sleek and streamlined, its wheels a blur of motion as it glides along the road.
trg: Velo ezali eloko ya kitoko, ya banzela ya kitoko, oyo bapneu na yango ebalukaka kaka na nzela.

src: But what happens when you bring a bike into a small room?
trg: Kasi nini esalemaka soki omemi velo na shambre ya moke?

src: Suddenly, all that grace and efficiency is lost, and the bike becomes a clumsy, awkward intruder.
trg: Na mbala moko, kitoko na makasi nyonso ebebi, mpe velo ekomi eloko ya mabe oyo emikotisi na ndako.

src: I once had a bike in a small room.
trg: Nazalaki kala na velo na shambre moko ya moke.

src: It was a cramped, dingy apartment in a rundown neighborhood, and the bike took up most of the space.
trg: Ezali apartema moko ya moke mpe etondi na biloko na kartie ya mbindo, mpe velo ezwaki esika ya monene.

src: I could barely get through the door without knocking it over, and I had to be careful not to trip over it when I was in the middle of the night.
trg: Nazalaki kokoka mpenza te kokota na porte kozanga kotuta yango, mpe esengelaki nakeba mpo nakwea te ntango nazalaki na katikati ya butu.

src: But even though the bike was a nuisance, I couldn't bring myself to get rid of it.
trg: Kasi ata velo ezalaki motungisi, nazalaki kokoka te nga moko na kobwaka yango.

src: It was a reminder of a better time, when I was young and free and full of hope.
trg: Ezalaki kokundwela nga ntango ya malamu, ntango nazalaki elenge, na bonsomi mpe elikya ebele.

src: I would sit on the bike and dream of all the places I could go, all the adventures I could have.
trg: Nazalaki kofanda likolo ya velo mpe kolota bisika nyonso oyo nakoki kokende, bisengo nyonso oyo nakoki kozwa.

src: One day, I finally decided to get rid of the bike.
trg: Mokolo moko, nsukansuka nazwaki ekateli ya kobwaka velo wana.

src: I took it to the curb and put it out for the trash.
trg: Namemaki yango na bordure mpe natyaki yango na poubele.

src: As I watched it being hauled away, I felt a pang of regret.
trg: Ntango nazalaki kotala ezali kokende, nayokaki mawa mingi.

src: In the early 1900s, Americans were introduced to the drug “morphine” through the use of over-the-counter cough syrups.
trg: Na ebandeli ya mibu 1900, bato ya Amerika bakotisaki nkisi "morphine" na kosalela nkisi ya mai mpo na kosukosu.

src: While this drug was initially used to treat pain, it soon became addictive and led to a rise in the number of drug addicts in the United States.
trg: Ata na ebandeli nkisi oyo basalaki nkisi oyo mpo na kosunga mpasi, kala mingi te bato bakomaki baombo na yango mpe ematisaki motango ya baombo ya bilangwiseli na États-Unis.

src: One of the most tragic stories of this era is that of the “Kitten Lady”.
trg: Lisolo moko ya mpasi makasi na eleko oyo ezali oyo ya "Mwasi ya Bana Baniawu".

src: This woman was a morphine addict who had a litter of kittens.
trg: Mwasi oyo azalaki moombo ya morphine oyo azalaki na bana baniawu.

src: She loved her kittens very much and would often play with them for hours on end.
trg: Azalaki kolinga bana ya baniawu na ye mingi mpe mbala mingi azalaki kosakana na bango bangonga ebele.

src: However, her addiction soon took over and she began to neglect her kittens.
trg: Atako bongo, boombo na ye ezwaki esika mpe abandaki kosundola baniawu na ye.

src: She would leave them for days at a time, only coming back to feed them and give them water.
trg: Azalaki kotika bango mikolo ebele, azalaki kozonga kaka mpo na koleisa bango mpe kopesa bango mai.

src: The kittens eventually began to suffer from the neglect.
trg: Nsukansuka bana ya baniawu babandaki konyokwama mpo basundolaki bango.

src: They became thin and sickly, and their fur began to fall out.
trg: Bakomaki nzoto mike mpe kobela-bela, mpe bapoil na bango ebandaki kokwea.

src: One by one, they started to die.
trg: Babandaki kokufa mokomoko.

src: The Kitten Lady was devastated by the loss of her kittens, but she was unable to stop her addiction.
trg: Mwasi ya Baniawu elembaki nzoto makasi ndenge bana baniawu na ye ekufaki, kasi akokaki te kosukisi boombo na ye.

src: She eventually died of a morphine overdose, leaving her kittens behind.
trg: Nsukansuka akufaki mpe amelaki morphine ebele, atikaki bana baniawu na ye.

src: This story is a reminder of the dangers of drug addiction.
trg: Lisolo oyo ezali kokundwela biso makama ya kozala moombo ya bilangwiseli.

src: It is also a reminder of the love and devotion that animals can have for their humans.
trg: Ezali mpe kokundwela biso bolingo mpe komipesa oyo banyama ekoki kozala na yango mpo na bato.

src: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people are people who identify with a sexual orientation or gender identity that is different from the majority population.
trg: Balesbienne, bapede, bato basangisaka nzoto na basi mpe mibali, mpe transgenre (LGBT) ezali bato yo bamimonisaka na lolenge ya kosangisa nzoto to identité ya genre oyo ekeseni na bato ebele.

src: Sexual orientation refers to a person's romantic and sexual attraction to others, while gender identity refers to a person's internal sense of being male or female.
trg: Lolenge ya kosangisa nzoto ezolobela ndenge moto alukaka bolngo mpe kobendana na makambo ya kosangisa na bato mosusu, kasi identité ya genre ezolobela ndenge moto amimonaka na kati soki azali mobali to mwasi.

src: LGBT people face discrimination in many areas of life, including employment, housing, and healthcare.
trg: Batyolaka ba LGBT na makambo ebele ya bomoi, ata mpe na mosala, na ndako, mpe na balopitalo.

src: They are also more likely to experience violence and abuse.
trg: Likoki ezali makasi ete basalela bango mobulu mpe banyokola bango.

src: There is no one single cause of LGBT identity.
trg: Ezali te na ntina moko mpamba mpo na identité ya LGBT.

src: Some people are born with an innate sense of their sexual orientation or gender identity, while others develop these feelings over time.
trg: Bato mosusu babotama na makanisi na bango na ndenge ya kosangisa nzoto to identité ya genre, kasi basusu bakolisaka mayoki wana na nsima.

src: LGBT people are just as diverse as the rest of the population.
trg: Ba LGBT bazali kaka bato neti bato nyonso mosusu.

src: They come from all walks of life and have a wide range of interests and experiences.
trg: Bauta na balolenge nyonso ya bomoi mpe balingaka mpe bakutana na makambo ndenge na ndenge.

src: The medical community recognizes that sexual orientation and gender identity are not mental illnesses.
trg: Minganga bandimaka ete lolenge ya kosangisa nzoto mpe koyeba identité ezali te maladi ya moto.

src: In fact, the American Psychiatric Association removed homosexuality from its list of mental disorders in 1973.
trg: Ya solo, Lisanga ya Psychiatrie ya Amerika elongolaki homosexualité na liste na yango ya maladi ya moto na 1973.

src: LGBT people should be able to live their lives openly and authentically.
trg: Ba LGBT basengeli kozala na bomoi na bango na polele mpe na bosolo.

src: They deserve to be treated with respect and dignity.
trg: Esengeli kosalela bango makambo na botosi mpe limemya.

src: In many countries, there are laws that protect LGBT people from discrimination.
trg: Na mikili ebele, ezali na mibeko mpo na kobatela ba LGBT mpo batyola bango te.

src: Doctor: Hello, and welcome to your annual checkup.
trg: Monganga: Mbote, mpe boyei malamu na checkup ya mbula na mbula.

src: How are you feeling today?
trg: Ozali koyoka ndenge nini lelo?

src: Patient: I'm feeling pretty good, all things considered.
trg: Mobeli: Nazali komiyoka mwa malamu, soki natali makambo nyonso.

src: I've been getting a little more sleep lately, and my diet has been pretty healthy.
trg: Nazalaki kolala mwa mingi na mikolo eleki, mpe nazali kolya bilei ya mwa malamu.

src: Doctor: That's great to hear.
trg: Monganga: Ezali malamu koyoka bongo.

src: I'm going to start by taking your vital signs.
trg: Nakobanda kozwa bilembo ezolakisa ozali na bomoi.

src: [The doctor takes the patient's blood pressure, pulse, and temperature.]
trg: [Monganga azwaki tension, kobeta ya motema mpe temperature ya moto ya maladi.]

src: Doctor: Everything looks good here.
trg: Monganga: Makambo nyonso ezali malamu awa.

src: Now, let's talk about your diet.
trg: Sikoyo, tolobela bilei olyaka.

src: What are you eating on a typical day?
trg: Bilei nini olyaka mbala mingi?

src: Patient: I usually have a bowl of cereal for breakfast, a sandwich for lunch, and a salad for dinner.
trg: Mobeli: Mbala mingi nalyaka sani ya cereale na ntongo, sandwiche na midi, mpe salade na mpokwa.

src: I also try to eat fruits and vegetables throughout the day.
trg: Nalyaka mpe bambuma na bandunda na mokolo.

src: Doctor: That sounds like a healthy diet.
trg: Monganga: Emonani neti ezali bilei ya malamu.

src: Are you getting enough exercise?
trg: Osalaka ngalasisi ndenge esengeli?

src: Patient: I try to get at least 30 minutes of exercise most days of the week.
trg: Mobeli: Namekaka kosala ngalasisi miniti ata 30 mikolo mingi na boumeli ya mposo.

src: I walk to work, and I play basketball once or twice a week.
trg: Nakendaka mosala na mokolo, mpe nabetaka baskeball mbala moko to mibale na mposo.

src: Doctor: That's great. Exercise is an important part of a healthy lifestyle.
trg: Monganga: Ezali malamu. Ngalasisi ezali eteni ya ntina ya bomoi ya malamu.

src: Patient: I know. I'm trying to be more active.
trg: Mobeli: Nayebi. Nasalaka nyonso na kosala mosala.

src: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is a country in Central Africa with a population of over 80 million people.
trg: Repiblike Demokratike ya Congo (RDC) ezali mboka moko ya Afrika ya Katikati oyo ezali na bato koleka bamilio 80.

src: It is the second-largest country in Africa by area, and is endowed with vast natural resources, including copper, cobalt, diamonds, and gold.
trg: Ezali mboka ya mibale ya monene na Afrika, mpe ezali na biloko mingi ya bozalisi, neti kwivre, cobalt, diama, mpe wolo.

src: However, the DRC has been plagued by conflict for decades, which has had a devastating impact on its people and economy.
trg: Kasi, RDC enyokwama na bitumba banda mibu ebele, bitumba wana ezali na bopusi mabe na bato mpe na ekonomi na yango.

src: The first major conflict in the DRC was the First Congo War, which lasted from 1996 to 1997.
trg: Bitumba ya monene ya liboso na RDC ezalaki Bitumba ya Liboso ya Congo, oyo esalemaki banda 1996 kino 1997.

src: This war was fought between the government of Mobutu Sese Seko and a rebel group led by Laurent Kabila.
trg: Bitumba oyo ebundamaki na kati ya guvernema ya Mobutu Sese Seko mpe etuluku ya batomboki ekambami na Laurent Kabila.

src: Kabila eventually succeeded in overthrowing Mobutu and taking power.
trg: Nsukansuka Kabila alongaki na kokweisa Mobutu mpe azwaki bokonzi.

src: However, Kabila's rule was short-lived.
trg: Atako bongo, boyangeli ya Kabila eumelaki te.

src: In 1998, he was overthrown by a new rebel group led by Jean-Pierre Bemba.
trg: Na 1998, bakweisaki ye na etuluku ya sika ya batomboki ekambami na Jean-Pierre Bemba.

src: This led to the Second Congo War, which lasted until 2003.
trg: Ememaki na Bitumba ya Mibale ya Congo, oyo eumelaki kino na 2003.

src: The Second Congo War was the deadliest conflict in modern African history, and resulted in the deaths of over 5 million people.
trg: Bitumba ya Mibale ya Congo ezalaki bitumba eboma bato ebele koleka na lisolo ya sika ya Afrika, mpe ebomisaki bato koleka bamilio 5.

src: The DRC has also been plagued by political instability.
trg: RDC enyokwamaka mpe na matata ya politiki.

src: Last week, my uncle was out in the field harvesting corn when he spotted a snake slithering across the ground.
trg: Mposo eleki, noko akendaki kolongola masangu na bilanga ntango amonaki nyoka abombani na mabele.

src: He decided to take a closer look, and as he got closer, he realized that it was a huge rattlesnake!
trg: Azwaki ekateli ya kotala yango na pene, mpe ntango azalaki kopusana pene, amonaki ete ezali nyoka oyo ebetaka piololo!

src: He quickly backed away, but the snake was already on the move.
trg: Azongaki nsima noki, kasi nyoka esilaki kobanda kotambola.

src: It headed straight for my uncle, who started to run.
trg: Eyaki mbala moko epai ya noko, oyo abandaki kokima.

src: He ran as fast as he could, but the snake was gaining on him.
trg: Apotaki mbango ndenge akokaki, kasi nyoka ezalaki kokoma pene na ye.

src: Just when it seemed like the snake was going to catch him, my uncle tripped and fell.
trg: Kaka ntango emonanki neti nyoka elingi kokanga ye, noko abetaki libaku mpe akweaki.

src: He landed in a big pile of manure, and the snake slid right past him.
trg: Akweaki likolo ya liboke ya monene ya mbindo, mpe nyoka elekaki ye.

src: My uncle was so relieved that he had escaped, but he was also covered in manure.
trg: Motema ya noko ekitaki mpo abikaki, kasi nzoto na ye etondaki mpe na mbindo.

src: The plastic bag is a ubiquitous object in our modern world.
trg: Basache ezalaka bisika nyonso na mokili na biso ya lelo.

src: It is used for everything from carrying groceries to picking up dog poop.
trg: Basalelaka yango mpo na biloko nyonso banda komema biloko kino kolokota mbindo ya mbwa.

src: But what is the true cost of this seemingly innocuous item?
trg: Kasi nini ezali motuya ya eloko oyo ezali komonana neti ezali mabe te?

src: Plastic bags are made from a type of plastic called polyethylene, which is derived from fossil fuels.
trg: Basache esalemaka na biloko babengi polyethylene, oyo eutaka na ba combustible fossile.

src: The production of plastic bags requires a great deal of energy, and it also releases harmful pollutants into the environment.
trg: Kosala basache esengaki energie mingi mpenza, mpe ebimisaka biloko oyo ezalaka mabe mpo na mopepe.

src: Once plastic bags are discarded, they can take hundreds of years to decompose.
trg: Soki babwaki basache, ekoki kozwa bankama ya bambula liboso ebeba.

src: This means that they can accumulate in landfills and oceans, where they can harm wildlife and pollute our water supply.
trg: Elakisi ete ekoki kosangana ebele na bisika babwaka biloko ya mbindo mpe na bambu, esika ekoki kobebisa biloko ya zamba mpe kobebisa mai na biso.

src: Plastic bags are also a major source of litter.
trg: Basache ezali mpe eloko monene oyo ememaka mbindo.

src: They can be found on beaches, in parks, and even in our own neighborhoods.
trg: Tokoki komona yango na mabongo, na baparke, mpe ata na bakartie na biso.

src: Litter is unsightly and can be a hazard to wildlife.
trg: Mbindo emonanaki te mpe ekoki kozala likama mpo na biloko ya zamba.

src: The plastic bag is a symbol of our throwaway culture.
trg: Sache ezali elembo ya culture na biso ya kobwaka biloko.

src: We use them for a few minutes and then discard them, never giving a thought to the environmental consequences.
trg: Tosalelaka yango na mwa miniti moke mpe na nsima tobwakaka yango, tokanisaka ata moke te na ba consequence na yango na mopepe.

src: We need to find ways to reduce our use of plastic bags.
trg: Tosengeli koluka koyeba balolenge ya sika ya kosalela mingi te basache.

src: We can bring our own reusable bags when we go shopping, and we can recycle plastic bags whenever possible.
trg: Tokoki komema basaki na biso moko oyo basalelaka mbala mingi ntango tokei kosomba, mpe kosalela basaki oyo basalelaka mbala mingi soki makoki ezali.

src: We can also lobby our elected officials to pass laws that restrict the use of plastic bags.
trg: Tokoki mpe kopusa bakonzi topona na kovote mobeko oyo etye bandelo na ndenge ya kosalela basache.

src: Kofi and Sameer met in college at a bar that Kofi's father owned.
trg: Kofi na Sameer bakutanaki na collège na bare ya papa ya Kofi.

src: They became fast friends, even though they were very different people.
trg: Bakomaki baninga noki, ata bazalaki bato oyo bakeseni makasi.

src: Kofi was outgoing and adventurous, while Sameer was more introverted and studious.
trg: Kofi azalaki kobimisa makanisi na ye mpe kosekisa, kasi Sameer azalaki koloba mingi te mpe koyekola ebele.

src: But they had a lot in common, and they quickly bonded over their shared love of music, movies, and books.
trg: Kasi bazalaki na eloko moko ya ndenge moko, mpe kozanga kozela boninga ekolaki mpo bolingo na bango ya miziki, bafilme mpe mikanda.

src: They spent hours talking about their favorite bands, movies, and books, and they even started a band together.
trg: Bazalaki kolekisa bangonga ebele na kolobela bituluku, bafilme, mpe mikanda oyo bazalaki kolinga mingi, mpe basalaki etuluku bango mibale.

src: After college, Kofi and Sameer moved to different cities, but they stayed in touch and visited each other regularly.
trg: Nsima ya collège, Kofi na Sameer bakendaki na bingumba ekeseni, kasi bakobaka kosolola mpe kotalana mbala na mbala.

src: They continued to be best friends, even though they lived far apart.
trg: Bakobaki kozala baninga ya malamu, ata bazalaki kofanda esika moko te.

src: They talked on the phone every week, and they always made time for each other when they were in town.
trg: Bazalaki kosolola na telefone mposo nyonso, mpe bazalaki ntango nyonso komibombela ntango ya kotalana soki bayei na engumba ya moninga.

src: Kofi and Sameer' friendship has lasted for over 30 years, and it shows no signs of slowing down.
trg: Boninga ya Kofi na Sameer esalaki mibu koleka 30, mpe ezalaki na elembo ata moko te ya kolemba.

src: The air was thick with the smell of sweat and freshly cut grass as the athletes lined up for the start of the 100-meter dash.
trg: Mopepe ezalaki na nsolo ya motoki mpe ya matiti bauti kokata ntango ba atlete babongamaki na kopota 100 metre.

src: The crowd was cheering wildly, eager to see who would come out on top.
trg: Bato bazalaki kokumisa bango makasi, bazali kozela nani akobima moto ya liboso.

src: The gun went off, and the runners sprinted out of the blocks.
trg: Ngonga ebetaki, mpe baboti-mbango balongwaki na bisika na yango.

src: They were all evenly matched, and it was anyone's race.
trg: Bango nyonso bazalaki ndenge moko, mpe ezalaki mbangu ya bato nyonso.

src: As they approached the finish line, the lead changed hands several times.
trg: Ntango bakomaki pene ya nsuka, moto ya liboso abongwanaki mbala ebele.

src: In the end, it was a photo finish, but the winner was clear: a young woman with long, flowing hair and a determined expression on her face.
trg: Na nsuka, ezalaki na foto ya nsuka, kasi molongi amonanaki polele: elenge mwasi ya molai, na nsuki ekwea mpe na mokano makasi na elongi na ye.

src: She had won the gold medal, and she had made her country proud.
trg: Asila kolonga mbano ya wolo, mpe azalaki lokumu ya mboka na ye.

src: As she stood on the podium, her national anthem played, and she waved to the cheering crowd.
trg: Ntango atelemaki na estrade, bayembaki loyembo ya mboka na bango, mpe apepaki bato oyo bazalaki kosepela.

src: She had achieved her dream, and she had shown the world that anything is possible if you work hard and never give up.
trg: Akokisaki ndoto na ye, mpe alakisaki mokili ete eloko nyonso ekoki kosalema soki osali makasi mpe otiki te.

src: This was just one of many stories that were being written that day.
trg: Ezali kaka moko ya masolo ebele oyo bazalaki kokoma mokolo wana.

src: All over the world, athletes were competing in their respective sports, all with the same goal in mind: to win.
trg: Na mokili mobimba, ba atlete bamekanaka na masano na bango, bazalaka na mokano kaka moko na makanisi: kolonga.

src: Some would succeed, and some would fail, but all would have their stories to tell.
trg: Mosusu bakolonga, mpe basusu bakopola, kasi bango nyonso bazali na masolo ya kobeta.

src: Organ Trafficking: A Growing Problem Organ trafficking is a serious problem that affects people around the world.
trg: Koteka Binama: Likambo Oyo Ezali Kokola Koteka binama ezali mokakatano makasi oyo ezali konyokola bato ebele na mokili mobimba.

src: Every year, thousands of people are tricked, coerced, or kidnapped into giving up their organs.
trg: Mbula nyonso, bankoto ya bato kokosama, kopusama, to kokangama mpo bapesa binama na bango.

src: These organs are then sold to wealthy people who can afford to pay for them.
trg: Na nsima bazali koteka binama oyo na bazwi oyo bakoki kofuta bango.

src: Organ trafficking is a lucrative business.
trg: Koteka binama ezali mombongo oyo ezali kopesa mosolo ebele.

src: The black market price for a single organ can range from \$100,000 to \$1 million.
trg: Ntalo ya enama kaka moko na zando ya moindo ekoki kobanda \$100,000 kino na \$1 million.

src: This makes it a very attractive option for criminals who are looking to make a quick buck.
trg: Yango ezali liponi ya kitoko mpo na bato mabe oyo balingaka kozwa mosolo nokinoki.

src: Organ trafficking is often carried out by organized crime groups.
trg: Koteka binama esalemaka mbala mingi na bituluku ya bato ya mabe.

src: These groups use a variety of methods to recruit victims, including force, fraud, and deception.
trg: Bituluku oyo esalelaka balolenge ekeseni mpo na kozwa bavictime ata makasi, kobuba, mpe kokosa.

src: Victims are often lured into the country with promises of a job or a better life.
trg: Bakosaka mbala mingi bavictime ete bakomema bango na mboka oyo ezali na mosala malamu to bomoi ya malamu.

src: Once they are here, they are held captive and forced to give up their organs.
trg: Soki bakomi kuna, bakomisaka bango baombo mpe bapusaka bango na kopesa binama na bango.

src: Organ trafficking can have devastating consequences for victims.
trg: Koteka binama ekoki kozala na ba consequence ya mabe mpenza mpo na bavictime.

src: Not only do they suffer physical and psychological trauma, but they may also die from the surgery.
trg: Banyokwamaka kaka te na mpasi na nzoto mpe na makanisi, kasi bakoki kokufa na ntango ya lipaso.

src: In addition, organ trafficking can spread diseases such as HIV and hepatitis.
trg: Lisusu, koteka binama ekoki kopanza maladi neti SIDA mpe hepatite.

src: The fight against organ trafficking is a complex one.
trg: Kobundisa koteka binama ezali bitumba ya mpasi.

src: There is no single solution that will work in every case.
trg: Ezali na solution kaka moko te oyo ekosimba na likambo nyonso.

src: A: Hey, have you heard about the new backpacking store that's opening up B: No, I haven't.
trg: A: Mbote, oyoki nsango ya butiki ya basaki ya mokongo oyo bazali kofungola B: Te, nanu te.

src: Where is it A: It's on Main Street, right next to the old bank B: Oh, that's a great location A: Yeah, I know.
trg: Ezali na wapi A: Ezali na Balabala Monene, pene ya banki ya kala B: Oh, ezali esika ya kitoko A: Ee, nayebi.

src: I'm really excited about it B: Me too.
trg: Nasepeli mingi mpo na yango B: Nga mpe.

src: I've been looking for a new place to buy backpacking gear A: Well, this is the place for you.
trg: Nazalaki koluka esika ya sika ya koluka esika ya kosomba basaki ya ndenge wana A: Malamu, esika wana ebongi mpo na yo.

src: They have everything you could ever need B: Awesome.
trg: Bazali na biloko nyonso oyo okoki kozala na mposa na yango B: Malamu.

src: I'll definitely check it out A: You won't be disappointed B: Thanks for the tip A: No problem A: Hey, did you see that ad for the backpacking trip to the Grand Canyon B: Yeah, I saw it.
trg: Nakokende mpenza kotala yango A: Okolemba nzoto te B: Matondi mpo na toli A: Likambo te A: Eh, omonaki piblisite ya mobembo na Canyon Monene B: Ee, namonaki yango.

src: It looks amazing A: I know, right?
trg: Ezali komonana ezali kitoko makasi A: Nayebi, bongo?

src: I'm so tempted to go B: You should do it.
trg: Neti nga mpe nakokende B: Osengeli kosala yango.

src: One day, a young girl named Mary was combing her hair when she saw a louse.
trg: Mokolo moko, elenge mwasi moko nkombo na ye Maria azalaki kosanola nsuki mpe amonaki sili.

src: She was horrified, and she ran to her mother for help.
trg: Abangaki, mpe akimaki epai ya mama na ye mpo asalisa ye.

src: Her mother told her that there were many traditional remedies for lice, and that she would try the one that required the least amount of action.
trg: Mama ayebisaki ye ete ezali na bankisi ebele mpo na koboma basili, mpe ete akomeka nkisi moko oyo ekosenga te ete asala makambo ebele.

src: The first thing her mother did was to boil a pot of water.
trg: Likambo ya liboso mama na ye asalaki ezalaki ya kotokisa mai.

src: Then, she added a handful of dried rosemary leaves and let them steep for a few minutes.
trg: Na nsima, abakisaki mwa nkasa ya romarin mpe kotika yango mwa miniti.

src: After the water had cooled, her mother poured it into a bowl and told Mary to sit down.
trg: Ntango mai ekomaki malili, mama atyaki yango na sani mpe ayebisaki Maria na kofanda.

src: She then used a comb to wet Mary's hair with the rosemary water.
trg: Na nsima asalelaki kisanola mpo na kopolisa nsuki ya Maria na mai ya romarin.

src: The lice started to die, and Mary was able to pick them out of her hair with ease.
trg: Basili ebandaki kokufa, mpe Maria akokaki kolongola yango na nsuki na ye na pete.

src: Her mother was so happy that she had been able to help Mary without having to take any drastic measures.
trg: Mama asepelaki mpo asalisaki Maria kozanga kosala makambo ya mindondomindindo.

src: She knew that Mary would be able to sleep soundly that night, knowing that she was free of lice.
trg: Ayebaki ete Maria akokoka kolala mpongi kitoko na butu wana, mpo ayebi ete azali te na basili.

src: The next day, Mary's mother went to the store and bought a bottle of lice shampoo.
trg: Mokolo elandaki, mama ya Maria akendaki na butiki mpe asombaki shampoin ebomaki basili.

src: She told Mary that it was important to use the shampoo to kill any remaining lice, and that she should follow the directions on the bottle carefully.
trg: Ayebisaki Maria ete ezalaki ntina ete asalela shampoin wana mpo na koboma basili nyonso oyo etikalaki, mpe ete asengeli kotosa malamumalamu malako ezali likolo ya molangi.

src: Work is worship is a principle that states that all work, no matter how menial or insignificant it may seem, is sacred.
trg: Mosala ezali kosambela malako oyo elobi ete mosala nyonso, ezala ya maboko to ata ezali komonana ya kozanga ntina, ezali mosantu.

src: It is a belief that every task we perform, from cooking dinner for our children to cleaning the house, is an opportunity to honor God and our fellow man.
trg: Ezali kokanisa ete mosala nyonso tozali kosala, banda na kolamba bilei mpo na bana na biso kino na kokombola ndako, ezali libaku ya kukumisa Nzambe mpe baninga na biso bato.

src: When we work with this mindset, we approach our tasks with a sense of reverence and respect.
trg: Soki tozali kosala na makanisi oyo, tokosala misala na biso na bobangi mpe botosi.

src: We take pride in our work and do our best to do it well.
trg: Tozalaka na esengo na mosala na biso mpe tosalaka nyonso mpo na kosala yango malamu.

src: We also become more mindful of the people who will benefit from our work, and we are more likely to go the extra mile to make sure that it is done well.
trg: Tokomaka mpe kokanisa bato oyo bakozwa matomba na mosala na biso, mpe likoki ezali ete tokosala makasi koleka mpo ete esalema malamu.

src: Working as worship can also help us to connect with our families and communities.
trg: Kotalela mosala neti losambo ekoki mpe kosalisa biso na koyokana na mabota mpe ba communauté na biso.

src: When we cook dinner for our children, we are not only providing them with nourishment, but we are also spending time with them and teaching them about the importance of food and family.
trg: Soki tozali kolambela bana na biso bilei ya ntongo, tozali kaka te kopesa bango bilei, kasi tozali kolekisa ntango na bango mpe koteya bango ntina ya bilei mpe ya libota.

src: When we clean the house, we are not only making our living space more comfortable, but we are also creating a sense of order and peace.
trg: Soki tokomboli ndako, tozali kaka te kokomisa esika na biso ya kofanda esika ya malamu, kasi tozali mpe kokotisa molongo na kimya na makanisi na bango.

src: Work is worship is a powerful principle that can transform our lives and our relationships.
trg: Kotalela mosala lokola losambo ezali malako ya makasi oyo ekoki kobongola bomoi mpe boyokani na biso.

src: When we work with this mindset, we can find meaning and purpose in even the most mundane tasks.
trg: Soki tozali kosala na makanisi oyo, tokoki kozwa ndimbola mpe mokano ata na misala ya kozanga ntina mpenza.

src: "Don't judge a book by its cover" is a popular saying that means one should not make assumptions about something based on its outward appearance.
trg: "Kosambisa mokanda te na mposo na yango" ezali maloba eyebana oyo elimboli ete moto asengeli te kolobela likambo moko na kotalela kaka oyo amoni na miso.

src: This can be applied to people, places, and things.
trg: Ekoki kotalela bato, bisika, mpe biloko.

src: For example, you might meet someone who has a bad reputation, but after getting to know them, you realize that they are actually a kind and gentle person.
trg: Na ndakisa, okoki kokutana na moto moko oyo azali na lokumu mabe, kasi nsima ya koyebana na ye, omoni ete azali moto ya motema malamu mpe ya boboto.

src: Or, you might see a building that looks old and rundown, but when you go inside, you find that it is actually a beautiful and historic place.
trg: To, okoki komona ndako oyo ezomonana ya kala mpe ya bongobongo, kasi ntango okoti na kati, omoni ete ezali mpenza esika ya kitoko mpe ekenda nsango.

src: There are many reasons why it is important not to judge things by their appearance.
trg: Ezali na bantina ebele oyo ezali ntina na kosambisa te biloko kana ndenge ezomonana na miso.

src: First, it can lead to making incorrect assumptions.
trg: Ya liboso, ekoki kotinda na kozwa makanisi mabe.

src: Second, it can prevent us from seeing the true value of something.
trg: Ya mibale, ekoki kokanga biso nzela ya komona motuya ya solo ya eloko moko.

src: Third, it can create unnecessary conflict and division.
trg: Ya misato, ekoki kobimisa kowelana mpe bokabwani ezangi ntina.

src: The next time you are tempted to judge something by its appearance, take a moment to pause and reflect.
trg: Mbala ya nsima oyo okomeka kosambisa eloko na kotalela ndenge ezali komonana, zwa ntango ya kopema mpe kokanisa.

src: Ask yourself if you are really making an informed decision, or if you are simply letting your biases cloud your judgment.
trg: Mituna soki ozali kozwa ekateli nsima ya koyeba makambo nyonso, to soki ozali kaka kosala yango na kolanda bosololi na yo ya mabe.

src: Remember, there is more to a person, place, or thing than meets the eye.
trg: Kobosana te, makambo ezali ebele mpo na moto, esika, to eloko koleka kotala na miso.

src: Imagine a small town in South Carolina where everyone knows everyone else.
trg: Kanisa mboka moko ya moke na Sud ya Californie esika bato nyonso bayebani.

src: The police chief's daughter, who is also the lead actress in the local theater company, is about to go on stage for her big performance.
trg: Mwana-mwasi ya mokonzi ya bapolisi, oyo azali actrice monene na kompani ya teyatre ya mboka, alingi komata na estrade mpo na kosala makasi.

src: But when she gets to the theater, she realizes that she has forgotten her lines.
trg: Kasi ntango akoti na esika ya teyatre, amoni ete abosani maloba na ye.

src: She panics and tries to think of what to do, but she can't come up with anything.
trg: Akomi likololikolo mpe ameki kokanisa nini akosala, kasi akoki kosala eloko moko te.

src: Just then, the police chief walks into the theater and sees his daughter's distress.
trg: Kasi na nsima, mokonzi ya bapolisi akoti na esika ya teyatre mpe amoni mpasi ya mwana na ye ya mwasi.

src: He knows that she is a good actress and that she will be able to pull this off, so he gives her a pep talk and tells her to go out there and do her best.
trg: Ayebi ete azali actrice ya makasi mep ete akoka kolongola mokakatano oyo, yango wana asaleli ye mwa lisolo mpe ayebisi ye nakobima mpe kosala oyo ayebi kosala.

src: She takes a deep breath and walks out on stage, ready to perform.
trg: Apemi makasi mpe amati na estrade, abongama na kosala mokumba na ye.

src: She delivers her lines perfectly and the audience is thrilled.
trg: Akokisi mokumba na ye malamu mpenza mpe bayoki basepeli makasi.

src: The young soldier lay on the battlefield, bleeding from a wound in his side.
trg: Elenge ya soda alalaki na esika ya bitumba, makila ezali kotanga na mpota azokaki na mopanzi.

src: He looked up at the sky and saw the clouds scudding past, and the sun shining down on him.
trg: Atalaki na likolo mpe amonaki mapata ezali koleka, mpe moi ezali kobeta ye.

src: He thought of his home town, and the food he would never eat again, and the people he would never see again.
trg: Akanisaki mboka na ye, mpe bilei oyo akotikala kolya lisusu te, mpe bato oyo akotikala komona lisusu te.

src: He closed his eyes and said a prayer.
trg: Akangaki miso mpe abondelaki.

src: A moment later, he heard a voice "Are you all right" The soldier opened his eyes and saw a woman standing over him.
trg: Ntango moke na nsima, ayokaki mongongo "Ozali malamu" Soda afungolaki miso mpe amonaki mwasi moko atelemi pene na ye.

src: She was tall and slender, with long black hair and green eyes.
trg: Azalaki molai mpe nzoto moke, na nsuki ya milai ya moindo mpe miso ya vert.

src: She was wearing a leather tunic and leggings, and she had a sword at her side "I'mI'm okay," the soldier said "You're hurt," the woman said "Let me help you" The woman helped the soldier to his feet.
trg: Alataki elamba ya kwire mpe collant, mpe azalaki na mopanga na mopanzi "Nazali malamu," ndenge soda alobaki "Ozali na mpasi," ndenge mwasi alobaki "Tika nasalisa yo" Mwasi asalisaki soda wana na kotelema.

src: She took off her cloak and wrapped it around him to stop the bleeding.
trg: Alongolaki kazaka na ye mpe azingaki yango na mpota mpo etika kotangisa makila.

src: Then she led him to a nearby town.
trg: Na nsima amemaki ye na mboka ya pene.

src: The town was small and quiet.
trg: Mboka yango ezalaki moke mpe kimya.

src: The people were friendly, and they gave the soldier food and a place to stay.
trg: Bato bazalaki na bonkonde, mpe bapesaki soda wana bilei mpe esika ya kofanda.

src: The woman stayed with him, and she helped him to heal.
trg: Mwasi wana atikalaki na ye, mpe asalisaka ye na kobika.

src: Many famous dictators have ruled over states throughout history.
trg: Badiktatere ebele oyo bayebana bayangela mikili na lisolo ya bato.

src: Some of the most notable include Adolf Hitler, who ruled over Nazi Germany from 1933 to 1945; Joseph Stalin, who ruled over the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1953; and Mao Zedong, who ruled over China from 1949 to 1976.
trg: Ndambo ya baoyo bayebana ebele ezali Adolf Hitler, oyo ayangelaki Allemange ya Nazi banda 1933 kino 1945; Joseph Stalin, oyo ayangelaki Union Sovietique banda 1922 kino 1953; mpe Mao Zedong, oyo ayangelaki Chine banda 1949 kino 1976.

src: These dictators were all responsible for the deaths of millions of people, and their regimes were characterized by violence, oppression, and totalitarianism.
trg: Badiktatere oyo nyonso babomisaki bamilio ya bato, mpe bokonzi na bango eyebanaki mpo na mobulu, konyokola bato mpe nkanza.

src: One of the most surprising things about these dictators is that they were able to maintain power for so long.
trg: Likambo moko ya kokamwa mingi mpo na badiktatere oyo ezali ete basalaki bambula ebele na bokonzi.

src: They were able to do this by using a combination of propaganda, intimidation, and violence.
trg: Basalaki yango na kosalelaka propagande, kobangisa bato mpe mobulu.

src: They also had the support of powerful militaries and secret police forces.
trg: Bazalaki mpe na lisungi ya basoda ya makasi mpe ya bapolisi ya sekele.

src: Despite their power, these dictators were eventually overthrown.
trg: Ata bazalaki na nguya, nsukansuka bakweisaki badiktatere oyo.

src: Hitler committed suicide in 1945, Stalin died of a stroke in 1953, and Mao died of natural causes in 1976.
trg: Hitler amibomaki na 1945, Stalin akufaki na avc na 1953, mpe Mao akufaki liwa ya normale na 1976.

src: [Scene: A railway station.
trg: [Likambo: Esika engunduka etelamaka.

src: A man and a woman are waiting for a train.] Man: I love trains.
trg: Mobali na mwasi moko bazali kozala engunduka.] Mobali: Nalingaka engunduka.

src: They're so romantic.
trg: Ezalaki kitoko makasi.

src: Woman: I don't know about that.
trg: Mwasi: Nayebi likambo wana te.

src: They're just a way to get from one place to another.
trg: Esalisaka kaka na kolongwa esika moko mpo na kokende na esika mosusu.

src: Man: But there's something about the sound of the train whistle, the smell of the coal smoke, the feeling of the wind in your hair as you're speeding through the countryside.
trg: Mobali: Kai ezali na eloko moko na makelele ya sifflet ya engunduka, nsolo ya milinga ya makala, koyoka neti mopepe ezali kati na nsuki na yo ntango bazali koleka na vitesi makasi na esobe.

src: It's all very romantic.
trg: Ezali mpenza kitoko makasi.

src: Woman: I guess you're right.
