trg: Mwasi: Nakanisi olobi solo.

src: Trains can be romantic.
trg: Bingunduka ekoki kozala kitoko makasi.

src: Man: Especially steam trains.
trg: Mobali: Mingimingi bingunduka ya mopepe.

src: There's something about the sight of a steam locomotive chuffing along the tracks that just takes me back in time.
trg: Ezali na eloko moko soki ozali komona engunduka ya mopepe ezali koleka na banzela na yango oyo ezali kokundwela nga makambo eleka.

src: Woman: I know what you mean.
trg: Mwasi: Nayebi nini olingi koloba.

src: Steam trains are beautiful.
trg: Bingunduka ya mopepe ezalaka kitoko.

src: Man: I'm glad you agree. [The train arrives.
trg: Mobali: Nasepeli mpo ondimi. [Engunduka ekomi.

src: The man and woman board the train.] Man: This is the best seat in the house.
trg: Mobali na mwasi bamati na engundukka.] Mobali: Oyo ezali kiti ya kitoko koleka na kati ya ndako.

src: Woman: It sure is.
trg: Mwasi: Ezali bongo.

src: We have a great view of the countryside.
trg: Bomoni malamu mpenza esobe.

src: Man: And the train is so smooth.
trg: Mobali: Mpe engunduka ezali moselu makasi.

src: It's like we're not even moving.
trg: Ezali neti kutu tozali kokende te.

src: The reality of acid rain is a four-letter word: ouch.
trg: Bosolo ya mbula ya acide ezali liloba ya makomi minei: ouch.

src: It's a serious problem that's harming forests, lakes, and even people.
trg: Ezali likama ya makasi oyo ezali kobebisa bazamba, balake, mpe kutu bato.

src: Acid rain is caused when chemicals like sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide are released into the air by power plants, factories, and cars.
trg: Mbula ya acide esalemaka soki biloko ya chimie neti dixiode ya soufre mpe oxide ya azote ebimi na mopepe na nguya ya ba izine mpe mituka.

src: These chemicals react with water in the atmosphere to form acids, which then fall to the ground in rain, snow, or fog.
trg: Biloko oyo ya chimie esalaka na mai na mopepe mpo na kosala ba acide, na nsima ekweaka na mabele na mbula, neze, to londende.

src: Acid rain can damage trees by making their leaves more acidic.
trg: Mbula ya acide ekoki kobebisa banzete na kokomisaka nkasa na yango na acide mingi.

src: This can cause the leaves to turn yellow and fall off, which can weaken the tree and make it more susceptible to disease.
trg: Ekoki kosala ete nkasa ekoma jaune mpe ekwea, yango ekoki kolembisa nzete mpe ekoma kozwa maladi na pete.

src: Acid rain can also kill fish and other aquatic life by making the water too acidic.
trg: Mbula ya acide ekoki koboma mbisi mpe biloko mosusu ezalaka na mai na kokomisaka mai na acide mingi.

src: In addition, acid rain can damage buildings and statues by corroding the materials they're made of.
trg: Lisusu, mbula ya acide ekoki kobebisa bandako mpe bikeko na kobebisaka biloko oyo basala yango.

src: There are a number of things that can be done to reduce acid rain.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kosalema mpo na mbula ya acide ezala mingi te.

src: One is to switch to cleaner energy sources, such as solar and wind power.
trg: Moko ezali ya kobanda kosalela biloko epetolaka energie mpe energie ya mopepe.

src: Another is to install pollution controls on factories and power plants.
trg: Mosusu ezali ya kotya biloko oyo ekontrolaka kobebisa mopepe na ba izine mpe ba centrale ya lotiliki.

src: And finally, we can all do our part by driving less, recycling more, and using energy more efficiently.
trg: Mpe na nsuka, biso nyonso tokoki kosalisa na kokumbaka motuka moke, kobongisa mingi, mpe kosalela energie na ndenge ya malamu.

src: So the next time you see a rainstorm, think about acid rain.
trg: Mbala ya nsima okomona mbula ya mabanga, kanisa mbula ya acide.

src: "College student's experiences with beer": As a college student, I have had my fair share of experiences with beer.
trg: "Makambo bayekoli ya collège basala na masanga": Lokola moyekoli ya collège, nakutanaki na makambo na nga na masanga.

src: Some of these experiences have been positive, while others have been less than ideal.
trg: Makambo mosusu ezalaki ya malamu, kasi mosusu ezallaki ya malamu mpenza te.

src: However, one experience that I will never forget is the time I got "prison beer" delivered to my dorm room.
trg: Kasi, likambo moko oyo nakotikal kobosana te ezali ntango bazalaki koya kotikela nga "masanga ya boloko" na porte ya chambre na nga.

src: It all started when I was hanging out with some friends one night, and we decided to order a pizza.
trg: Nyonso ebandaki ntango nazalaki kobima na mwa baninga na mpokwa moko, mpe tozwaki ekateli ya kosenga pizza.

src: We placed our order online, and within minutes, we received a notification that our pizza was being delivered.
trg: Tosalaki komande na internet, mpe nsima ya miniti, tozwaki nsango ete bazali koyela biso pizza na biso.

src: However, when the delivery guy showed up, he was not carrying a pizza.
trg: Kasi, ntango elenge oyo ayaki kotika yango akomaki, amemelaki biso pizza te.

src: Instead, he was carrying a case of beer.
trg: Na esika na yango, amemaki molangi ya masanga.

src: We were all confused, but the delivery guy explained that he had gotten our order mixed up with another order.
trg: Biso nyonso tokamwaki, kasi elenge wana alimbolaki ete komande na biso esanganaki na komande ya bato mosusu.

src: He said that the other person had ordered a case of beer, and he had accidentally delivered it to us instead.
trg: Alobaki ete moto mosusu asengaki masanga, kasi asalaki libunga yango wana ayelaki biso yango.

src: We were all a little hesitant at first, but we eventually decided to keep the beer.
trg: Biso nyonso tozalaki na badute na ebandeli, kasi nsukansuka tozwaki ekateli ya kozwa masanga wana.

src: After all, it was free beer.
trg: Kutu, ezalaki masanga ya ofele.

src: We opened the case of beer and started drinking.
trg: Tofungolaki molangi ya masanga mpe tobandaki komela.

src: The beer was actually pretty good, and we all had a great time.
trg: Masanga yango ezalaki kitoko, mpe tolekisaki ntnago malamu.

src: My colleague was a hard worker, but she was always getting passed over for promotions.
trg: Moninga na nga azalaki kosala makasi, kasi bazalaki te komatisa ye grade soki libaku emonani.

src: She was told that she needed to "work harder" or "be more visible," but it seemed like no matter what she did, she couldn't get ahead.
trg: Bayebisaki ye ee asengeli kosala "kosala makasi mpenza" to "komonana mingi," kasi emonanaki ete ata asalaki makasi ndenge nini, akokaki te kokende liboso.

src: The manager was also a problem.
trg: Mokonzi azalaki mpe mokakatano.

src: He was always micromanaging everyone, and he was quick to criticize.
trg: Azalaki ntango nyonso kolendelalandela bato nyonso, mpe azalaki koloba mabe noki.

src: He didn't seem to care about the employees' work-life balance, and he expected them to be available 24/7.
trg: Emonani ete azalaki na ye kokipe te bomoi ya bato ya mosal, mpe azalaki kozela bazala wana 24/7.

src: My colleague eventually reached her breaking point.
trg: Nsukansuka moninga na nga akomaki na nsuka.

src: She couldn't take the stress of the job anymore, and she knew that she wouldn't be able to advance her career there.
trg: Azalaki kokoka lisusu te motungisi ya mosala, mpe ayebaki ete akokende liboso na mosala na ye kuna.

src: She gave her two weeks' notice and started looking for a new job.
trg: Apesaki mokanda na ye mposo mibale liboso mpe abandaki koluka mosala ya sika.

src: She found a new job that was a much better fit for her.
trg: Azwaki mosala ya sika oyo ebongaki mpenza na ye koleka oy ya kala.

src: The pay was better, the hours were more reasonable, and the manager was supportive and understanding.
trg: Salere ezalaki ya malonga, bangonga ya mosala ezalaki ya malamu, mpe mokambi azalaki kosunga mpe koyokela bato.

src: She's much happier now, and she's glad that she made the decision to leave her old job.
trg: Azali na esengo ebele sikoyo, mpe azali na esengo mpo azwaki ekateli ya kolongwa na mosala wana.

src: I'm not sure what the manager is doing now, but I hope that he's learned his lesson.
trg: Nayebi te makambo azali kosala sikoyoo, kasi nazali kolikya ete azwaki liteya.

src: He can't treat his employees like that and expect them to stay.
trg: Akoki te kosalela bato na ye ya mosala makambo ndenge wana mpe kozela balongwa te.

src: If he wants to keep good people, he needs to change his ways.
trg: Soki alingi bato balongwa te, asengeli kobongola bizaleli na ye.

src: As for my colleague, she's doing great in her new job.
trg: Kasi moninga nga, azali kosepela na mosala na yeya sika.

src: She's getting the recognition that she deserves, and she's finally able to advance her career.
trg: Bazali kondima ye mpo na oyo azali kosala mpe nsukansuka azali kokende liboso na mosala na ye.

src: She's a great example of what happens when you stand up for yourself and refuse to put up with a bad situation.
trg: Azali ndakisa monene ya oyo ekoki kosalema soki otelemi mpo na yo moko mpe oboyi kokanga motema na likambo ya mabe.

src: Funny pictures and videos are a dime a dozen these days, but some of them stand out from the rest.
trg: Bafoto mpe bavideo ya kitoko ezali ebele mpenza na mikolo na biso, kasi mosusu kati na yango eleki misusu.

src: These are the ones that are so relatable or absurd that they make us laugh out loud.
trg: Baoyo wana ezali oyo ya malamu to bozoba yango wana esekisaka biso makasi.

src: One example is a recent video that went viral of a cat trying to fit into a small box.
trg: Ndakisa moko ezali video ya sika oyo bato mingi bamonaki ya niawu azali koluka kokoma na kesi ya moke.

src: The cat is clearly struggling, but it keeps trying, and the whole thing is just so funny.
trg: Niawu ezalaki mpenza kobunda, kasi ezali kokoba komeka, likambo wana nyonso ezali kosekisa.

src: Another example is a picture of a dog wearing a hat that is way too big for it.
trg: Ndakisa mosusu ezali foto ya mbwa alati ekoti oyo eleki yango mpenza na monene.

src: The dog looks so ridiculous that it's impossible not to laugh.
trg: Mbwa azali komonana zoba mpenza yango wana osengeli kaka koseka.

src: These types of funny pictures and videos are often shared on social media, and they can quickly become a "meme" A meme is a humorous image, video, or piece of text that is copied and shared online.
trg: Bafoto mpe bavideo ya kosekisa ya lolenge oyo, bakabolaka yango mbala mingi na resaux sociaux, mpe ekoki kokoma noki "meme" Meme ezali foto, video, to maloba ezosekisa oyo bakopie mpe bakabola na internet.

src: Memes often use familiar images or phrases, and they can be used to express a wide range of emotions.
trg: Mbala mingi bamemes esalelaka bilili to maloba bato bayeba, mpe bakoki kosalela yango mpo na komonisa mayoki ekeseni.

src: One thing that must happen when a funny picture or video goes viral is that it is shared with others.
trg: Likambo moko oyo esengeli kosalema ntango bato ebele bamoni foto to video moko ya kosekisa ezali bakaboli yango na bato mosusu.

src: This is what makes memes so popular.
trg: Yango nde esalaka ete memes eyebana mingi.

src: People see a funny picture or video, and they want to share it with their friends so that they can laugh too.
trg: Bato bamonaka foto to video ya kosekisa, mpe balingaka kokabola yango na baninga na bango mpo bango mpe baseka.

src: This is why memes can spread so quickly across the internet.
trg: Yango wana ba memes ekoki kopanzana noki na internet.

src: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world, standing at 8,848 meters above sea level.
trg: Ngomba Everest ezali ngomba ya molai koleka na mokili mobimba, ezali na molai bametre 8 848 likolo ya nivo ya mbu.

src: It is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.
trg: Ezalaka na Mahalangur Himal eteni ya nse ya Himalaya.

src: The mountain is a popular destination for mountaineers, and many people attempt to summit it each year.
trg: Ngomba oyo ezali esika bato batambolaka na bangomba balingaka mingi, mpe bato mingi bamekaka kokoma na nsonge na yango mbula nyonso.

src: However, the climb is dangerous, and many people have died trying to reach the top.
trg: Kasi, komata yango ezali likama, mpe bato ebele bakufa ntango bazalaki komeka kokoma na nsonge na yango.

src: The first recorded attempt to summit Everest was made in 1921 by a British expedition led by George Mallory.
trg: Lisolo ya liboso eyebana ya komeka kokoma na nsonge ya Everest esalemaki na 1921 na bato ya Grande-Bretagne oyo George Mallory azalaki kokamba.

src: Mallory and his climbing partner Andrew Irvine disappeared during their attempt, and their bodies were not found until 1999.
trg: Mallory na moninga na ye Andrew Irvine babungaka ntango bazalaki komeka komata, mpe bamonaki te bibembe na bango kino na 1999.

src: In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first people to successfully summit Everest.
trg: Na 1953, Edmund Hillary na Tenzing Norgay bakomaki bato ya liboso oyo balongaki kokoma na nsonge ya Everest.

src: Since then, thousands of people have followed in their footsteps.
trg: Banda wana, bankoto ya bato balanda matambe na bango.

src: The climb to the summit of Everest is a long and arduous journey.
trg: Komata kino na nsonge ya Everest ezali mobembo ya molai mpe ya likama.

src: It typically takes climbers about two months to complete the journey, and they must overcome a number of challenges along the way.
trg: Esengaka basanza pene ya mibale mpo bato oyo bamataka basilisa mobembo, mpe basengeli kolonga mikakatano ebele na nzela.

src: These challenges include altitude sickness, extreme weather conditions, and the risk of falling.
trg: Mikakatano yango ezali kobela mpo ozali na likolo, ba condition ya meteo ya mabe mpenza, mpe likama ya kokwea.

src: Despite the dangers, the climb to the summit of Everest is a rewarding experience.
trg: Atako makama oyo ezali, komata kino na nsonge ya Everest ezali likambo ya esengo.

src: Mother: The telescope is used to look at objects in space.
trg: Mama: Basalelaka teleskope mpo na kotala biloko ezali na mapata.

src: Child: Can I look through it?
trg: Mwana: Nakoki kotala na nzela na yango?

src: Mother: Sure, but be careful not to bump it.
trg: Mama: Likambo te, kasi zala mayele, kokweisa yango te.

src: The child looks through the telescope and sees a bright star.
trg: Mwana atali na nzela ya teleskope mpe amoni monzoto ezali kongenga.

src: Child: Wow, it's so beautiful!
trg: Mwana: Wawu, ezali kitoko makasi!

src: Mother: Yes, it is. The stars are so far away, but with a telescope, we can see them up close.
trg: Mama: Ee, ezali bongo. Minzoto ezalaka mosika makasi, kasi na lisalisi ya teleskope tokoki komona yango pene.

src: The child looks at other objects in space, including planets and moons.
trg: Mwana atali biloko mosusu na mapata, ata mpe baplanete mpe basanza.

src: They are amazed by how small and insignificant they feel compared to the vastness of the universe.
trg: Ezali kokamwisa soki omoni ndenge ezali moke mpi ntina te soki okanisi yango na universe oyo ezali monene koleka mpenza.

src: Child: I can't believe how big space is.
trg: Mwana: Ezali kokamwisa nga ndenge mapata ezali monene mpenza.

src: Mother: It is, but it's also full of amazing things.
trg: Mama: Ezali bongo, kasi etondi mpe na biloko oyo ekamwisaka.

src: I was worried that I might have contracted Lyme disease, but I went to the doctor and he said that I didn't have anything to worry about.
trg: Nazalaki komitungisa ete mbala mosusu nazwi maladi ya Lyme, kasi nakendaki na monganga mpe ayebisaki nga ete nazali na eloko te ya komitungisa mpo na yango.

src: He told me that the rash was probably just a reaction to the tick's saliva.
trg: Ayebisaki nga ete motane eutaki mbala mosusu na soi ya tique.

src: I was relieved to hear that I didn't have Lyme disease, but I was still a little bit concerned about the rash.
trg: Nakitisaki motema na koyoka ete nazalaki te na maladi ya Lyme, kasi nazalaki kaka komitungisa moke mpo na esika ya motane.

src: The doctor told me that it would go away on its own, but it took a few weeks for it to completely disappear.
trg: Monganga ayebisaki nga ete ekosila yango moko, kasi ezwaki mwa mposo mpo esila libela.

src: In the meantime, I tried to keep the rash clean and dry.
trg: Ntango nazali kozela, nazalaki kotika esika ya motane wana peto mpe ya kokauka.

src: I also applied some over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream to help relieve the itching.
trg: Natyaki mpe mafuta ya hydrocorstisone mpo na kolembisa mokusa.

src: The rash was itchy and unsightly, but it didn't cause me any other problems.
trg: Esika ya motane ezalaki mokusa mpe mpasi, kasi ememelaki nga mikakatano mosusu te.

src: I'm just glad that I didn't have Lyme disease.
trg: Nasepeli kaka mpo nabelaki te maladi ya Lyme.

src: If you find a tick attached to your body, it's important to remove it as soon as possible.
trg: Soki omoni tique ekangami na nzoto na yo, ezali ntina kolongola yango kozanga kozela.

src: You can use a pair of tweezers to grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull it straight out.
trg: Okoki kosalela bapense mpo na kokanga tique na pene ya mposo ya nzoto mpe kolongola yango mbala moko.

src: Don't twist or jerk the tick, as this could cause the head to break off and remain in your skin.
trg: Kobalusa te to koningisa yango te, mpo ekoki kosala ete moto na yango elongwa mpe etikala na mposo na yo.

src: Once you've removed the tick, wash the area with soap and water.
trg: Soki olongoli tick, sokola esika wana na sabuni mpe mai.

src: You can also apply a topical antibiotic ointment to help prevent infection.
trg: Okoki mpe kotya mafuta ya antibiotique mpo na kosalisa obela te.

src: It's important to watch for signs of Lyme disease after being bitten by a tick.
trg: Ezali ntina na kolandela bilembo ya maladi ya Lyme nsima wana Lyme eswi yo.

src: These symptoms can include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle aches, and a characteristic rash.
trg: Bilembo yango ekoki kozala fievre, moto mpasi, kolemba, misisa mpasi, mpe kosala na esika ekomi motane.

src: If you develop any of these symptoms, see your doctor right away.
trg: Soki okomi na moko ya bilembo oyo, kotana na monganga kozanga kozela.

src: Lyme disease is a serious illness, but it can be treated with antibiotics.
trg: Maladi ya Lyme ezali maladi ya makasi, kasi bakoki kobikisa yango na ba antibiotique.

src: Early diagnosis and treatment is important to prevent serious complications.
trg: Koluka koyeba maladi noki mpe kozwa lisungi ezali ntina mpo na kokutana te na mikakatano ya makasi.

src: If you have any questions about ticks or Lyme disease, talk to your doctor.
trg: Soki ozali na motuna etali batique to maladi ya Lyme, solola na monganga na yo.

src: Three women are sitting at a table, talking about their cats.
trg: Basi misato bafandi na mesa, bazali kolobela baniawu na bango.

src: Constance: My cat, Sangeetha, is always there to greet me at the door when I come home from work.
trg: Constance: Niawu na nga, Sangeetha, ezalaka ntango nyonso wana mpo na kopesa nga mbote na porte soki nazongi nsima ya mosala.

src: Ayanda: Me too! I have two cats of my own. They make me feel wanted.
trg: Ayanda: Nga mpe! Nazali na baniawu mibale. Basalaka namiyoka nazali na ntina.

src: Constance: I know what you mean. Sangeetha always makes me feel better when I'm having a bad day.
trg: Constance: Nayebi nini olingi koloba. Sangeetha asalaka namiyoka malamu ntango nyonso soki nazali kolekisa mokolo ya mabe.

src: Aditi: I've always wanted a cat, but I'm allergic.
trg: Aditi: Nazalaka ntango nyonso na mposa ya niawu, kasi nazali allergique.

src: Ayanda: That's too bad. Cats are really great companions.
trg: Ayanda: Mawa mpenza. Baniawu bazali baninga ya malamu.

src: Aditi:I know! I've always admired people who have cats. They seem to have such a special bond with their pets.
trg: Aditi: Nayebi! Nalingaka ntango nyonso bato oyo bazali na baniawu. Emonanaka bazalaka na boninga ya makasi na banyama na bango.

src: Constance: I think it's because cats are very independent animals. They don't need you to take care of them every minute of the day.
trg: Constance: Nakanisi ezali mpo baniawu bazali banyama ya kotyela mpenza motema. Bazali te na mposa okipe bango ngonga nyonso na mokolo.

src: But they still love you and enjoy your company.
trg: Kasi bakolinga yo kaka mpe bakosepela kozala na yo.

src: The history of Ethiopia is long and complex, with a rich and varied culture.
trg: Lisolo ya Ethiopie ezali lisolo ya molai mpe ya mindondo, ezali na culture mingi mpe ekeseni.

src: The earliest evidence of human settlement in Ethiopia dates back to the Paleolithic period, with the discovery of stone tools and other artifacts.
trg: Bilembeteli ya kala ya kozala ya bato na Ethiopie ebandi na eleko ya ba Paleolitique, ntango bamonaki bisaleli ya mabanga mpe mayemi mosusu.

src: The first major civilization in Ethiopia was the Aksumite Empire, which flourished from the 1st century BC to the 8th century AD.
trg: Sivilizasio monene oyo ya liboso na Ethiopie ezali neti Bokonzi ya Aksumite, oyo ezalaki makasi banda ekeke ya 1 BC kino na ekeke ya 8 AD.

src: The Aksumites were a powerful trading empire that controlled much of the trade between Africa and the Middle East.
trg: Ba Aksumite ezalaki sivilizasio makasi ya mombongo oyo ezalaki koyangela mombongo mingi kati ya Afrika mpe Moyen Orient.

src: They also built many impressive monuments, including the Great Stelae of Aksum.
trg: Basalaki mpe bamonima ya minene, ata mpe Stelae Monene ya Aksum.

src: After the fall of the Aksumite Empire, Ethiopia was ruled by a series of different kingdoms and dynasties.
trg: Nsima ya kokwea ya Bokonzi ya Aksumite, Ethiopie eyangelamaki na bikonzi mpe badynastie ebele ekeseni.

src: In the 16th century, Ethiopia was invaded by the Ottoman Empire, but the Ethiopians were able to defeat the Ottomans and maintain their independence.
trg: Na ekeke ya 16, Ethiopie ebotolamaki na Bokonzi ya Ottoman, kasi bato ya Ethiopie balongaki ba Ottoman mpe babatelaki lipanda na bango.

src: In the 19th century, Ethiopia was ruled by Emperor Tewodros II, who is considered one of the greatest Ethiopian rulers.
trg: Na ekeke ya 19, Ethiopie eyangelamaki na Mokonzi Tewodros II, oyo bato balobaka azali moko ya bakonzi minene ya Ethiopie.

src: Tewodros II was a strong and ambitious ruler who sought to unite Ethiopia and to modernize the country.
trg: Tewodros II azalaki mokonzi ya makasi oyo azalaki na mposa ya koyangela, alukaki kosangisa Ethiopie mpe kokomisa yango ekolo ya sika.

src: He also fought against European colonialism, and he is remembered for his famous letter to Queen Victoria of England, in which he demanded that she stop interfering in Ethiopian affairs.
trg: Abundisaki mpe bato ya nkanza ya Eropa, mpe bato bakanisaka ye mpo na mokanda ya ekende nsango akomelaki Mokonzi-Mwasi Victoria ya Angletere, kuna asengaki ye na kotika komikotisa na makambo ya Ethiopie.

src: Salesperson: What kind of style are you looking for?
trg: Moteki: Ozali koluka modele ya ndenge nini?

src: Customer: I'm mostly interested in something neutral and understated.
trg: Mosombi: Nazali koluka eloko moko ya neutre mpe ya langi makasi te.

src: Salesperson: We have a few options that might work. This one is made from wool and has a simple geometric pattern.
trg: Moteki: Tozali na mwa maponi oyo ekoki kosimba. Oyo esalemi na laine mpe forme moko ya mindondo te.

src: Customer: I like that. It's perfect for my living room.
trg: Mosombi: Nasepeli na yango. Ebongi mpenza mpo na shambre na nga.

src: Salesperson: Great! I'm happy to help. We can also deliver and install the rug for you if you'd like.
trg: Moteki: Malamu! Nasepeli kosalisa yo. Tokoki mpe koya kotikela yo tapis yango na ndako mpe kotya yango soki olingi.

src: Customer: That would be great. I'm willing to pay a little extra for that.
trg: Mosombi: Ekozala malamu. Nakobakisa mwa mbongo likolo mpo na yango.

src: Salesperson: No problem. We'll get started on that right away.
trg: Moteki: Likambo te. Tokobanda kosala yango kaka sikoyo.

src: Customer: Thank you.
trg: Mosombi: Matondi.

src: Sickness has been a part of human life since the beginning of time.
trg: Bokono ezalaka na kati ya bomoi ya bato banda na ebandeli mpenza.

src: From the common cold to the bubonic plague, countless diseases have ravaged our species, causing pain, suffering, and death.
trg: Banda na fievre kino na maladi ya makwanza, maladi ebele enyokola bato, ememela bango mpasi, minyoko, mpe liwa.

src: But where did these illnesses come from?
trg: Kansi maladi oyo nyonso euta wapi?

src: One popular myth about the origin of sickness is that it was caused by a curse from the gods.
trg: Lisapo moko ya ebandali ya maladi ya bato oyo eyebana mingi ezali ete euta na elakeli mabe ya banzambe.

src: According to this myth, the gods were angered by the behavior of humans, so they sent down a plague to punish them.
trg: Na kotalela lisapo wana, bizaleli mabe ya bato esilikisaki banzambe, yango wana batindaki bampasi mpo enyokola bato.

src: This myth is found in many cultures around the world, and it often features a similar story: the gods are angered by something humans have done, so they send down a plague to teach them a lesson.
trg: Lisapo oyo ezali na baculture ebele na mokili mobimba, mpe mbala mingi ezalaka na lisolo ya ndenge moko: banzambe basilikaki mpo na likambo moko oyo bato basalaki, yango wana batindaki mpasi mpo na kopesa bato liteya.

src: While this myth is certainly a powerful story, there is no evidence to support it.
trg: Atako lisapo oyo ezali mpenza lisolo ya makasi, ezali na elembeteli moko te mpo na kondimisa yango.

src: In fact, most scientists believe that sickness is caused by natural factors, such as bacteria and viruses.
trg: Na koloba solo, bato ebele ya siansi bakanisaka ete maladi euta na biloko ya bozalisi, neti bamikrobe na bavirisi.

src: These pathogens are always present in our environment, and they can cause disease when they enter our bodies.
trg: Biloko mabe oyo ezalaka na biso nyonso oyo tofandaka, mpe ekoki kobelisa biso soki ekoti na nzoto na biso.

src: Of course, the myth of the gods' curse is just one of many stories about the origin of sickness.
trg: Ya solo, lisapo oyo ya elakeli mabe ya banzambe ezali kaka lisolo moko na kati ya masolo ebele oyo elobeli esika maladi euta.

src: There are many other myths and legends that attempt to explain why we get sick.
trg: Ezali na masapo mpe masolo ebele ya kala oyo emekaka kolimbola mpo na nini tobelaka.

src: "I can't believe we're going to be learning how to cook Indian food today," said 10-year-old Priya excitedly.
trg: "Nazali kondima ete tokoyekola ndenge ya kolamba bilei ya Inde lelo," wana maloba ya Priya oyo aza na mibu 10 alobaki na esengo nyonso.

src: She had been looking forward to this day ever since her teacher, Ms. Singh, had announced that they would be doing a unit on different cultures. "I've never had Indian food before," said Priya's friend, Sam. "What's it like?"
trg: Azalaki kozela mokolo oyoo banda molakisi na ye, Madame Singh, alobaki ete bakobanda kozwa liteya etali bonkoko ya bato mosusu. "Nazwa nanu te bilei ya Inde," wana maloba ya Sam, moninga ya Priya. "Ezalaka ndenge nini?"

src: "It's delicious," said Priya "It's usually very flavorful, with a lot of spices. And there are so many different dishes to choose from."
trg: "Ezali elengi," ndenge Priya alobaki "Ezalaka ntango nyonso kitoko mingi, na biloko ebele ekomisaka biloko elengi. Ezali na bilei ebele ekeseni oyo okoki kopona kati na yango."

src: The class arrived at the kitchen, and Ms. Singh began to set up.
trg: Bana-kelasi bayaki na kikuku, kasi Madame Singh abandaki kobongisa biloko.

src: "Today, we're going to be making a simple dish called dal makhani," she said.
trg: "Lelo, tokolamba bilei ya pete babengi dal makhani," ndenge alobaki.

src: "It's a type of lentil soup that's very popular in India."
trg: "Ezali lolenge moko ya madesu oyo eyebana mingi na Inde."

src: Ms. Singh showed the class how to measure out the ingredients and cook the lentils.
trg: Madame Singh alakisaki bana-kelasi ndenge ya komeka biloko ya kotya na kati mpe kolamba madesu.

src: The students helped each other chop vegetables and stir the pot.
trg: Bana-kelasi basalisanaki na kokata bandunda mpe kobalusa nzungu.

src: As they worked, they chatted about their favorite foods and what they were looking forward to trying in India.
trg: Ntango bazalaki kosala, bazalaki kolobela bilei balingaka mingi mpe oyo bazalaki kozela komeka na Inde.

src: When the dal makhani was finished, the students sat down to eat.
trg: Ntango dal makhani esilaki kolambama, bana-kelasi bafandaka mpo na kolya.

src: My favorite season is the one in which all is green, the trees are in full bloom, and the birds are singing.
trg: Eleko nalingaka mingi ezalaka ntango biloko nyonso ezalaka vert, banzete etondi na nkasa, mpe bandeke bazali koyemba.

src: It is a time of new beginnings, as the world wakes up from its winter slumber and begins to grow and change.
trg: Ezali ntango ya ebandeli ya sika, ntango mokili elamukaka na mpongi ya hiver mpe ebandaka kokola mpe kobongwana.

src: I love to spend this time outdoors, enjoying the fresh air and sunshine.
trg: Nasepelaka kolekisa eleko oyo libanda, kosepela na mopepe ya kitoko mpe moi.

src: There is nothing quite like taking a walk in the woods on a spring day, breathing in the scent of the flowers and listening to the birdsong.
trg: Ezali na eloko moko te ekokani na kotambola na zamba na mokolo ya printemps, koyoka nsolo ya bafololo mpe koyoka loyembo ya bandeke.

src: It is a time of hope and renewal, and I always feel invigorated by it.
trg: Ezali ntango ya elikya mpe ya kobandela, mpe namonaka ntango oyo ete elendisaka nga.

src: The days are getting longer and the nights are getting shorter, and the sun is shining brighter.
trg: Moyi ekomaka molai mpe babutu ekomaka mokuse, mpe moi engengaka makasi.

src: The flowers are blooming and the trees are budding, and the air is filled with the sound of birdsong.
trg: Bafololo ezali kobota mpe banzete ezobimisa matiti, mpe mopepe etondi na loyembo ya bandeke.

src: The world is coming alive again after a long winter's sleep, and it is a beautiful sight to behold.
trg: Mokili ezali kozonga lisusu na bomoi nsima ya mpongi molai ya hiver, mpe ezali kitoko na kotala yango.

src: Spring is a time of new beginnings, and I am always excited to see what the new season will bring.
trg: Printemps ezali ntango ya ebandeli ya sika, mpe nazalaka ntango nyonso na esengo ya komona biloko eleko ya sika ekomema.

src: I love to watch the plants grow and change, and I enjoy seeing the animals come out and play.
trg: Nasepelaka kotala banzete ezali kokola mpe kobongwana, mpe nasepelaka kotala banyama ezali kobima mpe kosakana.

src: Spring is a time of hope and renewal, and I always feel invigorated by it.
trg: Printemps eza eleko ya elikya mpe ya makambo ya sika, mpe namonaka ete elendisaka nga ntango nyonso.

src: The assassination of Mohamed Bouazizi was a major turning point in the Tunisian Revolution.
trg: Kobomama ya Mohamed Bouazizi ezalaki mbongwana makasi na Botomboki ya Tunisie.

src: Bouazizi was a 26-year-old street vendor who set himself on fire in December 2010 in protest of police harassment and corruption.
trg: Bouazizi azalaki elenge ya mibu 26 oyo azalaki koteka na balabala, oyo amibimisaki na sanza ya zomi 2010 mpo na kotombokela minyokoli ya bapolisi mpe ndenge bazwaka kanyaka.

src: His death sparked a wave of protests across Tunisia that eventually led to the overthrow of President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali.
trg: Liwa na ye ebimisaki botomboki ebele na Tunisie oyo nsukansuka esalaki ete balongola Prezida Zine El Abidine Ben Ali na bokonzi.

src: Bouazizi's death was widely seen as a symbol of the Tunisian people's frustration with the government's economic policies and its authoritarian rule.
trg: Liwa ya Bouazizi emonanaki bisika mingi lokola elembo ya bampasi ya bato ya Tunisie na malako ya ekonomi ya guvernema mpe bokonzi na yango ya nkanza.

src: The protests that followed his death were met with violent repression by the government, but they ultimately succeeded in toppling Ben Ali.
trg: Botomboki oyo ebimaki nsima ya liwa na ye esanganaki na mobulu makasi ya boyangeli, kasi nsukansuka balongoki na kokweisa Ben Ali.

src: The Tunisian Revolution was a major turning point in the Arab world.
trg: Botomboki ya Tunisie ezalaki mbongwana monene na mikili ya ba Arabe.

src: It inspired other uprisings in the region, and it led to the overthrow of several authoritarian regimes.
trg: Epusaka bamboka mosusu ya eteni wana na kotomboka, mpe esalaki bikonzi mingi ya nkanza ekwea.

src: The revolution also had a significant impact on Tunisian society.
trg: Botomboki wana ezalaki mpe na bopusi makasi na ekolo Tunisie.

src: It led to the adoption of a new constitution, and it ushered in a new era of democracy and freedom.
trg: Esalaki ete babimisi mobeko-mokonzi ya sika, mpe ememaki na eleko ya sika ya demokrasi mpe lipanda.

src: Bouazizi's death is a reminder of the importance of human rights and the need for political change.
trg: Liwa ya Bouazizi ezali ekundolaka motuya ya balotomo ya bato mpe mposa ya mbongwana ya politiki.

src: His sacrifice helped to bring about a more just and democratic Tunisia.
trg: Mbeka na ye esalisaki na kozala na Tunisie ya boyengebene mingi mpe ya demokrasi.

src: Gift-giving is an important part of Chinese culture, and there are many different rules and customs to follow.
trg: Kopesa bakado ezali eteni ya ntina ya bonkoko ya Chine, mpe ezali na mibeko mpe malako ebele oyo esengeli kotosa.

src: Whenever you are invited to a Chinese person's home, it is customary to bring a gift.
trg: Soki babengisi yo na ndako moko ya moto ya Chine, bazalaka na ezaleli ya komema kado.

src: The type of gift you bring will depend on the occasion and the relationship you have with the host.
trg: Lolenge ya kado okomema ekoyokana na evenema mpe boyokani na yo na moto abengisi yo.

src: For example, if you are attending a birthday party, you might bring a gift of flowers or fruit.
trg: Na ndakisa, soki ozali kokende na feti ya aniversere ya mbotama, okoki komema kado ya bafololo to mbuma.

src: If you are visiting a friend's home, you might bring a small gift, such as a bottle of wine or a box of chocolates.
trg: Soki okei kotala moninga na ndako, okoki komema kado ya moke, neti molangi ya vinyo to liboke ya bachocolat.

src: It is important to wrap the gift nicely and to present it with both hands.
trg: Ezali ntina kozipa kado yango kitoko mpe kopesa yango na maboko nyonso mibale.

src: When you receive a gift, it is customary to open it immediately and to express your appreciation.
trg: Soki ozwi kado moko, bazalaka na ezaleli ya kofungola yango kozanga kozela mpe komonisa botondi.

src: You should also reciprocate by giving a gift of equal value whenever you are invited to someone's home.
trg: Osengeli mpe komema kado ya motuya ndenge moko mbala nyonso oyo babengisi yo na ndako ya moto moko.

src: If you are unsure of what to give, you can always ask a friend or family member for advice.
trg: Soki oyebi te kado ya kopesa, okoki ntango nyonso kosenga toli epai ya moninga to moto ya libota.

src: The young woman held her hand out to the man, her eyes pleading.
trg: Elenge mwasi apesaki loboko epai ya mobali wana, miso ya elenge mwasi ezobondela.

src: "Please," she said. "I need your help."
trg: "Palado," ndenge alobaki. "Nazali na mposa ya lisungi na yo."

src: The man looked at her, his expression hard.
trg: Mobali atalaki ye, elongi na ye ekanga.

src: "I don't know what you're talking about," he said.
trg: "Nayebi te makambo ozali koloba," wana maloba ya mobali yango.

src: "I'm from Toronto," she said. "I was kidnapped and brought here.
trg: "Nauta na Toronto," wana maloba ya elenge. "Bakanga nga na makasi mpe bamema nga awa.

src: I need to get back home."
trg: Nazolinga kozonga."

src: The man shook his head. "Get out of here before I call the police."
trg: Mobali aningisaki moto. "Longwa awa liboso nabenga polisi."

src: The woman's heart sank.
trg: Motema ya mwasi wana elembaki.

src: She was so close, but it looked like she was going to be caught again.
trg: Azalaki pene mpenza, kasi emonanaki neti bakokanga ye lisusu.

src: She turned to run, but the man grabbed her arm. "I said get out of here!" he shouted.
trg: Abalukaki mpo na kokima mbango, kais mobali wana akangaki ye na loboko. Agangaki ete "Nayebisaki yo longwa awa!"

src: The woman struggled, but the man was too strong.
trg: Mwasi abundaki, kasi mobali azalaki makasi mingi.

src: He pulled her close and slapped her across the face.
trg: Abendaki mwasi pene mpe abetaki mbata na elongi.

src: "You're not going anywhere," he said. "You're my property now." The woman cried out in pain and fear.
trg: "Okokende esika moko te," wana maloba ya mobali. "Ozali sikoyo eloko na nga." Mwasi wana alelaki na mpasi mpe na bobangi.

src: She didn't know what to do.
trg: Ayebaki te nini akosala.

src: She was trapped.
trg: Akangamaka na motambu.

src: Action films have undergone a major transformation in recent years.
trg: Bafilme ya action esala mbongwana ya monene na mibu euti koleka.

src: Gone are the days of simple, one-dimensional heroes and villains.
trg: Mikolo ya ba heros mpe ya bato mabe ya pete mpe ya kokamwa makasi esila.

src: Today's action films are more complex, with characters who undergo significant transformations over the course of the film.
trg: Bafilme ya action ya lelo ekoma mindondo, na bato oyo babongwanaka makasi na boumeli ya filme.

src: This transformation is often a reflection of the film's themes, which can range from the importance of family to the power of love.
trg: Mbongwana oyo emonisaka mbala mingi mito ya likambo ya filme, oyo ekoki ebandi na ntina ya libota kino na bokasi ya bolingo.

src: Several recent action films have featured this type of transformation.
trg: Bafilme ya action ebele ya kala mingi te ezalaki na mbongwana ya lolenge oyo.

src: In the film "The Batman," for example, the title character goes from being a vengeful vigilante to a symbol of hope for the city of Gotham.
trg: Na filme "The Batman," na ndakisa, moto ya moke abandi na moto azongisaka mabe mpe akomi elembo ya elikya mpo na engumba ya Gotham.

src: In "Black Panther," T'Challa must learn to embrace his role as king of Wakanda, even though it means giving up some of his personal freedoms.
trg: Na "Black Panther," T'Challa asengeli koyekola kokokisa mokumba na ye ya mokonzi ya Wakanda, atako ezali kosenga kotika ndambo ya bonsomi na ye moko.

src: And in "Captain Marvel," Carol Danvers must learn to control her powers and use them for good.
trg: Mpe na "Captain Marvel," Carol Danvers asengeli koyekola koyangela bokonzi na ye mpe kosalela yango malamu.

src: These films show that action films can be more than just mindless violence.
trg: Bafilme oyo ezali kolakisa ete bafilme ya action ekoki kozala kaka te mobulu ezangi makanisi.

src: They can also be used to explore complex themes and characters.
trg: Bakoki kosalela yango mpe mpo na kolandela mito ya makambo mpe bato ya mindondo.

src: The debate of man vs. machine is a long-standing one, with no easy answer.
trg: Kowelana kati ya moto na mashini eza ya kala mpe ezanga eyano ya pete.

src: On the one hand, machines are becoming increasingly sophisticated and capable, and they are already performing many tasks that were once thought to be the exclusive domain of humans.
trg: Na ngambo moko, bamashini ezali kokoba kokoma mindondo makasi mpe na makoki, mpe ezali kosala misala ebele oyo tozalaki kokanisi nanu ete bato mpamba nde bakoki kosala.

src: On the other hand, humans have a unique set of skills and abilities that machines are unlikely to ever replicate, such as creativity, empathy, and intuition.
trg: Na ngambo mosusu, bato bazalaki na mayele mpe makoki ya bango moko yo bamashini ekoki ata moke te kozala na yango, neti kokela, komitya na esika ya moto, mpe kosala eloko kozanga kokanisa.

src: One of the key areas where machines are rapidly outpacing humans is in the field of artificial intelligence (AI).
trg: Esika moko ya ntina oyo bamashini ezali mpenza koleka bato ezali na makambo ya intelligence artificielle (AI).

src: AI is a branch of computer science that deals with the creation of intelligent agents, which are systems that can reason, learn, and act autonomously.
trg: AI ezali eteni ya siansi ya ordinatere oyo etalaka makambo ya kokela biloko ya mayele, oyo ezali basisteme oyo ekoki kokanisa, koyekola, mpe kosala yango moko.

src: AI is already being used in a wide range of applications, from self-driving cars to medical diagnosis.
trg: AI esili kobanda kosalelama na ba application ebele, banda na mituka oyo ezokumbama yango moko kino na kokanga bato maladi.

src: And as AI continues to develop, it is likely to become even more powerful and capable.
trg: Mpe ndenge AI ezokoba kokola, emonani ete ekokoma makasi mpe na makoki mingi koleka.

src: However, there are also a number of areas where humans are likely to retain a significant advantage over machines.
trg: Atako bongo, ezali mpe na badomene ebele oyo bato bakokoba koleka na mosika bamashini.

src: For example, humans are much better at dealing with ambiguity and uncertainty.
trg: Na ndakisa, bato bazali na makoki ya malamu ya kobunda na makambo ya mpasi mpe oyo eyebani te.

src: We can also draw on our experience and intuition to make decisions in complex situations.
trg: Tokoki kosalela makambo tokutana na yango mpe mayele tobotama na yango mpo na kozwa bikateli na makkambo ya mpasi.

src: And finally, humans have a unique capacity for creativity and innovation.
trg: Mpe na nsuka, bato mpamba bazali na makoki ya kokela mpe kosala biloko ya sika.

src: Two men, one in his 30s and one in his 50s, are sitting at the bar, drinking.
trg: Mibali mibale, moko ya mibu 30 na ndambo mpe mosusu ya mibu 50 na ndambo, bafandi na bare, bazali komela.

src: Young Man: So, I heard that the new head of the liquor board is really cracking down on local stores.
trg: Elenge Mobali: Ebongo, nayoki ete mokambi ya sika ya makambo ya masanga ya makasi azali kozwa bikateli ya makasi mpo na bamagazin ya kartie.

src: Old Man: Yeah, I heard that too. They're saying that he's going to be doing random inspections of bars and restaurants to make sure that they're not selling liquor to minors.
trg: Mobange: Iyo, nayokaki yango mpe. Balobaki ete bakokende kotala babare na malewa kaka bongo mpo na koyeba soki bazali kotekela te bilenge masanga ya makasi.

src: Young Man: That's a good thing.
trg: Elenge Mobali: Ezali likambo ya malamu.

src: I mean, it's not fair to the responsible businesses that are following the rules when some other places are just selling liquor to anyone who walks in the door.
trg: Nalingi koloba, ezali malamu te mpo na bakambi ya mimbongo oyo bazali kotosa mibeko ntango bisika mosusu ezali kaka koteka masanga ya makasi na bato nyonso oyo bazali koya epai na bango.

src: Old Man: I agree. But I'm also worried about how it's going to affect my business.
trg: Mobange: Nandimi. Kasi nazali mpe komitungisa na bopusi oyo ekozala na yango na mombongo na nga.

src: I mean, I'm a good guy. I don't sell liquor to minors.
trg: Nalingi koloba, nazali moto malamu. Natekelaka te bilenge masanga ya makasi.

src: But I'm also not going to let some government bureaucrat tell me who I can and can't sell liquor to.
trg: Kasi nakoki mpe te kotikela bato ya guvernema oyo bazalaka kaka na biro bayebisa nga nani nakoki mpe nani nakoki te kotekela masanga ya makasi.

src: Young Man: I get what you're saying. But you have to be careful.
trg: Elenge mobali: Nakangi ntina ya oyo ozali koloba. Kasi osengeli kokeba.

src: Family planning in India has been a topic of debate for many years.
trg: Kobongisa libota na Inde ezali likambo oyo bazolobela banda mibu ebele.

src: In 1976, the Indian government passed the controversial National Emergency Act, which imposed a forced sterilization program on men and women.
trg: Na 1976, guvernema ya Inde ebimisaki Mobeko urgence ya Ekolo mobimba oyo bato batelemelaki, oyo ekotisaki na makasi programe ya kokanga mabota na mibali mpe basi.

src: This program was met with widespread resistance and eventually overturned by the Indian Supreme Court.
trg: Bato ebele batelemelaki programe oyo mpe nsukansuka Tribinale Monene ya Inde elongolaki mobeko yango.

src: In recent years, the Indian government has taken a more progressive approach to family planning.
trg: Na mibu euti koleka, guvernema ya Inde ekamataki mwa metode ya mwa malamu etali kobongisa libota.

src: In 2010, the government launched the National Family Planning Program, which provides free contraception and sterilization services to all Indian citizens.
trg: Na 2010, guvernema ebandisaki Programe ya Ekolo Mobimba ya Kobongisa Libota, oyo ezalaki kopesa misala ya ofele ya kokanga mabota mpe kokoma ekomba na bato nyonso ya Inde.

src: The program has been successful in reducing the fertility rate in India, but it still faces challenges, such as a lack of awareness and access to services.
trg: Mobeko yango elonga na kokitisa motango ya mabota na Inde, kasi ezali kaka kokutana na mikakatano, neti bato mosusu bayebi yango te mpe bakoki kozwa misala wana te.

src: One of the most important challenges to family planning in India is the lack of awareness about the benefits of family planning.
trg: Mokakatano moko ya makasi oyo kobongisa mabota na Inde ezokutana na yanog ezali ndenge bato bayebi te matomba ya kobongisa mabota.

src: Many Indian couples believe that it is their duty to have as many children as possible.
trg: Babalani ebele ya Inde bakanisaka ete bazali na mokumba ya kozala na motango ya bana oyo balingi.

src: This belief is often reinforced by cultural and religious norms.
trg: Likanisi oyo elendisamaka na mibeko ya bonkoko mpe ya losambo.

src: Another challenge to family planning is the lack of access to services.
trg: Mokakatano mosusu oyo kobongisa libota ekutani na yango ezali kozanga kozwa misala.

src: In rural areas, there are often few or no family planning clinics.
trg: Na bamboka, ezalaka te na balopitalo oyo esalisaka na kobongisa mabota to ezalaka moke.

src: This makes it difficult for couples to access the services they need.
trg: Esalaka ete ezala mpasi na babalani na kozwa misala oyo balingi.

src: Despite these challenges, the Indian government is committed to providing family planning services to all its citizens.
trg: Atako mikakatano oyo ezali, guvernema ya Inde emipesi na kopesa misala ya kobongisa mabota na bato nyonso ya Inde.

src: Science is a systematic enterprise that builds and organizes knowledge in the form of testable explanations and predictions about the natural world.
trg: Siansi ezali kompani oyo esalaka mpe ebongisaka mayele na lolenge ya bandimbola oyo bakoki komeka mpe makanisi etali biloko nzambe akela.

src: In its broadest sense, science encompasses all human knowledge and activity motivated by a desire to understand the natural world and its phenomena.
trg: Na ndenge elobelaka makambo, siansi elobelaka mayele mpe misala nyonso ya bato oyo epusami na mposa ya koyeba biloko nzambe akela mpe bafenomene na yango.

src: Science is also often seen as a particular body of knowledge derived from such investigation, as well as a method of discovery.
trg: Mbala mingi bato bamonaka siansi lokola lisanga ya mayele oyo euti na kolandela, mpe metode ya koyeba makambo.

src: The earliest roots of science can be traced to Ancient Greek philosophy, particularly the works of Aristotle, who attempted to explain natural phenomena through observation and reason.
trg: Misisa ya kala ya siansi ekoki komonana na filozofi ya Grese ya Kala, mingimingi na misala ya Aristote, oyo amekaki kolimbola fenomene ya bozalisii na nzela ya kotala mpe kokanisa.

src: Over the centuries, science has developed into a more rigorous discipline, with the development of the scientific method, which emphasizes evidence, hypothesis testing, and repeatability.
trg: Na nsima ya bamvula, siansi ekola mpe ekoma disipline ya makasi, basala metode ya siansi, oyo ebendaka likebi na bilembeteli, komeka makanisi, mpe kozongela yango.

src: Science has had a profound impact on human society, leading to the development of new technologies, medicines, and understanding of the natural world.
trg: Siansi ezala na bopusi makasi na bomoi ya bato, emema bango na kosala bateknolozi ya sika, kimonganga, mpe koyeba biloko ya bozalisi.

src: It has also played a role in shaping social and political thought.
trg: Ezala mpe na mosala makasi na kobongisa makanisi ya sociale mpe ya politiki.

src: Today, science is a major part of modern life, and it continues to play an important role in the advancement of knowledge and understanding.
trg: Lelo, siansi ezali eteni monene ya bomoi ya mikolo oyo, mpe ezali kokoba kozala na mokumba makasi na bokoli ya mayele mpe ya boyebi.

src: A: I'm so behind on my work!
trg: A: Nazali na retard makasi na devware na nga!

src: I have a paper due tomorrow, and I haven't even started it.
trg: Nazali na devware ya kozongisa lobi, mpe nabandi yango nkutu te.

src: B: Oh no! What are you going to do?
trg: B: Oh te! Okosala nini?

src: A: I don't know.
trg: A: Nayebi te.

src: I guess I'll just have to stay up all night and finish it.
trg: Nakanisi esengeli nalala te butu mobimba mpo na kosilisa yango.

src: B: That sounds like a terrible idea.
trg: B: Emonani neti ezali likansi ya mabe.

src: You'll just end up being more tired and stressed, and you won't do your best work.
trg: Nsukansuka okozala ya kolemba makasi mpe na basusi, mpe okosala mosala malamu te.

src: A: I know, but I don't have any other choice.
trg: A: Nayebi, kasi nazali na eloko mosusu ya kosala te.

src: B: There is always another choice.
trg: B: Liponi mosusu ezalaka ntango nyonso.

src: You could start working on it now, and take breaks throughout the day.
trg: Okoki kobanda kosala yango sikoyo, mpe kopema moke mokolo mobimba.

src: Or, you could ask for an extension from your professor.
trg: To, okoko kosenga molakisi abakisela yo mikolo.

src: A: I don't know if I can ask for an extension.
trg: A: Nayebi te soki nakoki kosenga abakisela nga mikolo.

src: I've already asked for one this semester, and I don't want to seem like I'm not taking my classes seriously.
trg: Nasilaki koseka moko na semestre oyo, mpe nalingi te emonana neti nazali kozwa kelasi na liseki.

src: B: Well, you have to do something.
trg: B: Malamu, osengeli kosala eloko.

src: You can't just keep procrastinating.
trg: Okoki te kaka kozongisa makambo nsima.

src: You're going to end up failing your class.
trg: Nsukansuka okolonga te na kelasi.

src: The year is 1920, and the place is New York City.
trg: Tozali na mobu 1920, mpe esika ezali engumba New York.

src: The flapper era is in full swing, and young women are enjoying their newfound freedom.
trg: Eleko ya bilenge basi ezali mpenza na ngala, mpe bilenge basi bazali kosepela na bonsomi na bango ya sika.

src: They are dressing in short skirts and bobbed hair, smoking cigarettes, and drinking cocktails.
trg: Bazali kolata bajupe ya mikuse mpe kokata bansuki ya mikuse, bazali komela makaya, mpe komela masanga.

src: They are also dating more freely than ever before.
trg: Bazali mpe kobima ndenge balingi koleka na kala.

src: One such flapper is named Josephine.
trg: Nkombo ya moko ya bilenge wana ezali Josephine.

src: She is a beautiful young woman with a sharp wit and a rebellious streak.
trg: Azali elenge mwasi ya kitoko oyo azali kokanisi noki mpe azali mwa motomboki.

src: She is not interested in finding a husband, but she does enjoy the attention of men.
trg: Azali na mposa ya koluka mobali ya kobala, kasi azali kosepela mibali batyela ye likebi.

src: One day, Josephine is at a party when she meets a young man named Jack.
trg: Mokolo moko, Josephine azali na feti ebongo akutani na elenge mobali moko nkombo na ye Jack.

src: Jack is everything that Josephine is not.
trg: Jack akeseni makasi mpenza na Josephine.

src: He is conservative, polite, and serious.
trg: Alobaki mingi te, azali botosi, mpe serieux.

src: But there is something about him that Josephine finds attractive.
trg: Kasi ezali na eloko moko epai na ye oyo ezali kobenda Josephine.

src: Jack and Josephine begin dating, and they quickly fall in love.
trg: Jack na Josephine babandi kobima elongo, mpe baumeli te kolingana.

src: They spend their days dancing at the bars and their nights talking for hours on end.
trg: Bazali kolekisa mikolo na bango na kobina na babare mpe babutu na bango na kosolola kozanga nsuka.

src: Josephine has never felt this way about anyone before.
trg: Josephine amiyoka nanu te bongo lolenge mpo na moto ata moko.

src: But Jack is not the only man in Josephine's life.
trg: Kasi Jack azali mobali moko mpamba te na bomoi ya Josephine.

src: She is still friends with her former boyfriend, Tom.
trg: Azali kaka moninga na makangu na ye ya kala, Tom.

src: Tom is a good man, and he loves Josephine very much.
trg: Tom azali mobali malamu, mpe alingaka Josephine mingi mpenza.

src: Egypt faces a number of challenges, including:
trg: Ezipito ezali kokutana na mikatano ebele, neti:

src: * A rapidly growing population. Egypt's population is expected to grow from 100 million today to 140 million by 2050.
trg: * Bato bazali kokoma ebele noki. Bato bazali kokanisa ete bato ya Ezipito bakolongwa na bamilio 100 oyo bazali lelo mpe bakokoma bamilio 140 na 2050.

src: This will put a strain on the country's resources, including its food supply, water supply, and infrastructure.
trg: Ekotya mokakatano na biloko oyo mboka ezali na yango, ata mpe bilei, masi mpe bandako.

src: * A widening gap between the rich and the poor. Egypt has a high Gini coefficient, which measures inequality.
trg: * Bokeseni ya makasi mpenza na kati ya bazwi mpe babola. Ezipito ezali na coéfficient Gini ya makasi, oyo emekaka bokeseni.

src: This means that the wealth is concentrated in the hands of a few, while the majority of the population lives in poverty.
trg: Elakisi ete bozwi esimbami kaka na bato moke, kasi bato ebele bazali na bango babola.

src: * High unemployment. Egypt's unemployment rate is around 12%.
trg: * Bato ebele bazangi mosala. Taux ya kozanga mosala na Ezipito ezali pene ya 12%.

src: This is especially high among young people.
trg: Ezali makasi mingi epai ya bilenge.

src: * A lack of economic opportunity. Egypt's economy is heavily reliant on tourism and agriculture.
trg: * Kozanga mabaku ya ekonomi. Ekonomi ya Ezipito esimbami makasi na tourisme mpe mosala ya bilanga.

src: These sectors are vulnerable to external shocks, such as the global financial crisis and the Arab Spring.
trg: Misala oyo ezali na mikakano euti na libanda, na ndakisa mpasi ya mbongo na mokili mobimba mpe printemps ya mikili ya Arabe.

src: * Political instability. Egypt has experienced a number of political upheavals in recent years, including the overthrow of Hosni Mubarak in 2011 and the subsequent military coup in 2013.
trg: * Nkokoso ya makambo ya politiki. Ezipito ekutanaki na mikakatano mingi ya politiki na mibu euti koleka, neti kokweisa of Hosni Mubarak na 2011 mpe coup d'état ya basoda oyo esalemaki na 2013.

src: This instability has made it difficult for the government to implement reforms and improve the economy.
trg: Mbutumbutu oyo esalaki ete ezala mpasi mpo guvernema esala mbongwana mpe ebongisa ekonomi.

src: Vehicle repair and maintenance is essential for keeping your car in good condition and preventing costly repairs down the road.
trg: Kobongisa motua mpe kosala maintenance na yango ezali ntina mingi mpo motuka ezala malamu mpe kokanga nzela ya kosala te badepanse ya makasi ya kobongisa yango na nzela.

src: There are a number of things you can do to maintain your vehicle, such as changing the oil and filters regularly, checking the tire pressure, and keeping the fluids topped up.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo okoki kosala mpo na kobatela motuka na yo, neti kobongola mafuta na bafiltre mbala na mbala, kotalaka mupepe ya bapneu, mpe kosala ete mafuta esila te.

src: If you're not comfortable doing these things yourself, you can take your car to a qualified mechanic.
trg: Soki oyebi malamu te kosala makambo oyo, okoki komema motuka na yo na mekanisie ayebi mosala.

src: When it comes to vehicle repair, there are a number of different paths you can take.
trg: Na oyo etali kobongisa motuka, ezali na banzela ebele oyo okoki kokamata.

src: You can go to a dealership, an independent repair shop, or a chain repair shop.
trg: Okoki kokende na kompani ya kobongisa mituka, na butiki ya lipanda ya kobongisa mitukba, to na molongo ya babutiki ya kobongisa mituka.

src: Each type of shop has its own advantages and disadvantages.
trg: Lolenge nyonso ya butiki eza na matomba mpe makambo na yango ya mabe.

src: Dealerships typically have the most experience working on specific makes and models of cars, but they can also be more expensive than other options.
trg: Bakompani ezalaka na mayele ya makasi ya kosala misala na mituka ya ndenge na ndenge, kasi bakoki mpe kosenga mbongo ebele koleka maponi misusu.

src: Independent repair shops are often less expensive than dealerships, but they may not have the same level of expertise.
trg: Babutiki ya lipanda ya kobongisa mituka ezalaka mbala mingi ntalo moke koleka bakompani, kasi bazali te na mayele ya mosala ya ndenge moko.

src: Chain repair shops typically offer a middle ground between dealerships and independent repair shops, with competitive prices and a variety of services.
trg: Molongo ya babutiki ya kobongisa mituka ezalaka na katikati ya bakompani mpe babutki ya lipanda ya kobongisa mituka, ezalaka na bantalo ya malmu mpe misala ekeseni.

src: No matter which path you choose, it's important to find a reputable shop that you can trust.
trg: Ata oponi nzela nini, ezali ntina koluka butiki eyebana oyo okoki kotyela motema.

src: You can do this by asking for recommendations from friends or family, or by doing some online research.
trg: Okoki kosala yango na kotunaka makanisi na baninga to bato ya libota, to na kosalaka mwa bolukiluki na internet.

src: [A group of people are gathered in a large room. They are all wearing white robes and have their heads bowed.]
trg: [Etuluku moko ya bato bayangani na ndako moko ya monene. Bango nyonso balati barobe ya mpembe mpe bakitisi mitu na nse.]

src: [A man in a black robe walks up to the front of the room.]
trg: [Mobali moko na robe ya moindo atelemi, akei na liboso ya ndako.]

src: Man: "We are gathered here today to exercise our right to free speech.
trg: Mobali: "Toyangani awa lelo mpo na kosalalela lotomo na biso ya bonsomi ya koloba.

src: We are here to protest the injustice that is being done to our people.
trg: Tozali awa mpo na kotelemela kozanga boyengebene oyo bazosalela bato na biso.

src: We are here to demand that our voices be heard.
trg: Tozali awa mpo na kosenga ete bayoka biso.

src: [The people raise their heads and look at the man.]
trg: [Bato batomboli mito mpe batali mobali yango.]

src: Man: "We are not here to cause violence.
trg: Mobali: "Tozali te awa mpo na kosala mobulu.

src: We are not here to destroy property.
trg: Tozali te awa mpo na kobebisa biloko.

src: We are here to exercise our right to be heard.
trg: Tozali awa mpo na kosalela lotomo na biso ete bayoka biso.

src: [The people begin to chant, "We want to be heard! We want to be heard!"]
trg: [Bato babandi koyemba, "Tolingi bayoka biso! Tolingi bayoka biso!"]

src: Man: "We will not be silenced! We will not be ignored! We will not be denied our rights!
trg: Mobali: "Tokofanda kimya te! Tokolinga te bamona biso mpamba! Bakopekisa biso balotomo na biso te!

src: [The people continue to chant.]
trg: [Bato bazali kokoba koyemba.]

src: Man: "We are the people! We are the future! We will not give up!
trg: Mobali: "Tozali bato! Tozali avenire! Tokotika te!

src: The museum was a treasure trove of history, artifacts, and stories.
trg: Mize ezalaki eloko ya motuya ya lisitwale, misala ya ntoki, mpe ya masolo.

src: From the ancient Egyptian mummies to the modern-day paintings, there was something for everyone to enjoy.
trg: Banda na bamomi ya Ezipito ya kala kino na ba peinture ya mikolo na biso, ezalaki eloko oyo moto nyonso akosepela na yango.

src: One of the most interesting exhibits was the collection of old toys.
trg: Eloko moko ya ntina mingi na exhibition ezalaki libeko ya biloko ya kosakana ya ntango ya kala.

src: There were dolls from the Victorian era, toy soldiers from the Civil War, and even a set of wooden blocks from the early 1900s.
trg: Ezalaki na bana ya popi ya eleko ya Victoria, biloko ya kosakana ya basoda euti na Bitumba ya Sivile, mpe ata liboke ya mabaya ya ebandeli ya mibu 1900.

src: Each toy had its own story to tell, and it was fascinating to see how they had changed over time.
trg: Eloko nyonso ya kosakana ezalaki na lisolo na yango, mpe ezalaki esengo na komona ndenge ebongwanaki nsima ya bambula.

src: One of the toys that caught my eye was a small wooden car.
trg: Moko ya biloko ya kosakana oyo ebendaki likebi na nga ezali motuka moke ya mabaya.

src: It was made in the 1950s, and it was in perfect condition.
trg: Esalemaki na mibu 1950, mpe ezali nanu kaka malamu.

src: The paint was still bright, and the wheels were still smooth.
trg: Langi ezalaki kaka makasi, mpe baroue ezalaki kitoko.

src: I picked it up and examined it closely.
trg: Nakamataki yango mpe natalaki yango malamumalamu.

src: It was a simple toy, but it was also very well-made.
trg: Ezalaki eloko ya kosakana ya pete, kasi esalemaki malamu mpenza.

src: I wondered who had played with this car all those years ago.
trg: Namitunaki banani asakanaki na motuka oyo na mibu nyonso oyo eleka.

src: What were their dreams and aspirations?
trg: Bandoto mpe makanisi na bango ezalaki nini?

src: What did they think the future held?
trg: Bazalaki kokanisa ete nini ekosalema na mikolo ezali koya?

src: I put the car back in its display case and continued on my way.
trg: Nazongisaki motuka wana esika batyaki yango mpe nakobaka nzela na nga.

src: As I walked through the museum, I thought about all the things that had changed in the world since these toys were made.
trg: Ntango nazalaki kotambola na mize, nakanisaki biloko nyonso oyo ebongwana na mokili banda basala biloko wana ya kosakana.

src: Islam is a religion that emphasizes surrender to the will of God.
trg: Mizilma ezali lingomba oyo ebetaka sete na komipesa na mokano ya Nzambe.

src: This concept of surrender, or "Islam" in Arabic, is often misunderstood as meaning submission or defeat.
trg: Likanisi oyo ya komipesa, to "Islam" na lokota ya Arabe, bato bakangaka ntina na yo malamu te mbala mingi bakanisaka ezali komitika to kolonga te.

src: However, in Islam, surrender is actually seen as a positive act, a way to achieve peace and happiness.
trg: Atako bongo, na Islam, komipesa emonanaka mbala mingi lokola likambo ya malamu, lolenge ya kokokisa kimya mpe bolamu.

src: When a Muslim surrenders to God, they are not giving up their own free will.
trg: Soki Mizilma moko amipesi na Nzambe, atikaka te bonsomi na ye moko ya kopona.

src: Rather, they are acknowledging that God is the one who has the power to control all things, and that by surrendering to His will, they are actually finding true freedom.
trg: Kasi, andimaka ete Nzambe nde moto azali na nguya ya kokamba makambo nyonso, mpe ete soki amipesi na mokano na Ye, akozwa mpenza bonsomi ya solo.

src: This concept of surrender is beautifully illustrated in the story of the Prophet Muhammad.
trg: Likanisi ya komipesa elimbolami malamu na lisolo ya Mosakoli Muhammad.

src: When Muhammad was first called to be a prophet, he was very afraid.
trg: Ntango Muhammad abengamaki na kokoma mosakoli, azalaki kobanga makasi.

src: He didn't want to be responsible for spreading God's message.
trg: Azalaki te kolinga kozala na mokumba ya kopanza nsango ya Nzambe.

src: However, after much prayer and reflection, Muhammad eventually surrendered to God's will.
trg: Kasi, nsima ya kobondela mpe kokanisa mingi, nsukansuka Muhammad amipesaki na mokano ya Nzambe.

src: He realized that it was not his own strength that would allow him to succeed, but the strength of God.
trg: Akangaki ntina ete akolonga te na makasi na ye moko, kansi na makasi ya Nzambe.

src: Muhammad's story is a reminder that surrender is not about giving up.
trg: Lisolo ya Muhammad ezali kokundwela biso ete komipesa ezali te komiboya.

src: I grew up in a small village in the middle of nowhere.
trg: Nakolaki na mboka moko ya moke na katikati ya eloko te.

src: There were only a few hundred people living there, and everyone knew everyone else.
trg: Ezalaki kaka na mwa monkama ya bato oyo bazalaki kofanda kuna, mpe bato nyonso bayebanaki.

src: We had a small school, a general store, and a post office.
trg: Tozalaki na eteyelo ya moke, butiki ya bato nyonso, mpe biro ya poste.

src: The pace of life was slow and relaxed, and there was always time to stop and chat with a neighbor.
trg: Bomoi ezalaki malembe mpe ya kimya, mpe bato bazalaki ntango nyonso na ngonga ya kotelema mpe kosolola na moto ya kartie.

src: When I was 18, I moved to the city to go to college.
trg: Ntango nazalaki na mibu 18, nakendaki na engumba mpo na kokota na collège.

src: At first, I was overwhelmed by the noise, the traffic, and the crowds.
trg: Na ebandeli, makelele, mituka, mpe bato ebele ezalaki kolekela nga.

src: It took me a while to adjust to city life, but eventually I came to love it.
trg: Ezwaki mwa ntango mpo namesana na bomoi ya engumba, kasi nsukansuka nakomaki kolinga yango.

src: I found that there were endless opportunities in the city, and I made some lifelong friends.
trg: Namonaki ete mabaku ezalaki ebele mpenza na engumba, mpe nazwaki baninga ya bomoi mobimba.

src: After college, I got a job in the city and stayed there for a few years.
trg: Nima ya collège, nazwaki mosala na engumba mpe nasalaki mwa mibu kuna.

src: But eventually, I started to miss the slower pace of life in the village.
trg: Kasi nsukansuka, nabandaki koyoka mposa ya bomoi ya malembe ya mboka.

src: I wanted to be able to raise a family in a place where I knew everyone and everyone knew me.
trg: Nazalaki kolinga kokolisa libota na esika oyo nayebi bato nyonso mpe bato nyonso bayebi nga.

src: So a few years ago, I moved back to the village where I grew up.
trg: Yango wana mwa bambula na nsima, nazongaki na mboka esika nakolaki.

src: It was like coming home.
trg: Ezalaki neti kozonga na ndako.

src: I'm now raising my family in the same small house where I grew up, and I'm so happy to be back.
trg: Sikoyo nazali kokolisa libota na nga na ndako ya moke oyo nakolaki, mpe nazali na esengo ndenge nazonga.

src: In a time long past, there lived a blind beggar who made his living by demonstrating the art of soil sculpting.
trg: Na mikolo ya kala mpenza, ezalaki na mosengi-biloko akufa miso oyo azalaki kobika na kosala biloko ya kitoko na mabele.

src: He would sit on the street corner, surrounded by his tools and materials, and invite passersby to watch him work.
trg: Azalaki kofanda na coin ya balaala, azangami na bisaleli mpe biloko na ye, mpe kobenga baleki-nzela na kotala ye azali kosala.

src: With his deft fingers, he would mold the soil into intricate shapes, creating animals, plants, and even entire landscapes.
trg: Na misapi na ye eyebi mosala, azalaki kobalusa mabele mpe kopesa yango baforme ya kokamwa, kosala banyama, banzete, mpe nkutu bapaysage mobimba.

src: His work was so beautiful that it was said to bring tears to the eyes of even the most hardened cynic.
trg: Mosala na ye ezalaki kitoko mingi yango wana balobaki ete ezalaki kobimisa mpisoli na miso ata ya bato ya motema makasi mpenza.

src: One day, a young woman named Amara was walking through the market when she saw the blind beggar.
trg: Mokolo moko, elenge mwasi moko nkombo na ye Amara azalaki koleka na zando mpe amonaki mosengi-biloko wana oyo akufa miso.

src: She was immediately captivated by his work, and she stopped to watch him for a long time.
trg: Asepelaki mbala moko na misala na ye, mpe atelemaki mpo na kotala ye na ngonga molai.

src: When he was finished, she approached him and asked if she could learn how to sculpt soil.
trg: Ntango asilisaki mosala, elenge wana apusanaki pene na ye mpe atunaki ye soki akoki koyekola ndenge ya kosala mayemi na mabele.

src: The beggar smiled and told her that he would be happy to teach her.
trg: Mosengi-biloko asekaki mpe ayebisaki ye ete akozala na esengo ya koteya ye.

src: Amara spent the next few weeks learning from the beggar.
trg: Amara alekisaki mwa bamposo na koyekolo epai ya mosengi-biloko wana.

src: He taught her the basics of soil sculpting, and he showed her how to create different shapes and textures.
trg: Ateyaki elenge wana mayele ntina ya kosala mayemi, mpe alakisaki ye ndenge ya kosala baforme mpe midele ekeseni.

src: Amara was a quick learner, and she soon became very skilled at the art.
trg: Amara azalaki koyekola noki, mpe aumelaki te na koyeba malamu mosala wana.

src: One day, the beggar told Amara that it was time for her to demonstrate her skills.
trg: Mokolo moko, mosengi-biloko ayebisaki Amara ntango ekokaki mpo Amara alakisa mayele na ye.

src: Vigilante justice is a term used to describe the act of taking the law into one's own hands, typically by meting out punishment to those who have been deemed to have committed crimes.
trg: Boyengebene ya bokengi ezali liloba basaleli mpo na kolimbola likambo ya kozwa mobeko na maboko, mingimingi na kopesaka etumbu na bato oyo bamona ete basala bambeba ya minene.

src: While vigilante justice may seem like a quick and easy way to get justice, it can often lead to more problems than it solves.
trg: Atako boyengebene ya bokengi ekoki komonana lolenge ya noki mpe ya pete ya kozwa boyengebene, mbala mingi ememaka mikakatano ebele olie ya kosilisa yango.

src: One of the biggest problems with vigilante justice is that it is typically not done in a fair and impartial manner.
trg: Moko ya makambo ya monene koleka ya boyengebene ya bokengi ezali ete esalemaka te na lolenge ya malamu mpe ya kozanga koponapona.

src: Vigilantes are often motivated by anger and emotion, which can lead them to make rash decisions and take actions that are not in the best interests of everyone involved.
trg: Mbala mingi bokengi ekambamaka na nkanda mpe mayoki, oyo ekoki komema na bikateli ya kozanga kokanisa mpe kosala makambo oyo ezali te mpo na bolamu ya bato nyonso oy yango etaleli.

src: Additionally, vigilantes often lack the training and experience necessary to properly handle criminals.
trg: Lisusu, mbala mingi bokengi ezangaka formation mpe eksperiansi ebongi mpo na kolandela malamu bato ya mabe makasi.

src: This can lead to situations where innocent people are harmed or even killed.
trg: Ekoki komema na makambo oyo esalaka ete basala mabe na bato oyo basali likambo te to nkutu baboma bango.

src: Another problem with vigilante justice is that it can quickly spiral out of control.
trg: Mokakatano mosusu ya boyengebene ya bokengi ezali ete kokoma noki likambo oyo bakoki koyangela te.

src: When one person takes the law into their own hands, it sends a message to others that they can do the same.
trg: Soki moto moko azwi mobeko na maboko na ye moko, ezali koyebisa bato mosusu ete bango mpe bakoki kosala ndenge moko.

src: This can lead to a cycle of violence and retribution that can be difficult to stop.
trg: Ekoki komema na mobulu mpe na etumbu oyo ekoki kozala mpasi na kosukisa.

src: In the long run, vigilante justice is rarely effective in deterring crime.
trg: Na ntango ya molai, boyengebene ya bokengi esimbaka ata moke te na kokanga bato na kosala mbeba.

src: In fact, it can often have the opposite effect, making criminals more likely to commit crimes in the future.
trg: Ya solo, ekoki kosala makambo ekeseni na oyo bakanisaki, kosala ete bato mabe basala lisusu mabe mingi koleka na mikolo ezali koya.

src: Son, did you know that there's a new array of craters on the moon?
trg: Mwana, oyebi ete liboke ya sika ya ba cratere ezali na sanza?

src: Scientists say that they were formed by a series of impacts from asteroids and comets.
trg: Bato ya siansi balobi ete esalemaki na molongo ya bopusi euti na ba asteroide mpe bakomete.

src: The largest crater is about 100 miles across and is named after the Greek god of war, Ares.
trg: Cratere ya monene koleka ezali pene ya 100 miles mosika mpe bapesa yango nkombo na kolana nzambe ya bitumba ya Grese, Ares.

src: The craters are so bright that they can be seen from Earth with the naked eye.
trg: Bacratere engengaka makasi yango wana ekoki komonana polele longwa na Mabele na miso mpamba.

src: They stand out against the dark surface of the moon like silver coins on a black velvet cloth.
trg: Ezalaka na libanda ya esika ya molili ya sanza neti mabende ya arza na elamba ya velours ya moindo.

src: Water is essential for life.
trg: Mai ezali ntina mingi mpo na bomoi.

src: It makes up over 60% of our body weight and is involved in many important bodily functions, such as regulating body temperature, transporting nutrients and oxygen to cells, and removing waste products.
trg: Ezali 60% ya kilo ya nzoto na biso mpe ekotaka na misala mingi ya nzoto, neti kobongisa temperature ya nzoto, komema bilei mpe mopepe na baselile, mpe kolongola biloko ya mbindo.

src: Water also helps to lubricate joints and protect organs and tissues.
trg: Mai esalisaka mpe na kolembisa bajoint mpe kobatela binama na misisa.

src: There are many reasons why we should conserve water.
trg: Ezali na bantina mingi oyo tosengeli kobatela mai.

src: One reason is that water scarcity is a growing problem around the world.
trg: Ntina moko ezali ete kozanga mai ezali kokoma mokakatano makasi na mokili mobimba.

src: In many parts of the world, people do not have access to clean water, and even in areas where water is plentiful, it is becoming increasingly scarce due to climate change.
trg: Na bisika mingi na mokili mobimba, bato bazali na mai ya peto, mpe nkutu na bisika mosusu oyo mai ezali ebele, ezali kokoma mpasi na kozwa yango mpo na mbongwana ya climat.

src: Another reason to conserve water is that it is a valuable resource.
trg: Ntina mosusu ya kobatela mai ezali ete ezali ntina mingi.

src: It takes a lot of energy to treat and transport water, and it is important to use water wisely so that we do not waste this precious resource.
trg: Esengaki energie ebele mpo na kobongisa mpe komema mai, mpe ezali ntina mingi na kosalela mai na mayele mpo tobebisa te eloko oyo ya motuya mingi.

src: There are many things we can do to conserve water.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo tokoki kosala mpo na kobatela mai.

src: We can take shorter showers, fix leaky faucets, and water our lawns less often.
trg: Tokoki kosokola ntango moke, kobongisa bisika mai ezali kotanga, mpe kosopa mai na pelouse mbala moke.

src: We can also choose to buy products that are made with recycled water.
trg: Tokoki mpe kopona na kosomba biloko oyo basala na mai oyo basila kosalela.

src: By making small changes in our daily lives, we can help to conserve water and ensure that this vital resource is available for future generations.
trg: Soki tosali mbongwana ya moke na bomoi na biso ya mokolo na mokolo, tokoki kosalisa na kobatela mai mpe kosala ete eloko oyo ya ntina ezala wana mpo na bato bakoya na mikolo ezali koya.

src: Floods are a natural disaster that can cause widespread damage and loss of life.
trg: Mpela ezali likama ya bozalisi oyo ekoki komema mbeba makasi mpe koboma bato.

src: They are often caused by heavy rainfall or snowmelt that exceeds the capacity of a river or other waterway, resulting in the overflow of water onto land.
trg: Mbala mingi ememaka mbula makasi to baneze oyo elekaka makoki ya ebale to ya nzela mosusu ya mai, esalaka ete mai esopana na mokili.

src: Floods can also be caused by dams or levees breaking, or by tsunamis.
trg: Mpela ekoki kouta mpe na kopasuka ya mazipa, to na ba tsunami.

src: The most common types of floods are river floods, which occur when a river overflows its banks, and flash floods, which occur when a large amount of rain falls in a short period of time.
trg: Mpela eyebani mingi ezali kotonda mai ya ebale, oyo esalemaka soki mai eleki bandelo ya ebale, mpe esalemaka soki bambula ya makasi ebeti na eleko ya mokuse.

src: Floods can also occur in coastal areas due to storm surges, which are large waves that are pushed inland by strong winds.
trg: Mpelo ekoki kosalema na bisika ya pene ya mbu mpo na orage, oyo ezali mbonge makasi oyo ebimisaka mai libanda na mipepe ya makasi.

src: Floods can cause a wide range of damage, including loss of life, property damage, and environmental damage.
trg: Mpela ekoki kobebisa biloko ebele, neti kobomisa bato, kobebisa biloko, mpe kobebisa environema.

src: They can also disrupt transportation and communication, and lead to food and water shortages.
trg: Ekoki kobebisa transport mpe masolo, mpe kosala ete mai eleka ndelo.

src: The resulting loss of homes and livelihoods can force people to relocate, which can lead to social and economic problems.
trg: Kozanga bandako mpe bilei ekoki kopusa bato na kokende kofanda esika mosusu, ebongo ekoki komema mikakatano ya sociale mpe ya ekonomi.

src: Our archive contains over 100 million records, including census records, birth records, death records, and marriage records.
trg: Biloko na biso ya kala eza na badosie koleka bamilio 100, ezali na mikanda ya kokomisa bankombo ya bato, ya mbotama, ya liwa, mpe ya mabala.

src: We also have a large collection of family group sheets and manuscripts.
trg: Tozali mpe na liboke monene ya baliste ya etuluku ya maboko mpe bamaniskri.

src: To search for your ancestors, you can use our surname search tool.
trg: Mpo na koluka bankoko, okoki kosalela esaleli na biso ya koluka bankombo.

src: This tool allows you to search by surname, first name, and date of birth.
trg: Esaleli oyo esalisaka na koluka nkombo ya libota, prénom, mpe dati ya mbotama.

src: You can also search by location.
trg: Okoki mpe koluka na kolanda esika.

src: Once you have found your ancestors, you can view their records.
trg: Soki ozwi bankoko na yo, okoki kotala badosie na bango.

src: You can also print copies of their records.
trg: Okoki mpe ko imprimer bakopi ya badosie na bango.

src: We also offer a subscription service that allows you to access our entire archive.
trg: Tozali mpe na mosala ya kokomisa nkombo oyo ekopesa yo nzela ya kotala mikanda na biso nyonso ya kala.

src: This service is perfect for genealogists who are looking for a comprehensive collection of records.
trg: Mosala oyo ebongi mpenza mpo bagenealogiste oyo balukaka badosie ya mobimba.

src: If you have any questions about our archive or our surname search tool, please do not hesitate to contact us.
trg: Soki ozali na motuna etali mikanda na biso ya kala to esaleli ya koluka bankombo ya mabota, kokakatana te na kobenga to kokomela biso.

src: We are here to help you find your ancestors.
trg: Tozali wana mpo na kosalisa yo koyeba bankoko na yo.

src: Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Juan who loved tacos.
trg: Na ntango moko boye, ezalaki na mwana mobali ya moke nkombo na ye Juan oyo azalaki kolinga tacos.

src: He loved them so much that he would eat them for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
trg: Azalaki kolinga yango mingi mpenza yango wnaa azalaki kolya yango na ntongo, na midi, mpe na mpokwa.

src: One day, Juan's mother decided to make him a special taco.
