trg: Ezali kaka mokumbi-motuka Uber ya malamu ya kartie na bino, azali awa mpo na komema yo esika nyonso olingi.

src: So, where are we headed today?
trg: Ozali kokende wapi lelo?

src: I'm glad you asked about integrity.
trg: Nasepeli mpo otuna makambo ya bosembo.

src: It's one of the most important things in life, in my opinion.
trg: Mpo na nga, ezali moko ya makambo ya ntina mingi na bomoi.

src: It's all about doing the right thing, even when it's hard.
trg: Etali mingi kosala makambo ya malamu, ata ntango ezali mpasi.

src: It means being honest, trustworthy, and ethical.
trg: Elimboli koloba solo, kozala moto bakoki kotyela motema, mpe na bizaleli ya malamu.

src: I think integrity is so important because it helps us build trust with others.
trg: Nakanisi bosembo ezali ntina mingi mpo esalisaka biso na kopusa basusu batyela biso motema.

src: When people know that we're honest and trustworthy, they're more likely to open up to us and share their thoughts and feelings.
trg: Soki bato bayebi ete tolobaka solo mpe bakoki kotyela biso motema, bakosolola na biso kozanga mpasi mpe koyebisa biso makanisi mpe mayoki na bango.

src: That can make for a richer and more fulfilling life.
trg: Ekoki kosalisa na kozala na bomoi ya kitoko mpe ya malamu mpenza.

src: Of course, it's not always easy to do the right thing.
trg: Ya solo, ezala te ntango nyonso pete na kosala makambo ya malamu.

src: Sometimes, we might be tempted to lie or cheat in order to get ahead.
trg: Bantango mosusu, tokoki kopusama na kokosa to koyiba mpo na kokende liboso.

src: But if we want to live a life of integrity, we have to be willing to stand up for what we believe in, even when it's difficult.
trg: Kasi soki tolingi kozala na bomoi ya bosembo, tosengeli kozala na mposa ya kotelema mpo na makambo yo tondimaka, ata ntango ezali mpasi.

src: I know that integrity is something that you value, too.
trg: Nayebi ete bosembo ezali eloko oyo yo mpe ozwaka na motuya.

src: That's why I'm so glad you're my passenger today.
trg: Yango wana nasepeli mingi ndenge ozali kiliya na nga lelo.

src: Fufu is a starchy, doughy food made from pounded plantains or cassava.
trg: Fufu ezali bilei balamba mpe ya pate oyo basali na makemba to manioko batuta.

src: It is a staple food in many West African countries, and is often served with soups or stews.
trg: Ezali bilei ya yambo na bamboka mingi ya Afrika ya Westi, mpe mbala mingi balyaka yango na basupu to biloko batumba.

src: Fufu is typically made by pounding the plantains or cassava in a large mortar and pestle until they are smooth and pasty.
trg: Basalaka fufu mbala mingi na kotutaka makemba to manioko na liboka ya monene na motute kino ekokoma pete mpe pate.

src: The resulting fufu is then shaped into balls or logs and served.
trg: Na nsima bapesaka fufu wana forme ya mbuma mpe bapesaka bato mpo balya.

src: Fufu is a very filling food, and it is often eaten as a main course.
trg: Fufu ezali bilei oyo etondisaka mpenza, mpe mbala mingi balyaka yango lokola bilei ya yambo.

src: It is also a good source of carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals.
trg: Ezalaka mpe bilei epesaka carbohydrate, bavitamine mpe baminerale.

src: Fufu is a traditional food that has been eaten in West Africa for hundreds of years.
trg: Fufu ezali bilei ya mboka oyo balyaka na Afrika ya Weste banda bankama ya bambula.

src: It is a part of the culture and identity of many West African societies.
trg: Ezali na kati ya bonkoko mpe identité ya bikolo ebele ya Afrika ya Weste.

src: Person A: There is a lack of originality in the perfume and fragrance industry. The perfumes all smell the same, and they don't really say anything about me.
trg: Moto A: Kompani ya parfum mpe ya bansolo ezali kozanga biloko ya originale. Baparfum nyonso ezali na nsolo kaka moko, mpe ezali koloba eloko moko te mpo na nga.

src: Person B: I know what you mean. I've been looking for a unique perfume that will make me stand out from the crowd, but I haven't had any luck.
trg: Moto B: Nayebi nini olingi koloba. Nazalaki koluka parfum ya kitoko oyo ekosala ete nakesana mpenza na bato mosusu, kasi natikala nanu te kozwa chance.

src: Person A: I think we should start our own perfume company. We could create fragrances that are truly original and that reflect our personality.
trg: Moto A: Nakanisi tosengeli kofungola kompani na biso moko ya parfum. Tokoki kosala bansolo oyo ezali mpenza ya originale mpe oyo ezali komonisa bomoto na biso.

src: Person B: That's a great idea! I'm so excited to get started.
trg: Moto B: Ezali likanisi ya malamu mpenza! Nazali na esengo mingi ya kobanda.

src: Person A: We could call it "Back to Australia". It would be a tribute to our home country and a celebration of our unique scents.
trg: Moto A: Tokoki kobenga yango "Kozonga na Australie". Ekozala lokumu mpo na mboka na biso mpe feti mpo na bansolo na biso ya kokamwa.

src: Person B: I love it! I can't wait to start creating fragrances that will make Australia proud.
trg: Moto B: Nalingaka yango! Nazali na mposa ya makasi ya kobanda kosala bansolo oyo epesi Australie lokumu.

src: The Suez Canal was a major engineering feat that connected the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
trg: Canale ya Suez ezalaki mosala makasi ya ba enzeniere oyo esangisaka Mbu ya Mediterane na Mbu ya Motane.

src: It was built by the French and opened in 1869.
trg: Esalemaki na bato ya France mpe bafungolaki yango na 1869.

src: The canal was a vital trade route for Egypt and the rest of the world.
trg: Canale wana ezalaki nzela ya ntina ya mombongo mpo na Ezipito mpe mikili mosusu ya mokili.

src: It also allowed for the movement of troops and supplies, which was important during wartime.
trg: Ezalaki mpe kosalisa basoda na bibundeli na koleka, likambo wana ezalaki ntina mingi na ntango ya bitumba.

src: In 1956, Egypt nationalized the Suez Canal, which led to the Suez Crisis.
trg: Na 1956, Ezipito ekomisaka Canale ya Suez eloko na bango, yango ebimisaki Matata ya Suez.

src: The crisis was a major international incident that was eventually resolved through a United Nations peacekeeping force.
trg: Matata wana ezalaki likambo ya monene ya mokili mobimba oyo nsukansuka basilisaki yango na nzela ya basoda ya kimya ya Nations-Unies.

src: The Suez Canal is still a vital trade route today and is one of the most important waterways in the world.
trg: Canale ya Suez ezali kaka nzela ya ntina ya mombongo lelo mpe ezali moko ya banzela ya mai ya ntina mingi na mokili.

src: Once upon a time, there was a young man named Rajiv who lived in a small village.
trg: Na ntango moko boye, ezalaki na elenge mobali moko nkombo na ye Rajiv oyo azalaki kofanda na mboka moko ya moke.

src: He was a poor man, and he and his mother often went hungry.
trg: Azalaki mobola, mpe ye na mama na ye bazalaki mbala mingi nzala.

src: One day, Rajiv decided to go into the forest to find some food.
trg: Mokolo moko, Rajiv azwaki ekateli ya kokende na zamba mpo na koluka mwa bilei.

src: As he was walking through the forest, Rajiv came across a strange tree.
trg: Ntango azalaki kotambola na zamba, Rajiv amonaki nzete moko ya kokamwa.

src: The tree was covered in golden apples, and Rajiv had never seen anything like it before.
trg: Nzete wana ezalaki ya kotonda na bapome ya wolo, mpe Rajiv atikala nanu te komona eloko moko ya ndenge wana.

src: He reached up to pick an apple, but as soon as he touched it, the tree spoke to him.
trg: Apusanaki mpo na kobuka pome moko, kasi ntango alingaki kosimba yango, nzete elobelaki ye.

src: "Do not touch my apples," the tree said. "They are not for you."
trg: "Kosimba te bapome na nga," wana maloba ya nzete. "Ezali te mpo na yo."

src: But Rajiv was hungry, and he didn't listen to the tree.
trg: Kasi Rajvi azalaki na nzala, mpe ayokelaki nzete te.

src: He picked an apple and took a bite.
trg: Azwaki pome moko mpe akataki eteni na mino.

src: As soon as he did, he felt a strange change come over him.
trg: Ntango asalaki yango, ayokaki mbongwana ya kokamwa esalemi na nzoto na ye.

src: He felt stronger and more powerful, and he knew that he had done something wrong.
trg: Amiyokaki makasi mpe na nguya mingi, mpe ayebaki ete asali likambo moko ya mabe.

src: "I am the Golden Apple Tree," the tree said. "And now that you have eaten my apple, you will be cursed.
trg: "Nazali Nzete ya Bapome ya Wolo," wana maloba ya nzete. "Mpe lokola olye pome na nga, olakelami mabe.

src: You will never be satisfied with what you have, and you will always be searching for more."
trg: Okotikala kosepela te na oyo ozali na yango, mpe okolukaka ntango nyonso kozala na ebele."

src: And so it was.
trg: Mpe esalamaki bongo.

src: Open-air markets are a popular attraction in many cities and towns.
trg: Bazando bazipa likolo te ebendaka bato na bingumba mpe bamboka mingi.

src: They offer a variety of goods and services, from fresh produce to handmade crafts.
trg: Ezalaka na biloko mpe misala ebele, banda na biloko bauti kobuka kino na biloko basali na maboko.

src: Visitors can find a bargain on everything from clothes to souvenirs.
trg: Bapaya bakoki kokakola eloko nyonso banda na bilamba kino na basuvenire.

src: Open-air markets are also a great place to people-watch and enjoy the local culture.
trg: Bazando bazipa likolo te ezalaka mpe bisika ya kitoko mpo bato batala mpe basepela na bonkoko ya esika wana.

src: One of the best things about open-air markets is the atmosphere.
trg: Moko ya biloko ya ntina mingi ya bazando bazipa likolo te ezali ambiance na yango.

src: They're usually bustling with activity, and there's always something to see and do.
trg: Mbala mingi ezalaka na misala ebele, mpe ezalaka ntango nyonso na eloko ya kotala mpe ya kosala.

src: You'll hear the sound of vendors calling out to customers, the smell of fresh-baked bread and pastries, and the sight of people haggling over prices.
trg: Okoyoka mongongo ya bateki bazali kobenga bakiliya, nsolo ya mama mpe bakado ya sika, mpe komona bato bazali kokokola.

src: Another advantage of open-air markets is the variety of goods and services available.
trg: Litomba mosusu ya bazando bazipa likolo te ezali biloko mpe misala ndenge na ndenge oyo ezalaka kuna.

src: You can find everything from fresh produce to handmade crafts.
trg: Okoki kozwa biloko nyonso banda na biloko bauti kobuka kino na biloko basali na maboko.

src: And because the vendors are independent businesses, they're often willing to negotiate prices.
trg: Mpe lokola bateki bazali bato ya mimbongo ya lipanda, bandimaka ntango nyonso okakola biloko.

src: So if you're looking for a bargain, an open-air market is the place to be.
trg: Yango wana soki ozali koluka eloko ya kokakola, osengeli kokende na zando bazipa likolo te.

src: Of course, no discussion of open-air markets would be complete without mentioning the food.
trg: Ya solo, lisolo moko te na bazando bazipa likolo te ekoki kosila kozanga kolobela bilei.

src: These markets are a great place to sample local cuisine.
trg: Bazando oyo ezalaka esika kitoko ya komona bilei ya mboka.

src: You'll find everything from grilled meats to fresh seafood to traditional desserts.
trg: Okokuta bilei nyonso banda na misuni ya kotumba, bilei ya kitoko ya mbu mpe bilei ya sukali ya bankoko.

src: Ambedkar Jayanti is a day of celebration in India and other countries around the world to honor the memory of Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, a social reformer, jurist, and political leader who was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and the architect of the Constitution of India.
trg: Ambedkar Jayanti ezali mokolo ya feti ya Inde mpe na bamboka ya zingazinga mpo na kokumisa Monganga Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, motomboki ya sociale, zuzi, mpe mokambi ya politiki oyo azalaki moto ya ntina na muvema ya Lipanda ya Inde mpe moto abandaki kosala Mobeko-Mokonzi ya Inde.

src: Ambedkar was born into a Dalit family, a group of people who were considered to be untouchables in the caste system of India.
trg: Ambedkar abotamaki na libota moko ya Dalit, etuluku ya bato oyo bato bamonaka ete bakoki kosimba bango te na ebongiseli ya Inde.

src: He faced discrimination and hardship throughout his life, but he never gave up on his dream of equality for all Indians.
trg: Batyolaki ye mpe akutanaki na mikakatano na bomoi na ye, kasi asundolaki te bandoto na ye ete bato nyonso ya Inde bazala ndenge moko.

src: Ambedkar was a brilliant student and went on to earn a doctorate in law from Columbia University in the United States.
trg: Ambedkar azalaki mwana-kelasi ya mayele mpe ozwaki diplome ya dokotolo ya makambo ya mibeko na Iniversite ya Columbia na États-Unis.

src: He also studied at the London School of Economics and became a barrister.
trg: Atangaki mpe na Eteyelo ya Ekonomi ya Londres mpe akomaki avoka.

src: After returning to India, Ambedkar became a leading figure in the Indian independence movement.
trg: Nsima ya kozonga na Inde, Ambedkar akomaki mokambi ya muvema ya Lipanda ya Inde.

src: He was a member of the Indian National Congress, but he eventually broke away from the party and formed his own political organization, the Scheduled Castes Federation.
trg: Azalaki moto ya Congres ya Ekolo ya Inde, kasi nsukansuka abimaki na parti mpe asalaki lisanga na ye moko ya politiki, Lisanga ya Bacaste oyo Batangi.

src: Ambedkar was also a key figure in the drafting of the Constitution of India.
trg: Ambedkar azalaki mpe moko ya bato ya ntina oyo basalaki Mobeko-Mokonzi ya Inde.

src: Animal cruelty is the intentional infliction of pain, suffering, or death upon an animal.
trg: Konyokola nyama ezali kopesa mpasi, minyoko, to koboma nyama.

src: It can take many forms, from physical abuse to neglect.
trg: Ekoki kozala na balolenge ebele, na kobeta yango to na kosundola yango.

src: Animals may be beaten, kicked, burned, starved, or even killed for no reason other than human entertainment.
trg: Bakoki kobeta banyama, kobeta bango makolo, kozika, kopimela bango bilei to nkutu koboma bango kaka mpo na kosepelisa bato.

src: Animal cruelty is a serious problem that affects millions of animals every year.
trg: Konyokola nyama ezali likambo ya mpasi oyo bamilio ya banyama ezali kokutana na yango mbula nyonso.

src: It is illegal in most countries, but enforcement is often lax.
trg: Epekisami na mikili ebele, kasi mbala mingi bato batosisaka mibeko basalaka eloko te.

src: There are many organizations that work to prevent and stop animal cruelty, but more needs to be done.
trg: Ezali na masanga ebele oyo esalaka mpo na kokanga nzela mpe kosukisa konyokola banyama, kasi esengeli kosala makambo ebele.

src: We can all help to stop animal cruelty by being more aware of the issue and by speaking out against it.
trg: Biso nyonso tokoki kosunga na kosukisa konyokola banyama soki toyebi malamu likambo wana mpe tolobi mpo na kotelemela yango.

src: We can also choose to buy from businesses that do not support animal cruelty and to support organizations that work to protect animals.
trg: Tokoki mpe kopona na kosomba biloko epai ya bato ya mombongo oyo bapesaka te maboko na konyokola banyama mpe kosunga masanga oyo esalaka mpo na kobatela banyama.

src: Animal cruelty is a terrible thing that happens every day.
trg: Konyokola nyama ezali likambo ya mabe makasi oyo esalemaka mikolo nyonso.

src: We can all help to make a difference by speaking out against it and by supporting organizations that work to stop it.
trg: Biso nyonso tokoki kosalisa na kosala bokeseni na kolobaka mpo na kotelemela mpe kosunga masanga oyo ezali kosala mpo na kosukisa yango.

src: This is because the average age of a woman's first menstrual period is 12 years old, and the average age of menopause is 45 years old.
trg: Ezali mpo mbula ya moyenne oyo mwasi amonaki makila na mbala ya liboso ezali 12, mpe mbula ya moyenene ya kosukisa komona makila ezali 45.

src: This means that a woman has approximately 33 years to bear children.
trg: Elakisi ete mwasi azali na mibu pene ya 33 mpo na kobota bana.

src: However, fertility begins to decline in a woman's mid-thirties, and by the time she is 40, her chances of conceiving naturally are significantly reduced.
trg: Kasi, makoki ya kobota ebandaka kokita soki mwasi akomi na mibu tuku misato na ndambo, mpe na ntango akokoma na mibu 40, bachance ya kozwa zemi ya normale ekitaka makasi.

src: There are a number of factors that can contribute to a woman's declining fertility, including age, smoking, obesity, and certain medical conditions.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kozala ete makoki ya mwasi ya kobota ekita, neti mbula, komela makaya, kozola monene koleka, mpe maladi mosusu.

src: As a woman ages, her eggs become less healthy and more likely to have chromosomal abnormalities.
trg: Ntango mwasi azokoma mokolo, maki na ye ekomaka na sante ya malamu mpenza te mpe ezalaka na mbeba ya ba chromosome.

src: This can increase the risk of miscarriage, stillbirth, and birth defects.
trg: Ekoki komatisa likama ya kosopa zemi, ya mwana akufa, mpe ya koboma mwana na mbeba.

src: Smoking can also damage a woman's fertility by reducing blood flow to the uterus and ovaries.
trg: Komela makaya ekoki kobebisa makoki ya mwasi ya kobota na kokitsaka ndenge makila etambolaka na uterus mpe na ba ovaire.

src: Obesity can lead to hormonal imbalances that can interfere with ovulation.
trg: Kokoma monene mingi ebebisaka ba hormone oyo ekoki kobebisa kokumba zemi.

src: And certain medical conditions, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometriosis, can also make it difficult for a woman to conceive.
trg: Mpe maladi mosusu, neti syndrome ya ovaire polycystique (PCOS) mpe endometriosise, ekoki mpe kosala ete ezala mpasi mpo mwasi akumba zemi.

src: If you are a woman who is over 30 and are thinking about having children, it is important to talk to your doctor about your fertility.
trg: Soki ozali mwasi oyo alekisi mibu 30 mpe ozali kokanisa kobota bana, ezali ntina kosolola na monganga na yo na ntina ya mabota na yo.

src: There are a number of things that you can do to improve your chances of conceiving, including losing weight if you are overweight or obese, quitting smoking, and getting regular exercise.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo okoki kosala mpo na komatisa bachance na yo ya kokumba zemi, neti kokitsa kilo soki ozali monene mingi to olekisa kilo, kotika komela makaya mpe kosala ngalasisi mbala na mbala.

src: Your doctor may also recommend fertility medications or other treatments to help you conceive.
trg: Monganga na yo akoki me kokomela yo bankisi to ba traitement mosusu mpo na kosalisa yo na kokumba zemi.

src: It is also important to remember that there are many other ways to have a family, even if you are unable to conceive naturally.
trg: Ezali mpe ntina na kobosana te ete ezali na bolenge ebele mosusu ya kozala na libota, ata soki ozali te na makoki ya kozwa zemi ndenge esengaka.

src: Adoption and surrogacy are two options that you may want to consider.
trg: Kosomba mwana mpe bamere porteuse ezali maponi mibale oyo okoki kolinga kotalela.

src: With the help of modern medicine, there are many ways to have a family, no matter what your age or fertility.
trg: Na lisungi ya kimonganga ya lelo, ezali na balolenge ebele ya kozala na libota, ata azali na mbula nini to okoki te kokumba zemi.

src: Elephants are the largest land animals on Earth and can weigh up to 15,000 pounds.
trg: Banzoko ezali banyama ya minene koleka na Mabele mpe ekoki kozala na kilo kino na 15 000 poounds.

src: They are herbivores and their diet consists mainly of leaves, bark, and fruit.
trg: Balyaka matiti mpe bilei na bango ezalaka mingimingi bankasa, bamposo ya banzete mpe bambuma.

src: Elephants have a long trunk that they use for many purposes, including drinking, bathing, and gathering food.
trg: Banzoko bazalaka na monoko ya molai oyo basalelaka mpo na mikano ebele, ata mpe komela, kosukola, mpe kosangisa bilei.

src: They also use their trunks to communicate with each other and to defend themselves from predators.
trg: Basalelaka mpe minoko mpo na kosolola kati na bango mpe komibatela na miyibi.

src: Elephants live in herds and are very social animals.
trg: Banzoko bafandaka na bituluku mpe bazali banyama balingaka kofanda elongo.

src: They form strong bonds with each other and care for their young.
trg: Bazalaka na boninga ya makasi kati na bango mpe babatelaka bana na bango.

src: Elephants are also very intelligent animals and have been known to use tools.
trg: Banzoko bazalaka mpe banyama ya mayele mingi mpe bayebana ete basalelaka bisaleli.

src: Unfortunately, elephants are threatened by habitat loss and poaching.
trg: Kasi ezali mawa mpo banzoko bazali na likama ya kobungisa esika bafandaka mpe mpo bazali koboma bango.

src: However, there are many conservation efforts underway to protect these amazing animals.
trg: Kasi, ezali na milende ebele ya kobatela bango oyo ezali kosalema mpo na banyama oyo ya kokamwa.

src: Up until that point, it had been a fairly standard fairy tale, with the princess living a sheltered life in her tower and the prince coming to rescue her.
trg: Kino na ngonga oyo, ezalaki lisapo ya mwa malamu, na princesse azali na bomoi na ye moko na ndako na ye mpe prince ayei kobikisa ye.

src: But once she steps outside, the story takes on a whole new tone.
trg: Kasi ntango azali kobima libanda, lisolo ebongwani mobimba.

src: The princess is immediately confronted with a harsh and unforgiving world.
trg: Princesse akutani mbala moko na mokili ya mabe oyo balimbisaka te.

src: She is forced to learn how to survive on her own, and she quickly discovers that she is not as helpless as she thought she was.
trg: Asengeli koyekola ndenge ya kobika ye moko, mpe ayebi noki ete azangi te lisungi ndenge azalaki kokanisa.

src: She meets a variety of interesting characters along the way, and she learns a lot about herself and the world around her.
trg: Akutani na nzela na bato ya ntina oyo bakeseni, mpe ayekoli makambo ebele mpo na ye moko mpe mokili ezingi ye.

src: The novel ends with the princess finding her own way in the world, and she is finally happy and content.
trg: Lisolo esuki ntango princesse azwi nzela na ye, ye moko na mokili, mpe nsukansuka azali na esengo mpe nsayi.

src: She has learned that she is strong and independent, and she is no longer afraid to face whatever challenges come her way.
trg: Ayekolaki ete azali makasi mpe na lipanda, mpe azali kobanga lisusu te mokakatano nyonso oyo akoki kokutana na yango.

src: The novel is a coming-of-age story, and it follows the princess as she grows from a sheltered young woman into a confident and capable adult.
trg: Lisolo oyo ezali lisolo ya mwa kala, mpe elandani na princesse azali kokola kolongwa na elenge mwasi oyo bazali kobatela mpe kokoma mokolo azali komityela motema mpe ya malonga.

src: It is a story about self-discovery and empowerment, and it is a reminder that we are all capable of achieving great things if we are willing to step outside of our comfort zones and face the challenges that life throws our way.
trg: Ezali lisolo ya komiyeba mpe kozwa makasi, mpe ezali kokundwela biso ete biso nyonso tokoki kosala makambo ya minene soki tondimi kobima na esika tomesana mpe kobundisa mikakatano oyo bomoi ekomemela biso.

src: As the global economy continues to grow, so too does the demand for cotton.
trg: Lokola ekonomi ya mobimba ezali kokola, bosengi ya coton mpe ezali kokola.

src: Furthermore, the increasing popularity of sustainable fashion is driving up demand for organic cotton.
trg: Lisusu, lokola bosengi ya midele ya kitoko ezali komata ezali mpe komatisa bosengi ya coton ya organique.

src: This has led to a surge in investment in the cotton industry, with new plantations being established in countries such as India and China.
trg: Esala ete batya mosolo ebele na mosala ya coton, mpe bazali kosala bilanga ya sika na mikili ebele neti na Inde mpe na Chine.

src: However, this growth has not been without its challenges.
trg: Kasi, bokoli oyo eya te kozanga mikakatano.

src: The increased demand for cotton has put a strain on water resources, and the use of pesticides and fertilizers has led to environmental pollution.
trg: Bosengi ya mingi ya coton ezali kosala ete basalela mai ebele, mpe kosalela ba pesticide mpe bankisi emema na kobebisa mopepe.

src: Furthermore, the low wages paid to cotton farmers in developing countries has led to concerns about labor exploitation.
trg: Lisusu, basalere ya mike oyo bafutaka bato basalaka na bilanga ya coton na mikili ya bobola ebimisa mitungisa etali kobuba bato ya mosala.

src: Despite these challenges, the cotton industry remains an important part of the global economy.
trg: Atako mikakatano oyo ezali, mosala ya coton etikala eteni ya ntina ya ekonomi ya mokili mobimba.

src: It provides jobs for millions of people and is a source of vital income for many developing countries.
trg: Epesaka mosala na bamilio ya baot mpe ezali esika mbongo ya ntina ya eutaka mpo na mikili mingi ya bobola.

src: Furthermore, cotton is a versatile and sustainable material that is used in a wide range of products, from clothing to home furnishings.
trg: Lisusu, coton ezali eloko ebongwanaka mpe ya makasi oyo basalelaka mpo na kosala biloko ebele, banda na bilamba kino n biloko ya ndako.

src: As the global population continues to grow, the demand for cotton is likely to remain high.
trg: Lokola bato bazali kokoba kokoma ebele na mokili mobimba, bosengi ya coton ekokoba mpe kozala likolo.

src: This presents both challenges and opportunities for the cotton industry.
trg: Ezali na mikakatano mpe mabaku mpo na mosala ya coton.

src: I remember the day I collected the first harvest of our family farm.
trg: Nazali kokanisa mokolo oyo nabukaki biloko ya liboso ya bilanga ya libota na biso.

src: It was a hot summer day, and the sun was beating down on us as we worked in the fields.
trg: Ezalaki mokolo ya moi makasi ya été, mpe moi ezalaki kobeta biso makasi ntango tozalaki kosala na bilanga.

src: But we didn't mind, because we were excited to see the fruits of our labor.
trg: Kasi tozalaki kokipe te, mpo tozalaki na esengo ya komona bambuma ya mosala na biso.

src: We had been working hard all season, and it was finally time to reap the rewards.
trg: Tozalaki kosala makasi mbula mobimba, mpe nsukansuka ntango ekoki mpo na kozwa mbano.

src: We picked the ripe tomatoes and peppers, and we carefully loaded them into the back of the truck.
trg: Tobukaki batomate mpe bapilipili, mpe totyaki yango na likebi na nsima ya motuka.

src: Then we drove them back to the farm, where we washed and sorted them.
trg: Na nsima tomemaki yango lisusu na bilanga, esika tosokolaki yango mpe tokabolaki yango.

src: After we had finished cleaning the vegetables, we put them in the smoker.
trg: Nsima ya kosilisa kosukola bandunda, totyaki yango na milinga.

src: The smoke from the wood fire slowly permeated the vegetables, giving them a delicious flavor.
trg: Milinga ya moto ya nkoni ekotaki malembemalembe na bandunda, epesaki yango elengi ya makasi.

src: We smoked them for several hours, until they were perfectly cooked.
trg: Totyaki yango na milinga bangonga ebele, kino ebelaka malamu mpenza.

src: We were all so proud of our work, and we couldn't wait to share the delicious vegetables with our family and friends.
trg: Biso nyonso tosepelaki na mosala na biso, tozalaki na esengo ya makasi ya kokabola bilei wana ya elengi na mabota mpe baninga na biso.

src: That night, we had a big feast, and we all ate and drank to our hearts' content.
trg: Na mpokwa wana, tosalaki feti monene, mpe biso nyonso tolyaki mpe tomelaki ndenge tolingaki.

src: It was a truly memorable day, and one that I will never forget.
trg: Ezalaki mokolo ya kokanisa mpenza, mokolo oyo tokoki kobosana ata moke te.

src: Scene: A meeting room in a business office.
trg: Likambo: Shambre ya likita na biro ya mombongo.

src: A man, Kevin, and a woman, Elena, are sitting at a table.
trg: Mobali moko, Kevni, mpe mwasi moko, Elena, bafandi na mesa.

src: Kevin: I've been thinking about starting a new business.
trg: Kevin: Nazalaki kokanisa kobanda mombongo ya sika.

src: Elena: That's great! What kind of business?
trg: Elena: Ezali malamu! Mombongo ya ndenge nini?

src: Kevin: I'm not sure yet.

src: The little girl stood on the street corner, shivering in the cold.
trg: Mwana-mwasi ya moke atelemaka na nsonge ya balabala, azali kolenga na malili.

src: She was about to give up when she saw a man approaching.
trg: Azalaki pene ya kotika ntango amonaki mobali moko azali kopusana.

src: He looked like he was in a hurry, but he stopped when he saw the little girl.
trg: Ezalaki komonana neti azali kokende noki, kasi atelemaki ntango amonaki mwana-mwasi wana ya moke.

src: "What are you doing out here all alone?" he asked.
trg: "Ozali kosala nini libanda awa yo moko?" atunaki.

src: "I'm trying to sell matches," the little girl said. "But no one will buy them."
trg: "Nazali koluka koteka ba allumette," wana eyano ya mwana-mwasi. "Kasi moto moko te asombi yango."

src: The little girl was so happy.

src: The elephants can roam freely without fear of being hunted, and the farmers can be sure that their crops will not be destroyed.
trg: Banzoko bakoki kotambola na kimya kozanga kobanga ete bakila bango, mpe basali-bilanga bakoki koyeba ete bakobebisa te milona na bango.

src: Radio collars are small devices that are attached to an animal's neck.
trg: Ba collier emetteur ezali ba aparei ya mike oyo batyaka na kingo ya nyama.

src: They emit a signal that can be tracked by a receiver.
trg: Epesaka signale oyo moto azozwa yango akoki kolandela.

src: This allows scientists to track the animal's movements over time.
trg: Esalisaka bato ya siansi na kolandela bisika oyo nyama yango ezali kokende.

src: In the case of elephants, this information can be used to create maps of their home ranges and to identify areas where they are most likely to come into conflict with humans.
trg: Mpo na banzoko, bakoki kosalela nsango oyo mpo na kosala bakarti ya bisika bafandaka mpe koyeba bisika oyo likoki ezali mingi ete baya kokutana na bato.

src: Farmers can use this information to take steps to protect their crops from elephants.
trg: Basali-bilanga basalelaka bansango oyo mpo na komibongisa na kobatela milona na banzoko.

src: They can build fences, plant thorny bushes, or use other methods to deter elephants from entering their fields.
trg: Bakoki kosala mapango, kolona banzete ya basende, to kosalela metode mosusu mpo na kobangisa banzoko na kokota na bilanga na bango.

src: By working together, scientists and farmers can help to keep both elephants and humans safe.
trg: Na kosalaka elongo, bato ya siansi na basali-bilanga bakoki kosalisa na kobatela banzoko mpe bato.

src: Here is an example of how radio collars have been used to help elephants and farmers.
trg: Oyo ndakisa ezolakisa ndenge basalela ba collier ya emetteur mpo na kosalisa banzoko mpe basali-bilanga.

src: In Kenya, scientists from the University of Cambridge have been working with local communities to track the movements of elephants.
trg: Na Kenya, bato ya siansi ya Iniversite ya Cambridge bazali kosala na bato ya bisika wana mpo na kolandela bisika banzoko bakendaka.

src: This information has been used to create maps of the elephants' home ranges.
trg: Basalelaka bansango oyo mpo na kosala bakarti ya bisika oyo banzoko bafandaka.

src: The maps have been shared with farmers, who have used them to build fences around their fields.
trg: Bapesaka bakarti wana na basali-bilanga, mpe basali-bilanga basalela yango mpo na kosala mapongo zingazinga ya bilanga na bango.

src: This has helped to reduce the number of conflicts between elephants and humans.
trg: Esalisa na kokitisa motango ya matata na kati ya banzoko mpe bato.

src: Radio collars are a valuable tool for studying elephants and for helping to reduce human-elephant conflict.
trg: Ba collier ya emetteur ezali bisaleli ya motuya mpo na koyekola banzoko mpe kosalisa na kokitisa matata kati na banzoko mpe bato.

src: They provide scientists with valuable information about elephant behavior, and they can help farmers to protect their crops.
trg: Epesaka bato ya siansi bansango ya ntina etali bizaleli ya nzoko, mpe ekoki kosalisa basali-bilanga na kobatela milona na bango.

src: By working together, scientists and farmers can help to create a future where elephants and humans can live together in harmony.
trg: Na kosalaka elongo, bato ya siansi na basali-bilanga bakoki kosalisa na kosala avenire esika banzoko na bato bakoki kofanda elongo na boyokani.

src: The Mali Empire was a West African empire that reached its peak in the 13th and 14th centuries.
trg: Bokonzi ya Mali ezali bokonzi moko na Afrika ya Weste oyo ezalaki makasi mpenza na ekeke ya 13 mpe ya 14.

src: It was founded by Sundiata Keita in 1235 and stretched from the Atlantic Ocean to the Niger River.
trg: Esalemaki na Sundiata Keita na 1235 mpe ezalaki kobanda na Mbu ya Atlantique mpe kokende kino na Ebale ya Niger.

src: The Mali Empire was a major center of trade and learning, and its rulers were known for their wealth and power.
trg: Bokonzi ya Mali ezalaki esika ya monene ya mombongo mpe ya koyekola, mpe bakonzi na yango bayebanaki mpo na bozwi mpe nguya na bango.

src: The empire declined in the 15th century, and was eventually conquered by the Songhai Empire in the 16th century.
trg: Bokonzi wana elembaki na ekeke ya 15, mpe nsukansuka balongaki yango na Bokonzi ya Songhai na ekeke ya 16.

src: One of the most important events in Mali's history was the Battle of Kirina in 1235.
trg: Moko ya makambo ya ntina mingi ya lisolo ya Mali ezalaki Bitumba ya Kirina na 1235.

src: This battle marked the end of the Ghana Empire and the rise of the Mali Empire.
trg: Bitumba oyo ezalaki nsuka ya Bokonzi ya Ghana mpe komata ya Bokonzi ya Mali.

src: Sundiata Keita, the founder of the Mali Empire, led his army to victory over the forces of the Ghana Empire.
trg: Sundiata Keita, mobandisi ya Bokonzi ya Mali, akambaki basoda na kolonga mampinga ya Bokonzi ya Ghana.

src: This victory gave Sundiata Keita control of the gold mines of the Sahel region, and helped to establish the Mali Empire as a major power in West Africa.
trg: Bolongi wana epesaki Sundiata Keita bokonzi ya koyangela mabulu ya wolo ya region ya Sahel, mpe esalisaka na kokomisa Bokonzi ya Mali nguya ya monene na Afrika ya Weste.

src: Another important event in Mali's history was the reign of Mansa Musa.
trg: Likambo mosusu ya ntina ya lisolo ya Mali ezali boyangeli ya Mansa Musa.

src: Mansa Musa was the third ruler of the Mali Empire, and he reigned from 1312 to 1337.
trg: Mansa Musa azalaki mokonzi ya misato ya Bokonzi ya Mali, mpe ayangelaki banda 1312 kino 1337.

src: In a Google spreadsheet, an absolute reference will always refer to the same cell, regardless of where it is copied or moved to.
trg: Na lokasa ya calcul ya Google, referanse absolue ekolobela kaka selile moko, ata soki bakopie yango esika nini to bamemi yango wapi.

src: Absolute references are useful for cells that contain data that you do not want to change when you copy or move the formula.
trg: Basalelaka bareferanse absolue mpo na baselile oyo ezali na badonnée oyo olingi kobongola te ntango ozali kokopie formule to komema yango esika mosusu.

src: For example, if you have a formula that calculates the total sales for each month, you would want to use an absolute reference for the cell that contains the starting date.
trg: Na ndakisa, soki ozali na formule oyo ezali kosala calcul ya koteka mobimba ya sanza nyonso, okolinga kosalela referansi absolue mpo na selila oyo ezali na dati ya ebandeli.

src: This way, the formula will always refer to the same cell, even if you copy it to a different row or column.
trg: Na lolenge wana, formule ekotalela ntango nyonso kaka selile moko ata soki okopie yango na molongo to na colonne mosusu.

src: You can create an absolute reference by adding a dollar sign ($) to the row number and column letter of the cell reference.
trg: Okoki kosala referansi absolue na kobakisaka elembo ya dolare ($) na nimero ya molongo mpe likomi ya colonne ya selile ya referansi.

src: For example, the absolute reference for the cell A1 would be $A$1.
trg: Na ndakisa, referansi absolue ya selile A1 ekozala $A$1.

src: You can also use absolute references to reference a range of cells.
trg: Okoki mpe kosalela bareferansi absolue mpo na kolobela baselile ebele.

src: To do this, add a dollar sign to the row number and column letter of each cell in the range.
trg: Mpo na kosala yango, bakisa elembo ya dolare na nimero ya molongo mpe likomi ya colonne na selile nyonso ya liboke wana.

src: For example, the absolute reference for the range A1:B1 would be $A$1:$B$1.
trg: Na ndakisa, referansi absolue ya molongo A1:B1 ekozala $A$1:$B$1.

src: Absolute references are a powerful tool that can be used to make your formulas more flexible and easier to use.
trg: Bareferansi absolue ezali esaleli ya makasi oyo okoki kosalela mpo na kosala baformule oyo ekoki kobongwana mpe ezali pete na kosalela.

src: By understanding how to use absolute references, you can create formulas that will work even when you copy or move them to different locations.
trg: Soki oyebi ndenge ya kosalela bareferansi absolue, okoki kosala baformule oyo ekosimba ata ntango okopie to omemi yango na bisika mosusu.

src: Here are some additional tips for using absolute references:
trg: Oyo mwa batoli mosusu mpo na kosalela bareferansi absolue:

src: * Use absolute references for cells that contain data that you do not want to change.
trg: * Salela bareferansi absolue mpo na baselile oyo ezali na badonnée oyo olingi te ebongwana.

src: * Use relative references for cells that contain data that you do want to change.
trg: * Salela bareferansi relative mpo na baselile oyo ezali na badonnée oyo olingi ebongwana.

src: * Be careful when using mixed references, which are references that contain both absolute and relative references.
trg: * Zala mayele ntango ozali kosalela bareferansi esangani, oyo ezali bareferansi oyo ezali na bareferansi absolue mpe relative.

src: * Use the F4 key to toggle between absolute, relative, and mixed references.
trg: * Salela F4 mpo na kotambola kati ya bareferansi ya absolue, ya relative, mpe esangana.

src: By following these tips, you can use absolute references to create powerful and flexible formulas that will make your work in Excel easier and more efficient.
trg: Soki osaleli mayele oyo, okoki kosalela bareferansi absolue mpo na kosala formule ya makasi mpe ebongwanaka oyo ekosala ete mosala na yo na Excel ezala pete mpe malamu mingi.

src: This is because they do not feed on blood.
trg: Ezali bongo mpo balyaka te makila.

src: Instead, they feed on nectar from flowers.
trg: Kasi, balyaka ba nectare ya bafololo.

src: Female mosquitoes, on the other hand, do feed on blood.
trg: Atako bongo, bangungi ya basi balyaka makila.

src: They need blood in order to produce eggs.
trg: Bazalaka na mposa ya makila mpo na kobota maki.

src: Male mosquitoes are attracted to light, so they are often found near windows and doors.
trg: Bangungi ya mibali ebandamaka na pole, yango wana bazalaka mbala mingi pene ya bafenetre mpe baporte.

src: They are also attracted to the smell of sweat and CO2.
trg: Ebendamaka mpe na bansolo ya mutoki mpe ya CO2.

src: Female mosquitoes are attracted to the same things, but they are also attracted to the smell of certain chemicals in human blood.
trg: Bangungi ya basi ebandamaka na biloko ya ndenge moko, kasi ebendamaka mpe na nsolo ya biloko mosusu ya chimie oyo ezalaka na makila ya bato.

src: When a female mosquito bites a human, she injects saliva into the skin.
trg: Soki ngungi ya mwasi eswi moto, ekotisaka soi na kati ya mposo ya nzoto.

src: This saliva contains anticoagulants, which prevent the blood from clotting.
trg: Soi wana ezalaka na ba anticoagulant, oyo ekangaka makila mpo ekoma bambuma te.

src: The mosquito then sucks up the blood.
trg: Na nsima ngungi emelaka makila.

src: Mosquito bites can cause itching and swelling.
trg: Koswa ya ngungi epesaka mokusa mpe evimbisaka.

src: In some cases, they can also cause an allergic reaction.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu, ekoki kobimisa reaction ya allergie.

src: The most common type of allergic reaction to mosquito bites is hives.
trg: Reaction ya allergie oyo eyebana mingi nsima ya koswa ya ngungi ezali likwanza babengi urticaire.

src: Hives are red, raised bumps that appear on the skin.
trg: Urticaire ezali likwanza ya monene mpe ya kovimba oyo emonanaka na mposo ya nzoto.

src: They can be itchy or painful.
trg: Ekoki kosala mokusa to kopesa mpasi.

src: In rare cases, mosquito bites can cause more serious problems.
trg: Na bandakisa moke, koswa ya ngungi ekoki komema maladi ya makasi.

src: For example, some people can develop an infection at the site of the bite.
trg: Na ndakisa, bato mosusu bakoki kobela na esika oyo ngungi eswaki bango.

src: In some cases, mosquito bites can even lead to death.
trg: Na bandakisa mosusu, koswa ya ngungi ekoki komema kutu na liwa.

src: The best way to avoid mosquito bites is to wear long sleeves and pants when you are outdoors.
trg: Lolenge ya malamu mpenza ya kokima koswa ya ngungi ezali kolata bilamba ya maboko milai mpe bapantalon soki ozali libanda.

src: You should also use insect repellent.
trg: Osengeli mpe kosalela nkisi oyo ekimisaka bangungi.

src: If you do get bitten by a mosquito, you can apply a cold compress to the bite to relieve the itching and swelling.
trg: Soki ngungi eswi yo, okoki kotya cotton ya malili na esika wana mpo na kokitisa mokusa mpe kovimba.

src: You can also take an over-the-counter antihistamine to relieve the symptoms of an allergic reaction.
trg: Okoki komela mpe nkisi antihistamine mpo na kokitisa bilembo ya reaction ya allergie.

src: Mosquitoes are important carriers of disease.
trg: Bangungi ezali mpe biloko oyo ememaka maladi.

src: They can transmit a variety of diseases, including malaria, dengue fever, and yellow fever.
trg: Bakoki kopesa maladi ndenge na ndenge neti malaria, fievre ya makasi, mpe fievre jaune.

src: Mosquitoes are responsible for the deaths of millions of people each year.
trg: Bangungi ememaka liwa ya bamilio ya bato mbula nyonso.

src: There are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations.
trg: Ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kosalema mpo na kopekisa ngungi enyokola bato te.

src: One way is to reduce the number of places where mosquitoes can breed.
trg: Lolenge moko ezali ya kokitisa motango ya bisika oyo bangungi ekoki kobota.

src: This can be done by draining standing water and clearing away vegetation.
trg: Ekoki kosalema na kokausaka mai oyo etelemaka mpe kolongola matiti.

src: Another way to control mosquito populations is to use insecticides.
trg: Lolenge mosusu ya kokanga bangungi nzela ezali ya kosalela bankisi oyo ebomaka bango.

src: Insecticides can be used to kill mosquitoes both indoors and outdoors.
trg: Bokoki kosalela bankisi ya koboma bangungi na kati ya bandako mpe na libanda.

src: Mosquitoes are a major public health problem.
trg: Bangungi ezali likama ya monene ya kolongono ya nzoto ya bato nyonso.

src: However, there are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations and reduce the risk of mosquito-borne diseases.
trg: Kasi, ezali na makambo ebele oyo ekoki kosalema mpo na kokanga bangungi nzela ya konyokola bato mpe kokitisa likama ya maladi oyo eutaka na bangungi.

src: He taught that all beings are caught in a cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and that this cycle is perpetuated by our attachments to things in the world.
trg: Ateyaki ete bikelamu nyonso ekangami na sikle ya kobotama, liwa, mpe kobotama lisusu, mpe sikle oyo elandanaka na bokangami na biso na biloko ezali na mokili.

src: These attachments can be to anything, from material possessions to ideas and beliefs.
trg: Bokangami wana ekoki kozala na eloko nyonso, banda na biloko ya mosuni kino na makanisi mpe bindimeli.

src: When we are attached to something, we become possessive and controlling, and we suffer when we lose or cannot have what we want.
trg: Soki tokangami na eloko moko, tokomisaka yango ya biso mpe toyangelaka yango, mpe tonyokwamaka soki tobungisi yango to tokoki te kozwa eloko tolingi.

src: The Buddha taught that the way to end suffering is to let go of our attachments.
trg: Buddha ateyaki ete lolenge ya kosukisa mpasi ezali ya kolongola bokangami na biso.

src: This is not easy, but it is possible through meditation and other spiritual practices.
trg: Ezali te pete, kasi ekoki kosalema na nzela ya komanyola mpe na misala mosusu ya elimo.

src: When we let go of our attachments, we become free from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and we can experience true peace and happiness.
trg: Soki totiki bokangami na biso, tolongwaka na sikle ya kobotama, kokufa, mpe kobotama lisusu, mpe tokoki kozwa kimya mpe esengo ya solo.

src: One of the most important things to remember when trying to let go of our attachments is that we are not our possessions.
trg: Moko ya makambo ya ntina mingi ya kobosana te ntango tozali kotika bokangami na biso ezali ete tozali te biloko na biso.

src: We are not our ideas or beliefs.
trg: Tozali te makanisi to bindimeli na biso.

src: We are simply beings who are experiencing the world through our senses.
trg: Tozali kaka bikelamu oyo bazali kosepela na mokili na nzela ya mayoki na biso.

src: When we can see ourselves in this way, it becomes easier to let go of the things that we think we need to be happy.
trg: Soki tokoki komimona na lolenge oyo, ekokoma pete na kotika biloko oyo tokanisaka ete tozali na mposa na yango mpo na kozala na esengo.

src: Letting go of our attachments does not mean that we have to give up everything.
trg: Kotika bokangami na biso elimboli te ete tozali kotika biloko nyonso.

src: It simply means that we need to be able to let go of things when it is time.
trg: Elimboli kaka ete tosengeli kozala na makoki ya kotika biloko soki ezali ntango ya kosala yango.

src: We need to be able to let go of the things that are no longer serving us, and we need to be able to let go of the things that we are attached to out of fear or insecurity.
trg: Tosengeli kozala na makoki ya kotika biloko oyo ezali lisusu te kosalisa biso, mpe tosengeli kozala na makoki ya kotika biloko oyo mpo na bobangi to insécurité.

src: When we can let go of our attachments, we open ourselves up to a new world of possibilities.
trg: Ntango tokoki kotika biloko tokangama na yango, tofungolaka nzela na mokili ya sika ya mabaku ebele.

src: We become free to live our lives in a way that is true to ourselves, and we become free to experience the joy and happiness that is our birthright.
trg: Tokomaka na bonsomi ya kozala na bomoi na lolenge oyo ezali solo mpo na biso moko, mpe tokomaka na bonsomi ya kozwa esengo mpe bolamu oyo ezali lotomo na biso ya mbotama.

src: Trains have been a vital part of transportation for centuries.
trg: Bingunduka ezala eteni ya ntina ya transport banda bikeke ebele.

src: They are a safe, efficient, and reliable way to travel long distances.
trg: Ezali lolenge ya malamu, ebongi, mpe kotyela motema ya kokende na bisika ya mosika.

src: However, the railroad industry requires regular updates to keep pace with the changing needs of passengers.
trg: Kasi, mosala ya nzela ya engunduka esengaka kobongisa mbala na mbala mpo na komesana na bamposa ya bakiliya oyo ebongwanaka.

src: One of the most important updates that trains need is the installation of new safety features.
trg: Moko ya biloko ya ntina mingi ya bingunduka ezali mposa ya kotya biloko ya sika ya libateli to securité.

src: In recent years, there have been a number of high-profile train accidents, which have highlighted the need for better safety measures.
trg: Na mibu euti koleka, ezalaki na ba aksida mingi ya makasi ya bingunduka, oyo emonisaki polele mposa ya miango ya malamu ya libateli to sécurité.

src: New safety features such as positive train control (PTC) can help prevent accidents by automatically stopping trains that are traveling too fast or that are about to collide with another train.
trg: Biloko ya sika ya libateli neti kolandela malamu engunduka (PTC) ekoki kosalisa na kokanga aksida esalema te na kokangaka automatiquement engunduka oyo ezali kotambola mbango koleka to oyo elingi kotutana na engunduka mosusu.

src: Another important update that trains need is the installation of new technology.
trg: Eloko mosusu ya sika ya ntina oyo bingunduka ezali na mposa na yango ezali kotya teknolozi ya sika.

src: In the past, trains were powered by steam engines.
trg: Na kala, bazalaki kotambwisa bingunduka na bamashine ya mopepe.

src: However, steam engines are inefficient and pollute the environment.
trg: Kasi, bamashine ya mopepe ezali makasi te mpe ebebisaka mopepe.

src: Today, most trains are powered by diesel engines or electric motors.
trg: Lelo, bingunduka mingi esalaka na bamashine ya mazute to ya bamotere ya lotiliki.

src: These engines are more efficient and environmentally friendly.
trg: Bamotere oyo ezali malamu mpenza mpe ebebisaka te mopepe.

src: In addition to safety and technology updates, trains also need to be updated to accommodate the needs of passengers.
trg: Longola biloko ya sika ya securité to libateli mpe ya teknolozi, bingunduka ezali mpe na ntina ya kobakisa biloko ya sika mpo na komesana na bamposa ya bakiliya.

src: In recent years, there has been an increase in the number of passengers who travel by train.
trg: Na mibu euti koleka, motango ya bato oyo basalaka mobembo na bingunduka emataki makasi.

src: This has led to overcrowding on trains, which can make for a less comfortable and enjoyable experience.
trg: Yango esala ete bato bazala ebele mpenza na kati ya bingunduka, ekoki kosala ete mobembo ezala malamu te to kitoko te.

src: She had always been a talented painter, but after her loss, she found that she was no longer interested in painting pretty landscapes or still lifes.
trg: Azalaka ntango nyonso peintre ya mayele, kasi nsima ya kobungisa ye, amonaki azalaki kosepela lisusu te na kosala bapeinture ya ba paysage to ya biloko oyo etambolaka te.

src: Instead, she began to create dark, brooding works of art that reflected her inner turmoil.
trg: Ksi, abandaka kosala misala ya art ya moindo mpe ezali kotungisa oyo ezali komonisa mitungisi azali na yango.

src: One of her most famous paintings, "The Death of My Son," is a stark and disturbing image of a young boy lying in a coffin.
trg: Moko ya ba peinture eyebana mingi, "Liwa ya Mwana na Nga," ezali elili ya kokesena mpe ezali kotungisa ya elenge mobali alili na kati ya sanduku.

src: The boy's face is peaceful, but his body is twisted and contorted in pain.
trg: Elongi ya elenge mobali ezali na kimya, kasi nzoto na ye ebebi mpe azali na mpasi.

src: The painting is full of symbolism, and it is clear that Mary is using her art to process her grief and anger.
trg: Peinture etondi na bilembo, mpe ezali polele ete Maria azali kosalela art na ye mpo na kolakisa mawa mpe nkanda na ye.

src: Mary's shift in artistic style was not without its critics.
trg: Mbongwana ya lolenge ya kosala art ya Maria ezali na bato oyo bazalaki kolobela yango mabe.

src: Some people accused her of being exploitative and insensitive.
trg: Bato mosusu bafundaki ye ete azali kobuba mpe kokipe te mayoki ya bato.

src: Others said that her paintings were too depressing and that they should not be shown in public.
trg: Basusu balobaki ete ba peinture na ye ezalaki ya mawa mingi mpe ete basengeli kolakisa yango te na bato nyonso.

src: However, Mary refused to back down.
trg: Kasi, Maria aboyaki kozonga nsima.

src: She believed that her art was important, and she wanted to share it with the world.
trg: Azalaki kokanisa ete art na ye ezalaki ntina, mpe azalaki kolinga kokabola yango na mokili mobimba.

src: Mary's work eventually found an audience, and she became one of the most respected artists of her time.
trg: Nsukansuka mosala ya Maria ezwaki bayoki, mpe akomaki moko ya bato ya art oyo bato batosaka mingi na ntango na ye.

src: Her paintings are now considered to be masterpieces, and they are still studied and admired by people all over the world.
trg: Bato balobaka sikoyo ete ba peinture na ye ezali misala ya kitoko koleka, mpe bato bakobaka koyekola yango mpe kosepela na yango na mokili mobimba.

src: Mary's story is a reminder that art can be a powerful tool for expression.
trg: Lisolo ya Maria ezali kokundwela biso ete art ekoki kozala esaleli ya makasi ya komonisa makanisi.

src: It can be used to process grief, anger, and other difficult emotions.
trg: Ekoki kosalelama na kobimisa mawa, nkanda, mpe mayoki mosusu ya mpasi.

src: It can also be used to communicate important messages about the human condition.
trg: Ekoki kosalelama mpe mpo na kolobela bansango ya ntina etali ndenge bato bazali.

src: Mary's paintings are a testament to the power of art, and they continue to inspire people to this day.
trg: Ba peinture ya Maria ezali kondimisa nguya ya art, mpe ezali kokoba kopesa bato makanisi kino lelo.

src: Sudan is a country in northeastern Africa.
trg: Soudan ezali ekolo moko ya ezali na norde-este ya Afrika.

src: It is bordered by Egypt to the north, Libya to the northwest, Chad to the west, the Central African Republic to the southwest, South Sudan to the south, Ethiopia to the southeast, and Eritrea to the east.
trg: Ekangama na Ezipito na norde, na Libye na norde-weste, na Tchad na weste, na Repiblike Centre Africaine na sude-weste, na Soudan du Sud na sude, na Ethiopie na sude-este, mpe na Érythrée na este.

src: Sudan has a population of over 40 million people and a land area of over 1.8 million square kilometers.
trg: Soudan ezali na bato koleka bamilio 40 mpe mokili na yango ezali monene koleka 1,8 milio ya bakilometre.

src: Sudan's history is long and complex.
trg: Lisolo ya Soudan ezali ya molai mpe ya mindondo.

src: The area has been inhabited by humans for thousands of years, and the first known civilization in Sudan was the Kingdom of Kush, which flourished from around 750 BC to 350 AD.
trg: Bato bafandaka kuna banda bankoto ya bambula, mpe sivilizasio ya liboso eyebana na Soudan ezalaki Bokonzi ya Kush, oyo ezalaki kotambola malamu pene ya 750 BC kino 350 AD.

src: Kush was a powerful kingdom that controlled much of the Nile River valley.
trg: Kush ezalaki bokonzi ya makasi oyo ezalaki koyangela eteni monene ya lobwaku ya Ebale Nile.

src: In the 7th century AD, Sudan was conquered by the Arabs, who brought Islam to the region.
trg: Na ekeke 7 AD, balongaki Soudan na ba Arabe, oyo bamemaki lingomba ya mizilma kuna.

src: Sudan was ruled by a series of Arab sultanates for centuries, until it was conquered by Egypt in 1821.
trg: Soudan eyangelamaki na bakonzi ebele ya ba Araba na bikeke ebele, kino balongaki yango na Ezipito na 1821.

src: Egypt ruled Sudan until 1885, when it was conquered by the Mahdi, a religious leader who led a rebellion against Egyptian rule.
trg: Ezipito eyangelaki Soudan kino 1885, ntango balongaki yango na Mahdi, mokonzi moko ya lingomba oyo akambaki bato oyo batombokelaki bokonzi ya Ezipito.

src: The Mahdi's rule was short-lived, and Sudan was reconquered by the British in 1898.
trg: Boyangeli ya Mahdi esalemi ntango moke, mpe balongaki lisusu Soudan na Grande-Bretagne na 1898.

src: My dear daughter, I know you've been wondering about the nature of light and darkness.
trg: Mwana na nga ya mwasi oyo nalingaka, nayebi ozali komitungisa mpo na pole mpe molili.

src: It's a big question, and one that scientists have been trying to answer for centuries.
trg: Ezali motuna monene, mpe motuna oyo bato ya siansi bazali koluka kozwa eyano banda bikeke ebele.

src: But I think I can give you a simple explanation that will help you understand it a little better.
trg: Kasi nakanisi nakoki kopesa yo ndimbola ya pete oyo ekosalisa yo na koyeba yango mwa malamu.

src: Light is a kind of energy that travels in waves.
trg: Pole ezali lolenge ya energie oyo etambolaka lokola mopepe.

src: We can see light because it enters our eyes and stimulates the retina, which is a light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye.
trg: Tomonaka pole mpo ekotaka na miso na biso mpe elendisaka retina, oyo eloko oyo ezali sensible na pole mpe ezalaka na nsima ya liso.

src: The retina sends signals to our brain, which interprets them as images.
trg: Retina etindaka ba signale na boongo na biso, mpe boongo ezwaka yango lokola bilili.

src: Darkness is the absence of light.
trg: Molili ezali kozanga pole.

src: When there is no light, we can't see anything.
trg: Soki pole ezali te, tokoki komona eloko te.

src: Light and darkness are two opposites, but they're also two sides of the same coin.
trg: Pole na molili ezali biloko mibale ekeseni, kasi ezali mpe bangombo mibale ya mbongo kaka moko ya libende.

src: Light is needed for us to see, but darkness is also important.
trg: Pole ezalaka ntina mpo tomona, kasi molili ezali mpe ntina.

src: Darkness helps us to rest and sleep.
trg: Molili esalisaka biso na kopema mpe kolala.

src: It also creates a sense of mystery and wonder.
trg: Esalisaka mpe na komona neti ezali na limbombami mpe komitungisa.

src: So next time you're outside at night, take a moment to appreciate the darkness.
trg: Yango wana mbala ya nsima oyo okozala libanda na butu, zwa ntango ya kosepela na molili.

src: It's just as important as light, and it has its own beauty.
trg: Ezali mpe ntina lokola pole, mpe ezali mpe na kitoko na yango.

src: Esteban was a concerned father.
trg: Esteban azalaki papa oyo azalaki komitungisa.

src: His daughter, Marcela, was listening to music that he didn't approve of.
trg: Mwana na ye ya mwasi, Marcela, azalaki koyoka miziki oyo papa azalaki kolinga te.

src: The lyrics were explicit and violent, and he didn't want his daughter exposed to that kind of material.
trg: Maloba ezalaki ya mabe mpe ya mobulu, mpe papa azalaki kolinga te ete mwana na yo alanda makambo ya ndenge wana.

src: He tried to talk to her about it, but she just shrugged him off.
trg: Amekaki kosolola na ye mpo na yango, kasi mwana abwakisaki ye.

src: He didn't know what else to do.
trg: Ayebaki te nini mosusu kosala.

src: One day, Esteban was listening to the radio when he heard a song that he thought Marcela would like.
trg: Mokolo moko, Esteban azalaki kolanda radio mpe ayokaki loyembo moko oyo akanisaki ete Marcela akolinga.

src: It was a catchy tune with a positive message.
trg: Ezalaki na ton mpe nsango ya malamu.

src: He decided to burn a copy of the song and give it to her.
trg: Azwaki ekateli ya kosala kopi ya loyembo wana mpe kopesa mwana na ye.

src: When she got home from school, he gave her the CD and told her to listen to it.
trg: Ntango mwana azongaki ndako nsima ya kelasi, papa apesaki ye CD mpe ayebisaki ye na koyoka yango.

src: Marcela was surprised by the gift, but she was also intrigued.
trg: Marcela akamwaki kado wana, kasi azalaki komituna.

src: She put the CD in her stereo and listened to the song.
trg: Akotisaki CD wana na stereo na ye mpe ayokaki loyembo wana.

src: She liked it so much that she listened to it over and over again.
trg: Alingaki yango mingi yango wana ayokaki yango mbala ebele.

src: The next day, Esteban asked Marcela what she thought of the song.
trg: Mokolo elandaki, Esteban atunaki Marcela soki azali kokanisa nini mpo na loyembo wana.

src: She told him that she loved it and that it had made her think about things in a new way.
trg: Ayebaki papa ete azalaki kolinga yango mpe ete epusaka ye na kotalela makambo na ndenge ya sika.

src: Esteban was thrilled.
trg: Esteban asepelaki.

src: He knew that he had made a difference in his daughter's life.
trg: Ayebaki ete asalaki likambo ya motuya mingi na bomoi ya mwana na ye.

src: From that day on, Marcela listened to more positive music.
trg: Banda mokolo wana, Marcela ayokaka miziki ya malamu koleka.

src: Question: My male neighbor complains of fatigue, sleep disturbances and thinks he has Sleeping sickness (Human African Trypanosomiasis) and asks, Doctor, how can I manage this sleeping sickness, as it has been affecting my work schedule?
trg: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali koyoka kolemba, mpongi ezali kokimakima ye mpe azali kokanisa ete azwi maladi ya mpongi (Trypanosomiase ya bato ya Afrika) mpe atuni, Monganga, lolenge nini nakoki kolandela maladi oyo ya mpongi, mpamba te, ezali kobebisa pologalame na ngai ya mosala?

src: Answer: While I understand your concern about sleeping sickness and how it's impacting your work, it's extremely unlikely that you have it, especially if you live in an area where it isn't endemic (like North America or Europe).
trg: Eyano: Atako nazali koyoka mitungisi na yo na oyo etali maladi ya mpongi mpe bopusi na yango na mosala na yo, ezali mpasi ozala na yango, mingimingi soki ofandaka na bisika oyo maladi epalangani makasi te (lokola Amerika ya Nordi mpe mikili ya Mpoto).

src: Human African Trypanosomiasis is primarily found in rural Africa and is transmitted through the bite of the tsetse fly.
trg: Maladi ya mpongi ezwamaka mingimingi na bamboka ya Afrika mpe ewutaka na koswa ya nzinzi ya etuná.

src: Have you recently travelled to sub-Saharan Africa?
trg: Owuti kosala mobembo na mboka moko ya Afrika ya sudi ya Sahara?

src: Your symptoms of fatigue and sleep disturbances are common and can be caused by a wide range of things, from stress and poor sleep hygiene to underlying medical conditions like sleep apnea, thyroid issues, or even depression.
trg: Bilembo na yo ya nzoto kolemba mpe kozanga mpongi ezali eloko oyo ekomaka mpe ekoki kowuta na biloko kilikili, totangi konyokwama na makanisi, nzoto bosoto, maladi oyo ebombami na nse lokola kokangama ya mpema, maladi ya thyroide mpe mpasi ya makanisi.

src: It's crucial to see a doctor to get a proper diagnosis.
trg: Kokende epai ya monganga ezali eloko ya motuya mpo na kosalisa ekzame oyo esengeli.

src: They will likely ask you detailed questions about your symptoms, medical history, travel history, and lifestyle.
trg: Bakotuna yo mituna ebele na mae matali bilembo na yo, maladi na yo ya kala, bisika oyo osala mobembo mpe lolenge ya bomoi.

src: They might also recommend some tests, like blood work, to rule out other potential causes.
trg: Bakoki mpe kosenga yo osalisa baekzame misusu, lokola baekzame ya makila, mpo na kolongola biwutelo misusu.

src: Do not self-treat or attempt to diagnose yourself with sleeping sickness.
trg: Komizwela yo moko nkisi te mpe komeka te komisala yo moko baekzame ya maladi ya mpongi.

src: It's a serious disease that requires specialized medical care and specific medications.
trg: Ezali bokono ya makasi oyo ezali kosenga bolandeli ya monganga monene mpe bankisi oyo esengeli.

src: Trying to treat it yourself could delay a proper diagnosis and treatment for the real cause of your symptoms.
trg: Komeka kobundisa yango biso moko ekoki kowumisa elombo moko mpe nkisi oyo esengeli mpo na ewutelo ya solo ya bilembo na yo.

src: So, to manage your fatigue and sleep disturbances, your first and most important step is to schedule an appointment with your doctor as soon as possible.
trg: Na yango mpo na kobundisa kolemba na yo mpe kozanga na yo ya mpongi, etambe ya liboso mpe ya motuya ezali ya kozwa programe ya kokutana na monganga na yo ntangu nyonso.

src: Explain your concerns and be honest about your symptoms.
trg: Limbolela ye mitungisi na yo mpe loba solo na mae matali bilembo na yo.

src: They are the best resource to help you figure out what's going on and recommend the right course of action.
trg: Bazali lisungi monene mpo na kosalisa yo na koyeba penza oyo ozali na yango mpe kolakisa yo lolenge malamu ya kosala makambu.

src: In the meantime, try to practice good sleep hygiene: maintain a regular sleep schedule, create a relaxing bedtime routine, and avoid caffeine and alcohol before bed.
trg: Liboso, meka kozala na bopeto ya malamu na mae matali mpongi: landela programe moko ya kolala, luka momesano moko ya kosala yambo ya kolala mpe tika komela biloko oyo ezali na kafé liboso ya komata na mbetu.

src: Question: My female friend complains of bleeding, neck pain and thinks she has Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever and asks, I hope it is not a dreadful thing?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya mwasi azali kobimisa makila, azali koyoka mpasi na kingo mpe azali kobanza ete azali na fefele ya makila ya Crimee-Congo mpe Atuni, Nazali kolikya ete ezali likama monene penza te?

src: Answer: Tell your friend to immediately go to a hospital or doctor.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo akende na lobangu epai ya monganga moko to na lopitalo.

src: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) is a serious viral disease and requires prompt medical attention.
trg: Fefele ya makila ya Crimee-Congo (CCHF) ezali bokono ya makasi oyo esengaka kolandelama na monganga.

src: It's not something to take chances with.
trg: Ezali eloko ya kosakana na yango te.

src: Trying to self-diagnose or treat it is dangerous.
trg: Komeka komizwela nkisi to komitalela yo moko ezali likama.

src: While bleeding and neck pain can be symptoms of CCHF, they are also symptoms of many other illnesses, some far less serious.
trg: Atako kobimisa makila mpe koyoka mpasi na kingo ezalaka bilembo ya bokono ya CCHF, ezalaka mpe bilembo ya maladi kilikili, misusu oyo ezalaka makasi penza te.

src: A doctor will be able to determine what's actually causing her symptoms and provide appropriate treatment.
trg: Monganga akoki kozala na makoki ya koyeba ndimbola ya solo ya bilembo na ye mpe kopesa ye nkisi oyo ebongi.

src: Reassure her that getting checked out is the best course of action, regardless of the cause.
trg: Kitisa motema na ye na kolakisa ye ete kokende kosalisa baekzame ezali eloko ya malamu ya kosala, ezala bilembo ya ndenge nini.

src: Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for CCHF and many other conditions.
trg: Ekzame moko mpe nkisi na lobangu ezali eloko ya motuya mpo na bokono ya CCHF mpe bamaladi misusu.

src: Question: My male neighbor complains of jaundice, fever, bleeding and thinks he has Yellow Fever and asks, What are the causes
trg: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai ya mobali azali na loposo ya mosaka, azali na fefele mpe kobima makila. Azali kobanza ete azali na bokono ya Kongo mpe atuni boye: Ewutaka wapi

src: Answer: While your neighbor's symptoms do overlap with Yellow Fever, it's crucial to understand that self-diagnosing is dangerous, especially with a serious illness like Yellow Fever.
trg: Eyano: Atako bilembo ya mozalani na yo ezali ndenge moko na oyo ya bokono ya Kongo, ezali likambo ya ntina koyeba ete komitalela biso moko ezalaka likama, mingimingi mpo na maladi lokola bokono ya Kongo.

src: He needs to see a doctor immediately for proper testing and diagnosis.
trg: Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu mpo na kosalisa baekzame oyo esengeli.

src: Yellow fever is caused by the yellow fever virus, which is spread through the bite of an infected Aedes aegypti mosquito.
trg: Bokono ya Kongo ewutaka na virisi ya Kongo, oyo epalanganaka na koswa ya ngungi babengi Aedes aegypti oyo azali na maladi.

src: These mosquitoes also transmit diseases like Zika and Dengue.
trg: Bangungi yango epesaka lisusu bamaladi lokola Zika mpe Dengue.

src: It's not contagious from person to person.
trg: Okoki kopesa yango bato mosusu te.

src: Essentially, the only cause of Yellow Fever is infection with the yellow fever virus transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito.
trg: Na bokuse, Bokono ya Kongo ewutaka na virisi ya Kongo oyo yaka na koswa ya ngungi oyo ezali kobela yango.

src: There's no other way to contract it.
trg: Lolenge mosusu ya kozwa bokono yango ezali te.

src: It's important to reiterate that your neighbor needs professional medical attention.
trg: Ezalika eloko ya motuya mingingi kokundola ete mozalani na yo azali na mposa ya lisalisi ya monganga.

src: His symptoms could be from a number of other illnesses, some serious, and delaying proper diagnosis and treatment can have serious consequences.
trg: Bilembo na ye ekoki kowuta na bamaladi misusu kilikili, misusu ezali ya makasi koleka, kozongisa ekzame mpe nkisi oyo ebongi na nsima ekoki komema mbeba ya makasi.

src: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills, headache and thinks she has Malaria and asks, Malaria is more common with people coming from Mozambique.
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi ya mwasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe mutu mpasi. Azali kokanisa etre azali na malaria mpe atuni soki malaria ezalaka mini na bato oyo bautaka mboka ya Mozambique.

src: So are you from there and how do you know you got it?
trg: Toloba ete owuti kuna mpe ndenge nini oyebi ete ozali na yango?

src: Answer: "I understand you're not feeling well and are worried about malaria.
trg: Eyano: Nazoyokela yo mawa na ndenge ozali komiyoka malamu te mpe mitungisi na yo mpo na malaria.

src: It's definitely important to take symptoms like fever, chills, and headache seriously.
trg: Ezali mpeza eloko ya motuya kotalela bilembo lokola bafefele, kolenga mpe mutu mpasi.

src: However, I can't diagnose you, and self-diagnosing can be risky.
trg: Kasi nakoki kosala penza ekzame te mpe mbano ekoki kopesa likama.

src: Lots of illnesses share those symptoms.
trg: Maladi ebele ezalaka na bilembo ya lolenge moko.

src: As for your question about where I'm from and my health, I’d prefer not to share personal details.
trg: Na oyo etali motuna na yo mpo na mboka na ngai mpe kolongono ya nzoto na ngai, nalingi te tolobela yango.

src: The most important thing right now is for you to see a doctor to figure out what's going on and get the right treatment.
trg: Eloko ya ntina na miniti oyo ezali ete okokoka kokutana na monganga mpo na ozwa ndimbola ya makambu mpe kozwa nkisi oyo ebongi.

src: They can run tests to determine if it’s malaria or something else and give you the best advice.
trg: Bakoki kosala baekzame mpo na koyeba soki ezali malaria penza, to biloko mosusu mpe kopesa yo ba toli ya malamu.

src: Delaying proper medical care can be harmful, so please make an appointment as soon as possible."
trg: Kozangisa na nsima likambu ya kolanda nkisi epai ya monganga ekoki kozala mabe, kende kokutana na monganga noki.''

src: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills and thinks she has Malaria and asks, "What specific precautions or measures should I take to prevent malaria recurrence?"
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi ya mwasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe azali kobanza ete azali na malaria mpe Atuni boye, "Makambu nini nakosala penza mpo na koboya kozonga ya malaria ?"

src: Answer: Tell your classmate that it's crucial she doesn't self-treat and sees a doctor immediately for diagnosis and treatment.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo ya kelasi ete asengeli komizwela nkisi te mpe akende kokutana na monganga na lobangu mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi.

src: Malaria can be serious, even fatal, if not treated promptly.
trg: Malaria ekoki kozala makasi penza, ntangu mosusu ekoki koboma, soki ozweli yango nkisi na lobangu te.

src: Suspecting malaria isn't the same as having a confirmed diagnosis.
trg: Kobanza ete ozali na malaria ezali lolenge moko te na kozwa mbano na yango na nsima ya ekzame.

src: Once she has seen a doctor and if she is diagnosed with malaria and completes her prescribed medication, these are some precautions she can take to prevent recurrence:
trg: Ntangu akokutana na monganga moko, soki bayebisi ye ete azali na malaria mpe ntangu akosilisa komela bankisi oyo bakokomela ye, tala makambu asengeli kosala mpo na koboya ezongela ye lisusu:

src: Continue preventative medication as prescribed: Her doctor may prescribe medication to be taken regularly during and after travel to malaria-endemic areas.
trg: Kokoba komela bankisi ya komibatela oyo bokomeli ye: Monganga na ye akoki kokomela ye bankisi ya komela mikolo nyonso na boumeli mpe na nsima ya kosala mobembo na bisika oyo malaria epalanganaka makasi.

src: It’s crucial to adhere to the prescribed regimen.
trg: Ezali eloko ya motuya kolandela nkisi bakomeli yo.

src: Mosquito bite prevention is paramount:
trg: Komibatela na koswa ya bangungi ezali eloko ya motuya:

src: Sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets (ITNs): Ensure the net is properly tucked in and has no holes.
trg: Lela na mosikitele oyo ezali na nkisi ya koboma banyama-nkeke (ITNs): sala ete mosikitele ezala ya kokota malamu mpe ezali na lidusu te.

src: Wear long-sleeved clothing and long pants, especially during dawn and dusk: Mosquitoes are most active during these times.
trg: Lata bilamba ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo ya milayi, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa: Bangungi bazalaka makasi na ntangu wana.

src: Use insect repellents containing DEET (diethyltoluamide), picaridin, or IR3535: Follow the instructions on the product label.
trg: Salela bankisi oyo ebenganaka ba nyama-nkeke oyo ezali na DEET (diethyltoluamide), pikardini to IR3535: landa malako oyo ezali na nkoma oyo ezali likolo.

src: Consider using mosquito coils or insecticide-treated vaporizers indoors.
trg: Kanisa kosalela bibaluka oyo ebenganaka bangungi to masini ya kopupola oyo ezali na nkisi ya nyama-nkeke na kati.

src: Eliminate mosquito breeding grounds around her home: This includes removing standing water from flower pots, buckets, and other containers.
trg: Boma bandako ya banyama oyo bangungi esalaka na nzinganzinga ya naku: Yango elakisi kolongola mayi oyo etelamaka na banzungu ya fololo, bakatini to bibombeli misusu.

src: If travelling to malaria-endemic regions again, consult her doctor well in advance: They can recommend appropriate preventative medication and other precautionary measures based on the specific region and her medical history.
trg: Soki akosala lisusu mobembo na bisika oyo malaria ezali kopalangana makasi, kutana liboso na monganga: akoki kokomela ye bankisi oyo ebongi ya komela liboso mpe kosala makambu misusu na kolanda esika mpe maladi na ye ya kala.

src: Be aware of potential relapse symptoms and seek immediate medical attention if they occur: Even after treatment, malaria parasites can sometimes persist in the liver and cause a relapse.
trg: Tya likebi penza na bilembo oyo ekoki komonisa konzolea ya maladi mpe kutana na lobangu na monganga soki bilembo ezongi lisusu: Atako na nsima ya komela nkisi moko, virisi ya malaria ekoki kobombama na libale mpe kozongela yo lisusu.

src: Again, the most important first step is to encourage her to seek immediate medical attention.
trg: Nalobi yango lisusu, litambe ya liboso oyo ezali ya ntina ezali kolendisa ye mpo na kokutana na monganga moko na lobangu.

src: Don't delay!
trg: Kozela te!

src: Question: What precautions should I take to prevent the spread of typhoid fever to others, particularly my household members or close contacts?
trg: Motuna: Makambo nini nakoki kosala mpo na koboya kopalangana ya fefele ya typhoide na batu mosusu, mingimingi na bato na ngai ya libota mpe bamisusu oyo nafandaka na bango?

src: Answer:
trg: Eyano:

src: Typhoid fever is a serious bacterial infection that can spread easily to others through contaminated food and water or close contact.
trg: Fefele ya typhoide ezali bokono moko ya mikrobe ya makasi oyo ekoki kopalangana na pete na batu mosusu na nzela ya bilei mpe mayi to na kosimba makasi.

src: Here's a breakdown of the precautions:
trg: Tala bozongeli moko ya makambu ya kosala:

src: Handwashing: This is the single most important measure.
trg: Kosukola maboko: Ezali likambu ya motuya mingi.

src: Thorough handwashing with soap and water, especially after using the toilet and before handling food, removes bacteria and prevents transmission.
trg: Kosukola maboko malamu na mayi mpe sabuni, mingimingi na nsima ya kowuta zongo mpe liboso ya kosimba bilei, ezali koboma mikrobe mpe kopekisa kopalangana na yango.

src: Disinfecting Contaminated Surfaces: Typhoid bacteria can survive on surfaces.
trg: Kopetolama ya bisika oyo ezali na mikrobe: Mikrobe ya typhoide ekoki kofanda na bisika mingi.

src: Regularly disinfecting frequently touched surfaces like countertops, doorknobs, and bathroom fixtures with a household disinfectant helps prevent spread.
trg: Petola mbala na mbala bisika ya polele oyo osimbaka mingimingi lokola kontware, bisimbeli ya bikuke mpe bisaleli ya kikoso na nkisi ya kopetola na yango, ezali kopekisa kopalangana.

src: Food Handling Precautions: Individuals with typhoid fever should not prepare or serve food for others while they are ill and for a period after recovery as determined by a healthcare professional.
trg: Makebisi na kosalela bilei: bato oyo bazali na fefele ya typhoide basengeli te kolamba to kokabola bilei na batu misusu na boumeli ya bokono na bango mpe na nsima ya eleko moko soki basilisi komela nkisi, na kolanda lolenge ekomama na monganga.

src: This prevents contamination of food.
trg: Yango nde ezali kopekisa bokono na bilei.

src: Avoid Sharing Personal Items: Sharing personal items like towels, utensils, and drinking glasses can spread the bacteria.
trg: Tika kosalela biloko moko na bato misusu: Kosalela biloko moko na batu lokola esume, bisaleli mpe bakopo ekoki kopalanganisa bamikrobe.

src: Each individual should use their own dedicated items.
trg: Moto na moto asengeli kosalela biloko na ye moko.

src: Vaccination: Typhoid vaccines are available and can provide substantial protection against the disease.
trg: Kokatama mangwele: Mangwele mpo na kobundisa typhoide ezali komonana mpe ekoki kobatela moto na maladi.

src: Vaccination is recommended for travelers to areas where typhoid is common and for individuals with close contact with a typhoid carrier.
trg: Mangwele masengami na baoyo bazali kosala mobembo na bisika oyo bokono ya typhoide ezali mingi mpe mpo na bato oyo bafandaki penza na baoyo babandaki kobela bokono ya typhoide.

src: Prompt Treatment: Getting prompt medical treatment with appropriate antibiotics helps shorten the duration of illness and reduces the risk of complications and spread to others.
trg: Nkisi na lobangu: Komela bankisi lokola baantibiotique oyo ebongi na lobangu ezali kosunga na kokitisa koumela ya maladi mpe kobatela na makama mpe na kopalanganisa yango na bamisusu.

src: It's also crucial to complete the full course of antibiotics even if symptoms improve.
trg: Ezali mpe malamu makasi kokende kino na nsuka ya baantibiotique oyo ozali komela atako bilembo esi esila.

src: Question: My male coursemate complains of fever, chills, sweats and thinks he has Malaria and asks, I have had malaria for the 3rd time this year, Is there any preventive measures that can be taken?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe motoki. Abanzi azali na malaria mpe atuni: Nazali na malaria elandani mbala 3 na mobu oyo. Ezali na makambu moko nakoki kosala mpo na kopekisa yango ezwa ngai?

src: Answer: "It sounds pretty rough dealing with what you think is malaria multiple times.
trg: Eyano: ''Ezali mpasi mingi kofanda na maladi oyo ozali kobanza ete ezali malaria mbala mingi bongo.

src: It's definitely worth getting checked out by a doctor each time to confirm the diagnosis and get the right treatment, because recurring fevers can be a sign of other things too.
trg: Ezali penza eloko ya motuna kokutana na monganga mbala nyonso mpo kondimisa ete ezali bongo maladi yango mpe kozwa lisalisi lisengeli, mpamba te, bafefele ya mbala na mbala ekoki mpe komonisa bokono mosusu.

src: Self-treating can sometimes mask the real problem.
trg: Komizwela biso moko nkisi ekoki kobomba bokono ya solo.

src: As for prevention, there are a few things you can do, especially if you're in an area where malaria is common.
