trg: Na mae matali komibatela, ezali na makambo moko oyo okoki kosala, mingimingi soki ofandaka na bisika malaria ezalaka ebele.

src: Using mosquito nets, especially ones treated with insecticide, is really important.
trg: Kosalela musikitele, mingimingi oyo ezali na nkisi ya bangungi, ezali eloko ya motuya.

src: Also, wearing long sleeves and pants, particularly during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active, can help.
trg: Kolata mpe biloko ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa ntangu bangungi bazali ebele, ekoki mpe kosunga.

src: There are also insect repellents containing DEET or picaridin that are effective.
trg: Ezali mpe na nkisi ya kobengana nango bangungi oyo ezali na DEET to pikaridini ya makasi na kati.

src: Some people also take antimalarial medication preventatively if they're traveling to or living in high-risk areas, but you should talk to a doctor about that to see if it's the right option for you and what type would be best.
trg: Batu misusu bamelaka bankisi ya kobundisa malaria mpo na komibatela na ntangu ya kosala mobembo to soki bafandaka na bisika ya likama makasi, kasi osengeli kolobela yango monganga moko mpo na kopesa yo liponi ya malamu mpo na yo.

src: They can assess your individual risk and make sure you're aware of any potential side effects."
trg: Bakoki kotalela likama na yo moko mpe kolakisa yo bampasi nyonso oyo eyaka na nsima.''

src: Question: My male neighbor complains of joint pain, vomiting and thinks he has Rift Valley fever and asks, What measures can I take to prevent further transmission of Rift Valley fever to others, especially considering its potential for spreading through mosquito bites or contact with infected animals?
trg: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali koyoka matonga mpasi, kosanza mpe abanzi azali na bokono ya fefele ya ngomba ya Rift. Atuni: Makambo nini nakoki kosala mpo na kozanga kopanza bokono ya fefele ya ngomba ya Rift na batu mosusu, na kotalela mingimingi bokasi ya bopalangani bwa yango na koswa ya bangungi to kosimbasimba ba nyama oyo bazali kobela yango?

src: Answer: Tell your neighbor he needs to see a doctor immediately to get a proper diagnosis and treatment.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa mozalani na yo ete asengeli kokende kokutana na monganga kaka sikoyo mpo na kosalisa baekzame mpe kozwa lisalisi oyo esengeli.

src: Rift Valley Fever can be serious, and self-treating is dangerous.
trg: Fefele ya ngomba ya Rift ekoki kozala makasi mpe komizwela nkisi ekoki kobimisa likama monene.

src: While waiting for medical attention, he should take the following precautions to minimize the risk of spreading the disease (if it is indeed RVF):
trg: Na kozela nkisi ya monganga, asengeli kosala makambu oyo mpo na kokitisa likama ya kopanza bokono oyo (soki ezali penza bokono ya RVF):

src: Mosquito bite prevention: This is paramount.
trg: Komibateka na koswa ya bangungi: Ezali eloko ya motuya koleka.

src: He should use mosquito repellent containing DEET, picaridin, or IR3535 liberally.
trg: Asengeli kosalela makasi penza nkisi ya kobenganela bangungi oyo ezali na DEET, pikardini, to IR3535.

src: He should wear long sleeves, long pants, and socks whenever possible, especially during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active.
trg: Asengeli kolata biloko ya maboko milayi, pantalo ya molayi mpe elamba ya nse ya bozito, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa ntangu bangungi bazalaka mingi.

src: Mosquito netting around his bed would also be helpful.
trg: Kotya musikitele na mbetu na ye ezali mpe na motuya.

src: Eliminate standing water around his home where mosquitoes breed (e.g., flower pots, buckets, discarded tires).
trg: Kolongola mayi oyo etelemaka na nzinganzinga ya ndaku esika wapi bangungi babotamaka (na ndakisa, nzungu ya fololo, bakantini, piné ya kala).

src: Animal contact precautions: Avoid contact with any animals, especially livestock, that appear sick or are dead.
trg: Libateli na oyo etali kosimbasimba ba nyama: Boya kosimbasimba nyama nyonso, mingimingi bibwele oyo ezali komonana maladi to baoyo bakufa.

src: If he must handle animals (e.g., he's a farmer), he should wear protective clothing, including gloves and a mask.
trg: Soki asengeli kosimbasimba banyama (na ndakisa soki azali mosali bilanga) asengeli kolata bilamba ya komibatela, mingimingi ba gan mpe maske.

src: He should not slaughter any animals himself and should report any suspicious animal deaths to the local veterinary authorities.
trg: Asengeli te komibomela ye moko banyama mpe asengeli kolakisa liwa nyonso ya nyama oyo ezali kokamwisa na baminganga oyo balandelaka makambu ya nyama.

src: Raw milk should not be consumed – it must be pasteurized.
trg: Asengeli komela miliki ya malili te, asengeli kotya yango na moto.

src: Hygiene: Frequent handwashing with soap and water is crucial, especially after handling animals or animal products.
trg: Bopeto: Kosokola mingi maboko na mayi mpe sabuni ezali eloko ya motuya koleka, mingimingi na nsima ya kosimbasimba banyama to biloko oyo ewutaka na bango.

src: Avoid touching his eyes, nose, and mouth with unwashed hands.
trg: Tika komisimba misu, zolo mpe monoko na maboko oyo esokolami naino te.

src: He should also practice good hygiene when coughing or sneezing, covering his mouth and nose with a tissue or his elbow.
trg: Asengeli lisusu kozala na bopeto ya malamu ntangu azali kokosola to kosala likisé, na kozipa monoko to zolo na mwa elamba ya maboko to lipeko.

src: He should avoid sharing personal items like towels, eating utensils, and drinking glasses.
trg: Asengeli kotika kosalela biloko na ye moko elongo na batu misusu lokola sani to kopo.

src: Isolation (to a reasonable extent): While complete isolation might not be necessary at this stage (before a diagnosis), he should limit close contact with others as much as possible until he sees a doctor.
trg: Kokabwana na bato (na lolenge moko ya malamu): Atako kokabwana penza na batu nyonso ezali naino na ntina te (liboso ya kosalisa ekzame), asengeli kokitisa bokutani na bato misusu tii na ntangu akokutana na monganga.

src: This is particularly important for pregnant women, who are at higher risk of severe complications from RVF.
trg: Yango ezali na motuya mingi mpo na basi ya zemi oyo bazali na likama monene ya kozwa mikakatano mingi oyo ewuti na RVF.

src: Emphasize to your neighbor again that these are precautionary measures and do not replace the need to see a doctor immediately.
trg: Yebisa lisusu mozalani na yo ete oyo elandi ezali bongoi makambu ya kosala kaka mpo na komibatela kasi ezali kolongola ata moke te bokutani na monganga na lombangu.

src: A blood test is needed to confirm the diagnosis and appropriate treatment will be necessary.
trg: Asengeli kosalisa ekzame ya makila mpo na kondimisa bokono mpe kozwa nkisi oyo esengeli.

src: Also, if he suspects he has RVF, he needs to inform local health authorities so they can monitor the situation and take appropriate public health measures.
trg: Kutu soki azali komiyoka ete azwi bokono ya Fefele ya ngomba ya Rift (RVF) asengeli koyebisa yango na mbala moko bataleli ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto mpo bakoka kotalela likambo mpe kozwa bikateli bisengeli mpo na kobatela bato.

src: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills, headache and thinks she has Malaria and asks, Besides testing for malaria, are there any other potential causes for my symptoms, especially considering my recent travel history?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasiazali kolenga, koyoka mutu pasi mpe azali kobanza ete azali kobela malaria mpe Atuni boye, Longola ekzame ya kotalela malaria, ekoki kozala na biwutlo mosusu ya bilembo na ngai, na kotalela mingimingi mibembo na ngai nawuti kosala?

src: Answer: Yes, absolutely.
trg: Eyano: Ee, ezali.

src: While malaria is a possibility, especially with travel to a malaria-endemic region, several other illnesses can cause fever, chills, and headache.
trg: Atako ekoki kozala malaria, mingimingi soki osalaki mobembo na esika oyo malaria epanzanaka mpamba mpamba, babokono misusu ekoki mpe kosala yo fefele, kolenga mpe mutu pasi.

src: Depending on where she traveled, some of the possibilities include:
trg: Na kolanda bisika akendaki, botala makoki:

src: Other mosquito-borne illnesses: Dengue fever, Zika virus, Chikungunya virus, and West Nile virus all share similar symptoms with malaria.
trg: Bokono misusu ewutaka na bangungi: maladi ya dengue, irisi ya z, virisi ya chikungunya mpe virisi ya Nile, yango nyonso ezali na bilembo ya ndenge moko na malaria.

src: Viral infections: Influenza, common cold, COVID-19, and other viral infections can cause these symptoms.
trg: Bokono ya mimpumpululu: Gripe, miyoyo, corona mpe bokono misusu ya mimpumpululu ekoki komonisa mpe bilembo yango.

src: Bacterial infections: Typhoid fever, urinary tract infections, and bacterial pneumonia can also present with fever, chills, and headache.
trg: Bokono ya bavirisi: fefele ya typhoidi, bokono ya nzela ya masuba mpe bokono ya mpema ekoki mpe komonisama na fefele, kolenga mpe moto mpasi.

src: Tick-borne illnesses: Lyme disease, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and other tick-borne illnesses can cause these symptoms, though headache is less prominent in some.
trg: Mpe bokono misusu ewutaka na basili ekoki kobimisa bilembo yango, atako mutu mpasi eyokanaka mingi te epai bato misusu.

src: Parasitic infections: Other parasitic infections besides malaria, like amebiasis or giardiasis (depending on where she travelled and what she ate/drank) are possibilities, though they often come with gastrointestinal symptoms as well.
trg: Bokono ya mikrobe: Bokono misusu ya mikrobe na malaria na kati, lokola amibiaze to giardiaze (na kolanda bisika wapi asalaki mobembo, biloko alyaki mpe amelaki) ekoki komonana, atako mingimingi yango ebelisaka libumu.

src: Heat stroke/heat exhaustion: If she was in a hot climate and exerted herself, this could be a cause.
trg: Moto na nzoto/kolemba likolo ya moto: Soki azalaki na klima ya moto mpe asalaki mosala makasi, ekoki kozala moko ya biwutelo.

src: Other less common infections: Depending on the region of travel, things like leptospirosis or brucellosis could be considered, although these are less common.
trg: Bokono misusu oyo ekutanaka na mpasi: Na kolanda esika oyo asalaki mobembo, maladi lokola leptospirose to brucellose ekoki mpe kotangama, atako ezwamaka na mpasi.

src: It's crucial that she tell her doctor exactly where she traveled and what she did there (e.g., hiking, swimming in fresh water, eating street food).
trg: Ezali likambo ya ntina akoka koyebisa polele na monganga na ye esika wapi asalaki mobembo mpe makambo asalaki kuna (na ndakisa, kotambola makolo, kosukola na mayi ya moto, bilei batekaka na balabala).

src: This information will help the doctor narrow down the possibilities and order the appropriate tests.
trg: Makambo yango ekosalisa monganga ya kokitisa motango ya makoki mpe kokomela yo baekzame oyo esengeli.

src: It's important she doesn't self-treat and seeks professional medical advice.
trg: Ezali ntina makasi koboya komizwela nkisi ye moko mpe akende kokutana na monganga.

src: Question: My male coursemate complains of fever, chills, sweats and thinks he has Malaria and asks, What specific precautions or preventive measures should I take to avoid contracting malaria in the future, especially if I'm traveling to endemic areas?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali kolenge lenga, azali kotoka mpe abanzi ete azali na malaria. Makambo nini akoki kosala mpo na komibatela na likama oyo ya kozwa malaria na mikolo mizali koya, mingimingi soki nasali mobembo na bisika epai wapi malaria ezali kopalangana makasi?

src: Answer: Tell your friend to see a doctor immediately to get tested and treated if he does have malaria.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo mpo akende kokutana mbala moko na monganga mpo asalisa baekzame mpe azwa nkisi ya malaria.

src: It's not something to mess around with.
trg: Ezali eloko ya kozwa na maseki te.

src: As for his question about prevention, here's what you can tell him:
trg: Na oyo etali motuna na ye mpo na komibatela, tala makambo oyo tokoki koyebisa ye:

src: Malaria prevention is multi-pronged and depends heavily on where he's travelling, as different regions have different mosquito species and resistance patterns.
trg: Komibatela na bokona ya malaria ezali na makambo ebele ya kosala mpe ezali kotalela mingimingi bisika epai wapi asalaka mibembo, mpamba te, bisika kilikili ezali na bangungi ya ndenge na ndenge mpe bokasi na bango ezalaka na lolenge moko te.

src: He should consult a travel health specialist or his doctor for personalized recommendations, but generally speaking, here are the key precautions:
trg: Asengeli kokutana na nganga buka ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto ya baoyo basalak amibembo to mpe monganga na ye moko mpo na kopesa ye ba toli ebongi na ye, kasi na bokuse, tala makambo ya ntina oyo akoki kosala:

src: Antimalarial medication: This is crucial.
trg: Ba nkisi ya kobundisa malaria: Ezali eloko ya motuya koleka.

src: There are several different types, and the best one for him will depend on his destination, medical history, and other factors.
trg: Ezalaka ya ndenge na ndenge, mpe oyo ya malamu penza ekotalela esika azali kosala mobembo, makambo na ye ya kala na mae matali maladi mpe makambu mosusu.

src: A doctor needs to prescribe this, and it's often taken before, during, and after the trip.
trg: Monganga moko asengeli kokomela ye yango mpe mingi mingi ezwamaka liboso ya kosala mobembo wana, na nzela mpe na nsima na yango.

src: Do not self-medicate.
trg: Komizwela nkisi yo moko te.

src: Mosquito bite prevention: This is the cornerstone of malaria prevention and includes:
trg: Komibatela na koswa ya bangungi: ezali libanga ya litumu na mae matali komibatela na malaria mpe osengeli:

src: Insect repellent: Use repellents containing DEET (20-50%), picaridin (20%), or IR3535 (20-30%).
trg: Nkisi ya kobenga nango bangungi: Salela nkisi oyo ezali na DEET (20-50%), pikardini (20%) to IR3535 (20-30%).

src: Apply to exposed skin and clothing, following product instructions.
trg: Kotya yango na loposo ya polele mpe na bilamba, na kolanda malako mapesameli na mosali na yango.

src: Long-sleeved clothing and pants: Wear loose, light-colored clothing that covers most of your body, especially during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active.
trg: Bilamba ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo: Lata bilamaba oyo etiki nzoto mpe ya langi ya pole oyo ezali kozipa eteni monene ya nzoto na yo, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa, ntangu bangungi bazalaka makasi.

src: Treat clothing with permethrin insecticide for added protection (don't apply directly to skin).
trg: Tya nkisi ya koboma na yango nyama-nkeke oyo esalema na permethrine na kati na bilamba na yo mpo na komibatela na bangungi (kopakola nkisi yango na loposo ya nzoto te).

src: Mosquito nets: Sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets, ensuring they are properly tucked in and have no holes.
trg: Mosikitele: Lala na nse ya mosikitele oyo etyami na nkisi ya nyama-nkeke, tala soki okotisi yango malamu mpe soki ezali na madusu te.

src: Mosquito-proof accommodation: Stay in places with screened windows and doors, or use air conditioning to keep mosquitoes out.
trg: Ndaku oyo ekotisaka bangungi te: Fanda na bisika oyo ezali na maninisa mpe bikuke ebombama na mosikitele, to salela bapakapaka ya malili mpo na kopekisa kokota ya bangungi.

src: Consider mosquito coils or vaporizers if needed.
trg: Kanisa mpe kosalela bilingama oyo ebenganaka bangungi to masini ya kopupola.

src: Environmental control: While this is more of a public health measure, being aware helps.
trg: Kotalela nzinganzinga: Atako ezali likambo oyo etalaka misala ya leta oyo elandelaka kolongono ya nzto ya bayi mboka, bolendisi ezali na motuya.

src: Minimizing standing water around accommodations can reduce breeding grounds for mosquitoes.
trg: Kokitisa mayi oyo etelemaka nzinganzinga ya ndaku ekoki koboma bisika mingi oyo ebotaka bangungi.

src: Be aware of symptoms: Even with precautions, there's a small risk of contracting malaria.
trg: Tya llikebi na yo na bilembo: Atako osali makambo wana mpo na komibatela, okoki kaka kozwa maladi ya malaria.

src: Knowing the symptoms (fever, chills, sweats, headache, muscle aches, fatigue, nausea, vomiting) is crucial.
trg: Koyeba bilembo (fefele, kolenga, motoki, mpasi na misunyi, kolemba, koyoka motema ya kobaluka, kosanza) ezali na ntina mingi.

src: If he develops any of these during or after travel to a malaria-endemic area, he should seek medical attention immediately.
trg: Soki abandi moko ya bilembo oyo naboumeli to na nsima ya kosala mobembo moko na esika epai wapi malaria epalanganaka mingi, asengeli kokutana na monganga mbala moko.

src: Early diagnosis and treatment are essential.
trg: Kosala ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi noki ezali malamu penza.

src: Again, emphasize to your friend that seeing a doctor right away is the most important step right now for his health.
trg: Loba lisusu na moninga na yo ete, kokende noki kokutana na monganga na ye ezali litambe moko ya motuya mpo na kolongono ya nzoto na ye.

src: These prevention tips are for future trips.
trg: Ba toli ya lolenge ya komibatela oyo ezali mpo na mibembo na yo mizali koya.

src: Question: My male neighbor complains of fever, rash and thinks he has Dengue Fever and asks, "What specific precautions should I take to prevent dengue fever complications?"
trg: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali na fefele mpe azali kobanza ete azali kobela bokono ya Dengue. Azali kotuna ngai: "Makambu nini oyo nakoki kosala mpo na koboya mikakatano ya fefele?''

src: Answer: Tell your neighbor that since he suspects dengue fever, it's crucial he see a doctor immediately for proper diagnosis and management.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa mozalani na yo ete lokola azali kobanza na fefele ya Dengue, ezali malamu makasi akende kosalisa baekzame noki epai ya monganga mpo na koyeba mpe kozwa lisalisi oyo ebongi.

src: Dengue can be dangerous, and complications can arise quickly.
trg: Fefele ya Dengue ekoki kokoma likama monene mpe kokola na yango ekoki kosalema mbangu.

src: Self-treating is risky.
trg: Komizwela nkisi ekoki komema likama penza.

src: While waiting for his appointment, he should:
trg: Na kozela bokutani na ye, asengeli:

src: Rest: This helps the body fight the infection.
trg: Kopema: Yango ezali kosalisa nzoto mpo na kobundisa bokono.

src: He needs to avoid strenuous activities.
trg: Asengeli koboya kosala misala ya makasi.

src: Hydrate: Drink plenty of fluids, like water, electrolyte solutions, or broths, to prevent dehydration, which is a common dengue complication.
trg: Mela mayi: Mala biloko ya maimai ebele, lokola mayi ya komela, biloko mosusu to supu, mpo na kopekisa kozanga mayi na nzoto, likama oyo ewutaka mingimingi na fefele ya Dengue.

src: Avoid sugary drinks.
trg: Boya bimeli oyo esalemi na sukali.

src: Pain Relief: He can take over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen (Tylenol) to manage fever and pain.
trg: Kosilisa mpasi: Akoki kosomba nkisi ya kokitisa na yango mpasi oyo eekemaka pambapamba lokola acetaminophene (Tylenol) mpo na kokitisa fefele mpe mpasi.

src: Absolutely avoid ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), aspirin, and naproxen (Aleve) as these can increase the risk of bleeding, a serious dengue complication.
trg: Boya penza ibuprofene (Advil, Motrin), aspirine mpe naproxene (Aleve), mpamba te ekoki kobimisisa yo makila, oyo ezali likama monene ya fefele ya Dengue.

src: Monitor for Warning Signs: He should watch closely for any warning signs like severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums, rapid breathing, or fatigue/restlessness.
trg: Kotalela bilembo ya likebisi: Asengeli kolandela elembo nyonso ya likebisi lokola mpasi makasi na libumu, kosanzasanza, makila na minu, kopema na lobangu, kolemba/ kozala likolo likolo.

src: If any of these occur, he should seek immediate medical attention, potentially going to the emergency room.
trg: Soki moko ya bilembo oyo emonani, asengeli kokutana noki na monganga, mpe ntangu mosusu kokende na lopitalo.

src: These could indicate severe dengue.
trg: Makambo oyo elandi ekoki komonisa fefele ya Dengue ya makasi.

src: Mosquito Control: Even though he's already likely infected, he should prevent further mosquito bites to avoid spreading dengue to others.
trg: Bundisa bangungi: Atako azali kobela bokono yango, asengeli kokima koswa mosusu ya bangungi mpo na koboya kopalanganisa Dengue epai ya bato misusu.

src: This means using mosquito repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants, and sleeping under a mosquito net.
trg: Elingi koloba kosalela nkisi ya kobengana bangungi, kolata bapatalo ya mikuse mpe kolala na nse ya mosikitele.

src: Emphasize again that he needs to see a doctor as soon as possible.
trg: Lobela ye lisusu ete asengeli kokutana na monganga.

src: This advice is not a substitute for professional medical care.
trg: Toli oyo ezali kopekisa te kozwa misala ya nganga buka.

src: Question: My female friend complains of varied by disease and thinks she has Zoonotic Diseases and asks, What are the specific zoonotic diseases I should be concerned about based on my activities, lifestyle, and environment, and how can I prevent them
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ezali komonisa bilembo kilikili, azali kobanza ete azali na maladi ya nyama babengi zoonoses mpe autuni ngai boye, Nasengeli kolandela virisi nini ya zoonoses na kotalela misala na ngai, lolenge na ngai ya kosalela bomoi mpe nzinganzinga na ngai, mpe lolenge nini nakoki komibatela

src: Answer: It's important to preface this by saying I am not a medical professional.
trg: Eyano: Ezali na ntina ya kolakisa polele ete tozali kolobela nganga buka moko ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto.

src: Your friend needs to see a doctor, not ask the internet, especially since she believes she has multiple diseases.
trg: Moninga na yo asengeli kokende kokutana na monganga kasi kaka te kotuna na lifulume, mingimingi soki abanzi ete azali na maladi ebele.

src: Self-diagnosing zoonotic diseases is particularly dangerous as some can be serious if left untreated.
trg: Komizela nkisi ya maldi ya zoonoses ezali na likama monene, mpamba te misusu ekoki kozala mabe koleka soki bazweli yango nkisi te.

src: I can give some general information, but it should not be taken as medical advice.
trg: Nakoki kopesa malako ya minene, kasi yango esengeli te kotalelama lokola masengi ya monganga.

src: To answer her question properly, she needs to provide more information to a doctor.
trg: Mpo na koyanola penza na motuna na ye, asengeli komemela monganga makambu oyo.

src: However, some common zoonotic diseases and associated risk factors include:
trg: Kasi, bandenge misusu ya maladi ya zoonoses oyo eyebani mpe makama na yango etalelaka:

src: Common Zoonotic Diseases & Associated Risk Factors:
trg: Maladi ya zoonoses oyo eyebani mpe makama oyo ememaka:

src: Lyme disease: Transmitted by ticks.
trg: Maladi ya Lyme: Ewtaka na bansili.

src: Risk factors include spending time in wooded or grassy areas, having pets that go outdoors, and not performing regular tick checks.
trg: Makama ezali kotalela kolekisa ntangu na kati ya ba nzete, kobokola banyama ya ndaku oyo ebimakabimaka mpe koboya kotalelama.

src: Rocky Mountain spotted fever: Also tick-borne.
trg: Fefele ya motane ya ngomba ya mabanga: Yango mpe ewutaka na bansili.

src: Similar risk factors to Lyme disease.
trg: Makama na yango ekokani na oyo ya maladi ya Lyme.

src: Toxoplasmosis: Caused by a parasite often found in cat feces and undercooked meat.
trg: Toxoplasmose: Ewutaka na mikrobe moko boye oyo ezalaka na mitsiopo mpe na mosunyi oyo ebeli malamu te.

src: Pregnant women and individuals with weakened immune systems are at higher risk.
trg: Basi ya zemi mpe bato oyo bibundeli ya nzoto na bango ekomi ya kolemba bakoki kolokota yango na pete.

src: Gardening and handling cat litter are risk factors.
trg: Bilanga mpe kosimbasimba bilaleli ya nyau ekoki komonisa makama.

src: Rabies: Transmitted through the bite of an infected animal (e.g., bats, raccoons, skunks).
trg: Kanda: Ewutaka na koswa ya nyama-nkeke oyo azali na bokono (na ndakisa bangembo, bapuku, ngambala).

src: Risk factors include contact with wildlife, especially if the animal is behaving strangely.
trg: Makama mawutaka mingimingi na bokutani na banyama ya zamba, ntangu nyama asalaka makambu na lolenge ya malamu te.

src: Salmonella and Campylobacter: Bacterial infections often acquired through contact with contaminated food (especially poultry, eggs, and unpasteurized milk), reptiles, or contaminated water.
trg: Salmonella mpe Campylobacter: bokono ya bamikrobe oyo ewutaka na bilei oyo ezali na bokono (bansoso, maki mpe miliki ya malili), banyama oyo elandaka na libumu to mayi.

src: Ringworm: A fungal infection that can be transmitted from animals (especially cats and dogs) to humans through direct contact.
trg: Mpomboli: maladi oyo ezala lokola mayebo ewutaka na banyama (mingimingi banyau mpe bambwa) na kosimba bango.

src: Psittacosis (Parrot Fever): A bacterial infection spread by birds, particularly parrots, parakeets, and pigeons.
trg: Psittacose (fefele ya tshaku): bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ezwaka mingimingi batshaku, ndeke ya perruche, mpe bibenga.

src: Risk factors include handling infected birds or inhaling dust from their droppings.
trg: Makama ewuta mingimingi na kosimba ba ndeke oyo ezali na bokono to kosimba ba nyei na bango.

src: Leptospirosis: A bacterial infection spread through contact with the urine of infected animals (e.g., rodents, livestock).
trg: Leptospirose: Bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ewutaka na masuba ya banyama oyo bazali na maladi (na ndakisa bapuku, banyama).

src: Risk factors include exposure to contaminated water or soil.
trg: Makama ewutaka mingimingi na kosimba biloko oyo ezali na bokono lokola mayi to mabele.

src: Prevention:
trg: Komibatela:

src: General preventative measures for zoonotic diseases often include:
trg: Makambu minene ya kosala mpo na komibatela na zoonoses ezali:

src: Regular handwashing: Especially after handling animals, their food, or waste.
trg: Kosokola maboko ntangu nyonso: mingimingi na nsima ya kosimba bilei to bosoto.

src: Safe food handling: Cook meat thoroughly, wash fruits and vegetables, and avoid unpasteurized dairy products.
trg: Esaleli ya malamu ya bilei: Kolamba na kobelisa penza musuni, kosokola ndunda mpe koboya komela miliki oyo ezali na moto te.

src: Tick checks: After spending time outdoors, thoroughly check yourself, your children, and your pets for ticks.
trg: Kolandela bansili: Na nsima ya kolekisa ntangu libanda, mitalela, talela bana na yo mpe banyama na yo ya ndaku mpo na kolukaluka bansili.

src: Remove them promptly and correctly.
trg: Longola yango noki mpe na lolenge esengeli.

src: Vaccinations: Vaccinate your pets against rabies and other diseases.
trg: Kokata mangwele: katisa banyama na yo ya ndaku mangwele ya maladi ya kanda.

src: There are also human vaccines for some zoonotic diseases (e.g., rabies).
trg: Ezali mpe na mangwele ya bato mpo na kobundisa ba ndenge mosusu ya maladi ya zoonoses (na ndakisa maladi ya kanda).

src: Pest control: Control rodent and insect populations in and around your home.
trg: Bundisa mikrobe: Landela ebele ya bapuku nyonso mpe ba nyama-nkeke na nzinganzinga ya ndaku na bino.

src: Avoid contact with wildlife: Do not handle or feed wild animals.
trg: Boya kosimbasimba banyama nyonso ya zamba: Kosalela to kosimba te.

src: Be cautious around unfamiliar animals, especially those exhibiting unusual behavior.
trg: Sala keba na banyama oyo oyebi te, mingimingi soki ezali komonisa ezaleli moko oyo omesana nango te.

src: Protective clothing: Wear long sleeves, pants, and closed-toe shoes in areas where ticks or other disease-carrying insects may be present.
trg: Bilamba ya komibatela: Lata bilamba ya maboko ya milayi, patalo moko mpe sapatu na bisika oyo ezali na bansili to biloko misusu oyo epesaka maladi ekoki kozala.

src: Use insect repellent containing DEET.
trg: Salela nkisi ya kobengana ba nyama-nkeke oyo ezali na DEET na kati.

src: Again, this is not medical advice.
trg: Nalobeli yango mosusu, oyo ezali ekomeli ya monganga te.

src: Your friend needs to consult a doctor.
trg: Moninga na yo asengeli kosalisa baekzame epai ya monganga.

src: Her concerns about having multiple zoonotic illnesses warrant professional medical evaluation.
trg: Mitungisi na ye na mae matali botaleli ya monganga mpo na bamaladi ebele ya zoonoses.

src: It's possible her symptoms have a different underlying cause altogether.
trg: Ntangu mosusu bilembo na ye ekoki kozala na ndimbola mosusu penza.

src: Encourage her to seek medical attention as soon as possible.
trg: Lendisa ye mpo na kokutana na monganga na lobangu.

src: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills and thinks she has Malaria and asks, What is the best way to treat malaria?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali na fefele, azali kobanza ete azali na malaria mpe atuni, Nkisi ya malamu penza mpo na kosilisa malaria ezali oyo wapi?

src: Answer: She needs to see a doctor immediately.
trg: Eyano: Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu.

src: Malaria is a serious illness and requires a proper diagnosis and prescription medication.
trg: Malaria ezali bokono monene oyo ezali kosenga kolandela nkisi oyo esengeli na mokanda ya monganga.

src: Self-treating can be dangerous and delay effective treatment, leading to complications.
trg: Komizwela nkisi ekoki kobimisa makama mpe kobebisa bolamu ya nkisi, yango nde ekoki komema mbemba.

src: Tell her to go to a doctor or clinic as soon as possible to get tested and receive the appropriate care.
trg: Yebisa ye mpo akende epai ya monganga to na lopitalo moko ntangu mosusu, mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi oyo esengeli.

src: Question: My male neighbor complains of severe itching, blindness and thinks he has Onchocerciasis (River Blindness) and asks, Are there any over the counter supplements that I can use regularly to prevent this from going further?
trg: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali na maladi makasi ya kokufa-miso mpe azali kobanza ete bokono ya Onchocercose (kokufa-miso) mpe atuni boye: Ezali na nkisi moko oyo batekaka pambapamba oyo akoki kobanda kosalela ntagu nyonso mpo na kosala ete maladi yango ekola te?

src: Answer: Tell your neighbor that he absolutely should not attempt to self-treat suspected onchocerciasis with over-the-counter supplements.
trg: Eyano: Yebisa mozalni na yo ete asengeli te komizwela nkisi ye moko soki azali kobanza ete ekoki kozala Onchocercose na kozanga mokanda ya monganga.

src: There are no over-the-counter supplements that prevent or treat river blindness.
trg: Ezali na eloko ata moko te ya kobakisa na bilei na kozanga mokanda ya monganga oyo ekoki kosilisa kokufa-miso oyo ewuti na mingala.

src: His symptoms (severe itching, blindness) are serious and warrant immediate medical attention from a qualified doctor.
trg: Bilembo (mokusa ya makasi, kokufa-miso) ezali penza makasi mpe ezali kosenga penza lisalisi ya monganga na lobangu.

src: He needs to be properly diagnosed and, if he does have onchocerciasis, receive the appropriate prescription medication.
trg: Asengeli kosalisa malamu baekzame mpe, soki bazwi ye na bokono yango ya Onchocercose, azwa nkisi ya monganga oyo ebongi.

src: Delaying proper medical care can lead to permanent vision loss and other serious complications.
trg: Kozongisa nkisi ya monganga na nsima ekoki komemela yo bambeba ya ntangu nyonso mpe mikakatano ya makasi.

src: He should see a doctor as soon as possible.
trg: Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu.

src: Question: My male friend complains of blood in urine, abdominal pain and thinks he has Schistosomiasis and asks, Is schistosomiasis associated to genetics; what I mean is, can this condition be passed from one generation to the other?
trg: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya mobali azali komona makila na masuba, azali koyoka libumu mpasi mpe azali kobanza ete azali na bokono babengi schistosomiase. Bokono ya schistosomiase ezali bokono oyo babotamaka na yango? Maladi wana oyo etambolaka na molongo nyonso ya libota ellimboli nini?

src: Answer: No, schistosomiasis is not a genetic disease and cannot be passed directly from parents to their children through genes.
trg: Eyano: Te, bokono ya schistosomiase ezalaka bokono oyo babotama na yango te mpe ekoki te kolongwa na papa mpo na kokanga mwana na nzela ya kobotama.

src: It's a parasitic infection caused by flatworms called schistosomes.
trg: Ezali bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ewutaka na banyama moko epapala bebengaka schistosomes.

src: You get it by coming into contact with contaminated freshwater where the parasite larvae live.
trg: Tozwaka yango soki tomeli mayi moko oyo ezali na bokono oyo, esika wapi banyama oyo bafandaka.

src: These larvae penetrate the skin and develop inside the body.
trg: Banyama yango ezali kokota na loposo ya nzoto mpe ezali kokola na kati ya nzoto.

src: So, while family members might be at higher risk if they share the same contaminated water source, it's due to shared environmental exposure, not inheritance.
trg: Yango wana, atako bato ya libota moko bakoki kozwa likama yango bango nyonso lokola bazali kosalela mayi moko, yango ewuti na likambo ya kosalela nzinganzinga moko, kasi te na likambo ya kobotama.

src: He should definitely see a doctor to get diagnosed and treated properly, as untreated schistosomiasis can lead to serious long-term health issues.
trg: Asengeli penza kokutana na monganga mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi oyo ebongi, mpamba te, bokono ya schistosomiase soki ezwi nkisi te ekoki komemela yo makama ya nzoto mingi na mikolo mizali koya.

src: Dear Dr. Ibrahim,
trg: Molingami Dr. Ibrahim,

src: I am writing to refer my patient, Mrs. Valentina Gallo, for further evaluation and management of persistent neck pain. Mrs. Gallo is a 34-year-old stay-at-home mother who has been experiencing discomfort in her neck region for the past three weeks.
trg: Nakomeli yo mpo na kotinda mobeli na ngai, Madame Valentina Gallo, mpo na botaleli mpe boalndeli malamu ya bampasi na ye ya nkingo oyo ezali koumela. Mradame Gallo azali mama ya bana oyo avandaka na ndako, azali na mibu 34, mpe azali koyoka mpasi na nkingo na ye banda baposo misato oyo eleki.

src: Mrs. Gallo reports that the pain is dull and aching, occasionally radiating to her shoulders and upper back. She describes the pain as worse in the mornings and after prolonged periods of sitting or standing. She denies any recent trauma or injury to the area.
trg: Madame Gallo alobi ete mpasi yango ezali makasi mpe ezali kopesa ye mpasi mingi, ntango mosusu ezali komata kino na mapeka na ye mpe na mokongo na ye na likolo. Alobi ete mpasi yango eyokanaka makasi mingi na ntongo mpe nsima ya kofanda to kotelema ntango molai. Alobi atikala kozwa likama moko to pota moko te na esika yango.

src: Upon examination, I noted tenderness along the cervical paraspinal muscles and limited range of motion in her neck, particularly with rotation and lateral flexion. Neurological examination was unremarkable, with no signs of weakness or sensory deficits in her upper extremities.
trg: Ntango natalaki ye, namonaki ete misisa ya nkingo na ye ezalaki na mpasi mpe akokaki te koningisa nkingo na ye malamu, mingi mingi ntango azali kobalula yango to kogumba yango na mopanzi. Ekzamɛ ya boongo emonisaki eloko moko te ya mabe, elembo moko te ya bolembu to ya kozanga koyoka na binama na ye ya likolo.

src: I have recommended conservative measures such as rest, heat application, and over-the-counter pain relievers, which have provided only minimal relief. Given the persistence of her symptoms and the impact on her daily activities, I believe a specialist evaluation is warranted to rule out any underlying pathology and determine the most appropriate course of treatment.
trg: Napesaki ye toli ya kopema, kotya eloko ya moto, mpe komela bankisi ya mpasi oyo etekamaka mpambapamba, kasi yango esalisaki ye mpenza te. Lokola bilembo na ye ezali koumela mpe ezali kopekisa ye kosala misala na ye ya mokolo na mokolo, nakanisi ete esengeli moto ya mayele atala ye mpo na koyeba soki azali na maladi mosusu na nse mpe koyeba nkisi oyo esengeli kopesa ye.

src: Mrs. Gallo is eager to return to her full capacity as a homemaker and is seeking a doctor's note to excuse her from her responsibilities for a period of time to allow for recovery. I would appreciate your assessment and recommendations regarding her condition and any necessary work restrictions.
trg: Madame Gallo azali na mposa makasi ya kozonga na mosala na ye lokola mama ya ndako mpe azali koluka mokanda ya monganga mpo na kopesa ye konje mpo apema mwa moke. Nakosepela soki okoki kotala ye mpe kopesa biso toli na yo mpo na maladi na ye mpe soki esengeli apekisama kosala misala mosusu.

src: Thank you for your time and expertise in evaluating Mrs. Gallo. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions or require further information.
trg: Matondi mpo na ntango na yo mpe mayele na yo na kotala Madame Gallo. Soki ozali na mituna to soki olingi koyeba makambo mosusu, kokakatana te mpo na kobenga ngai.

src: Sincerely,
trg: Na motema mobimba,

src: Dr. Mendoza Thompson
trg: Dr. Mendoza Thompson

src: Here's the draft account of a primary care appointment for prominent ears:
trg: Tala lisolo ya kokatama mpo na bokutani ya monganga ya liboso mpo na matoi minene:

src: So, I finally went to my GP, Dr. Majid, about my ears sticking out. It's something that's bothered me since I was a kid, you know? I was nervous to bring it up, but she was really understanding.
trg: Nsukasuka, nakei epai ya monganga na ngai ya GP, Dr. Majid, mpo na matoi na ngai oyo ebimi libanda. Ezali likambo oyo etungisaka ngai banda bomwana, oyebi? Nazalaki na kobanga kolobela yango, kasi azalaki mpenza na bososoli.

src: We talked about how it affects my confidence, and she examined them gently. She explained that it's a common condition called otoplasty, and that surgery is an option if I really want to change how they look. It's a bit scary to think about surgery, but she said it's usually a straightforward procedure with a quick recovery.
trg: Tosololaki ndenge nini yango ebebisaka komindima na ngai, mpe atalaki yango na bopolo. Alimbolaki ete ezali likambo ya momesano oyo babengaka otoplasti, mpe ete lipaso ezali moko ya maponi soki nalingi mpenza kobongola ndenge emonanaka. Ezali kobangisa mwa moke kokanisa mpo na lipaso, kasi alobaki ete mbala mingi ezalaka lolenge ya kosala ya pɛtɛ mpo na kobika noki.

src: Dr. Majid also mentioned that there are non-surgical options, like ear splints for babies, but obviously that ship has sailed for me! We discussed the pros and cons of surgery, the risks involved, and the expected outcome. She even showed me some before-and-after photos, which helped me visualize the potential change.
trg: Dr. Majid alobaki mpe ete ezali na maponi ya lipaso te, lokola masini babengi atele orikilere mpo na bana mike, kasi ezali komonana polele ete ete ntango wana eleki mpo na ngai! Tosololaki mpo na bolamu mpe mabe ya lipaso, makama oyo yango ememaka, mpe mbano oyo tozelaka. Atako alakisaki ngai mwa bililingi ya liboso mpe nsima, oyo esungaki ngai komona mbongwana oyo ekoki kosalema.

src: Hey there, Joe! Good to see you, even if it's not under the best circumstances. Have a seat, get comfy. How have you been holding up since we last saw each other?
trg: Mbote, Joe! Eza malamu komona yo, ata soki eza na libaku ya malamu te. Fanda penza malamu. Oza ndenge nini banda tomonanaki mbala ya nsuka?

src: I know today is a big day with the surgery coming up. It's completely normal to feel a bit anxious about it. But you're in good hands here, and we're going to take excellent care of you. Remember, this surgery is a crucial step towards getting you back to feeling like yourself again. We've talked about the procedure and what to expect, but do you have any last-minute questions or concerns on your mind? Anything at all, big or small.
trg: Nayebi ete lelo eza mokolo monene na lipaso oyo ezali koya. Eza mabe penza te komiyoka na mwa kobanga mpo na yango. Kasi ozali na maboko ya malamu awa, mpe tokobatela yo malamu mpenza. Kobosana te, lipaso oyo eza litambe ya ntina mpo na kozongisa yo nzoto malamu ndenge ozalaka. Tolobelaki lolenge ya kosala lipaso mpe nini tokoki kozela, kasi oza na mituna to mitungisi ya ntangu ya nsuka na makanisi na yo? Likambo nyonso, ya monene to ya moke.

src: Also, I wanted to touch base on your overall health. We've discussed your weight before, and I know it's been a struggle. While today's focus is the surgery, afterwards, when you're recovered, let's really tackle that together. Small, sustainable changes can make a world of difference, not just for your liver but for your overall well-being. But one step at a time, right? Let's get through today first.
trg: Lisusu, nalingaki kolobela kolongono na yo mobimba. Tolobelaki kilo na yo liboso, mpe nayebi ete ezalaki etumba. Atako likebi ya lelo ezali lipaso, na nsima, ntango okobika, tiká tobunda mpenza elongo. Mbongwana ya mikemike mpe ya koumela ekoki kosala bokeseni monene, mpo na libale na yo kaka te, kasi mpe mpo na bolamu na yo mobimba. Tozwa litambe moko na moko, boye te? Totya naino makanisi na biso na lelo.

src: How's the family doing? Are they here with you today? It's always good to have that support system around. And remember, Joe, you've got me in your corner too. We've been through a lot over the years, and we'll get through this together. You just focus on resting up and letting us do the work today. Sound like a plan?
trg: Libota ezali ndenge nini? Baza awa elongo na yo lelo? Eza ntango nyonso malamu kozala na lisungi wana pembeni. Mpe kobosana te, Joe, ozali mpe na ngai na ngambo na yo. Toleki na makambo mingi na boumeli ya bambula, mpe tokoleka na oyo elongo. Yo tyá kaka makanisi na kopema mpe tika biso tósala mosala lelo. Osepeli bongo?

src: Reason for Visit: Bone pain, particularly in the back, ribs, or hips.
trg: Ntina ya bokutani: mpasi na mikuwa, mingi mingi na mokongo, mipanzi, to loketo.

src: Possible Causes:
trg: Makambo oyo ekoki kopesa yango:

src: Multiple Myeloma: This is a type of blood cancer that affects plasma cells, which are a type of white blood cell that helps fight infection. Multiple myeloma can cause bone pain, especially in the back, ribs, or hips. Other symptoms may include fatigue, weakness, frequent infections, and kidney problems.
trg: Myelome multiple: Oyo ezali lolenge ya kanser ya makila oyo ekendaka na baselile ya plasma, oyo ezali lolenge ya baselile ya pembe ya makila oyo esalisaka mpo na kobundisa bokono. Myelome multiple ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa, mingi mingi na mokongo, mipanzi, to loketo. Bilembo misusu ekoki kozala bolembu, kozanga makasi, kozwama na babokono mbala na mbala, mpe mikakatano ya bangei.

src: Metastatic Cancer: This is cancer that has spread from another part of the body to the bones. Metastatic cancer can cause bone pain, fractures, and high levels of calcium in the blood.
trg: Kanser métastatique: Oyo ezali kanser oyo eutaki esika mosusu ya nzoto mpe ekendeke na mikuwa. Kanser métastatique ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa, kobukana, mpe kozala na kalsium mingi na makila.

src: Osteoporosis: This is a condition that causes bones to become weak and brittle. Osteoporosis is more common in older adults, but it can also affect younger people. Symptoms may include back pain, stooped posture, and fractures.
trg: Ostéoporose: Oyo ezali maladi oyo esalaka ete mikuwa ezala na makasi te mpe ebukana noki. Ostéoporose emonanaka mingi epai ya mikolo, kasi ekoki mpe kozwa bilenge. Bilembo ekoki kozala mpasi ya mokongo, kotambola ya kogumbama, mpe kobukana.

src: Other Conditions: Other conditions that can cause bone pain include infections, fractures, and arthritis.
trg: Bokono misusu: Makambo misusu oyo ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa ezali babokono, kobukana, mpe maladi ya mingai.

src: Next Steps:
trg: Makambo oyo ekolanda:

src: Your doctor will order tests to determine the cause of your bone pain. These tests may include:
trg: Monganga na yo akosenga ba ekzamɛ mpo na koyeba ntina ya mpasi na yo na mikuwa. Ba ekzamɛ yango ekoki kozala:

src: Blood tests: Blood tests can check for anemia, high calcium levels, and other signs of illness.
trg: Ekzamɛ ya makila: Ekzamɛ ya makila ekoki koluka kosila makila, nivo ya kalsium ya likolo, mpe bilembo misusu ya maladi.

src: Urine tests: Urine tests can check for protein in the urine, which can be a sign of kidney problems.
trg: Ekzamɛ ya masuba: Ekzamɛ ya masuba ekoki koluka protéini na masuba, oyo ekoki kozala elembo ya mikakatano ya bangei.

src: X-rays: X-rays can show bone fractures and other abnormalities.
trg: Ekzame ya Radio: Ekzame ya Radio ekoki komonisa mikuwa oyo ebukani mpe mikakatano misusu.

src: MRI or CT scan: These imaging tests can provide more detailed pictures of your bones.
trg: IRM to skaner CT: Ba ekzamɛ ya bililingi oyo ekoki komonisa bafoto ya polele ya mikuwa na yo.

src: Bone marrow biopsy: This procedure involves removing a small sample of bone marrow to be examined under a microscope.
trg: Bolongoli ya ndambo ya libubu ya mikuwa: Mayele oyo esengaka kolongola mwa ndambo ya mikuwa mpo na kotala yango na mikroskope.

src: Treatment:
trg: Lisungi:

src: Treatment for bone pain will depend on the underlying cause. Treatment options may include:
trg: Lisungi ya mpasi na mikuwa ekotalela euteli ya likambo yango. Mayele ya lisungi ekoki kozala:

src: Medications: Pain relievers, chemotherapy, and other medications may be used to treat bone pain and other symptoms.
trg: Nkisi: Nkisi ya kosilisa mpasi, chimiothérapie, mpe nkisi misusu ekoki kosalelama mpo na kosunga mpasi na mikuwa mpe bilembo misusu.

src: Radiation therapy: Radiation therapy uses high-energy beams to kill cancer cells and relieve pain.
trg: Radiothérapie: Radiothérapie esalelaka ba rayons ya nguya mingi mpo na koboma baselile ya kanser mpe kosilisa mpasi.

src: Surgery: Surgery may be used to repair fractures or stabilize bones.
trg: Lipaso: Lipaso ekoki kosalelama mpo na kobongisa mikuwa oyo ebukani to kopesa mikuwa makasi.

src: It is important to follow your doctor's instructions carefully and attend all follow-up appointments. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to ask.
trg: Ezali ntina kolanda malako ya monganga na yo na likebi mpe kokende na bokutani nyonso ya bolandeli. Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te na kotuna yango.

src: Please note: This handout is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Please consult with a qualified healthcare professional for diagnosis and treatment.
trg: Tika ete: Mokanda oyo ezali kaka mpo na kopesa nsango mpe ezali toli ya monganga te. Kende kosolola na monganga oyo azali na mayele mpo na koyeba maladi mpe lisungi.

src: I am so sorry for my lateness, doctor. My wife, Martha, usually drives me to my appointments, but she's laid up with a bad cold, so I had to figure out the bus schedule on my own. It's been a while since I've had to navigate public transportation, and I got a bit turned around.
trg: Nazali kosenga bolimbisi mpo na retare na ngai, monganga. Mwasi na ngai, Martha, amemaka ngai mbala mingi na bokutani na ngai, kasi azali kobela maladi ya miyoyo makasi, yango wana esengelaki nabunda ngai moko mpo na koyeba bangonga ya bisi. Nasali mikolo ebele oyo nabandaki kosalela babisi te, mpe natungisamaki mwa moke.

src: I remember back in 2019, I was really worried about this lump I found in my breast. My primary care doctor sent me for a mammogram, and they saw something suspicious, so they recommended a core needle biopsy. I wasn't too thrilled about the idea, so I decided to get a second opinion.
trg: Nabanzi lisusu na 2019, namitungisaki mpenza mpo na mwa mbuma moko namonaki na libele na ngai. Monganga na ngai atindaki ngai nasala ekzame ya kosimbasimba libele, mpe bamonaki eloko moko ya kokamwa, yango wana bapesaka ngai toli ete nasala biolongoli misuni na ntonga. Nasepelaki mpenza te na likanisi yango, yango wana nazwaki ekateli ya kozwa botaleli ya mibale.

src: I made an appointment with a specialist, Dr. Gupta. She was really nice and took the time to listen to my concerns. She explained the biopsy procedure in detail and answered all my questions. She even showed me some diagrams to help me understand what was going on.
trg: Nazwaki mokolo ya bokutani na monganga moko ya mayele, Dr. Gupta. Azalaki mpenza malamu mpe azwaki ntango ya koyoka mitungisi na ngai. Alimbolelaki ngai malamu lolenge oyo basalaka bolongoli ya misuni mpe ayanolaki na mituna na ngai nyonso. Atalisaki ngai mpe mwa bandakisa mpo na kosunga ngai nasosola nini ezalaki koleka.

src: After the consultation, I felt much better about going ahead with the biopsy. Dr. Gupta made me feel comfortable and confident in her expertise. The biopsy itself wasn't too bad, just a little pinch. And thankfully, the results came back benign!
trg: Na nsima ya kosolola na ye, namiyokaki malamu mpenza mpo na kokoba na ekzame ya bolongoli misuni. Dr. Gupta asalisaki ngai mpo namiyoka malamu mpe nazala na elikya na mayele na ye. Bolongoli misuni yango moko ezalaki mpasi mingi te, kaka mwa kotutula moke. Mpe eloko ya malamu, bambano ebimaki malamu!

src: Getting a second opinion was definitely the right decision for me. It gave me peace of mind and helped me make an informed decision about my healthcare. I would recommend it to anyone facing a similar situation.
trg: Kozwa likanisi ya mibale ezalaki mpenza ekateli ya malamu mpo na ngai. Epesaki ngai kimya ya makanisi mpe esalisaki ngai nazwa ekateli ya malamu mpo na kolongono ya nzoto na ngai. Nakoki kopesa toli yango na moto nyonso oyo azali na likambo ya ndenge wana.

src: I'm calling because I'm having a horrible headache, like the worst one of my life, and I'm worried it might be an aneurysm. My name is Brenda, and I'm 54. I'm a bit overweight, about 250 pounds, and I've been feeling a bit dizzy too. My neck feels stiff, and I'm getting a bit nauseous. I don't have a history of aneurysms in my family, but I do have high blood pressure. Should I go to the emergency room?
trg: Nazali kobenga mpo motó ezali koswa ngai na ndenge ya somo, lokola moto oyo eswaka ngai te banda nabotama, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kozala aneurysm. Kombo na ngai Brenda, mpe nazali na mibu 54. Nazali na kilo mwa mingi, pene na 250 kilo, mpe nazali koyoka lokola miso ezali kozunguluka. Nkingo na ngai ezali makasi, mpe nazali koyoka mwa katu. Nazali na moto na libota te oyo aza na maladi ya aneurysm, kasi nazali na tansyo. Nasengeli kokende na lobiko ya lobangu?

src: Hi, Harold! It's always good to see you. I understand you're interested in exploring some options for your spasticity. You mentioned reading about Dr. Amelia Grant online and her work with spasticity management.
trg: Mbote, Harold! Ezalaka ntango nyonso esengo komona yo. Nayoki ete ozali na mposa ya koluka makambo oyo okoki kosala mpo na makolo na yo oyo ezali kokatana. Olobaki ete otangaki makomi na internet na oyo etali Dr. Amelia Grant mpe mosala na ye ya kosunga baoyo bazali na makolo oyo ezali kokatana.

src: I'm happy to refer you to Dr. Grant. I've actually heard good things about her from other patients as well. She's a neurologist who specializes in movement disorders, and she has a lot of experience with spasticity.
trg: Nazali kotinda yo penza epai ya Dr. Grant. Nayoki mpe makambo ya malamu mpo na ye epai ya babeli misusu. Azali monganga ya misisa ya boongo oyo ayebi mingi makambo ya koningana ya nzoto, mpe azali na eksperiansi mingi na makambo ya makolo oyo ezali kokatana.

src: Before we send off the referral, let's chat a bit about what to expect. Spasticity can be tricky to manage, and finding the right approach often involves some trial and error. Dr. Grant will likely start by doing a thorough evaluation to understand your specific symptoms and how they're affecting your daily life. She might also order some tests, like an MRI or EMG, to get a better picture of what's going on.
trg: Liboso ya kotinda bosenga na yo ya bokutani, tosolola mwa moke mpo na koyeba nini okokutana na yango kuna. Makolo oyo ezali kokatana ekoki kozala mpasi mpo na kosungama, mpe mpo na kozwa lisungi ya malamu esengaka komekameka makambo mingi. Dr. Grant akobanda na kotala yo malamu mpo na koyeba bilembo na yo mpe bopusi na yango na bomoi na yo ya mokolo na mokolo. Akoki mpe kosenga yo osalisa ba ekzame misusu, lokola MRI to EMG, mpo na kolimbola malamumalamu likambu.

src: Based on her assessment, she'll develop a treatment plan tailored to you. This could include things like physical therapy, medications, or even injections. She'll also work with you to set realistic goals and track your progress.
trg: Na kotalela oyo akomona, akopesa yo lobiko oyo ebongi na yo. Ekoki kozala masaje, bankisi ya komela, to mpe tonga. Akosalisa yo mpe mpo bozwa mikano oyo bokoki kokokisa mpe kolandela bokoli na yo.

src: Remember, managing spasticity is a journey, not a sprint. It might take some time to find the right combination of treatments that work for you. But with Dr. Grant's expertise and your commitment, I'm confident you'll find some relief.
trg: Kobosana te ete, kosunga makolo oyo ezali kokatana ezali lokola kobanda mobembo, ezali te kokima mbangu. Ekoki kozwa ntango mpo na kozwa lobiko oyo ekosunga yo. Kasi na mayele ya Dr. Grant mpe milende na yo, nandimisami ete oko bika.

src: I'll get that referral sent over right away. In the meantime, if you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to call me. You know where to find me!
trg: Nakotinda mokanda wana kaka sikoyo. Na ntango wana, soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te na kobenga ngai. Oyebi esika nini okoki kokuta ngai!

src: To Whom It May Concern,
trg: Likambo oyo etali nani,

src: I'm here for my DOT physical because my grandfather and two uncles had aplastic anemia, and I know that puts me at higher risk. But honestly, that's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to my health. It feels like I've got a laundry list of issues going on.
trg: Nazali awa mpo na ekzame na ngai ya DOT mpo nkoko na ngai ya mobali mpe ba noko na ngai mibale bazalaki na anemi aplastique, mpe nayebi ete yango etye ngai na likama ya makasi. Kasi ya solo, oyo ezali kaka ebandeli ya makambo matali kolongono na ngai ya nzoto. Emonani lokola nazali na liste ya molayi ya mikakatano ya nzoto.

src: Fatigue is a big one. I'm constantly tired, even after a full night's sleep. It's a deep kind of exhaustion that makes it hard to get through the day, especially with the physical demands of my job. I also get short of breath pretty easily, even with just moderate exertion. Sometimes I get dizzy spells too, which can be a little scary when I'm driving or operating machinery.
trg: Kolemba ezali likambo monene. Nazalaka na bolembu ntango nyonso, ata soki nalali butu mobimba. Ezali bolembu moko ya makasi oyo esalaka ete ezala mpasi kolekisa mokolo, mingi mingi na kotalela mosala na ngai ya makasi. Nakatanaka mpema noki, ata soki nasali kaka mwa mosala moke. Ntango mosusu nazalaka mpe na kizunguzungu, oyo ekoki kozala na likama penza ntango nazali kokumba motuka to kosalela bamasini.

src: I bruise really easily. I'll bump into something lightly and end up with a huge purple mark that takes forever to go away. And I get nosebleeds more often than I'd like to admit. Sometimes my gums bleed when I brush my teeth, too.
trg: Nazokaka noki mpenza. Nakoki kotutana na eloko moko mpe nakozoka pota monene ya violé oyo eumelaka mpo na kolongwa. Mpe zolo na ngai etangaka makila mbala mingi koleka ndenge nalingaka kondimela. Ntango mosusu nonga na ngai ebimaka mpe makila ntango nasukolaka mino na ngai ya bibubutu.

src: I've been dealing with these persistent infections lately. Seems like I catch every cold or flu that goes around, and they linger for weeks. I've had a few bouts of pneumonia in the last couple of years, which really knocked me down.
trg: Nazalaki komona mpasi na maladi oyo eumelaka mikolo oyo. Emonani lokola nazwaka maladi ya miyoyo mpe bagripe nyonso oyo elekaka, mpe eumelaka baposo mingi. Nazalaki na maladi ya mpema mbala moke na mibu mibale mileki, oyo elembisaki ngai mpenza.

src: On top of that, I have type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. I take medication for all of those, but it's a lot to manage. And I have this chronic back pain from an old injury that flares up whenever I do too much heavy lifting.
trg: Likolo ya yango, nazali na diabeti ya tnivo 2, tensyo ya komata, mpe kolesterole ya likolo. Namelaka nkisi mpo na yango nyonso, kasi ezali mpasi mpo na kokoba. Mpe nazali na mpasi oyo esilaka te na mokongo kouta na pota moko ya kala oyo eyaka lisusu ntango nyonso oyo namemaka biloko ya bozito mingi.

src: So yeah, it's a lot. I'm hoping this physical goes well, but I'm definitely worried about all these symptoms and how they might affect my ability to keep working. I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to stay healthy and keep providing for my family.
trg: Ya solo, ezali mingi. Nazali kolikya ete ekzame oyo ekoleka malamu, kasi nazali mpenza komitungisa mpo na bilembo oyo nyonso mpe bopusi na yango na likoki na ngai ya kokoba kosala mosala. Nalingi kaka komindimisa ete nazali kosala nyonso oyo nakoki mpo na kozala na kolongono ya nzoto mpe kokoba kokokisa bamposa ya libota na ngai.

src: Michael Harris
trg: Michael Harris

src: Patient presents to the urgent care clinic with dystonia. The patient's child, Leo, is present and quite active during the examination.
trg: Mobeli aye na ndako ya lisalisi na lombango mpo na dystonie. Mwana na ye, Leo, azali wana mpe azali na makasi mingi ntango ya ekzame.

src: History:
trg: Lisolo:

src: Patient reports involuntary muscle contractions, causing repetitive or twisting movements. These symptoms started recently and have been causing significant discomfort. The patient denies any recent trauma or changes in medication. No family history of dystonia or other neurological disorders.
trg: Mobeli alobi ete azali koyoka kokangamakangama ya misisa, oyo ezali kosalisa ye bamuvema ya kozongelazongela to ya kobaluka. Bilembo oyo ebandi kala te mpe ezali kopesa ye mpasi mingi. Mobeli awangani ata likama moko mikolo oyo to mbongwana moko ya bankisi. Na libota na ye, lisolo ya bokono ya distoni to bamaladi misusu oyo etali boongo etikala komonana te.

src: Physical Exam:
trg: Ekzame ya nzoto:

src: Patient appears uncomfortable due to muscle spasms. Vital signs are stable. Neurological exam reveals sustained muscle contractions in the neck and shoulders, consistent with cervical dystonia. No other neurological deficits noted. Leo is energetic and curious, exploring the exam room throughout the visit.
trg: Mobeli amonani ete azali kobela kokangamakangama ya misisa. Bilembo ya bomoi na ye ezali makasi. Ekzame ya misisa emonisi kokangamakangama ya misisa na nkingo mpe na mapeka, oyo eyokani na distoni ya kingo. Ata mbeba mosusu ya misisa emonani te. Leo azali na makasi mpe na mposa ya koyeba, azali kotambolatambola na ndako ya ekzame na boumeli nyonso ya botaleli.

src: Assessment:
trg: Botaleli:

src: Likely cervical dystonia. Will need to rule out other causes and consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation and management.
trg: Ekoki kozala penza distoni ya kingo. Ekosenga kolongola bantina misusu mpe kokanisa kosalisa ekzame epai ya monganga ya misisa mpo na botaleli mpe boyangeli ya mozindo.

src: Plan:
trg: Mwango:

src: 1. Prescribed muscle relaxant to help alleviate symptoms.
trg: 1. Ekomelami nkisi ya kolembisa misisa mpo na kosalisa bilembo.

src: 2. Referral to Dr. Fischer Chen, a neurologist specializing in movement disorders, for further evaluation.
trg: 2. Kotindama epai ya Dr. Fischer Chen, monganga ya misisa oyo ayebi malamu makambu ya mikakatano ya bamuvema mpo na botaleli na mozindo.

src: 3. Advised patient to rest and avoid strenuous activities that may exacerbate symptoms.
trg: 3. Mobeli azwaki toli ya kopema mpe koboya misala ya makasi oyo ekoki kobakisa bilembo.

src: 4. Follow up in one week or sooner if symptoms worsen.
trg: 4. Kolandela na poso moko to liboso soki bilembo bibebi.

src: Reassurance:
trg: Kopesa elikya:

src: Provided reassurance to the patient regarding the diagnosis and treatment plan. Addressed concerns about Leo's behavior, emphasizing that children are naturally curious and active. Encouraged the patient to reach out with any further questions or concerns. Leo was given a sticker for being a good helper during the visit.
trg: Napesi elikya na mobeli na oyo etali bambano ya ekzame mpe mwango ya lobiko. Nalobeli mitungisi mpo na bizaleli ya Leo, na komonisa ete bana bazalaka na mposa ya koyeba mpe bazalaka na makasi. Na lendisaki mobeli mpo na kobenga ngai soki azali na mituna to mitungisi mosusu. Leo azwaki sticker moko mpo azalaki mosungi malamu na ntango ya bokutani.

src: Pre-Operative Instructions
trg: Malako ya liboso ya lipaso

src: Please read and follow these instructions carefully before your hernia repair procedure with Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka.
trg: Palado, tanga mpe tosa malako oyo malamumalamu liboso ya lipaso na yo ya hernie epai ya Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka.

src: Fasting:
trg: Kokila:

src: Do not eat or drink anything (including water, gum, or candy) after midnight the night before your surgery.
trg: Kolya eloko moko te to komela eloko moko te (ata mayi, bazoka, to babonbon) nsima ya midi ya butu liboso ya lipaso na yo.

src: If you take medication, please consult with Dr. Tanaka or your primary care physician regarding which medications to take and when. You may be instructed to take certain medications with a sip of water on the morning of surgery.
trg: Soki ozali komela nkisi, kende komona Dr. Tanaka to monganga na yo ya liboso mpo ayebisa yo bankisi nini okoki komela mpe ntango nini. Bakoki koyebisa yo omela bankisi mosusu na mwa mayi na ntongo ya lipaso.

src: Medications:
trg: Bankisi:

src: Inform Dr. Tanaka about all medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you are currently taking.
trg: Yebisa Dr. Tanaka bankisi nyonso, bavitamini mpe bilei mosusu ya kobakisa oyo ozali kozwa sikoyo.

src: You may need to stop taking certain medications, such as blood thinners (e.g., aspirin, warfarin) or anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), several days before surgery. Follow Dr. Tanaka's specific instructions regarding medication adjustments.
trg: Ekoki kosenga okata komela bankisi mosusu, neti oyo ekómisaka makila pɛtɛpɛtɛ (ndakisa, aspirine, warfarine) to oyo esilisaka mpasi (ndakisa, ibuprofene, naproxene), mwa mikolo liboso ya lipaso. Tosa malako ya Dr. Tanaka mpo na kobongisa komela na yo ya bankisi.

src: Hygiene:
trg: Bopeto:

src: Shower or bathe the night before or morning of your surgery.
trg: Sokola nzoto butu moko liboso to na ntongo ya lipaso na yo.

src: Do not shave the surgical area yourself. If shaving is necessary, it will be done at the surgical center.
trg: Komikata nsuki te na esika ya lipaso. Soki esengeli bakata suki, bakosala yango na ndako ya lipaso.

src: Remove all jewelry, piercings, and contact lenses before arriving for your surgery.
trg: Longola mayaka nyonso, piercings, mpe matalatala ya misu liboso osalisa lipaso na yo.

src: Clothing:
trg: Bilamba:

src: Wear loose-fitting, comfortable clothing that is easy to put on and take off.
trg: Lata bilamba oyo ezali na bonsomi mpe ya malamu oyo eza pete na kolata mpe kolongola.

src: Avoid wearing clothing with zippers or buttons near the surgical site.
trg: Boyá kolata bilamba oyo ezali na ekoti to babuto pene na esika ya lipaso.

src: Transportation:
trg: Transport:

src: Arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home after your surgery. You will not be allowed to drive yourself.
trg: Bongama mpo moto moko ya mokolo akende kotika yo na ndako nsima ya lipaso na yo. Bakopesa yo ndingisa ya kokumba yo moko mutuka te.

src: Have someone stay with you for the first 24 hours after surgery.
trg: Senga moto atikala na yo mpo na bangonga 24 ya liboso nsima ya lipaso.

src: Post-Operative Care:
trg: Kobatela nzoto na nsima ya lipaso:

src: Follow all post-operative instructions provided by Dr. Tanaka and the surgical center staff.
trg: Tosa malako nyonso ya nsima ya lipaso oyo Dr. Tanaka mpe bato ya mosala ya centre ya lipaso basili kopesa.

src: Take prescribed pain medication as directed.
trg: Mela nkisi ya mpasi oyo bakomeli yo ndenge bapeseli yo yango.

src: Apply ice packs to the surgical area as instructed to reduce swelling.
trg: Tya ngalasi na esika ya lipaso ndenge bayebisi yo mpo na kokitisa kovimba.

src: Avoid strenuous activity and heavy lifting for several weeks following surgery.
trg: Boyá kosala misala ya makasi mpe komema kilo mpo na mwa baposo nsima ya lipaso.

src: Keep the surgical site clean and dry.
trg: Batela esika ya lipaso peto mpe ekauka.

src: Attend all follow-up appointments with Dr. Tanaka.
trg: Kende kokutana na Dr. Tanaka na mikolo nyonso oyo bukatani na bino ebongisamaki.

src: Contact Information:
trg: Makambo matali banimero:

src: If you have any questions or concerns before or after your surgery, please contact Dr. Tanaka's office at 555-0199.
trg: Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi liboso to nsima ya lipaso na yo, benga biro ya Dr. Tanaka na 555-0199.

src: In case of an emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.
trg: Soki likama ebimi, benga 911 to kende na ndako ya bosalisi ya lobangu oyo ezali pene.

trg: Malako Mosusu:

src: Bring your insurance card and photo ID to the surgical center.
trg: Mema karte na yo ya Asiransi mpe karte ya mboka oyo ezali na elongi na yo na centre ya lipaso.

src: Leave valuables at home.
trg: Tika biloko na yo ya nmotuya na ndako.

src: Arrive at the surgical center at the designated time.
trg: Koma na centre ya lipaso na ntango oyo bakataki.

src: We look forward to providing you with excellent care during your hernia repair procedure.
trg: Tozali kozela kopesa yo lisalisi ya malamu mpenza na ntango ya lipaso na yo ya hernie.

src: "Okay, I see. So, the inflammation is making my blood cells clunky and sink faster?"
trg: "Ok, nayoki. Boye, kovimba ezali kosala ete biloko ya mikemike ya makila na ngai ekangama mpe ezinda na lobangu?"

src: "Exactly. Now, we also checked your 'CRP' or C-reactive protein. This is another marker for inflammation produced by your liver. Think of it like a smoke alarm going off when there's a fire. A high CRP level is like a loud alarm telling us there's significant inflammation happening somewhere in your body. Both the elevated ESR and CRP confirm that your body is fighting something, likely related to your joint pain."
trg: "Ezali bongo. Sikoyo, tomekaki mpe proteine C-reactive na yo to 'CRP'. Oyo ezali elembo mosusu ya kovimba oyo libale na yo ebimisaka. Kanisa yango lokola apareyi oyo elelaka soki milinga etondi na ndako oyo ebɛtaka ntango mɔtɔ ezali. CRP ya likolo ezali lokola apareyi yango oyo ezali koyebisa biso ete kovimba ya makasi ezali na esika moko na nzoto na yo. Komata ya VS mpe CRP endimisaka biso ete nzoto na yo ezali kobunda na eloko moko, oyo mbala mosusu etali mpasi na yo ya matonga."

src: "So, my body is basically sending out distress signals?"
trg: "Boye, nzoto na ngai ezali kotinda mingimingi bilembo ya mpasi?"

src: "Precisely. These results help us understand the severity of the inflammation and guide our treatment plan. We'll likely start with anti-inflammatory medication and physical therapy to help reduce the inflammation and improve your mobility. We'll also monitor these levels over time to see how you're responding to treatment."
trg: "Yango wana. Mbano oyo esalisaka biso toyeba soki kovimba ezali makasi mpe etambwisaka biso na mwango ya kopesa nkisi na biso. Mbala mosusu tokobanda na bankisi ya kobundisa kovimba mpe ngalasisi mpo na kosalisa yo okitisa kovimba mpe otambola malamu. Tokolandela mpe nivo oyo na ntango mpo na komona ndenge nini ozali koyanola na nkisi."

src: Patient: No... wait... I have... a question... about... my surgery... scheduled... for... next week.

Soki ozali malamu, tokoki koyanola mituna nyonso oyo ozali na yango mpo na lipaso na yo. Palado, mpo na libateli na yo, luka lisalisi sikoyo.

src: Silas Graves: "Thank you, doctors."
