src: I am a 47-year-old female with a long history of medical issues. I have been dealing with an anal fistula for several months now, and it has become increasingly painful and disruptive to my life. I have tried various home remedies and over-the-counter medications, but nothing has worked. My primary care physician referred me to a colorectal surgeon, who recommended surgery to repair the fistula.
trg: Nazali mwasi ya mibu 47 oyo azali na lisolo molai ya makambo ya minganga. Nazalaki kotungisama na bozali ya nzela mosusu ya mabe na lifwini na boumeli ya basanza ebele sikoyo, mpe yango ekómaki kopesa mpasi mingi mpe kobebisa bomoi na ngai. Nameki nkisi ndenge na ndenge ya ndako mpe nkisi oyo esengaka mokanda ya monganga te, kasi ata moko te esalaki. Monganga na ngai ya liboso atindaki ngai epai ya monganga ya kolorektale, oyo asɛngaki básala ngai lipaso mpo na kobongisa nzela yango.

src: I have a history of Crohn's disease, which was diagnosed in my early 20s. I have had multiple surgeries for Crohn's related complications, including a bowel resection and an ileostomy. I also have a history of depression and anxiety, which have been exacerbated by my chronic health issues. I take several medications for my Crohn's disease and my mental health conditions.
trg: Nazali na maladi ya Crohn, oyo emonanaki ntango nazalaki na mibu 20. Nasali mapaso mingi mpo na makambo etali maladi ya Crohn, kati na yango kolongola misopo mpe ileostomi. Nazali mpe na maladi ya mitungisi na makanisi mpe minyoko, oyo ekomaki makasi mpo na makambo ya kolongono ya nzoto na ngai ya mikolo nyonso. Namelaka nkisi ebele mpo na maladi na ngai ya Crohn mpe bokono ya makanisi na ngai.

src: I am very nervous about this surgery. I have had so many surgeries in the past, and I am worried about the recovery process. I am also worried about the possibility of complications, given my complex medical history. However, I know that I need to have this surgery done in order to improve my quality of life. I am hopeful that the surgery will be successful and that I will be able to get back to my normal life soon.
trg: Nazali na mitungisi mingi mpo na lipaso oyo. Nasalaki mapaso ebele na kotala makambo oyo eleki, mpe nazali na mitungisi mpo na ndenge nakozonga malamu. Nazali mpe na mitungisi mpo na makambo oyo ekoki kobima, kotala lisolo na ngai ya bomoi ya mae matali kolongono ya nzoto na ngai. Kasi, nayebi ete nasengeli kosala lipaso oyo mpo na kobongisa bomoi na ngai. Nazali na elikya ete lipaso yango ekolonga mpe ete nakozonga na bomoi na ngai ya kala mingi te.

src: As I sat in the waiting room, clutching my husband's hand, my mind raced through the last few weeks. It felt like a lifetime ago that we were planning weddings, discussing floral arrangements and seating charts. Now, our world revolved around doctors' appointments, medical jargon, and the constant worry etched on our faces.
trg: Ntango nazalaki kofanda na esika ya kozela, nasimbaki loboko ya mobali na ngai, nabandaki kokanisi baposo oyo eleki. Emonani lokola eleki ntango mingi penza banda tozalaki kobongisa makambo ya libala, kosolola ndenge ya kotia bafololo mpe esika bato bakofanda. Sikoyo, bomoi na biso ekomi kobalukaka na bakutani na minganga, maloba ya minganga, mpe mitungisi ya ntango nyonso oyo ekomami na bilongi na biso.

src: Our little miracle, baby boy Leo, had been born just a month ago. But instead of joyous coos and sleepless nights filled with cuddles, our first few days were a blur of panic and confusion. Leo had suffered seizures shortly after birth, a terrifying experience that left us feeling helpless and scared.
trg: Ka mwa likamwisi na biso, mwana na biso ya mobali Leo, abotamaki sanza moko esili koleka. Kasi na esika ya koyoka esengo mpe kozanga mpongi na butu mpo na koyambayamba mwana, mikolo na biso ya liboso etondaki na kobanga mpe kozanga koyeba. Leo azalaki na maladi ya ndeke mwa moke nsima ya kobotama na ye, eksperiansi moko ya kobanga oyo etikaki biso na mawa mpe kobanga.

src: The doctors had explained that Leo's seizures were caused by a temporary lack of oxygen during birth. They assured us that with proper care and monitoring, he would likely outgrow them. But the fear lingered, a constant shadow over our newfound parenthood.
trg: Minganga balimbolaki ete maladi ya ndeke ya Leo ewutaki na kozanga oxygène mwa ntango moke na ntango na ye ya kobotama. Balobelaki biso ete na lisalisi ya malamu mpe bokengeli oyo esengeli, akoki kolonga yango. Kasi kobanga ezalaki kaka, elili ya ntango nyonso na bomoi na biso ya sika ya kozala baboti.

src: Today was our follow-up appointment with Dr. Kapoor, the neurologist who had been caring for Leo. I took a deep breath, trying to steady my nerves as we were called into his office. Dr. Kapoor greeted us with a warm smile, his eyes crinkling at the corners. He examined Leo thoroughly, asking us about his progress and any changes we had noticed.
trg: Lelo ezalaki mokolo ya bokutani na biso na Dr. Kapoor, monganga ya boongo oyo azalaki kosalisa Leo. Napemaki makasi, mpo na komeka kozwa kimya ntango babengaki biso na biro na ye. Dr. Kapoor ayambaki biso na mwa koseka na ye ya esengo, azalki kobalula matúmu ya miso na ye. Asalaki Leo ekzame malamu, abandaki kotuna biso soki akoli ndenge nini mpe mbongwana nini oyo tomoni.

src: "Leo looks fantastic," Dr. Kapoor announced, his voice filled with genuine delight. "His reflexes are strong, and his development is right on track." He explained that Leo's EEG results showed no signs of seizure activity, a huge relief that washed over me like a wave.
trg: Dr. Kapoor alobaki ete: "Leo azali malamu mpenza," mongongo na ye etondaki na esengo ya solo. "Mimesano na ye ezali makasi, mpe bokoli na ye ezali na nzela ya malamu." Alimbolaki ete mbano ya EEG ya Leo emonisaki elembo ata moko te ya maladi ya ndeke, esengo moko monene oyo elataki ngai lokola mbonge.

src: Dr. Kapoor continued, explaining that while we still needed to be vigilant, the chances of Leo having further seizures were minimal. He discussed weaning Leo off his medication gradually, a process that filled me with both hope and trepidation.
trg: Dr. Kapoor akobaki, na kolimbola ete ata soki tosengeli kokeba, litomba mpo ete Leo akweya lisusu na maladi ya ndeke ezali moke. Alobelaki kolongola nkisi ya Leo mokemoke, likambo oyo etondisaki ngai na elikya mpe kobanga.

src: Leaving Dr. Kapoor's office, I felt a weight lift off my shoulders. The fear that had been my constant companion for weeks began to recede, replaced by a tentative sense of optimism. Leo was going to be okay. We were going to be okay.
trg: Ntango nabimaki na biro ya Dr. Kapoor, nayokaki kilo moko elongwe na mapeka na ngai. Kobanga oyo ezalaki moninga na ngai ya ntango nyonso na baposo ebandaki kosila, mpe esengo ya mwa moke eyaki na esika na yango. Leo akokaki kobika. Tokokaki kokoma malamu.

src: As we walked out of the hospital, the sun shining brightly, I looked at my husband and smiled. "Maybe we can start planning that first birthday party after all," I said, a hint of my old self returning. He squeezed my hand, his eyes filled with love and relief. "Absolutely," he replied. "And maybe even a few weddings too."
trg: Ntango tozalaki kobima na lopitalo, moi engengaki makasi, natalaki mobali na ngai mpe nasekaki. Nlobaki ete "Mbala mosusu tokoki kobanda kobongisa feti yango ya mbotama ya liboso," mwa ndabu ya bomoto na ngai ya kala ebandaki kozonga. Asimbaki loboko na ngai, miso na ye etondaki na bolingo mpe esengo. Alobaki na ngai "Ya solo". "Mpe ntangu mosusu kutu, ata mabala mwa mingi lisusu."

src: Hey kid, listen up. We've got a patient here for a postpartum depression screening. She's here at the urgent care, which, let's be honest, isn't exactly the Ritz-Carlton for mental health, but we do what we can.
trg: Hey mwana, yoka malamu. Tozali na mobeli awa mpo na kotala soki azali na mitungisi ya makanisi na nsima ya kobota. Azali awa na esika ya lobiko ya nokinoki, oyo, toloba solo, ezali penza te nsuka na mae matali kolongono ya makanisi, kasi tozali kosala oyo tokoki.

src: Now, this isn't your typical "run-of-the-mill" check-up. We're dealing with a new mom, probably running on fumes and coffee, possibly feeling like she's drowning. So, tread lightly, okay? Be gentle, be empathetic. This isn't the time for your usual blunt force trauma approach.
trg: Sikoyo, oyo ezali te botaleli ya momeseno. Tozali kolobela mama ya elenge, ntangu mosusu azali bolembu mpe asuki motema, ntangu mosusu azali koyoka lokola azali kozinda. Bongo, kende malembe, ok? Zala na boboto, zala na mawa. Oyo ezali ntango te ya kosalela bandenge ya mobulu mpe ya makasi.

src: First things first, establish rapport. Make her feel comfortable, like she can actually talk to you without judgment. Ask about the baby, how she's sleeping (or not sleeping), how she's feeling emotionally. Don't just stick to the script; listen to what she's saying, and more importantly, what she's not saying.
trg: Ya liboso mpenza, bongisa boyokani. Sala ete amiyoka malamu, lokola akoki kosolola na yo na kozanga kosambisama na nsima. Tuna ye bebe azali ndenge nini, ndenge nini azali kolala (to kolala te), ndenge nini azali komiyoka. Kokakatana te na kotya likebi na oyo azali koloba, mpe ya ntina koleka, makambo oyo azali koloba te.

src: Then, dive into the screening tool. Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, anyone? Yeah, I know, thrilling stuff. But it's important. Go through the questions, explain what they mean, and pay attention to her answers. A high score doesn't automatically mean she's got PPD, but it's a red flag waving in your face.
trg: Na nsima, bolobela bisaleli ya ekzame. Emekelo ya mitungisi ya makanisi oyo eyaka na nsima ya kobota ya Edinburgh, moto moko ayebi? Iyo, nayebi, eloko ya kokamwa. Kasi ezali na ntina. Talela mituna, sosola ndimbola na yango mpe tyela biyano na ye likebi. Pwé ya likolo elimboli te ete azali na bokono ya PPD, kasi ezali elembo ya likama.

src: If she does score high, don't panic. This isn't a death sentence. Talk to her about treatment options, therapy, medication, support groups. Let her know she's not alone, that this is common and treatable. And for the love of all that is holy, make sure she has a follow-up plan. Don't just send her out into the wild with a pat on the back and a "good luck."
trg: Soki azwi pwé ya likolo, kobanga te. Oyo ezali etumbu ya liwa te. Solola na ye mpo na bankisi oyo akoki kozwa, lobiko, bankisi, bituluku ya lisungi. Yebisa ye ete azali ye moko te, ete oyo ekomelaka batu ebele mpe ekoki kosila. Mpe mingimingi penza, sala ete azala na mwango ya bolandeli. Kotinda ye kaka libanda te akende kobunda ye moko na koyebisa ye kaka ete ''Ekosimba''.

src: Remember, we're not just treating symptoms here; we're dealing with a person, a mother, someone's wife, daughter, friend. So, treat her with the respect and compassion she deserves. And if you screw up, well, that's on you. But don't worry, I'll be watching like a hawk. Now go get 'em, tiger.
trg: Kobosana te, ezali kaka likambu ya kosilisa bilembo te; ezali likambo ya moto, mama, mwasi ya moto, mwana mwasi, moninga. Bongo, monisa ye limemya mpe mawa oyo abongi na yango. Mpe soki obebisi, wana eza likambo na yo. Kasi komitungisa te, nakokengela yo na mosika. Sikoyo, kende liboso.

src: Hey there, Dr. Navarro here. Just finished up with a patient, Leticia Ramirez, who came in for her follow-up on that encephalitis she's been battling. Poor thing was limping pretty noticeably when she walked in, favoring her left leg quite a bit.
trg: Mbote, ezali Monganga Navarro. Nautaki kosilisa na mobeli moko, Leticia Ramirez, oyo ayaki mpo na kolandela maladi na ye ya ensefalite oyo azalaki kobunda na yango. Mawa mingi, abandaki kotenguma makasi ntango akotaki, kotambolela mingi na lokolo na ye ya mwasi.

src: She's a hotel housekeeper, you know, on her feet all day, so that limp's gotta be tough. Said she's been feeling a bit better overall, head's cleared up some, fever's down, but that leg's giving her trouble. Mentioned it started hurting a few days ago, kinda dull ache at first, then got worse. Doesn't recall any specific injury, just woke up with it sore one morning.
trg: Azali mwana-mosala na otele, boyebi, azalaka ya kotelema mokolo mobimba, yango wana kotenguma yango ezali penza mpasi. Alobaki ete azali koyoka mwa malamu na nzoto mobimba, makanisi na ye ebongi mwa moke, fefele na ye ekiti, kasi lokolo wana ezali komonisa ye mpasi. Alobaki ete mpasi yango ebandaki mwa mikolo mileki, mpasi ya moke na ebandeli, na nsima ekomaki makasi penza. Azali kominkundola pota moko te azokaki na esika moko, na ntongo moko boye, alamukaki kaka na mpasi yango.

src: Examined the leg, didn't see any obvious swelling or redness, but she winced when I pressed around the calf area. Range of motion seemed okay, but definitely some tenderness there. Neurological exam was mostly normal, reflexes intact, though she did seem a bit unsteady on her feet, maybe related to the encephalitis still lingering a bit.
trg: Natalaki lokolo, namonaki te kovimba to esika moko oyo ekomaki motane, kasi agangaki ntango nabandaki kofina zingazinga ya lokolo. Koningisa lokolo ezalaki mwa malamu, kasi mpasi moko ezalaki mpenza wana. Ekzame ya misisa ezalaki mwa malamu, mimesano ebebaki te, atako azalaki na mpasi ya kotelema tende na makolo na ye, ntango mosusu mpo na ensefalite oyo ezalaki naino mwa moke.

src: Overall, she seems in good spirits despite everything. Tough cookie, that Leticia. Just hope we can get her back on her feet – literally – soon. Encephalitis is no joke, and adding a leg issue on top of it just complicates things. But we'll keep monitoring her closely, make sure she gets the care she needs.
trg: Na mokuse, azali komonana na esengo atako minyoko nyonso. Leticia azali mwasi ya makasi. Tozali kolikya ete toko sunga ye mpo abika – kala mingi te. Ensefalite ezali liseki te, mpe kobakisa lisusu likambo ya lokolo ezali kokómisa makambo mpasi koleka. Kasi tokokoba kolandela ye penepene, koyeba penza ete azali kozwa lisalisi oyo abongi na yango.

src: Dr. Aris Thorne: Good afternoon, Mr. Sterling. I see you're concerned about the changes you've noticed in your skin, particularly on your face, neck, hands, and arms. It's quite common for individuals in high-stress professions like yours to notice these signs of aging.
trg: Dr. Aris Thorne: Mbote, Mr. Sterling. Namoni ozali komitungisa mpo na mbongwana oyo omoni na loposo na yo, mingi mpenza na elongi, na nkingo, na maboko mpe na loboko. Ezali likambo ya somo te mpo na bato oyo basalaka misala ya mpasi makasi lokola yo bakoka komona bilembo oyo ya konuna.

src: Atticus Sterling: Yes, doctor. It's not just vanity; it's affecting my confidence in the courtroom. I feel like I look older than I am, and I worry it might impact my clients' perception of me.
trg: Atticus Sterling: Iyo, monganga. Ezali kaka te likambo ya lolendo; ezali kobebisa komindima na ngai na esika ya esambiselo. Namiyokaka lokola nazali konuna koleka ndenge nazali, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kobebisa ndenge oyo bakiliya na ngai batalelaka ngai.

src: Dr. Thorne: I understand completely. Let's talk about what's happening. As we age, our skin loses collagen and elastin, the proteins that give it structure and elasticity. This leads to wrinkles, sagging, and thinning skin. Sun exposure, which I imagine you get plenty of during your travels, accelerates this process.
trg: Dr. Thorne: Nayoki yo malamu. Tolobela mpo na oyo ezali kosalema. Ntango tozali kokola, mposo na biso ebungisaka collagene na elastine, ba proteini oyo epesaka yango kozalela mpe kobendana. Yango ememaka na kobimisa banzelanzela na elongi, na kosilisa makasi na loposo, mpe na kokomisa loposo patatalu. Kotikala na moi, oyo nakanisi ozwaka mingi ntango osalaka mibembo, epusaka noki na nzela wana.

src: Atticus Sterling: I do spend a lot of time outdoors, and I haven't always been diligent with sunscreen.
trg: Atticus Sterling: Nasalaka ngonga mingi na libanda, mpe nazalaka ntango nyonso makasi te na kopakola pomade ya moi.

src: Dr. Thorne: That's a significant factor. Sun damage causes age spots, uneven pigmentation, and further breakdown of collagen. Additionally, stress can contribute to premature aging by increasing cortisol levels, which can damage skin cells.
trg: Dr. Thorne: Wana ezali likambo ya ntina mingi. Mbeba ya moi ememaka na matona ya konuna, langi ya loposo ebebaka, mpe ebevisaka lisusu colagene. Lisusu, mitungisi ya makanisi ekoki kopesa maboko na konuna ya mbangu na komatisa nivo ya kortisole, oyo ekoki kobebisa baselile ya loposo.

src: Atticus Sterling: So, what can be done? Is it too late to reverse the damage?
trg: Atticus Sterling: Boye, nini ekoki kosalema? Ngonga esi eleki mpo na kobongisa mbeba wana?

src: Dr. Thorne: Not at all. There are several options available, ranging from topical treatments to minimally invasive procedures. We can start with a personalized skincare regimen incorporating retinoids, antioxidants, and broad-spectrum sunscreen. For more noticeable results, we could consider chemical peels, laser therapy, or injectables like Botox or fillers.
trg: Dr. Thorne: Ata moke te. Ezali na banzela mingi, kobanda na lobiko ya loposo kino na lipaso ya moke. Tokoki kobanda na programe ya kobatela loposo oyo ebongisami mpo na yo na kosangisa retinoide, ba antioxydant, na pomade ya moi ya makasi. Mpo mbano ya komona, tokoki kokanisa ba peeling chimique, lobiko na ba laser, to biloko ya kotshiuba lokola Botox to fillers.

src: Atticus Sterling: I've heard of those, but I'm hesitant about anything too invasive.
trg: Atticus Sterling: Nayokaka mpo na yango, kasi nazali na kobanga mpo na eloko nyonso oyo ezali kozwa loposo mingi.

src: Dr. Thorne: That's perfectly understandable. We can tailor a plan that suits your comfort level and goals. Perhaps we can start with a series of chemical peels to improve skin texture and tone, coupled with a consistent home care routine. As we see progress, we can discuss other options if you wish.
trg: Dr. Thorne: Wana ezali mpenza likambo ya koyeba. Tokoki kobongisa mwango oyo ekokani na nivo na yo ya malamu mpe na mikano na yo. Mbala mosusu tokoki kobanda na molongo ya ba peeling chimique mpo na kobongisa bonene mpe langi ya loposo na yo, elongo na momesano ya bobateli na ndako ntango nyonso. Ntango tokomona bokoli, tokoki kotalela banzela misusu soki okosepela.

src: Atticus Sterling: That sounds reasonable. I appreciate your thorough explanation, Dr. Thorne. It's reassuring to know there are steps I can take to improve my skin's appearance.
trg: Atticus Sterling: Eza malamu. Nasepeli na ndenge olimboli, Dr. Thorne. Ezali kopesa kimia koyeba ete ezali na matambe oyo nakoki kozwa mpo na kobongisa ndenge loposo na ngai emonanaka.

src: Dr. Thorne: My pleasure, Mr. Sterling. Remember, taking care of your skin is an investment in yourself, both personally and professionally. Let's schedule a follow-up appointment to monitor your progress and adjust the plan as needed.
trg: Dr. Thorne: Ezali esengo na ngai, M. Sterling. Kobosana te, kobatela loposo na yo ezali botyami mosolo na mopanzi moko mpo na yo moko, ezala na bomoi na yo mpe na mosala. Tozwa mokolo ya bokotani mpo na kolandela bokoli na yo mpe kobongisa mwango soki ezali ntina.

src: Frequent urination, especially at night, is a common issue during pregnancy. It happens because your growing uterus presses on your bladder, and your body is producing more fluids. While it can be annoying, it's usually harmless.
trg: Kosuba mbala na mbala, mingimingi na butu, ezali likambo esalemaka mingi na ntango ya zemi. Esalemaka mpo matrisi na yo ezali kokola mpe ezali kofina libenga ya masuba, mpe nzoto na yo ezali kobimisa mayi mingi. Atako ekoki koyokisa mwa nsoni, ememaka penza likama te.

src: Here are some tips to help manage it:
trg: Tala mwa batoli mpo na kosunga yo na yango:

src: Drink plenty of fluids during the day, but limit your intake in the evening.
trg: Mela biloko ya mayi mingi na moi, kasi kitisa komela yango na mpokwa.

src: Avoid caffeine and alcohol, which can irritate your bladder.
trg: Boya kafe na masanga, mpo ekoki kotungisa libenga na yo ya masuba.

src: Try to empty your bladder completely when you go.
trg: Meka kobimisa masuba nyonso soki okei kosuba.

src: Lean forward when you urinate to help empty your bladder.
trg: Gumbama liboso ntango ozali kosuba mpo esunga yo na kobimisa masuba nyonso.

src: If you experience pain or burning when you urinate, or if you have a fever or chills, see your doctor right away, as these could be signs of a urinary tract infection.
trg: Soki oyoki mpasi to kozika moko ntango ozali kosuba, to soki ozali na fefele to ozali koyoka nzoto kolenga, kende kokutana monganga na yo mbala moko, mpo ekoki kozala bilembo ya bokono ya nzela ya masuba.

src: Don't hesitate to talk to your doctor if you have any other concerns. They can offer more personalized advice and support.
trg: Kokakatana te mpo na kosolola na monganga na yo soki ozali na mitungisi misusu. Akoki kopesa yo toli mpe lisungi oyo ebongi na yo moko.

src: Provider: Hi there, I'm Dr. Yusuf. You must be Ichiro. Nice to meet you.
trg: Monganga: Mbote, nazali Dr. Yusuf. Yo osengeli kozala Ichiro. Nasepeli komona yo.

src: Ichiro: Yeah, hi.
trg: Ichiro: Ee, mbote.

src: Provider: I understand you're here because of some abnormal Pap smear results. Can you tell me a bit about what brought you in today?
trg: Monganga: Nayoki ete oye awa mpo na mbano ya mabe ya Liyaka ya matrisi. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa moke nini ememi yo awa lelo?

src: Ichiro: My partner made me come. I feel fine, honestly. I don't see why this is such a big deal.
trg: Ichiro: Molongani na ngai nde atindaki ngai awa. Nazali komiyoka malamu, na bosolo mpenza. Namoni te mpo na nini likambo oyo ezali kokomisama monene boye.

src: Provider: I hear you. It can be frustrating to come in when you're feeling okay. But abnormal Pap results are something we want to keep an eye on. It doesn't necessarily mean anything bad, but it's important to follow up just to be sure.
trg: Monganga: Nayoki yo. Ekoki kozala mpasi mpo na koya ntango ozali komiyoka malamu. Kasi mbano ya mabe ya liyaka ya matrisi ezali eloko oyo tosengeli kotala malamu. Elingi koloba te ete ezali mabe, kasi ezali na ntina kolandela mpo na kozala na asiransi.

src: Ichiro: I guess. But what does it even mean? Is it cancer or something?
trg: Ichiro: Nakanisi bongo. Kasi elingi koloba nini mpenza? Ezali kanser to eloko mosusu?

src: Provider: Not necessarily. Abnormal results can mean a few different things, most of which are easily treatable. It could be something as simple as an infection or inflammation. We just need to do a few more tests to figure out exactly what's going on.
trg: Monganga: Te, ezali kaka bongo te. Mbano ya mabe ekoki kolimbola makambo mingi, oyo mingi na yango ekoki kosalisama. Ekoki kozala likambo ya pamba neti mwa bokono to kovimba. Tosengeli kaka kosala mwa ekzame mosusu mpo na koyeba mpenza nini ezali koleka.

src: Ichiro: Okay, so what kind of tests?
trg: Ichiro: Oke, kasi baekzame ya ndenge nini?

src: Provider: We'll start with a colposcopy. It sounds scary, but it's really just a close look at your cervix with a special magnifying instrument. It's quick and usually painless. Depending on what we see, we might take a small sample of tissue for further testing.
trg: Monganga: Tokobanda na colposcopie.Yango ekoki kobangisa, kasi ezali kaka kotala malamu liyaka na yo ya matrisi na lisungi ya bisaleli ya sikisiki. Ezali noki mpe mbala mingi ezalaka na mpasi te. Na kotalela oyo tokomona, tokoki kozwa mwa eteni ya mosuni mpo na kosala baekzame mosusu.

src: Ichiro: And then what?
trg: Ichiro: Na nsima nini kolanda?

src: Provider: Once we have the results from the colposcopy and any biopsy, we'll have a better idea of what's causing the abnormal cells. Then we can discuss the best course of action, whether it's just monitoring, medication, or a minor procedure.
trg: Monganga: Soki tozwi mbano ya colposcopie mpe ya bolongoli mosuni, tokoyeba malamu nini ezali kopesa baselile ya mabe. Na nsima tokoki kosolola mpo na likambo ya malamu ya kosala, ezala kaka kolandla, kopesa nkisi, to lipaso moko ya moke.

src: Ichiro: Alright, I suppose that makes sense. Thanks for explaining it.
trg: Ichiro: Malamu, nakanisi ete ezali na polele. Matondi mpo na kolimbola yango.

src: Provider: Of course. It's always better to be safe than sorry, right? And remember, we're here to help you through this every step of the way. Any other questions for me right now?
trg: Monganga: Ya solo. Kobongama liboso ezali malamu koleka kobundisa, boye te? Mpe kobosana te, tozali awa mpo na kosalisa yo na bitambe nyonso. Ozali na mituna misusu mpo na ngai sikoyo?

src: Ichiro: No, I think I'm good for now. Thanks.
trg: Ichiro: Te, nakanisi ete nazali malamu mpo na sikoyo. Matondi.

src: Provider: You're welcome. Let's get started with the exam then.
trg: Monganga: Likambo te. Tobanda ekzame sikoyo.

src: Nurse Adeline: Good morning, Mr. Kianpour. I see you're here to discuss some drug interactions with Dr. Ortiz. Could you tell me a little bit more about what's going on?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Mbote, Mr Kianpour. Namoni oyei koyebisa Dr. Ortiz makambo etali nkokoso ya bankisi. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa moke makambo oyo ezali kosalema?

src: Mr. Kianpour: Uh, yeah. I've been having some... stomach issues lately. And I think it might be because of the new medication I started taking for my anxiety.
trg: Mr Kianpour: Ee. Nazali na mwa... mikakatano na libumu mikolo oyo. Mpe nakanisi ezali mpo na nkisi ya sika oyo nabandaki komela mpo na basusi na ngai.

src: Nurse Adeline: I see. And what medication is that?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Namoni. Nkisi nini yango?

src: Mr. Kianpour: It's called Alprazolam. My psychiatrist prescribed it about a week ago.
trg: Mr. Kianpour: Eza Alprazolam. Psykiatre na ngai akomelaki ngai yango pene na poso moko moleki.

src: Nurse Adeline: Okay. And what other medications are you currently taking?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Malamu. Mpe bankisi nini mosusu ozali komela sikoyo?

src: Mr. Kianpour: Just some over-the-counter stuff for allergies. Claritin, I think.
trg: Mr. Kianpour: Kaka mwa bankisi oyo etekamaka mpambapamba na kozanga mokanda ya monganga mpo na baalergi. Nabanzi ezali Claritin.

src: Nurse Adeline: Alright. And have you noticed any other symptoms besides the stomach issues?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Ok. Omoni mpe bilembo mosusu longola mikakatano ya libumu?

src: Mr. Kianpour: Well, I've been feeling really tired lately. Like, more than usual. And sometimes I get dizzy when I stand up too fast.
trg: Mr Kianpour: Ee, nazali koyoka neti nalembi mingi mikolo oyo. Koleka ndenge nazalaka mbala mingi. Mpe ntango mosusu nazalaka na kizunguzungu soki natelemi noki.

src: Nurse Adeline: Okay, those are important things to note. Have you experienced any changes in your mood or behavior?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Malamu, wana makambo ya ntina ya koyeba. Ozali komona mbongwana na ezalela to bizaleli na yo?

src: Mr. Kianpour: Not really. Just a little anxious about... everything.
trg: Mr. Kianpour: Te mpenza. Kaka mwa susi mpo na... nyonso.

src: Nurse Adeline: Understandable. It sounds like you might be experiencing some side effects from the Alprazolam, or possibly an interaction with the Claritin. Dr. Ortiz will be able to review your medications and discuss your symptoms in more detail. Is there anything else you'd like to mention before you see him?
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Nayoki. Emonani neti ozali komona nkokoso ya Alprazolam oyo eyaka na nsima ya komela yango, to mbala mosusu boyokani na Claritin. Dr. Ortiz akotala bankisi na yo mpe akolobela bilembo na yo na bozindo. Ezali na eloko mosusu olingi koloba liboso omona ye?

src: Mr. Kianpour: No, I think that's it. I just... I really need to get this sorted out. I have a big event coming up next week and I can't afford to be feeling like this.
trg: Mr Kianpour: Te, nakanisi yango wana. Kaka... nazali na mposa ya kobongisa likambo oyo. Nazali na milulu moko ya motuya oyo ekokoma poso ekoya mpe nakoki te koyoka boye.

src: Nurse Adeline: I understand completely. Dr. Ortiz is very experienced and I'm sure he'll be able to help you find a solution. Just have a seat in the waiting area and he'll be with you shortly.
trg: Lifulume Adeline: Nayoki mpenza. Dr. Ortiz aza na eksperiansi mingi mpe nayebi ete akosalisa yo kozwa lobiko. Fanda na ndaku ya kozela mpe akokoma na ye kala te.

src: Mr. Kianpour: Thank you.
trg: Mr. Kianpour: Matondi.

src: Doctor: Hey, Uche. You're back already? Didn't the treatment work?
trg: Monganga: Mbote, Uche. Ozongi lisusu? nkisi yango esalaki te?

src: Uche Okafor: No, Doc, it didn't. I'm still tired all the time, and I'm starting to get really frustrated. I have a deadline coming up, and I can't focus on my work.
trg: Uche Okafor: Te, monganga, esalaki te. Nazali kaka kolemba ntango nyonso, mpe nakomi koyoka nkanda makasi. Nazali na mosala oyo esengeli nasilisa, mpe nazali kokoka kotya makanisi na mosala na ngai te.

src: Doctor: I understand your frustration, Uche. But your medical history is complex, and we need to be careful. We can't just try random treatments.
trg: Monganga: Nayoki nkanda na yo, Uche. Kasi lisolo ya kala na mae matali kolongono ya nzoto na yo ezali mindondo, mpe tosengeli kokeba. Tokoki te kobanda komekameka bankisi nyonso oyo tolingi.

src: Uche Okafor: I know, but I need something to help me now. Can't you give me something stronger?
trg: Uche Okafor: Nayebi, kasi nazali na mposa ya eloko mpo na kosalisa ngai sikoyo. Okoki kopesa ngai eloko ya makasi te?

src: Doctor: I can't just prescribe something stronger without knowing what's causing your fatigue. We need to run some more tests.
trg: Monganga: Nakoki te kopesa yo nkisi ya makasi soki nayebi te nini ezali kopesa yo bolembu. Tosengeli kosala ba ekzamɛ mosusu.

src: Uche Okafor: More tests? I don't have time for more tests! I need a solution now!
trg: Uche Okafor: Ba ekzamɛ mosusu? Nazali na ntango ya kosala ba ekzamɛ mosusu te! Nazali na mposa ya nkisi sikoyo!

src: Doctor: I know you're impatient, Uche, but we need to be thorough. Rushing into treatment could make things worse. Let's schedule some tests and see what we find.
trg: Monganga: Nayebi ete ozangi motema molai, Uche, kasi tosengeli kotala malamumalamu. Kokende mbangu na kopesa nkisi ekoki kobebisa makambo. Tika totya programɛ ya ba ekzamɛ mpe totala nini tokozwa.

src: Uche Okafor: Fine. But make it quick. I can't keep living like this.
trg: Uche Okafor: EMalamu. Kasi sala yango mbangu. Nakoki te kokoba kofanda boye.

src: Living with excessive sweating, or hyperhidrosis, can be frustrating and sometimes embarrassing. While we understand it's a sensitive topic, open communication with your healthcare provider is key to finding the best treatment plan for you. Sometimes, patients may hesitate to share all their symptoms or lifestyle factors due to various reasons. We want to assure you that our primary goal is to help you feel comfortable and confident in your skin.
trg: Kozala na bokono ya kotoka mingi, to hyperhidrosis, ekoki kopesa nkanda mpe ntango mosusu nsoni. Atako toyebi ete ezali likambo ya mpasi, kosolola polele na monganga na yo ezali nzela ya malamu mpo na kozwa bankisi oyo ebongi na yo. Ntango mosusu, bato ya maladi bakoki kokakatana koyebisa bilembo na bango nyonso to ndenge bafandaka mpo na bantina ndenge na ndenge. Tolingi koyebisa yo ete mokano na biso ya liboso ezali ya kosalisa yo oyoka malamu mpe ozala na kondima na nzoto na yo.

src: Here are a few things to consider when discussing your sweating concerns with your doctor:
trg: Talá makambo oyo osengeli kotalela ntango ozali kosolola na monganga na yo mpo na kotoka na yo:

src: Honesty is the best policy: While it might feel awkward to discuss certain details, your doctor needs a complete picture of your symptoms, including when and where you sweat most, triggers, and how it affects your daily life. This information helps them determine the underlying cause and tailor treatment options specifically for you.
trg: Koloba solo ezali malamu mingi: Atako ekoki kozala mpasi kosolola makambo mosusu, monganga na yo azali na mposa ya koyeba bilembo na yo nyonso, ata mpe ntango nini mpe esika nini otokaka mingi, biloko nini esalaka ete otoka, mpe ndenge nini yango ebebisaka bomoi na yo ya mokolo na mokolo. Makambo oyo esalisaka bango bayeba ntina ya bokono na yo mpe bapesa yo bankisi oyo ebongi na yo.

src: Lifestyle factors matter:  Your daily habits, including diet, exercise, and stress levels, can play a role in sweating. Be open about your lifestyle choices, as simple modifications can sometimes make a significant difference.
trg: Ndenge ya kofanda ezali na ntina: Mimeseno na yo ya mokolo na mokolo, ata mpe biloko olyaka, ngalasisi, mpe mitungisi, ekoki kosala ete otoka mingi. Lobá polele ndenge ofandaka, mpo ntango mosusu kobongola mwa makambo ekoki kosala bokeseni monene.

src: Don't hold back on concerns:  If you have any worries or questions about potential treatments or side effects, please don't hesitate to voice them. Your doctor is there to address your concerns and work with you to find a solution that fits your needs and preferences.
trg: Kobanga te kolobela mitungisi na yo: Soki ozali na mitungisi to mituna mpo na bankisi to mabe na yango, kobanga te kolobela yango. Monganga na yo azali wana mpo na koyanola na mituna na yo mpe kosala elongo na yo mpo na kozwa lisalisi oyo ebongi na bamposa mpe bolingo na yo.

src: Remember, you're not alone: Hyperhidrosis is a common condition affecting many people. Sharing your experiences and concerns with your doctor can empower you to take control of your sweating and improve your quality of life.
trg: Kobosanaka te, ozali yo moko te: Hyperhidrosis ezali bokono oyo ezwaka bato mingi. Koyebisa monganga na yo makambo okutanaka na yango mpe mitungisi na yo ekoki kosalisa yo oyeba kopekisa kotoka na yo mpe obongisa bomoi na yo.

src: We encourage you to schedule a follow-up appointment with Dr. Anika Sharma to discuss your recent lab results and any other concerns you may have. Together, we can work towards finding effective solutions and helping you feel your best.
trg: Tolendisi yo ozwa bokutani mosusu na Dr. Anika Sharma mpo na kosolola mpo na mbano ya labo na yo ya sika mpe mitungisi mosusu nyonso oyo okoki kozala na yango. Elongo, tokoki kosala mpo na kozwa makambo ya malamu mpe kosalisa yo oyoka malamu mingi.

src: Hair Loss: A Common and Manageable Condition
trg: Kokweyisama ya Suki: Maladi Moko oyo ezwaka Bato Mingi mpe Ekoki Kosalisama.

src: Hair loss is a common concern for many people, including women. It can be caused by a variety of factors, including workplace injuries, stress, hormonal changes, and nutritional deficiencies. While hair loss can be distressing, it is often temporary and treatable.
trg: Kokweisama ya suki ezali likambo moko oyo epesaka bato mingi mitungisi, mingimingi epai ya basi. Ekoki kouta na makambo ndenge na ndenge, lokola kozoka na esika ya mosala, mitungisi ya makanisi, mbongwana na nzoto, mpe kozanga bilei ya malamu na nzoto. Atako kokweisa suki ekoki kopesa mpasi na motema, ezalaka mbala mingi ya ntango moke mpe ekoki kosalisama.

src: Causes of Hair Loss After a Workplace Injury
trg: Ntina ya Kokeisama ya Suki Nsima ya Kozoka na Mosala

src: In some cases, hair loss can occur after a workplace injury. This may be due to the physical trauma of the injury itself, or it could be a result of the stress and anxiety associated with the injury. Additionally, certain medications used to treat pain or inflammation may also contribute to hair loss.
trg: Na bantangu mosusu, kokweyisa suki ekoki kosalema nsima ya kozoka na mosala. Ekoki kozala mpo na mpasi ya nzoto ya kozoka yango moko, to ekoki kozala mpo na mitungisi ya makanisi mpe kobanga oyo eyaka na kozoka. Kutu, bankisi mosusu oyo basalelaka mpo na kosilisa mpasi to kovimba ekoki mpe kosala ete suki ekweya.

src: Treatment Options
trg: Ndenge ya Kozwa lobiko

src: The treatment for hair loss will depend on the underlying cause. If your hair loss is related to stress or anxiety, finding ways to manage these emotions may help. This could involve techniques such as relaxation exercises, yoga, or meditation. If your hair loss is due to a nutritional deficiency, your doctor may recommend dietary changes or supplements.
trg: Lobiko ya kokweyisama ya suki elandaka ntina na yango. Soki eutaka na mitungisi ya makanisi to kobanga, koluka koyeba ndenge ya koyanola na mayoki wana ekoki kosalisa. Ekoki kozala na nzela ya ba tekiniki neti bangalasisi ya kopema malamu, yoga, to komanyola. Soki euti na kozanga bilei ya malamu na nzoto, monganga na yo akoki kobongola bilei oyo okobanda kolya to bilei mosusu ya kobakisa.

src: Reassurance
trg: Kolendisa

src: It is important to remember that hair loss is often a temporary condition. With proper treatment and care, your hair is likely to grow back. If you are concerned about your hair loss, please do not hesitate to talk to your doctor. They can help you determine the cause of your hair loss and recommend the best course of treatment.
trg: Ezali na ntina kobmikundola ete kokweyisa suki ezalaka mbala mingi likambo ya ntango moke. Na nzela ya lobiko mpe bozwi likebi ya malamu, suki na yo ekoki kokola lisusu. Soki ozali na mitungisi mpo na kobungisa suki na yo, tobondeli yo osolola na monganga na yo. Akoki kosalisa yo koyeba ntina ya kokweyisama ya suki na yo mpe kopesa yo toli ya lobiko oyo eleki malamu.

src: Additional Tips
trg: Batoli Mosusu

src: Be gentle with your hair. Avoid harsh brushing or styling, and use a mild shampoo and conditioner.
trg: Kipé suki na yo. Boya kosanola yango to kokanga suki na makasi, mpe salela sabuni ya kosukola suki mpe kokawusa yango na boboto.

src: Eat a healthy diet. Make sure you are getting enough protein, iron, and other nutrients that are important for hair health.
trg: Lya bilei ya malamu. Sala ete olyaka ba proteine ya kokoka, fer, mpe bavitamini mosusu oyo ezali na ntina mpo na kolongono ya suki.

src: Manage stress. Find healthy ways to cope with stress, such as exercise, relaxation techniques, or spending time with loved ones.
trg: Yangela mitungisi ya makanisi. Luka ndenge ya malamu ya koyangela mitungisi ya makanisi, lokola kosala bangalasisi, ba teckiniki ya kopema, to kolekisa ntango na bato oyo olingaka.

src: Be patient. It takes time for hair to grow back. Do not get discouraged if you do not see results immediately.
trg: Zala na motema molai. Esengaka ntango mpo suki ekola lisusu. Kolɛmba nzoto te soki omoni bambano ya mbala moko te.

src: Remember, you are not alone. Many women experience hair loss at some point in their lives. With the right support and treatment, you can manage your hair loss and regain your confidence.
trg: Kobosana te, ozali yo moko te. Basi mingi bakutanaka na kokweyisama ya suki na ntango moko boye na bomoi na bango. Na lisalisi mpe lobiko ya malamu, okoki koyangela na kokweyisama ya suki na yo mpe kobanda komindima yo moko.

src: My name's Nikolai Petrovich, and I work security. Look, I don't have time for games. My family, yeah, they've got this thing, Shwachman-Diamond syndrome. Messes with their blood, their pancreas, whole lot of stuff. I haven't been feeling right lately, either. Tired all the time, can't shake a cold, stomach's been acting up.
trg: Kombo na ngai Nikolai Petrovich, mpe nasalaka mosala ya kokengela. Yoka, nazali na ntango ya kolekisa te. Libota na ngai, ɛɛ, bazali na maladi oyo, maladi ya Shwachman-Diamond. Ebebisaka makila na bango, yéka na bango, mpe makambo mingi. Ngai mpe nazali komiyoka malamu te mikolo oyo. Nazali ya kolemba ntango nyonso, nazali kokoka te kolongola maladi ya miyoyo, nazali mikakatano na likundu.

src: It started a few weeks back. Just felt... off. Dragging myself through shifts, catching every bug going around. Thought maybe I was just run down, you know? But then the stomach issues started. Greasy, foul-smelling stuff, if you catch my drift. And the bruising... I barely bump into anything and I look like I've been in a fight.
trg: Ebandaki mwa baposo eleki. Nazalaki kaka komiyoka... mabe. Nazalaki komibenda nzoto na mosala, kozwa maladi nyonso oyo ezali koleka. Nakanisaki mbala mosusu ezali kaka kolemba ya mpamba, oyebi? Kasi na nsima, mikakatano ya likundu ebandaki. Biloko ya mafuta, ya nsolo mabe, soki olimboli oyo nalingi koloba. Mpe bapota... nazali kotutana mpenza na eloko te kasi nazali komonana lokola nde nabundaki.

src: My cousin, Dmitri, he's got it bad. Always sick, in and out of the hospital. Short for his age, too. My aunt says it's genetic. Something about bone marrow not working right, not making enough white blood cells to fight infection. And the pancreas not making enzymes to digest food properly. That explains the stomach problems, I guess.
trg: Ndeko na ngai, Dmitri, azali na yango makasi. Azali kobela ntango nyonso, kokende mpe kozonga na lopitalo. Azali mpe mokuse na kolanda mbula na ye. Tata-mwasi na ngai alobi ete ezalaka ya libota. Eloko moko oyo etali libúbu oyo ezali kosala malamu te, ezali kobota malamu te baselile ya mpembe na makila mpo na kobundisa maladi. Mpe yéke ezali kosala baanzyme te mpo na kosala boyangeli malamu ya bilei. Nakanisi yango nde elimboli mikakatano na ngai ya likundu.

src: So here I am. Figured I better get checked out before I end up like Dmitri. I need to know if I've got this thing, and if so, what we're gonna do about it. I got a job to do, people depending on me. Can't be calling in sick every other day. Just give it to me straight, doc. What are my chances?
trg: Yango wana nazali awa. Namilobeli ete ezali malamu namitalisa liboso ete nakóma lokola Dmitri. Nazali na mposa ya koyeba soki nazali na bokono yango, mpe soki ezali bongo, tokoki kosala nini mpo na yango. Nazali na mosala ya kosala, bato bazali kotyela ngai motema. Nakoki te kobelabela mikolo nyonso. Yebisa ngai kaka bosolo, monganga. Matomba na ngai ezali nini?

src: Mr. Silas Hawthorne, a 52-year-old electrician, presented to the emergency department for a biopsy of a suspicious lesion on his right forearm. He reported noticing the lesion several weeks ago but initially dismissed it as a minor scrape from work. However, the lesion has since grown in size and become increasingly painful, prompting him to seek medical attention.
trg: Mr. Silas Hawthorne, Mosali ya lotiliki ya mbula 52, ayaki na departema ya lobiko ya lobangu mpo na bolongoli misuni ya pota moko oyo ezali kopesa ntembe na loboko na ye ya mobali. Alobaki ete amonaki pota yango pɔsɔ mingi eleki kasi na ebandeli akanisaki ete ezalaki pota ya moke oyo azwaki na mosala. Kasi, pota yango ekomi monene mpe ezali kosala mpasi mingi, yango nde etindi ye aluka lisungi ya monganga.

src: Upon examination, the lesion appeared as an ulcerated nodule with irregular borders and surrounding erythema. Mr. Hawthorne denied any history of skin cancer or significant sun exposure. He also reported no other symptoms such as fever, chills, or weight loss.
trg: Na ntango ya ekzame, pota yango ezalaki lokola nodule ya pota oyo ezali na bandelo ya mabe mpe na erytheme na zingazinga. M. Hawthorne alobaki ete atikala kobela kanser ya loposo te to atambolaki mingi na moi te. Alobaki mpe ete azalaki na bilembo mosusu te lokola fefele, malili, to kokita kilo.

src: Given the concerning appearance of the lesion, a punch biopsy was performed under local anesthesia. The procedure was well-tolerated, and Mr. Hawthorne was discharged with instructions for wound care and follow-up with dermatology for results.
trg: Lokola pota yango ezalaki kopesa mitungisi, basalaki ye bolongoli misuni na punch na nse ya anesthésie locale. Procedure yango elekaki malamu, mpe M. Hawthorne abimaki na malako mpo na kobatela mpota mpe kozwa boukutani ya bolandeli ya makambo ya loposo mpo na koyeba mbano.

src: The biopsy specimen was sent to pathology for evaluation. The results are pending.
trg: Ndakisa moko ya bolongoli misuni etindamaki na pathologie mpo na botaleli. Mbano ezali kozelama.

src: "Hello, this is Swee Lan Lim, a medical student. I understand you're looking for some information about an arterial biopsy?"
trg: "Mbote, nazali Swee Lan Lim, moyekoli na kelasi ya minganga. Nabanzi ete bozali koluka kozwa bansango mpo na biopisie ya ya misisa?"

src: "That's correct, Swee. My name is Kavita Singh, and I'm a librarian. I've been having some concerning symptoms lately, and my doctor suggested I look into getting a biopsy."
trg: "Ezali bongo, Swee. Kombo na ngai Kavita Singh, mpe nasalaka na biblioteke. Nazalaki koyoka mwa bilembo ya kobangisa na mikolo mileki, mpe monganga na ngai alobaki ete naluka kosala bolongoli ya ndambu ya mosuni."

src: "Okay, Kavita. Can you tell me a little bit more about what's been going on? What kind of symptoms have you been experiencing?"
trg: "Malamu, Kavita. Okoki koyebisa nga mwa moke makambo oyo ezali kosalema? Okutanaki na bilembo nini?"

src: "Well, I've been having some numbness and tingling in my hands and feet, and sometimes my fingers turn white or blue when I'm cold. My doctor mentioned something called vasculitis, and said an arterial biopsy could help confirm the diagnosis."
trg: "Nazali koyoka nzoto kolemba mpe koswa na maboko mpe na makolo, mpe na bantango mosusu misapi na ngai ekomaka mpembe to ble soki nazali koyoka malili. Monganga na ngai alobelaki eloko moko babengi vaskilarité, mpe alobaki ete bolongoli misuni ekoki kosalisa mpo na koyebanisa maladi yango."

src: "That sounds like Raynaud's phenomenon, which can sometimes be associated with vasculitis. An arterial biopsy involves taking a small sample of tissue from an artery, usually the temporal artery on the side of your head, to look for inflammation under a microscope."
trg: "Yango ezali lokola fenomene ya Raynaud, oyo na bantango mosusu ekoki kokokisama na vaskilarité. Bolongoli misuni esengaka kozwa mwa eteni moke ya mosuni na nzoto, mbala mingi mosuni ya monene oyo ezalaka mopanzi ya motó na yo, mpo na koluka kovimba moko na mikroskope."

src: "Is it a painful procedure? Will I need to stay in the hospital?"
trg: "Kosalisa yango esalaka mpasi? Ekosenga ngai natikala na lopitalo?"

src: "It's generally a minor procedure performed under local anesthesia, so you shouldn't feel much pain during the biopsy itself. You might have some soreness afterwards, but over-the-counter pain medication should help. It's usually done as an outpatient procedure, so you'll likely be able to go home the same day."
trg: "Mbala mingi ezalaka kaka likambo ya moke oyo basalaka na nse ya anastézi ya mboka, yango wana okoyoka mpasi mingi te ntango bazali kosala bolingoli ya misuni yango. Okoki kozala na mwa mpasi na nsima, kasi bankisi ya kosilisa mpasi oyo batɛkaka na farmasi ekoki kosunga yo. Mbala mingi basalaka yango na kozanga kolala na lopitalo, yango wana mbala mosusu okoki kozonga na ndako mokolo yango kaka."

src: "That's a relief. Are there any risks involved?"
trg: "Ezali kopesa ngai kimya. Ezalaka na makama?"

src: "As with any procedure, there are some risks, such as bleeding, infection, or nerve damage, but these are rare. Your doctor will discuss the risks and benefits with you in more detail before the procedure."
trg: "Ndenge moko na mosala nyonso, ezalaka na mwa makama, lokola kobima makila, bokono, to kozoka na misisa, kasi makambo yango ekomaka mpenza te. Monganga na yo akolobela yo oyo etali makama mpe matomba na yango malamumalamu liboso ya kosala yango."

src: "Okay, that sounds reasonable. How do I go about scheduling the biopsy?"
trg: "Malamu, ezali komonana malamu. Ndenge nini nakoki kosala mpo na kozwa programe ya bolongoli misuni?"

src: "Since this is a telehealth service, I can help you connect with a specialist who performs arterial biopsies. We can schedule a consultation for you to discuss the procedure further and answer any other questions you may have. Would you like me to do that for you?"
trg: "Lokola ezali kozwa lisungi ya monganga na mosika, nakoki kosalisa yo okutana na nganga-buka oyo asalaka bolongoli misuni. Tokoki kozwela yo bokutani mpo botalela lisusu likambo yango mpe ayanola yo na mituna mosusu oyo okoki kozala na yango. Olingi nasala yango mpo na yo?"

src: "Yes, please. That would be very helpful."
trg: "Ee, palado. Ekosalisa penza."

src: "Great. Let me get some information from you, and we'll get that set up."
trg: "Malamu. Tiká nazwa mwa sango epai na yo, mpe tokobongisa yango."

src: Good morning, Hanna! It's wonderful to meet you. I understand you're here for the clinical trial screening related to food allergies. That's fantastic! Participating in research like this is incredibly valuable. It helps us understand allergies better and potentially develop new treatments that could benefit so many people, including yourself.
trg: Mbote, Hanna! Ezali esengo komona yo. Nayoki ete oye mpo na botaleli ya boyekoli ya maladi etali bopekisi ya bilei. Ezali malamu mpenza! Kosangana na boyekoli ya ndenge wana ezali na ntina mingi. Esalisaka biso na koyeba malamu bipekiseli mpe kosala bankisi ya sika oyo ekoki kosunga bato mingi, ata mpe yo moko.

src: I know the idea of a clinical trial can sometimes feel a bit daunting, but please know that your safety and well-being are our top priorities throughout the entire process. The screening today is just the first step, and it's a great opportunity for you to learn more about the study and ask any questions you might have.
trg: Nayebi ete likanisi ya kosangana na boyekoli ya maladi ekoki kopesa mwa bobangi, kasi yeba ete libateli mpe bolamu na yo nde ekozwa esika ya liboso na ntango nyonso ya mosala oyo. Botaleli ya lelo ezali kaka etambe ya liboso, mpe ezali libaku ya malamu mpo na yo oyeba makambo mingi etali boyekoli mpe otuna mituna nyonso oyo okoki kozala na yango.

src: Remember, you're not just a participant; you're a partner in this journey towards better health. Your contribution could make a real difference in the lives of others facing similar challenges. So take a deep breath, relax, and let's get started. We're here to support you every step of the way. Do you have any questions before we begin? We're so glad you're here, Hanna. Let's do this together!
trg: Yeba ete, ozali kaka moto oyo azali kosangana na boyekoli te; ozali moninga na biso na mobembo oyo ya koluka lobiko ya malamu. Lisungi na yo ekoki kobongisa mpenza bomoi ya bato mosusu oyo bazali na mikakatano ndenge moko na yo. Yango wana pema makasi, fanda kimia, mpe tobanda. Tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo na etambe nyonso. Ozali na mituna liboso tobanda? Tozali na esengo mingi ndenge oye, Hanna. Tosala yango elongo!

src: Attending Physician (Dr. Shreya Patel): Okay, so the patient is a 67-year-old female calling with concerns about worsening shortness of breath. Her name is Mrs. Elara Vance. Let's go through her history.
trg: Monganga ya sika (Dr. Shreya Patel): Ok, mobeli azali mwasi ya mibu 67 azali kobenga mpo na mitungisi na ntina na kokatana mpema oyo ezali kobakisama. Kombo na ye Madame Elara Vance. Tótala lisolo na ye ya kala na mae matali kolongono ya nzoto na ye.

src: Resident (Dr. Ravi Kapoor): Alright, Mrs. Vance reports a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She's been taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for several years. Recently, she's noticed increasing difficulty breathing with exertion, like climbing stairs or walking uphill.
trg: Resident (Dr. Ravi Kapoor): Ok, Madame Vance alobi ete azalaka na tansyo ya likolo mpe hyperlipidémie. Amelaka nkisi ya lisinopril mpe atorvastatin na boumeli ya mibu mingi. Kala mingi te, amoni ete azali kokatana mpema mingi ntango azali kosala makasi, lokola komata na baeskalyé to kotambola na ngomba.

src: Dr. Dupont: Any other symptoms? Chest pain, palpitations, dizziness?
trg: Dr. Dupont: Bilembo mosusu? Mpasi na ntolo, motema kobeta nokinoki, kizunguzungu?

src: Dr. Kapoor: No chest pain, but she mentions occasional palpitations and some mild dizziness when standing up quickly. She also reports some swelling in her ankles towards the end of the day.
trg: Dr. Kapoor: Ayokaka mpasi na ntolo te, kasi alobeli motema kobeta nokinoki na bantango mosusu mpe mwa kizunguzungu soki atelemeli noki. Alobi mpe ete makolo na ye evimbaka mwa moke na nsuka ya mokolo.

src: Dr. Dupont: Okay, let's check her vitals. What's her blood pressure and heart rate?
trg: Dr. Dupont: Ok, totalela binama na ye ya bomoi. Tansyo mpe vitesi ya motema na ye ezali boni?

src: Dr. Kapoor: Her blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, and her heart rate is 88 beats per minute. Oxygen saturation is 96% on room air.
trg: Dr. Kapoor: Tansyo ya makila na ye ezali 145/90 mmHg, mpe vitesi ya motema na ye ezali 88 beats na miniti moko. Botongisami ya oxygène ezali 96% na libanda.

src: Dr. Dupont: That blood pressure is a bit high, even with medication. And the ankle swelling could be a sign of fluid retention. Let's ask about her diet and salt intake.
trg: Dr. Dupont: Tansyo wana ezali mwa likolo, atako ameli nkisi. Mpe kovimba ya makolo ekoki kozala elembo ya kobomba mayi na nzoto. Tótuna ye mpo na bilei mpe mungwa oyo alyaka.

src: Dr. Kapoor: She says she tries to eat healthy but admits to enjoying salty snacks occasionally. She hasn't been monitoring her salt intake closely.
trg: Dr. Kapoor: Alobi ete amekaka kolya malamu, kasi andimi ete alyaka biloko ya mungwa na bantango mosusu. Alandelaka penza te mungwa oyo alyaka.

src: Dr. Dupont: We should advise her on reducing salt intake and monitoring her weight daily. Sudden weight gain can indicate fluid retention. Also, let's schedule an echocardiogram to assess her heart function.
trg: Dr. Dupont: Tosengeli kopesa ye toli mpo na kokitisa mungwa oyo alyaka mpe kolandela kilo na ye mokolo na mokolo. Kobakisama ya kilo na mbalakaka ekoki komonisa kobomba mayi na nzoto. Lisusu, tóbongisa echocardiographi mpo na kotala ndenge motema na ye ezali kosala.

src: Dr. Kapoor: Should we adjust her medications?

trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Mbote, namoni oye kozua lisusu mokanda ya nkisi na yo, ezali bongo?

trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Ee, monganga, ezali mpo na nkisi na ngai ya maladi ya jonise. Nazali komela yango banda mwa ntango, kasi emonani lokola esili.

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: I understand. Can you tell me a little bit more about how you've been feeling lately? Have you noticed any changes in your symptoms since you started taking the medication?
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Nayoki. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa moke ndenge ozali komiyoka mikolo oyo? Omoni mbongwana ya bilembo na yo banda obandaki komela nkisi yango?

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Well, to be honest, doctor, I haven't been feeling very well at all. My stomach has been hurting quite a bit, and I've been feeling very tired and weak. And my skin still looks quite yellow, don't you think?
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Malamu, mpo na koloba solo, monganga, nazali komiyoka malamu ata moke te. Libumu na ngai ezali koswa ngai makasi penza mpe nazali koyoka bolembu mpe nazali na makasi te. Mpe loposo na ngai ezali langi ya mosaka, omoni yango te?

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: I do see that your skin has a yellowish tint, Ms. Sinclair. And I'm sorry to hear about your stomach pain and fatigue. Those can be symptoms of jaundice, but they can also be signs of other underlying conditions. Have you noticed any other changes, perhaps in your appetite or digestion?
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Namoni ete loposo na yo ezali na langi ya mosaka, Madame Sinclair. Mpe nayoki mawa mpo na mpasi ya libumu na yo mpe bolembu. Yango ekoki kozala bilembo ya jonise, kasi ekoki mpe kozala bilembo ya maladi mosusu. Omoni bambongwana misusu, na ndakisa na mae matali mposa na yo ya kolya to na ndenge ozali konika bilei?

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Now that you mention it, I haven't had much of an appetite lately. And I've been feeling a bit nauseous after eating.
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Lokola olobeli yango, nazali na mposa ya kolya mingi te mikolo oyo. Mpe motema ezali kobalukabaluka na nsima ya kolya.

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: I see. It's important that we get to the bottom of what's causing your symptoms, Ms. Sinclair. While I can certainly refill your prescription for the jaundice medication, I would also like to schedule some further tests to rule out any other potential causes for your discomfort.
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Nayoki. Ezali na ntina ete toyeba nini ezali kopesa yo bilembo oyo, Madame Sinclair. Ata soki nakoki kopesa yo lisusu mokanda ya bankisi ya jonise, nalingi mpe osalisa baekzame mosusu mpo na koyeba kolongola ntina mosusu ya mpasi na yo.

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Tests? What kind of tests?
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Baekzame? Baekzame ya ndenge nini?

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: We'll start with some blood work to check your liver function and bilirubin levels. Depending on the results, we may also need to do an ultrasound or other imaging tests to get a better look at your liver and gallbladder.
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Tokobanda na botaleli ya makila mpo na kotala ndenge libale na yo ezali kosala mpe nivo ya bilirubine. Na kolanda mbano, tokoki mpe kosala ekografi to baekzame misusu ya bililingi mpo na komona malamu libale na yo mpe mwa saki moke ya nsongi.

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Oh, I see. Is it serious, doctor?
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Ah, nayoki. Ezali makasi, monganga?

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: It's too early to say for sure, Ms. Sinclair. But by running these tests, we can get a better understanding of what's going on and ensure that we're providing you with the most appropriate treatment.
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Tozali naino na ebandeli penza mpo na kolobela yo yango na bosikisiki, Madame Sinclair. Kasi baekzame oyo, ekoki kosunga biso tozala na bososoli malamu ya makambo oyo ezali kosalema mpe kopesa lobiko oyo ebongi mpenza.

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Alright, doctor. Whatever you think is best.
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Malamu, monganga. Nyonso oyo okanisi ezali malamu.

src: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Thank you for your cooperation, Ms. Sinclair. I'll go ahead and write you a prescription for the refill, and my nurse will help you schedule the blood work. We'll get to the bottom of this together.
trg: Dr. Roberto Gonzales: Matondi mpo na boyokani na yo, Madame Sinclair. Nakokomela yo mokanda ya bankisi ya komela lisusu, mpe lifulume na ngai akosalisa yo mpo na kokanga mokolo ya bokutani mpo na ekzame ya makila. Tokolonga likambo yango elongo.

src: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Thank you, doctor. I appreciate your help.
trg: Ms. Ophelia Sinclair: Matondi, monganga. Nasepeli mingi mpo na lisungi na yo.

src: Given your garrulous nature and family history of Bloom syndrome, understanding your situation is crucial. Bloom syndrome is a serious, inherited disorder characterized by significant growth delays, sun sensitivity, and an increased risk of various cancers. It's vital to be aware of the potential signs and symptoms, which include:
trg: Na kolanda ezalela na yo ya koloba mingi mpe lisolo ya libota na yo mpo na maladi ya Bloom, kososola ezalela na yo ezali na ntina. Maladi ya Bloom ezali maladi monene oyo basangolaka, bilembo na yango ezalaka kozanga kokola malamu, komiyoka mabe na moi mpe bakanser ya ndenge na ndenge. Ezali likambo ya ntina koyeba bilembo mpe bimoniseli oyo ekoki kozala:

src: Severe sun sensitivity: Even brief sun exposure can lead to skin rashes and blisters.
trg: Komiyoka mabe makasi na moi: Ata kotikala na nse ya moi mpo na mwa ntangu moke ekoki kopesa mpasi na loposo mpe maputu.

src: Short stature: Individuals with Bloom syndrome typically experience significant growth delays.
trg: Kozala mokuse: Bato oyo bazalaka na maladi ya Bloom mbala mingi bakolaka na lobangu te.

src: Distinctive facial features: A long, narrow face with a small jaw and prominent nose is often characteristic.
trg: Bilembo ya kokesenisa elongi: Elongi ya molai mpe moke, na mbanga ya moke mpe zolo ya monene ezalaka mbala mingi bilembo.

src: Increased cancer risk: Bloom syndrome significantly increases the risk of developing various cancers, including leukemia, lymphoma, and solid tumors.
trg: Likama monene ya kozwa kanser: Maladi ya Bloom ematisaka mingi likama ya kozwa bakanser ya ndenge na ndenge, lokola lesemi, limfoma, mpe ba mbuma ya makasi.

src: Recurrent infections: Due to a weakened immune system, individuals with Bloom syndrome may be more susceptible to infections.
trg: Mikrobe ya mbala na mbala: Lokola ebongiseli oyo ebatelaka nzoto ezali na bolembu, bato oyo bazali na maladi ya Bloom bakoki kozwa mikrobe nokinoki.

src: Learning difficulties: Some individuals may experience learning difficulties or intellectual disabilities.
trg: Mikakatano ya koyekola: Bato mosusu bakoki kozala na mikakatano ya koyekola tokozala bozoba.

src: Given these potential complications, it's imperative to adhere to the following instructions:
trg: Na kolanda mikakatano oyo ekoki kozala, ezali na ntina mingi kolanda malako oyo elandi:

src: Strict sun protection: Avoid direct sun exposure as much as possible. Wear protective clothing, hats, and sunglasses, and apply sunscreen liberally.
trg: Komibatela makasi na moi: Kokima kotikala na nse ya moi. Lata bilamba ya komibatela, ekoti mpe maneti ya moi, mpe pakola kreme ya moi ebele.

src: Regular medical checkups: Schedule regular appointments with your doctor to monitor growth, development, and overall health.
trg: Kozongela monganga mbala na mbala: Zongelaka monganga na yo mbala na mbala mpo na kolandela bokoli, botomboli, mpe kolongono ya nzoto mobimba.

src: Cancer screening: Discuss appropriate cancer screening protocols with your doctor, considering your increased risk.
trg: Kotala kanser: Solola na monganga na yo mae matali ba ndenge ya kotalela kanser oyo ebongi, na kolanda likama na yo ya monene.

src: Genetic counseling: Consult a genetic counselor to understand the inheritance pattern of Bloom syndrome and its implications for your family.
trg: Toli ya genetike: Solola na mopesi-toli ya genetike mpo na kososola ndenge maladi ya Bloom epanzanaka mpe ntina na yango mpo na libota na yo.

src: Support groups: Connect with support groups or organizations dedicated to Bloom syndrome for information and emotional support.
trg: Bituluku ya lisungi: Solola na bituluku ya lisungi to ba bibongiseli oyo etalelaka maladi ya Bloom mpo na kozwa bansango mpe lisungi ya mayoki.

src: Remember, while Bloom syndrome presents challenges, early diagnosis and management can significantly improve outcomes. By following these instructions and working closely with your healthcare team, you can navigate this condition effectively.
trg: Kobosana te, atako maladi ya Bloom ezali na mikakatano, koyeba yango noki mpe kobongama mpo na yango ekoki kobongisa makambo. Na kolanda malako oyo mpe na kosala na boyokani na ekipi na yo ya baminganga, okoki kolonga ezalela oyo malamu.

src: The waiting room is a symphony of coughs and crying children. I perch on the edge of a plastic chair, clutching the paperwork Maya filled out for me. "History of heart murmur," it says. "Slight tremor in hands." I try to hide the tremor by gripping the papers tighter. A nurse calls my name, "Pape Gueye?" She's young, with bright eyes and a kind smile.
trg: Ndako ya kozela ezali na makelele ya batu bazali kokosola mpe bana bazali kolela. Nafandi na nsonge ya kiti ya plastiki, nasimbi ba papyé oyo Maya atondisaki mpo na ngai. Bakomaki,"Lisolo ya kala ya bopemi na motema". "Kolenga muke na maboko." Nameki kobomba kolenga wana na kosimbaka ba papyé makasi. Lifulume moko abengi kombo na ngai, "Pape Gueye?" Azali elenge, na miso ya kongenga mpe na koseka ya malamu.

src: "That's me," I say, pushing myself up. My knees pop audibly.
trg: Nayanolaki na kotombola elongi, "Ezali ngai". Mabolongo na ngai ebeti makelele ya koyokana.

src: "Right this way, Mr. Gueye."
trg: "Leka boye, Mr. Gueye."

src: She leads me to an exam room, takes my vitals, asks about my medications. I rattle off the list - blood pressure, cholesterol, something for the tremor. She nods, typing away on her computer. Then the doctor comes in. Dr. Fassi. He's a tall man with a gentle voice and hands that feel surprisingly warm when he checks my pulse.
trg: Amemi ngai na ndako moko ya baekzame, ameki bilembo na ngai ya bomoi, atuni mpo na bankisi na ngai. Natangi liste na yango - tansyo, kolesterole, nkisi moko mpo na kolenga. Andimi na moto, misu kaka na ordinatere na ye. Na nsima monganga akoti. Dr. Fassi. Azali mobali molayi na mongongo ya malamu mpe maboko oyo ezali na molunge mwa mingi ntango amekaki bokasi na ngai ya bomoyi.

src: "So, ballroom dancing?" he asks, raising an eyebrow.
trg: Atunaki na kotombola mankiki moko "Ebongo, mabina ya ballroom?"

src: "My partner is very persuasive," I admit.
trg: Nandimi, "Moninga na ngai azali na nguya ya kondimisa ngai."

src: He listens to my heart, checks my reflexes, makes me walk back and forth across the small room. I try to stand tall, to move with some semblance of grace. He doesn't say anything, just hums thoughtfully. Finally, he sits down on his stool and looks at me.
trg: Ayoki motema na ngai, atali bajeste na ngai, atambwisi ngai bipayi na bipayi epai na mwa ndako ya muke. Nameki kotelema semba, kotambola na mwa ngolu. Alobi eloko te, kaka konyonyo, azali koknisa. Nsukansuka, afandi na ebonga na ye mpe atali ngai.

src: "Mr. Gueye," he says, "your heart is a little irregular, and your balance isn't what it used to be. But..." He pauses, a small smile playing on his lips. "I see a spark in your eyes. And if Mrs. Gupta is anything like you describe her, I imagine she'll keep you on your toes. Literally."
trg: "Mr. Gueye," alobaki na ngai, "motema na yo ezali mabe, mpe bokatikati na yo ezali lisusu te ndenge ezalaka. Kasi..." Atelemi mwa moke, koseka muke na mbebo na ye. "Namoni mwa moto na miso na yo. Mpe soki Madame Gupta azali ndenge olimboleli ngai ye, nakanisi akomonisa yo mpasi. Ya solo penza."

src: He signs the form with a flourish. "You're cleared to dance, Dikembe. Just... take it easy on the dips, alright?"
trg: Atyaki sinyatire na formilere na lombangu. "Opesami nzela ya kobina, Dikembe. Kaka... malembe na bamuvema ya mukongo na yo, ok?"

src: I walk out of the exam room feeling lighter than I have in years. Maybe I am a dried twig, but even dried twigs can dance in the wind. And with Maya leading, I might just surprise myself.
trg: Nabimi na ndako ya ekzame nazali komiyoka pɛpɛlɛ koleka ndenge nazalaki na mibu mingi. Mbala mosusu nazali etambe ya nzete ekauka, kasi ata bitambe ya nzete bikauka ekoki kobina na mopepe. Mpe na bosungi ya Maya, nakoki komikamwisa ngai moko.

trg: Mosali: Mbote, ezali MediCall, kombo na ngai Anya Petrova. Lolenge nini nakoki kosalisa yo lelo?

src: Operator: It's okay, Leo. Nausea can be very uncomfortable, but we're here to help. Can you tell me a little more about what's been going on?
trg: Mosali: Malamu, Leo. Mposa ya kosanza ekoki kozala mabe makasi, kasi tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo. Okoki koloba na ngai mwa moke makambo oyo ezali koleka?

trg: Mosali: Ok, nayoki. Ozali koyoka bilembo mosusu, neti kosanza to koleka lubumu?

trg: Mosali: Ezali malamu. Tobanda na kopesa yo mayi. Okoki komela ndambu ya biloko ya mayi ya polele, neti mayi to soda ya tangawisi?

trg: Mobeli: Nakoki komeka.

src: Patient: Okay, thank you.
trg: Mobeli: Ok, matondi.

src: Operator: You're welcome, Leo. We'll check back in with you in a little while to see how you're doing. In the meantime, try to rest and relax.
trg: Mosali: Likambu te Leo. Tokobenga yo lisusu na nsima ya mwa ntangu mpo na koyeba nsango na yo. Kasi sikawa, meka kopema mpe kofanda kimia.

src: Patient: Okay, I will. Thank you again.
trg: Mobeli: Ok, nakosala bongo. Matondi lisusu.

src: Operator: No problem. Take care, Leo.
