trg: Ozali komela bankisi sikoyo, ata mpe bankisi oyo batekaka na farmasi to biloko ya kobakisa na bilei ?

src: Okay, noted. Do you have any family history of significant illnesses, particularly cancers or autoimmune diseases?
trg: Ok, nakangi yango. Na libota na bino, esi bobela maladi ya makasi penza lokola kancer to maladi oyo ebundisaka nzoto?

src: And finally, can you tell me a bit about your lifestyle? Do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use any recreational drugs?
trg: Mpe ya suka, okoki kobetela ngai mwa moke na oyo etali bomoi na yo ? Omela makaya, masanga, to omelaka bilangwiseli moko ?

src: Thank you for being so open with me. I'm going to discuss everything we've talked about with the doctor, and we'll come back together to figure out the next steps. Is there anything else you'd like to mention or ask before I go?
trg: Matondi na ndenge olobi na ngai polele. Nakei koyebisa monganga makambo nyonso tosololi, mpe tokoya elongo mpo na koyeba nini tokosala na nsima. Ezali na likambo mosusu oyo olingi koloba to kotuna yambo ete nakende ?

src: Cashier: Hi Dr. Islam, thanks for fitting me in. I'm a cashier at the grocery store, and standing all day has been getting tougher lately. My back and hips have been aching a lot, and I'm worried it might be my osteoporosis.
trg: Kalaka: Mbote Dr. Islam, matondi na ndenge oyambi ngai. Nazalaka kalaka na magazini ya monene biloko ya kolia, mpe kotelema mokolo mobimba ekomi mpasi mingi mikolo oyo. Mokongo mpe loketo na ngai ezali kosala mpasi mingi, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kozala osteoporose na ngai.

src: Dr. Islam: I understand. Osteoporosis can definitely cause pain and make it harder to do things like stand for long periods. Have you noticed any new or worsening pain recently?
trg: Dr. Islam: Nasosoli. Osteoporose ekoki mpenza kopesa mpasi mpe kokomisa makambo makasi lokola kotelema ntango molayi. Omoni mpasi ya sika to oyo ezali kobakisama mikolo oyo?

src: Cashier: Yeah, especially after a few hours on my feet. It feels like a deep ache, and sometimes sharp pains shoot down my legs. I've had to call out a few times because it's just too much.
trg: Kalaka: Ee, mingi mingi na nsima ya mwa bangonga na kotelema. Nazali koyoka mpasi na ndenge ya kati, mpe ntango mosusu mpasi ya makasi ezali kokita mpe komata na makolo na ngai. Esengelaki nabenga mpo na kozwa konje mbala mibale to misato mpo eleki ndelo.

src: Dr. Islam: That sounds tough. It's important to listen to your body. Have you been taking your medication and doing any exercises we discussed?
trg: Dr. Islam: Yango ezali penza mpasi. Ezali ntina koyoka nzoto na yo. Ozali komela nkisi na yo mpe kosala ngalasisi oyo tosololaki?

src: Cashier: I try, but it's hard to find time with my schedule. And honestly, sometimes the exercises make it hurt more.
trg: Kalaka: Namekaka, kasi ezali mpasi kozwa ntango na programe na ngai. Mpe ya solo, ntango mosusu ngalasisi ezali kopesa mpasi koleka.

src: Dr. Islam: That's understandable. Maybe we can adjust your exercise plan to something gentler. In the meantime, given your pain and the nature of your job, I think it would be reasonable to provide you with a note for a few days off to rest and see if that helps.
trg: Dr. Islam: Yango ezali kososolama. Ntangu mosusuete tokoki kobongisa programe ya ngalasisi na yo na eloko ya pete koleka. Na ntango wana, kotalela mpasi na yo mpe lolenge ya mosala na yo, nakanisi ete ekozala malamu kopesa yo mokanda mpo na mwa mikolo ya konje mpo opema mpe omona soki yango ekosalisa yo.

src: Cashier: Really? That would be amazing. I don't want to lose my job, but I just can't keep pushing through the pain like this.
trg: Kalaka: Ya solo? Yango ekozala malamu mingi. Nalingi kobungisa mosala na ngai te, kasi nazali kokoka lisusu te mpasi oyo.

src: Dr. Islam: I can write a note excusing you from work for the next three days. That should give you some time to rest and see if the pain improves. We can also schedule a follow-up appointment to check in and discuss adjusting your treatment plan if needed.
trg: Dr. Islam: Nakoki kokoma mokanda ya kopesa yo konje na mosala mpo na mikolo misato oyo ekoya. Yango esengeli kopesa yo mwa ntango ya kopema mpe komona soki mpasi ekokita. Tokoki mpe kobongisa mokolo ya bokutani ya bolandeli mpo na kotala mpe kosolola bambongwana ya programe ya lisalisi na yo soki esengeli.

src: Cashier: Thank you so much, Dr. Islam. That's a huge relief. I'll definitely rest up and try to do some gentle stretching like you suggested.
trg: Kalaka: Matondi mingi, Dr. Islam. Yango ezali libondisi monene. Nakopema mpenza mpe nakomeka konyolola nzoto na ndenge ya pete lokola opesaki toli.

src: Dr. Islam: You're welcome. Remember, taking care of yourself is the most important thing. If the pain gets worse or doesn't improve after resting, please don't hesitate to call the office.
trg: Dr. Islam: Likambo te. Kobosana te, komibatela yo moko ezali likambo ya ntina mingi koleka. Soki mpasi ekomi makasi to ezali kobonga te na nsima ya kopema, kokakatana te na kobenga na biro.

src: Cashier: I will. Thanks again!
trg: Kalaka: Nakosala yango. Matondi lisusu!

src: Patient Instructions
trg: Malako ya babeli

src: Diagnosis: Post-Cholecystectomy Syndrome
trg: Diagnostiki: Maladi ya nsima ya kolongola sakosi ya nsongi

src: Medication:
trg: Nkisi:

src: Cholestyramine powder: Take 1 scoop mixed with water or juice once daily before breakfast. This medication helps bind bile acids and can relieve diarrhea.
trg: Mputulu ya Cholestyramine: Mela lutu 1 esangisami na mayi to jus mbala moko na mokolo liboso ya kolia bilei ya ntongo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka kokanga acidi ya nsongi mpe ekoki kosilisa pulupulu.

src: Omeprazole 20 mg capsule: Take 1 capsule daily before breakfast. This medication reduces stomach acid and can help with heartburn and indigestion.
trg: Liyunda ya Omeprazole 20 mg: Mela liyunda 1 na mokolo liboso ya kolia bilei ya ntongo. Nkisi oyo ekitisaka asidi ya likundu mpe ekoki kosalisa na kotumba na motema mpe mpasi ya konika bilei.

src: Dicyclomine 10 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet three times daily as needed for abdominal cramping.
trg: Mbuma ya Dicyclomine 10 mg: Mela mbuma 1 mbala misato na mokolo soki osengeli mpo na mpasi ya libumu.

src: Diet:
trg: Bilei:

src: Low-Fat Diet: Avoid fatty, greasy, and fried foods. These can worsen diarrhea and gas.
trg: Bilei ya mafuta moke: Boya bilei ya mafuta, oyo ya kalingama mpe oyo etonda mafuta. Oyo ekoki kovimbisa pulupulu mpe mikinza.

src: Small, Frequent Meals: Eat smaller meals throughout the day instead of three large ones. This helps your digestive system handle food more easily.
trg: Bilei ya mike, mbala na mbala: Lya bilei ya mike na boumeli ya mokolo na esika ya misato ya minene. Yango ekosalisa nzoto na yo na konika bilei.

src: Fiber: Gradually increase fiber intake from fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Fiber can help regulate bowel movements.
trg: Bafibre: Bakisa malembe malembe kolya na yo ya bafibre uta na bambuma, bandunda, mpe mbuma ya mobimba. Fibre ekoki kosalisa kobongisa botamboli ya misopo.

src: Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, especially if experiencing diarrhea.
trg: Komela: Mela biloko ya mayi mingi mpo na kopekisa bokawuki ya mayi na nzoto, mingimingi soki ozali na pulupulu.

src: Activity:
trg: Mosala:

src: Gradually return to normal activities as tolerated.
trg: Zongela malembe malembe misala ya momeseno na kolanda bokoki na yo.

src: Avoid heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for the first few weeks.
trg: Boya komema biloko ya kilo to kosala ngalasisi ya makasi na baposo ya liboso.

src: Follow-up:
trg: Kolandela:

src: Schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to monitor progress.
trg: Bongisa mokolo ya bokutani ya kolandelama na baposo 2 mpo na kotala bokoli.

src: Call the office if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
trg: Benga biro soki bilembo bibebi to bibongi te.

src: Keep a food diary to identify trigger foods that worsen symptoms.
trg: Batela kahier ya bilei mpo na koyeba bilei oyo ebandisaka bilembo.

src: Avoid alcohol and caffeine, as they can irritate the digestive system.
trg: Boya masanga mpe kaféine, mpamba te ekoki kosuasa binama ya konikela bilei.

src: Quit smoking, as it can delay healing and worsen digestive problems.
trg: Tika komela makaya, mpamba te ekoki kowumisa lobiko mpe kobebisa mikakatano ya bonikami ya bilei.

src: Manage stress, as it can exacerbate symptoms.
trg: Yeba koyangela mitungisi na yo ya makanisi, mpamba te ekoki kobakisa bilembo.

src: Emergency Warning Signs:
trg: Bilembo ya likebisi ya mbangu:

src: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience:
trg: Luka lisalisi ya monganga nokinoki soki ozali na bilembo biye bilandi:

src: Severe abdominal pain
trg: Mpasi makasi ya libumu

src: Fever over 101°F (38.3°C)
trg: Fefele koleka 101°F (38.3°C)

src: Jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes)
trg: Jonise (Loposo to miso ekomi na langi ya mosaka)

src: Persistent vomiting
trg: Kosanza mbala na mbala

src: Bloody or black stools
trg: Nyei ya makila to ya moindo

src: Please do not hesitate to contact our office with any questions or concerns. We are committed to helping you feel better.
trg: Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te kobenga biro na biso. Tozali awa mpo na kosalisa yo oyoka malamu.

src: Doctor: Kwame! Oh, my goodness, it's so good to see you! I was just telling my husband the other day that I hadn't seen you in ages. How are you doing? How's the family?
trg: Monganga: Kwame! Ee, Nzambe na ngai, nasepeli makasi penza komona yo! Nabandaki koyebisa mobali na ngai lobi kuna ete namoni yo te banda kala penza. Boni yo? Boni libota?

src: Kwame: Hello, Dr. Rodriguez. It's good to see you too, although I wish it were under better circumstances. The family is fine, thank you.
trg: Kwame: Mbote, Dr. Rodriguez. Nasepeli komona yo mpe, atako nalingaki ezala na libaku moko ya malamu. Libota ezali malamu, matondi.

src: Doctor: I understand, I understand. Now, I see here that you're in for some pain. Can you tell me a little more about what's going on?
trg: Monganga: Nayebi, nayebi. Sikoyo, namoni awa ete ozali na mpasi. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa moke makambo oyo ezali koleka?

src: Kwame: Yes, well, it's... it's embarrassing, really. I've been having these terrible cramps in my lower abdomen, and it feels just like... well, like period pain.
trg: Kwame: Ee, likambu te, ezali... ezali kosala ngai nsoni. Nazali koyoka mpasi ya makasi penza na nse ya libumu na ngai, mpe ezali koyokana lokola... lokola mpasi ya kokoma ya sanza na ngai.

src: Doctor: Oh, Kwame, I'm so sorry to hear that. I can imagine how uncomfortable and confusing that must be for you. Have you been experiencing any other symptoms? Nausea, vomiting, anything like that?
trg: Monganga: Oh, Kwame, nazali na mawa mingi koyoka yango. Nakoki kokanisa ndenge nini omiyoki mabe mpe ozali kotungisama mingi mpo na yango. Otikala kozala na bilembo misusu? Motema ya kobaluka, kosanza, to eloko ya ndenge wana?

src: Kwame: No, just the pain. It comes and goes, but when it hits, it's excruciating.
trg: Kwame: Te, kaka mpasi. Eyaka mpe ekendaka, kasi ntangu eyaka, epesaka mpasi makasi.

src: Doctor: I see. And how long has this been going on?
trg: Monganga: Namoni. Mpe ezali kosalayo bongo banda ntango nini?

src: Kwame: A few days now. I tried taking some painkillers, but they haven't really helped.
trg: Kwame: Esali mwa mikolo sikoyo. Namekaki komela mwa bankisi ya mpasi, kasi esalisaki mpenza te.

src: Doctor: Okay. Well, let's get you checked out and see if we can figure out what's causing this. It could be a number of things, so we'll need to run some tests. But don't worry, we'll get to the bottom of it.
trg: Monganga: OK. Tiká tósala yo ekzame mpe tómona soki tokoki koyeba mpo na nini ezali kosala bongo. Ekoki kolakisa makambo ebele, yango wana tosengeli kosala mwa ba ekzame. Kasi komitungisa te, tokoyeba ntina na yango.

src: Kwame: Thank you, Dr. Rodriguez. I appreciate your help.
trg: Kwame: Matondi, Dr. Rodriguez. Nazali kosepela na lisalisi na yo.

src: Doctor: Of course, Kwame. You know I'm always here for you. Now, let's get you into an exam room and see what we can find.
trg: Monganga: Ya solo, Kwame. Oyebi ete nazalaka ntango nyonso awa mpo na yo. Sikoyo, tókende na esika ya kosala ekzame mpe tómona nini tokoki kozwa.

src: Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gutierrez. I see you've been experiencing some symptoms after your injury at work. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
trg: Monganga: Mbote, Madame Gutierrez. Namoni ozali na bilembo na nsima ya likama na yo na mosala. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa makambo mingi oyo ezali kosalema?

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: Good morning, Doctor. Yes, ever since the accident, I've been having these terrible headaches. And my stomach... it just feels like it's in knots all the time. I've seen a few other doctors, but they can't seem to find anything wrong with me physically.
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Mbote, Monganga. Iyo, uta likama esalemaki, nazali koyoka motu mpasi makasi. Mpe libumu na ngai... nayokaka lokola nde ekangamaka ntango nyonso. Namonaki minganga mosusu, kasi bamonaki eloko te ya mabe na nzoto na ngai.

src: Doctor: I understand that must be frustrating. It's important to explore all possibilities. Have you noticed any patterns with these symptoms? Do they get worse at certain times or in certain situations?
trg: Monganga: Nayebi ete ezali mpasi. Ezali na ntina kotala makambo nyonso oyo ekoki kozala. Omonaki soki bilembo yango ezali koya na lolenge moko boye? Ezali kokoma makasi na bantango mosusu to na bantangu mosusu?

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: Now that you mention it, they do seem to get worse when I think about going back to work. Or even just when I drive past the building where it happened. My heart starts racing, and I just feel... panicked.
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Sikoyo lokola olobi yango, emonani ete ezali kokoma makasi ntango nazali kokanisa kozonga na mosala. To ata ntango naleki pene ya ndako esika likama esalemaki. Motema na ngai ebandi kobeta makasi, mpe nayokaka... kobanga.

src: Doctor: It sounds like you might be experiencing something called somatic symptom disorder. Sometimes, our bodies react to emotional stress or trauma with physical symptoms. It's like your body is trying to tell you something that your mind is having trouble processing.
trg: Monganga: Emonani lokola ozali na maladi oyo babengi somatoform. Ntango mosusu, nzoto na biso esalaka makambo mpo na mitungisi na biso ya makanisi to likama na nzela ya bilembo ya nzoto. Ezali lokola nzoto na yo ezali komeka koyebisa yo likambo oyo makanisi na yo ezali na mokakatano ya kokanga ntina.

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: Really? I never thought of it that way. But it makes sense. I've been so worried about everything – money, my job, whether I'll ever feel normal again.
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Ya solo? Nakanisaki naino bongo te. Kasi ezali na ntina. Nazalaki komitungisa mingi mpo na makambo nyonso – mbongo, mosala na ngai, soki nakozala lisusu malamu.

src: Doctor: It's completely understandable to feel that way after a traumatic event. The good news is that there are treatments available that can help. We can work together to address both the physical symptoms and the underlying emotional stress.
trg: Monganga: Ezali mpenza mabe te komiyoka bongo nsima ya likama ya mpasi. Nsango ya malamu ezali ete ezali na bankisi oyo ekoki kosunga. Tokoki kosala elongo mpo na kosilisa bilembo ya nzoto mpe mitungisi ya makanisi na mayoki oyo ezali ekomaka.

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: That sounds promising. What kind of treatments are we talking about?
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Emonani malamu ete ekoki kosunga. Tozali kolobela bankisi ya ndenge nini?

src: Doctor: Cognitive-behavioral therapy, or CBT, is often very effective. It can help you identify and change negative thought patterns that might be contributing to your symptoms. We can also discuss medication options if necessary, or other therapies like relaxation techniques or mindfulness.
trg: Monganga: Lobiko ya bizaleli ya komona, to CBT, mbala mingi ezalaka na mosala makasi. Ekoki kosunga yo koyeba mpe kobongola makanisi ya mabe oyo ekoki kozala kopesa nzela na bilembo na yo. Tokoki mpe kolobela nkisi soki esengeli, to lobiko mosusu lokola mayele ya kominyolisisa nzoto to kobenda makanisi.

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: I'm willing to try anything that might help. I just want to feel like myself again.
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Nalingi komeka eloko nyonso oyo ekoki kosunga ngai. Nalingi kaka komiyoka lisusu ngai moko.

src: Doctor: That's a great attitude to have. We'll take it one step at a time. Let's start by scheduling some regular appointments so we can monitor your progress and adjust your treatment plan as needed. And remember, you're not alone in this. We're here to support you every step of the way.
trg: Monganga: Yango ezali makanisi ya malamu. Tokokende mokemoke. Tokobanda na kozwa bokutana ya mbala na mbala mpo tokoka kolanda bokoli na yo mpe kobongisa mwango ya lobiko na yo soki esengeli. Mpe kobosana te, ozali yo moko te na likambo oyo. Tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo na bitambe nyonso.

src: Mrs. Gutierrez: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate that.
trg: Madame Gutierrez: Matondi, Monganga. Nasepeli mingi na yango.

src: Pharmacist: I understand you're looking for something to help with your adrenal glands and fatigue. Can you tell me more about what your doctor said and what symptoms you're experiencing?
trg: Moteki na Farmasi: Nayoki ete ozali koluka eloko mpo na kosalisa yo na maladi ya glande surrénale mpe kolemba. Okoki koyebisa ngai lisusu nini monganga na yo alobaki mpe bilembo nini ozali komona?

src: Patient: Look, I just told you! I'm tired, I'm stressed, and my doctor said it might be adrenal fatigue. I need a supplement or something to fix it. Don't you have anything like that? Why do you need to know all the details? Just give me something that works!
trg: Mobeli: Tala, nauti koyebisa yo! Nazali na bolembu, nazali kotungisama na makanisi, mpe monganga na ngai alobaki ete ekoki kozala bolembu ya baselile. Nazali na mposa ya bilei moko ya kobakisama to eloko mosusu mpo na kobongisa yango. Ozali na eloko ya bongo te? Mpo na nini ozali na mposa ya koyeba makambo nyonso? Pesa ngai kaka eloko oyo esalaka!

src: Pharmacist: I appreciate you sharing that. To recommend the best product, I need to know if you're taking any other medications or have any other health conditions. Some supplements can interact with medications. Did your doctor recommend a specific product or ingredient?
trg: Moteki na Farmasi: Natondi botondi na ndenge oyebisi ngai yango. Mpo na kopesa toli ya nkisi oyo eleki malamu, nasengeli koyeba soki ozali komela nkisi mosusu to ozali na maladi mosusu. Bilei misusu ya kobakisa ekoki kobebisa makasi ya bankisi mosusu. Monganga na yo apesaki yo toli moko na oyo etali nkisi to vitamini moko boye?

src: Patient: No, he didn't give me a specific name. He just said to look for something for adrenal support. And I'm not taking any other medications, okay? Just give me whatever is best. I don't have all day to stand here answering questions!
trg: Mobeli: Te, apesaki ngai kombo moko te. Alobaki na ngai kaka ete naluka nkisi moko mpo na kosunga baselile. Mpe nazali komela nkisi mosusu te, oyoki? Pesa ngai kaka oyo eleki malamu. Nazali na mokolo mobimba awa te mpo na kopesa biyano na mituna!

src: Pharmacist: Okay, I can show you some options for adrenal support supplements. However, since you haven't had a specific recommendation, I would advise consulting your doctor again to be sure which product is right for you. These supplements are not regulated like prescription drugs, and their effectiveness for "adrenal fatigue" isn't fully established medically.
trg: Moteki na Farmasi: Ok, nakoki kolakisa yo biponi mwa mingi ya bilei ya kobakisa mpo na kosunga baselile. Kasi, lokola otikala kozwa toli moko boye te, nasengi yo osolola lisusu na monganga na yo mpo na koyeba eloko nini ebongi na yo. Bilei ya kobakisa oyo ezalaka ndenge moko te na bankisi oyo monganga akomaka, mpe makasi na yango mpo na "bolembu ya baselile" endimisami naino malamu te na baminganga.

src: Patient: What do you mean "not established"? My doctor said it's a real thing! Are you saying he's wrong? I just want something to help me feel better! Why are you making this so difficult? Just give me the best one you have!
trg: Mobeli: Olingi koloba nini na "eendimami naino malamu te"? Monganga na ngai alobaki ete ezali likambo ya solo! Olingi koloba ete azali na libunga nini? Nalingi kaka eloko mpo na kosalisa ngai na koyoka malamu! Mpo na nini ozali kokomisa likambo oyo pasi boye? Pesa ngai kaka oyo eleki malamu oza na yango!

src: Pharmacist: I'm not saying your doctor is wrong. I'm just saying that different products have different ingredients and effects. Without a specific recommendation, it's hard to know which one would be most helpful and safe for you. I can show you the aisle where these supplements are located, but I recommend discussing specific options with your doctor.
trg: Moteki na Farmasi: Nazali koloba te ete monganga na yo azali na libunga. Nazali kaka koloba ete nkisi nyonso ezalaka na ndenge na yango mpe mbuma na yango. Soki toli moko boye ezali te, ezali mpasi koyeba oyo wapi ekoki kosunga yo mingi mpe kozala malamu mpo na yo. Nakoki kolakisa yo esika bilei ya kobakisa yango ezalaka, kasi napesi yo toli ya kosolola na monganga na yo mpo na koyeba oyo wapi okopona.

src: Patient: Fine! Just show me where they are. I'll figure it out myself. You pharmacists are useless sometimes! I'll talk to my doctor, but I'm buying something today regardless!
trg: Mobeli: Ezali malamu! Lakisa ngai kaka esika ezali. Nakoluka ngai moko. Bino bateki nkisi bozali na ntina te na bantango mosusu! Nakosolola na monganga na ngai, kasi nakosomba eloko lelo atako ndenge nini!

src: I'm here for an evaluation, I guess. My boss said I needed to come after I got hurt at work. I fell off a ladder, maybe six feet? I don't remember much, just waking up with a headache and my back hurting. I've always been a bit clumsy, I suppose. My mom used to say I had two left feet.
trg: Nazali awa mpo na komekama, nakanisi. Patron na ngai alobaki na ngai ete nasengeli koya nsima ya kozoka na ngai na mosala. Nakweaki na ebutelo, mbala mosusu na bolai ya makolo motoba? Nazali komikundola makambu mingi te, nayebi kaka ete ntangu nalamukaki, motó na mukongo ebandaki kosala ngaoi mpasi. Nazalaka ntango nyonso mwa kilo, nakanisi. Mama na ngai azalaki koloba nazalaka na makolo mibale ya mwasi.

src: But this is about more than just the fall, right? They keep asking me about school and stuff. I struggled a lot in school. Reading and math were always hard. I got held back in second grade, and I think I was in special classes for reading until high school. I dropped out in 11th grade. Just couldn't keep up.
trg: Kasi oyo etali makambo mosusu longola kaka kokwea, boye te? Bazali kotuna ngai makambo ya kelasi mpe biloko mosusu. Nasalaki milende mingi na kelasi. Kotanga mpe matematiki ezalaki ntango nyonso mpasi. Nazongaki nsima na kelasi ya mibale, mpe nakanisi nazalaki na bakelasi ya sipesiale mpo na kotanga tii na secondaire. Natikaki kelasi na kelasi ya 11. Nabandaki kokoka lisusu makambu te.

src: I've always had trouble learning new things. Like, at work, if they change the way we do something, it takes me a long time to get it. My boss gets frustrated sometimes. I try my best, but things just don't stick in my head like they do for other people.
trg: Nazalaka na mokakatano ya koyekola makambo ya sika. Na ndakisa, na mosala, soki babongoli lolenge tomesana kosala eloko moko, ezwaka ngai ntango molai mpo nako kanga yango. Patro na ngai asilikaka ntango mosusu. Nasala milende penza, kasi makambo ekotaka na motó na ngai te ndenge ekotaka na mitó ya bato misusu.

src: And remembering things... that's a struggle too. I forget names, appointments, even simple things like where I put my keys. My wife helps me keep track of stuff, but it's embarrassing sometimes.
trg: Mpe komikundola makambo... wana mpe ezali etumba. Nabosanaka bankombo, bokutani, ata biloko ya mpamba lokola esika natie bafungola na ngai. Mwasi na ngai asalisaka ngai mpo na kolandela yango, kasi ezali koyokisa ngai nsoni ntango mosusu.

src: I've had other health problems too. Diabetes, high blood pressure... I take a lot of pills. And I get these headaches sometimes, really bad ones. They make me dizzy and sick to my stomach.
trg: Nazwaki mpe mikakatano mosusu ya kolongono ya nzoto mpe. Diabeti, tansyo... Namelaka bankisi mingi. Mpe motó ebetaka ngai na bantango mosusu, ya makasi mpenza. Epasaka ngai kizunguzungu mpe ebelisaka likundu na ngai.

src: Instructions for Mr. Zondi:
trg: Malako mpo na Mesyé Zondi:

src: Furosemide: Take one 40 mg tablet by mouth every morning. This medication helps remove excess fluid from your body, which can improve your heart function and reduce swelling.
trg: Furosemide: Mela komprimé moko ya 40 mg na monoko ntongo nyonso. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kokawusa mayi oyo eleki na nzoto, oyo ekoki kobongisa esaleli ya motema na yo mpe kokitisa kovimba.

src: Metoprolol: Take one 50 mg tablet by mouth twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. This medication helps control your heart rate and blood pressure.
trg: Metoprolol: Mela komprimé moko ya 50 mg na monoko mbala mibale na mokolo, moko na ntongo mpe moko na mpokwa. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kotalela ebeteli ya motema na yo mpe tensyo ya makila.

src: Lisinopril: Take one 20 mg tablet by mouth once daily. This medication helps relax your blood vessels and lower your blood pressure.
trg: Lisinopril: Mela komprimé moko ya 20 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kofongola misisa ya makila mpe kokitisa tensyo ya makila na yo.

src: Atorvastatin: Take one 40 mg tablet by mouth once daily at bedtime. This medication helps lower your cholesterol levels.
trg: Atorvastatin: Mela komprimé moko ya 40 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo na ntango ya kolala. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kokitisa kolesterole na yo.

src: Aspirin: Take one 81 mg tablet by mouth once daily. This medication helps prevent blood clots.
trg: Aspirin: Mela komprimé moko ya 81 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kopekisa kokangama ya makila.

src: Limit your salt intake to less than 2,000 mg per day. Avoid adding salt to your food and choose low-sodium options when possible.
trg: Kitisa kolya mungwa na yo na nse ya 2,000 mg na mokolo. Boya kobakisa mungwa na bilei na yo mpe pona biloko oyo ezali na sodium moke soki likoki ezali.

src: Limit your fluid intake to 2 liters per day. This includes water, juice, soup, and other beverages.
trg: Kitisa komela na yo ya biloko ya mayi na balitre 2 na mokolo. Yango etali mayi, jus, supu, mpe masanga mosusu.

src: Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Avoid processed foods, sugary drinks, and excessive amounts of saturated and trans fats.

src: Avoid strenuous activity or heavy lifting.

src: Rest when you feel tired.
trg: Pema soki ozali komiyoka ya kolemba.

src: Today, I saw Dr. Wilson because I've been struggling lately, acting in ways that feel completely out of character. It's embarrassing to admit, but I've been having these intense outbursts—tantrums, even hitting things—and it's honestly scary. I'm a PhD candidate, researching complex social dynamics, and here I am, unable to regulate my own emotions. It feels like a huge pressure cooker inside me, and sometimes the lid just blows off.
trg: Lelo, nakutanaki Dr. Wilson mpo nazali konyokwama mikolo oyo, kozala na bizaleli oyo ezali ya ngai te. Ezali kosala mwa nsoni kondima, kasi nazali na nkanda makasi, ata kobeta biloko, mpe ezali kobangisa. Nazali moyekoli ya PhD, nasalaka bolukiluki ya makambo ya bomoi ya bato, mpe sikoyo, nakoki te koyangela mayoki na ngai moko. Ezali lokola esaleli ya kikuku na kati na ngai, mpe na bantango mosusu epanzanaka.

src: I tried to explain to Dr. Wilson that the stress of my dissertation, the constant deadlines, and the isolation of academic work are getting to me. But it's more than just stress; it feels like something deeper is wrong. Maybe it's a lack of sleep, or maybe it's just the sheer weight of expectations I've placed on myself. I found myself getting teary-eyed just talking about it, which is another thing I'm not used to.
trg: Namekaki kolimbwela Dr. Wilson ete mitungisi ya ekzame na ngai, ntango ya kosilisa mosala, mpe kozanga komona bato na mosala ya kelasi ezali kopesa ngai mitungisi. Kasi ezali koleka mitungisi ya mpamba; emonani lokola likambo mosusu ya mozindo ezali mabe. Mbala mosusu ezali kozanga mpongi, to mbala mosusu ezali kaka kilo ya makambo oyo namityelaki. Namonaki ete nazali kolela ntango nazalaki kolobela yango, likambo oyo namesana na yango te.
